reason: A 60-patient pilot with a time-to-healing endpoint has little power to show a modest healing-speed gain over silver sulfadiazine, even if MW-III is somewhat faster.
rationale: Silver sulfadiazine is known to slow re-epithelialization relative to modern dressings, so a topical alternative plausibly heals faster (HR ~1.3-1.5). But with 60 patients and ~45 healing events, power for such an effect is only about 30-40%. Tiny private sponsor, trial registered in 2011, started 2022 and still recruiting, so timely public results are very unlikely; enrolment probably slips past the registered completion date.
evidence: Wasiak et al., Cochrane review of dressings for superficial and partial thickness burns, 2013

assumptions.claim: Silver sulfadiazine is associated with slower healing of partial-thickness burns than several alternative dressings.
assumptions.source: Wasiak et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2013

reason: CT densitometry is noisy (inspiration level, scanner changes over 3 years) and placebo decline may be slower than assumed, so a real but small density benefit could miss significance.
rationale: RAPID showed alpha1-PI 60 mg/kg slowed annual CT density loss by ~0.74 g/L/yr (p=0.03 at TLC) with ~90 per arm over 2 years; EXACTLE trended the same way. SPARTA runs 3 years with ~115 per arm and tests a higher 120 mg/kg dose, so power should exceed RAPID's, giving a fair chance of significance. Risks are measurement noise, dropouts over 3 years and a possibly flat dose-response. Grifols, as a listed company, will likely announce topline in H1 2027.
evidence: EXACTLE (Dirksen et al., Eur Respir J 2009)
RAPID-OLE (McElvaney et al., Lancet Respir Med 2017)

assumptions.claim: In RAPID, annual decline in CT lung density at TLC was 1.45 g/L/yr with alpha1-PI 60 mg/kg vs 2.19 g/L/yr with placebo (p=0.03).
In EXACTLE, alpha1-PI augmentation showed a non-significant trend toward slower decline in 15th-percentile lung density over about 2.5 years.
assumptions.source: Dirksen et al., Eur Respir J 2009 (EXACTLE)

reason: The comparator already gets GnRH agonist plus bicalutamide and radiotherapy, so metastasis and death events are rare and partly non-cancer deaths, diluting the apalutamide advantage.
rationale: Intensifying ADT with a next-generation AR-pathway inhibitor improved MFS markedly in high-risk non-metastatic disease (STAMPEDE abiraterone HR 0.53), and enzalutamide beat first-generation antiandrogens in ENZAMET. Here the comparator is bicalutamide plus ADT, so the expected HR is ~0.7-0.78; with ~300-350 events power is roughly 70-80%. Event-driven timing has slipped for years, so a readout by mid-2027 is uncertain.
evidence: STAMPEDE abiraterone M0 meta-analysis (Attard et al., Lancet 2022)

assumptions.claim: Adding abiraterone to ADT in high-risk non-metastatic prostate cancer improved metastasis-free survival with HR about 0.53.
In SPARTAN, discontinuation due to adverse events was 10.6% with apalutamide vs 7.0% with placebo.

reason: Completed Takeda pediatric PREA study; results likely posted on ClinicalTrials.gov around the one-year deadline (July 2027), with little reason to stop or rewrite the primary outcome.
rationale: Trial is already completed (primary completion July 2026), so termination is near impossible. Takeda generally posts results within the 12-month window, and this pediatric study supports a regulatory requirement, so posting by August 2027 is likely though not certain. Primary outcome changes after completion are uncommon beyond rewording at results posting.

reason: Spleen response should clearly favour pacritinib, but the second primary (TSS50 at week 24) is noisy and the physician's-choice arm, including low-dose ruxolitinib, can improve symptoms, so the symptom co-primary may miss.
rationale: In PERSIST-2, pacritinib 200 mg BID gave SVR35 in 22% vs 3% for best available therapy, larger in platelets <50k, so the spleen primary is very likely met with 271 vs 136 patients. The listed TSS50 primary is weaker: 32% vs 14% for 200 BID in PERSIST-2, but the pooled analysis missed. Both must succeed under the round's rules, so p_met is ~0.9 x ~0.65. Sobi, as the confirmatory-trial sponsor, should report topline in early 2027.

assumptions.claim: In PERSIST-2, pacritinib 200 mg BID achieved at least 35% spleen volume reduction at week 24 in about 22% vs 3% with best available therapy.
In PERSIST-2, at least 50% TSS reduction at week 24 occurred in about 32% with pacritinib 200 mg BID vs 14% with best available therapy.

reason: The BPD signal from the earlier phase 2 was a secondary finding in a small trial; a smaller true effect on severe BPD or death cannot reach significance with about 148 infants per arm.
rationale: rhIGF-1/rhIGFBP-3 missed its ROP primary in phase 2 but showed lower severe BPD as a secondary outcome, which motivated this trial. Such secondary signals usually shrink on replication. With ~148 per arm and a ~35% control rate, a 10-point reduction gives only ~50% power, and a realistic 5-7 point effect much less. The small private sponsor may delay announcing results.
evidence: Ley et al., J Pediatr 2019 (rhIGF-1/rhIGFBP-3 phase 2, NCT01096784)

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial in extremely preterm infants, rhIGF-1/rhIGFBP-3 did not reduce ROP, but severe BPD was roughly halved as a secondary outcome.

reason: Pediatric functional GI trials have high placebo responses on diary-based stool scores, and with several dose arms the per-arm sample is small, so a modest eluxadoline effect is unlikely to separate.
rationale: In adults, eluxadoline gave only modest stool-consistency gains over placebo (composite responders ~25-30% vs ~16-17%). In this pediatric dose-ranging study the highest-dose arm likely has ~60-70 patients, giving low power for a ~0.3-point BSFS difference against a sizeable placebo response. Pediatric GI drug trials frequently fail on efficacy. AbbVie will likely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov near the August 2027 deadline rather than issue a press release.

assumptions.claim: In adult IBS-D phase 3 trials, eluxadoline 100 mg achieved composite response over weeks 1-12 in about 25-30% of patients vs 16-17% with placebo.

reason: HDAC inhibitors have no randomized proof of benefit in RCC; abexinostat's added PFS benefit over pazopanib is likely small and toxicity may limit dose intensity.
rationale: Support rests on a phase 1b with responses, including in pazopanib-refractory patients; no randomized HDAC-inhibitor combination has improved PFS in RCC. Expected HR ~0.85 gives modest power despite 413 patients. The small, financially constrained sponsor has been recruiting since 2018, so the trial will likely slip or stop and report late.
evidence: Aggarwal et al., Clin Cancer Res 2017 (abexinostat plus pazopanib phase 1)

assumptions.claim: First-line pazopanib median PFS was about 8.4 months in COMPARZ.

reason: Adolescent schizophrenia trials, especially at Eastern European and Latin American sites, show large placebo responses that can swamp a 5-7 point PANSS drug effect.
rationale: Cariprazine is effective in adult schizophrenia (PANSS differences ~6-9 points). Adolescent antipsychotic trials succeed roughly two-thirds of the time (aripiprazole, quetiapine, lurasidone positive; asenapine, ziprasidone failed), mainly limited by placebo response. With ~165 per arm and SD ~17, a 5.5-point difference gives ~75% power. Still recruiting near its registered completion, with Russia/Ukraine sites disrupted, so delays are likely.
evidence: Durgam et al., Schizophr Res 2014 (cariprazine adult phase 3)
Goldman et al., J Child Adolesc Psychopharmacol 2017 (lurasidone adolescents)
Findling et al., Am J Psychiatry 2008 (aripiprazole adolescents)

assumptions.claim: In the adolescent lurasidone trial, PANSS total improved by about 18 points with lurasidone 40-80 mg vs about 10.5 with placebo at week 6.
assumptions.source: Goldman et al., J Child Adolesc Psychopharmacol 2017

reason: Ipilimumab's added benefit over nivolumab alone may be modest for PFS (HR ~0.8), and both PFS and ORR must succeed; with ~437 patients and split alpha the PFS primary could miss.
rationale: This post-marketing study isolates ipilimumab's contribution. Indirect data: nivo+ipi in CheckMate 214 intermediate/poor risk gave ORR 42% and median PFS ~11.6 months, while first-line nivolumab alone gave ORR ~34% and PFS ~7.4 months (HCRN GU16-260). ORR is likely met; PFS benefit is plausible (HR ~0.75-0.8) but power is moderate. Both primaries must be met. Readout after March 2027 makes a statement before June 2027 unlikely.
evidence: HCRN GU16-260 (Atkins et al., J Clin Oncol 2022)

assumptions.claim: In CheckMate 214 intermediate/poor-risk patients, nivolumab plus ipilimumab had ORR 42% and median PFS 11.6 months by independent review.
First-line nivolumab monotherapy in clear-cell RCC had ORR about 34% and median PFS about 7.4 months.
assumptions.source: Atkins et al., J Clin Oncol 2022 (HCRN GU16-260)

reason: Large-sponsor phase 3 already past enrolment and at its registered primary completion; it should run to completion, with results posting more likely near the 12-month FDAAA deadline than before August 2027.
rationale: Active, not recruiting with primary completion October 2026; Sarepta restructuring is a small termination risk; posting deadline falls around October 2027, after the read date.

reason: Both arms are titrated to keep total Kt/V above 1.7, so equivalence in adequacy is expected; failure would most likely come from dropouts, PD transfer and residual renal function decline widening the interval past an unstated margin in a modest sample.
rationale: Non-inferiority on total weekly Kt/V with protocolised titration to a common adequacy target favours success: Kt/V depends mostly on exchange volume, dwell schedule and residual renal function rather than the osmotic agent, and the xylitol/carnitine solution should give similar clearance and ultrafiltration. Main uncertainties are the unknown margin, attrition in a 170-patient open-label PD trial, and the still-recruiting status making a report by mid-2027 unlikely.

assumptions.claim: ISPD practice recommendations use a minimum total weekly Kt/V urea of 1.7 as the adequacy target for peritoneal dialysis.
assumptions.source: ISPD guideline, Brown 2020, Perit Dial Int

reason: Lilly paediatric phase 3 at its registered primary completion with enrolment closed; expected to complete normally, with results posting likely close to the 12-month deadline.
rationale: Active, not recruiting, primary completion October 2026; Lilly reliably posts results but usually near 12 months, which falls just after the read date.

reason: Persistent oral HPV infection is rare in adult men, so the main threat is too few placebo cases for a tight interval, not vaccine weakness.
rationale: HPV L1 VLP vaccines give roughly 85-95% efficacy against persistent vaccine-type infection in HPV-naive per-protocol populations at every site studied, and observational and Costa Rica trial data show large reductions in oral HPV16/18. With about 6000 men followed for years, the trial should accrue enough cases. This is the confirmatory study for Gardasil 9's accelerated oropharyngeal cancer indication, so Merck designed it to succeed. Main risks are low event counts and oral PCR noise.
evidence: Herrero 2013 PLoS One (Costa Rica Vaccine Trial oral HPV)

assumptions.claim: In the Costa Rica Vaccine Trial, oral HPV16/18 prevalence 4 years after vaccination was about 93% lower in the bivalent vaccine arm than in controls.
FDA granted accelerated approval of Gardasil 9 for prevention of oropharyngeal and other head and neck cancers in June 2020, with continued approval contingent on a confirmatory trial.
Quadrivalent HPV vaccine efficacy against persistent HPV6/11/16/18 infection in men 16-26 was about 86% in the per-protocol population.

reason: Concurrent PD-1 blockade with chemoradiotherapy has a mixed record (positive in cervix, negative in head and neck and lung); a modest HR near 0.8 with about 230 events would sit right at the significance boundary.
rationale: Urothelial cancer is immunotherapy-responsive and perioperative IO has succeeded (NIAGARA), and phase 2 pembrolizumab-CRT studies showed high complete response rates. But adding PD-1 inhibitors to concurrent CRT failed in head and neck (KEYNOTE-412) and NSCLC (PACIFIC-2) while succeeding in cervix (KEYNOTE-A18). With 520 patients and roughly 230 events, an HR near 0.77 is needed; my median reported HR is 0.78, so success is close to a coin flip. No positive interim announced to date, a slight negative.

assumptions.claim: In BC2001, 2-year locoregional disease-free survival was 67% with chemoradiotherapy vs 54% with radiotherapy alone in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
Adding pembrolizumab to chemoradiotherapy improved progression-free survival in high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer (HR about 0.70).
Adding pembrolizumab to chemoradiotherapy did not significantly improve event-free survival in locally advanced head and neck cancer (HR about 0.83).

reason: Diacerein's structure-modifying effect is small and unproven in the knee, and the trial lists four structural primary outcomes that would all have to be significant in about 60 patients per arm.
rationale: Diacerein showed a modest slowing of joint space narrowing in hip OA (ECHODIAH) but knee structural evidence is weak and inconsistent. MRI cartilage loss over two years is small relative to measurement noise, so a single-site trial of 128 patients has limited power even for cartilage volume alone; requiring cartilage volume, bone marrow lesions, synovitis and joint space width all to be met makes success very unlikely. Publication from a single Thai site by mid-2027 is also unlikely.
evidence: Raynauld 2004 Arthritis Rheum (MRI cartilage loss in knee OA)

assumptions.claim: In ECHODIAH, diacerein over 3 years reduced the proportion of hip OA patients with radiographic progression compared with placebo (about 51% vs 60%).
A Cochrane review found low-quality evidence of a small benefit of diacerein on joint space narrowing in hip OA and no clear structural benefit in knee OA.

reason: About 50 patients per arm against a high placebo response on a noisy symptom-medication score gives limited power for the modest effects mite SCIT typically shows in its first year.
rationale: House dust mite immunotherapy reduces combined symptom-medication scores with a moderate standardised effect in meta-analyses, but individual small trials often miss significance because placebo responses and between-patient variability are large and first-year effects are modest. With 50 per arm and two doses (either dose meeting is enough), power is roughly 40-60%. The record still says recruiting with a December 2026 completion, so a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: The EAACI position paper recommends the combined symptom and medication score as the primary endpoint in allergen immunotherapy trials.
A systematic review found subcutaneous immunotherapy reduces symptom and medication scores in allergic rhinitis with moderate standardised mean differences.

reason: Non-GCB by GEP mixes BTK-dependent (MCD-like) and BTK-independent tumours, R-CHOP already cures ~70%, and PHOENIX showed BTK inhibitor benefit only in younger patients; patients aged 60-75 may again lose chemo dose intensity, diluting the PFS effect.
rationale: ESCALADE builds on PHOENIX, where ibrutinib+R-CHOP failed overall in non-GCB DLBCL but improved EFS/OS in patients under 60. Acalabrutinib is better tolerated and the age cap is 75, but half the patients are likely 60-75, where toxicity offset benefit before. Lenalidomide (ROBUST) also failed in ABC DLBCL. With ~190 events the trial detects HR ~0.67-0.7; my central HR is 0.80, giving roughly 40% chance of significance. AstraZeneca reliably discloses Phase 3 toplines.

assumptions.claim: Ibrutinib plus R-CHOP did not improve EFS in the overall non-GCB DLBCL population but improved EFS in patients younger than 60.
Two-year PFS with R-CHOP was about 70% in previously untreated DLBCL with IPI 2-5.
Adding lenalidomide to R-CHOP did not significantly improve PFS in ABC-type DLBCL.

reason: Enrolment fell to ~54 randomized patients versus ~120 planned, so with ~40 PFS events even a SOLAR-1-like HR of 0.65 would reach two-sided significance only about a third of the time.
rationale: Alpelisib plus fulvestrant has proven activity in PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- breast cancer (SOLAR-1 HR 0.65, PFS 11.0 vs 5.7 months), so the drug effect is likely real in Chinese patients too. The problem is size: about 54 randomized patients and ~40 events give SE(log HR) ~0.32, so significance needs an observed HR below ~0.54. Hyperglycaemia and rash-driven discontinuation could also blunt the effect. Probability of significance about one third.

assumptions.claim: In the PIK3CA-mutant cohort of SOLAR-1, median PFS was 11.0 months with alpelisib plus fulvestrant vs 5.7 months with placebo plus fulvestrant (HR 0.65).
About 25% of alpelisib-treated patients in SOLAR-1 discontinued because of adverse events, versus about 4% on placebo.

reason: Arginine deprivation helps only ASS1-deficient tumours, a minority of GBM, and add-ons to Stupp have almost all failed; with ~100 patients the trial needs an HR near 0.6 for OS significance.
rationale: Newly diagnosed GBM has a long record of failed add-ons to radiotherapy plus temozolomide. ADI-PEG 20 (pegargiminase) showed an OS benefit in ASS1-deficient mesothelioma (ATOMIC-Meso), but only part of GBM is arginine-auxotrophic and the trial does not select by biomarker. About 100 patients and ~70 deaths give low power for a realistic HR of ~0.85. Control median OS of ~17 months reflects Asian sites and inclusion of IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma.

assumptions.claim: Radiotherapy plus temozolomide gave a median overall survival of 14.6 months in newly diagnosed glioblastoma.
ADI-PEG 20 plus chemotherapy improved overall survival over placebo plus chemotherapy in non-epithelioid mesothelioma.
assumptions.source: ATOMIC-Meso, Szlosarek et al., JAMA Oncol 2024

reason: The primary analysis is restricted to the CNS-metastasis subset of 217 patients, perhaps 80-100 patients and ~65 events, so a true HR of 0.65 gives only about 40-60% power even though entrectinib's CNS advantage over crizotinib is real.
rationale: Entrectinib penetrates the CNS well (intracranial ORR ~80% in ROS1 NSCLC), while crizotinib is a P-gp substrate with poor CNS exposure and frequent intracranial progression, so in patients with baseline brain metastases the PFS gap should be meaningful (HR ~0.6-0.7). Systemic PFS of the two drugs is similar, which limits the effect, and the analysed subgroup is small. I put the chance of significance just under one half.
evidence: Entrectinib integrated ROS1 analysis (Drilon, JTO Clin Res Rep 2022)

assumptions.claim: Crizotinib gave a median PFS of about 19 months in ROS1-rearranged NSCLC in a population largely without brain metastases.
assumptions.source: PROFILE 1001, Shaw et al., Ann Oncol 2019

assumptions.claim: Entrectinib produced an intracranial response rate of roughly 80% in ROS1 NSCLC patients with measurable CNS metastases.
assumptions.source: Drilon et al., JTO Clin Res Rep 2022 (integrated STARTRK analysis)

reason: Adjuvant immunotherapy-plus-antiangiogenic benefit in HCC has proved fragile (IMbrave050's early RFS gain faded) and apatinib toxicity drives early discontinuation, so the BIRC-assessed RFS effect may be too small or too transient for significance.
rationale: Camrelizumab plus rivoceranib is among the most active HCC regimens (CARES-310 OS HR 0.62) and the perioperative CARES-009 trial improved EFS, so an early RFS reduction versus surveillance is plausible in a large 687-patient Phase 3. Against that, IMbrave050's initial RFS HR of 0.72 later regressed toward 0.9, sorafenib (STORM) failed, and no positive interim has been announced despite primary completion in July 2026. Roughly even odds, slightly favouring met.

assumptions.claim: Adjuvant atezolizumab plus bevacizumab initially improved RFS versus active surveillance with HR 0.72 in high-risk HCC.
Camrelizumab plus rivoceranib improved overall survival versus sorafenib in first-line unresectable HCC (HR 0.62).
Adjuvant sorafenib did not improve RFS after resection or ablation of HCC.
assumptions.source: STORM, Bruix et al., Lancet Oncol 2015

reason: Roche's Phase IIIb PDS refill-interval study is fully enrolled with a fixed Week 72 primary endpoint, so it should complete near February 2027, with CT.gov results likely posted toward the 12-month deadline in early 2028.
rationale: Velodrome is fully enrolled (451) and active, not recruiting, with a fixed-time primary at Weeks 68/72, so completion around the registered February 2027 date is likely despite earlier disruption from the 2022 PDS implant recall. Roche typically posts results close to the one-year FDAAA deadline, so posting by end of August 2027 is unlikely. Termination is improbable this close to completion, and the BCVA primary is unlikely to be changed.

reason: SV2A ligands have only modest activity against typical absences (levetiracetam is clearly inferior to ethosuximide/valproate), and complete EEG-verified seizure freedom after only 14 days is a strict bar that a modest drug effect may not clear.
rationale: Brivaracetam is a higher-affinity SV2A ligand than levetiracetam, which had only modest placebo-controlled efficacy in absence epilepsy. The primary is strict (no absences on awake 24-h EEG at Day 14), so placebo should be ~5-10% and brivaracetam perhaps ~20%. With ~150 patients, a 13-15 point gain is borderline detectable. The adaptive trial completed rather than stopping for futility, which mildly supports some activity. Results are due on CT.gov by July 2027.

assumptions.claim: Ethosuximide and valproate were superior to lamotrigine for childhood absence epilepsy, with ethosuximide freedom-from-failure around 50% at 16 weeks.
Levetiracetam monotherapy showed only modest efficacy over placebo for absence seizures in CAE/JAE.

reason: A small Korean sponsor's France-only Phase 2 safety study past primary completion will likely finish quietly in 2027, with results reported in a congress or press release rather than posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.
rationale: Radotinib in early Parkinson's disease is in follow-up (active, not recruiting), with primary completion passed in September 2026 and study completion planned for April 2027, so termination now is unlikely. The trial has no US sites and the sponsor is a small Korean company that has not posted results on ClinicalTrials.gov, making posting unlikely. The safety-only primary outcome is unlikely to change.

reason: Pembrolizumab is inactive in MSS colorectal cancer and liver metastases blunt immunotherapy further; a tirapazamine embolization add-on is unproven, and about 37 patients per arm can only detect a very large overall survival effect.
rationale: Refractory MSS mCRC with liver metastases is among the least immunotherapy-responsive settings; pembrolizumab alone gives essentially no responses, and checkpoint combinations with liver-directed therapy have shown little OS benefit. TATE has only small early-phase data. The control (TAS-102 or regorafenib) gives a median OS of about 6-7 months. With roughly 37 patients per arm, significance needs an HR near 0.5. A small sponsor with three sites, still recruiting five years in, so any early report would likely be interim or descriptive.

assumptions.claim: Trifluridine/tipiracil gave a median OS of 7.1 months in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.
Regorafenib gave a median OS of 6.4 months in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.
Pembrolizumab produced no objective responses in mismatch-repair-proficient colorectal cancer.

reason: Failure would come from insufficient sustained anti-VEGF expression or vitrectomy-related vision loss leaving gene-therapy eyes a few letters behind monthly ranibizumab, so the lower confidence bound crosses the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: Non-inferiority on BCVA at week 54 versus ranibizumab in anti-VEGF-responsive, pseudophakic eyes, with supplemental injections presumably allowed in gene-therapy arms, is a forgiving design; recent long-acting anti-VEGF NI trials (HAWK/HARRIER, Archway, TENAYA/LUCERNE, PULSAR) all met their margins. The subretinal phase 1/2a showed stable BCVA with fewer injections at the higher doses. Risks are vitrectomy-related vision loss, inflammation and weak rescue rules; the margin is unstated (probably 4-4.5 letters). Two doses, either can win, and AbbVie expanded the programme after seeing data.
evidence: RGX-314 subretinal phase 1/2a (Campochiaro et al., Lancet 2024)
Archway 2021 (port delivery system vs monthly ranibizumab)

assumptions.claim: In the subretinal RGX-314 phase 1/2a, higher-dose cohorts kept BCVA roughly stable over 2 years with substantially fewer anti-VEGF injections.
The port delivery system with ranibizumab met non-inferiority to monthly ranibizumab on BCVA using a 4.5-letter margin.

reason: Pediatric bipolar depression trials often fail because placebo improvement on the CDRS-R is large (15-27 points), shrinking the drug-placebo gap; cariprazine's modest adult antidepressant effect leaves little margin.
rationale: Pediatric bipolar depression trials have high placebo response: lurasidone and olanzapine/fluoxetine separated by about 5-6 CDRS-R points, while quetiapine IR and XR failed. Cariprazine's adult bipolar depression effect is modest (positive in 2 of 3 trials at 1.5 mg, effect size about 0.3). Flexible dosing with titration helps somewhat. Still recruiting in late 2026 with Russian sites, so results by mid-2027 are unlikely and would most likely appear via registry posting later.

assumptions.claim: Lurasidone reduced CDRS-R by 21.0 vs 15.3 points with placebo at week 6 in pediatric bipolar depression.
Quetiapine XR did not separate from placebo on CDRS-R in adolescents with bipolar depression.
assumptions.source: Findling et al., J Child Adolesc Psychopharmacol 2014

assumptions.claim: Cariprazine 1.5 mg separated from placebo on MADRS in two of three adult bipolar I depression phase 3 trials.
assumptions.source: Earley et al., Am J Psychiatry 2019; Earley et al., J Affect Disord 2020

reason: With patency around 80-90% in the sham arm and 40 patients per arm, only an implausibly large improvement could reach significance, and the patency, PTS and safety primaries would all need to be met.
rationale: After thrombus removal, stenting and anticoagulation in femoropopliteal DVT, 6-month clinically relevant patency is already high, leaving little room for a perivascular anti-inflammatory to show a significant difference with about 40 patients per arm. The dexamethasone rationale (less vein-wall inflammation and rethrombosis) is plausible but untested in randomized venous trials. Three primary outcomes must all be met. A small device sponsor, still recruiting past its planned primary completion, so a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: DANCE trial (perivascular dexamethasone in femoropopliteal arteries, 2018)

assumptions.claim: Pharmacomechanical thrombolysis did not reduce post-thrombotic syndrome at 24 months versus anticoagulation alone (47% vs 48%).

reason: Atezolizumab has added nothing in several breast cancer trials, including with T-DM1 in KATE2 and neoadjuvant HER2+ IMpassion050; the T-DM1 control is strong with few IDFS events, so a modest effect confined to PD-L1+ tumours would not reach significance overall.
rationale: Atezolizumab has failed repeatedly in breast cancer outside first-line PD-L1+ TNBC: IMpassion030 and ALEXANDRA adjuvant, IMpassion050 neoadjuvant HER2+ (no pCR gain) and KATE2 with T-DM1 in metastatic HER2+ (no significant PFS gain). HER2+ residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy is relatively immune-cold, and the T-DM1 control is strong (3-year IDFS about 88% in KATHERINE). A PD-L1+ signal may exist but the primary is the full population. An early public result is more likely if an interim stops for efficacy.

assumptions.claim: Adjuvant T-DM1 gave a 3-year IDFS of 88.3% in HER2+ residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy.
assumptions.source: KATHERINE, von Minckwitz et al. NEJM 2019

assumptions.claim: Adding atezolizumab to T-DM1 did not significantly improve PFS in previously treated HER2+ metastatic breast cancer.
assumptions.source: KATE2, Emens et al. Lancet Oncol 2020

assumptions.claim: Adding atezolizumab to neoadjuvant pertuzumab-trastuzumab-chemotherapy did not increase pCR in high-risk HER2+ early breast cancer.

reason: SLE trials on SRI-4 often fail because placebo response on background therapy is high and disease is heterogeneous; litifilimab's phase 2 SRI-4 signal was modest, so its effect may be too small to separate at week 52.
rationale: Litifilimab (anti-BDCA2) met its joint-count primary in phase 2 LILAC with numerically higher SRI-4, but SLE phase 3 programmes fail often (TULIP-1 on SRI-4, among others), placebo SRI-4 at week 52 runs about 40-50%, and blocking pDCs removes only part of type I IFN. Two doses are tested and either can win; 183 per arm detects about a 10-point difference. Primary completion has passed and Biogen guides to a readout, so a public result by mid-2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: Litifilimab reduced the total active joint count more than placebo at week 24 in phase 2 SLE (LILAC part A).
Anifrolumab did not meet its SRI-4 primary endpoint at week 52 in TULIP-1.
Placebo SRI-4 response at week 52 was about 44% in BLISS-52.

reason: A short drug-vaccine interaction study with enrollment closed; the January 2027 date looks like a placeholder, so either a slipped date or an un-updated estimate is plausible, with posting due a year after completion.
rationale: Short drug-vaccine interaction study (59 days per subject) with enrollment closed; the round January 2027 date looks like a placeholder, so slippage or a stale estimated date are both plausible. Government-funded with SIGA; results posting is legally due a year after primary completion, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely unless completion was earlier than registered.

reason: Failure would most likely come from an unusually high placebo ACR20 at week 24 in a single-country Chinese population, though JAK1 inhibition has produced large ACR20 gains in every psoriatic arthritis phase 3 so far.
rationale: JAK inhibitors reliably beat placebo on ACR20 in psoriatic arthritis (upadacitinib, tofacitinib, filgotinib), with differences of about 20-35 points. SHR0302 (ivarmacitinib) has shown efficacy in Chinese rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis trials. A week-24 ACR20 comparison with about 139 per arm is well powered for any plausible effect. The uncertainty lies mostly in whether and when Hengrui reports, not in efficacy.
evidence: EQUATOR filgotinib PsA (Mease et al., Lancet 2018)

assumptions.claim: Upadacitinib 15 mg gave ACR20 at week 12 of 70.6% vs 36.2% with placebo in psoriatic arthritis.
Tofacitinib 5 mg gave ACR20 at month 3 of 50% vs 33% with placebo in psoriatic arthritis.
assumptions.source: OPAL Broaden, Mease et al. NEJM 2017

reason: Global SLE trials on background standard of care often show placebo SRI-4 responses of 40-50% at week 52, and litifilimab's phase 2 benefit was clearest in joints and skin, so the roughly 10-point SRI-4 gap needed may not appear.
rationale: Litifilimab (anti-BDCA2) met its phase 2 LILAC primary on active joint count, with skin benefit, but global SRI-4 gains were modest. Phase 3 SLE trials fail often (TULIP-1, SLE-BRAVE-II), with placebo SRI-4 near 40-50% at week 52. With about 187 per arm, roughly a 10-point gap is needed for p<0.05; I expect about 8 points, with a slight boost from having two doses. Biogen's continued investment shows conviction but does not remove the high SLE failure base rate.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 LILAC trial, litifilimab reduced the total active joint count versus placebo at week 24 in SLE, meeting its primary endpoint.
In TULIP-1, SRI-4 response at week 52 was about 36% with anifrolumab 300 mg versus about 40% with placebo, missing the primary endpoint.
In BLISS-52, SRI response at week 52 was 58% with belimumab 10 mg/kg versus 44% with placebo.

reason: Adolescent migraine prevention trials routinely see large placebo responses that shrink drug-placebo differences, and with about 95 per arm a 1.5-day gap in monthly migraine days is near the detection limit.
rationale: Eptinezumab 300 mg cut monthly migraine days about 2.6 more than placebo in adult chronic migraine (PROMISE-2), but adolescent preventive trials often fail on placebo response (CHAMP stopped for futility). Fremanezumab succeeded in pediatric episodic migraine with about a 1-day gap. With about 95 per arm and SD near 5.5, a gap of about 1.6 days is needed; I expect about 1.4 days, giving near-even odds, trimmed for pediatric failure history and helped slightly by the second dose arm.

assumptions.claim: In PROMISE-2, eptinezumab 300 mg reduced monthly migraine days over weeks 1-12 by about 8.2 versus about 5.6 with placebo in adults with chronic migraine.
The CHAMP pediatric migraine prevention trial was stopped for futility with a placebo responder rate of about 61%.

reason: Cytokine-induced killer cell therapy has no randomized evidence in pancreatic cancer, and adding it to adjuvant gemcitabine may not shift recurrence enough in such an aggressive disease.
rationale: Immuncell-LC (autologous CIK cells) cut recurrence after HCC resection, but pancreatic cancer is far more aggressive and there is no randomized pancreatic evidence. Adjuvant gemcitabine alone gives median RFS of about 12-13 months. With about 280 events, an HR of about 0.79 or lower is needed; I expect about 0.82. The trial is still recruiting with follow-up of 36 months after the last patient, so any result by mid-2027 would most likely be an early stop or futility, which lowers the earlier-deadline estimates.
evidence: Lee et al., Gastroenterology 2015 (Immuncell-LC adjuvant HCC)

assumptions.claim: Adjuvant Immuncell-LC prolonged recurrence-free survival after curative treatment of HCC, with a hazard ratio of about 0.63.
Adjuvant gemcitabine monotherapy gave a median recurrence-free survival of about 13 months in ESPAC-4.

reason: Enrolment is closed and primary completion is aligned with the study end in March 2027, so the trial should complete near schedule; results posting and changes to primary outcomes before August 2027 are unlikely.
rationale: Merck basket study with no formal hypothesis testing, enrolment closed (ESCC cohort closed in 2025). Primary and study completion share the March 2027 date, which Merck tends to hold or shift modestly; some risk it is extended for patients still on treatment. Merck usually posts results close to the 12-month deadline, so posting by end of August 2027 is unlikely. Termination this late is rare.

reason: Cohort A is a small open-label subset of a 200-patient phase 2b, so even a real HR near 0.7 may miss two-sided 0.05; BET-inhibitor toxicity may also limit dosing.
rationale: ZEN-3694 plus enzalutamide gave median rPFS of about 9 months in mCRPC after prior AR-pathway therapy in phase 1b/2a, versus a few months expected for enzalutamide after abiraterone failure in poor responders, where cross-resistance is high. The randomized cohort A is small (perhaps 100-130 patients), open-label, and thrombocytopenia limits dosing. An expected HR of about 0.72 gives modest power. Still recruiting since 2021, so timelines will likely slip.
evidence: Aggarwal et al., Clin Cancer Res 2022 (NCT02711956)
Khalaf et al., Lancet Oncol 2019 (abiraterone/enzalutamide sequencing)

assumptions.claim: In the phase 1b/2a study of ZEN-3694 plus enzalutamide in mCRPC after prior AR-signalling inhibitor therapy, median rPFS was about 9 months.
assumptions.source: Aggarwal et al., Clin Cancer Res 2022 (NCT02711956)

assumptions.claim: Enzalutamide after abiraterone shows marked cross-resistance, with PSA declines of at least 30% in only about a third of patients.

reason: Higher octreotide exposure from CAM2029 may not translate into longer PFS than standard-dose somatostatin analogues, whose antiproliferative effect may plateau at current doses.
rationale: CAM2029 delivers several-fold higher octreotide exposure than octreotide LAR, but superiority on blinded PFS over standard SSAs is unproven; dose-intensification evidence (CLARINET FORTE) is single-arm in progressors. Control median PFS is likely about two years in mostly SSA-naive well-differentiated disease (CLARINET placebo 18 months, lanreotide longer). With about 180 events, an HR near 0.75 or lower is needed; I expect about 0.78, so roughly one-in-three odds. OS will be immature.

assumptions.claim: In CLARINET, lanreotide prolonged PFS versus placebo in GEP-NET with HR 0.47, and placebo median PFS was 18 months.
In PROMID, octreotide LAR gave a median time to tumour progression of 14.3 months in metastatic midgut NETs.

reason: Clemizole's anti-seizure effect rests mainly on zebrafish data and serotonergic rationale; with little human efficacy evidence and variable LGS seizure counts, a 260-patient trial may not detect a modest effect.
rationale: Clemizole emerged from a zebrafish Dravet screen and acts on serotonin receptors, the pathway behind fenfluramine's LGS benefit, but human efficacy data are minimal. LGS placebo arms show median reductions of about 8-20%, and seizure counts are highly variable, so detecting a roughly 10-point median difference with 130 per arm is uncertain. The trial is still recruiting at its registered completion date, so a result by mid-2027 is unlikely and, if it comes, more likely a stop.
evidence: Knupp et al., JAMA Neurol 2022 (fenfluramine LGS)

assumptions.claim: In the phase 3 fenfluramine LGS trial, median reduction in drop seizures was 26.5% with 0.7 mg/kg/day versus 7.8% with placebo.
Clemizole reduced seizure activity in a zebrafish scn1lab Dravet model, attributed to serotonin receptor signalling.
assumptions.source: Baraban et al., Nat Commun 2013; Griffin et al., Brain 2017

reason: Many prolonged seizures stop on their own soon after dosing, so a high placebo success rate in caregiver-judged outpatient episodes could narrow the gap, and both co-primaries must be met.
rationale: The phase 2b showed treatment success (cessation within 90 seconds and no recurrence in 2 hours) of about 65% versus about 43% with placebo, a gap of roughly 22 points, and inhaled alprazolam reaches the brain within minutes. With about 175 per arm, even a regressed 15-point gap gives high power for each co-primary. Risks are that both co-primaries must be met, outpatient caregiver judgement adds noise, and spontaneous termination inflates placebo success.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2b study, Staccato alprazolam gave treatment success (seizure cessation within 90 seconds and no recurrence within 2 hours) in about 65% versus about 43% with placebo.
Staccato alprazolam suppressed the photoparoxysmal EEG response within minutes of inhalation.

reason: Enrolment is complete and the last primary visit is the 48-month group's Day 1471, so the trial should complete around March 2027 as registered; GSK usually posts within a year, often not within six months.
rationale: GSK's MenABCWY dosing-schedule study is active, not recruiting, with the primary completion set by the final 0-48-month booster visit plus one month, which is fixed by the enrolment dates. Large sponsors like GSK usually hold such dates. Results are due within 12 months of completion, so posting by end of August 2027 (about five months) is possible but not likely. Termination or substantive outcome changes at this stage are rare.

reason: Perioperative PD-1 benefit is well established, so the main risk is that the ITT EFS primary is immature or not formally declared when the stage III EFS result is reported.
rationale: Every perioperative PD-1/PD-L1 plus chemotherapy trial in resectable NSCLC (KEYNOTE-671, Neotorch, RATIONALE-315, CheckMate 77T, AEGEAN) met EFS with HRs of about 0.4-0.6, largest in stage III. Sintilimab is an established PD-1 antibody with positive Chinese lung trials. Placebo-chemotherapy median EFS in stage III is about 15-20 months. The main uncertainty is the dual primary structure, where the ITT EFS may be reported later than stage III EFS.

assumptions.claim: In Neotorch, perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy improved EFS in stage III NSCLC versus placebo plus chemotherapy with an HR of about 0.40.
In KEYNOTE-671, perioperative pembrolizumab improved EFS with HR 0.58, and the placebo arm's median EFS was 17.0 months.

reason: Enrolment is closed and the registered primary completion (Sept 2026) has passed, so the record will most likely move to completed; a small sponsor may post results near the one-year deadline or late.
rationale: Phase 2a safety study by a small biotech, active not recruiting with primary completion Sept 2026 at 6 US sites. Termination is unlikely once enrolment is over; FDAAA posting falls due about Sept 2027, so posting by end Aug 2027 is possible but small sponsors are often late. Safety-only primary outcomes rarely get rewritten.

reason: A DHODH inhibitor with mild lymphocyte effects may cut relapses by only about 20%, which roughly 260 events over 72 weeks cannot reliably detect, especially if modern placebo relapse rates run low.
rationale: Vidofludimus calcium (IMU-838) is a DHODH inhibitor whose phase 2 EMPhASIS MRI lesion reduction resembled teriflunomide, which cut relapses about 30% vs placebo. I expect HR ~0.70; with ~1,120 treatment-naive patients and ~30% placebo relapse by 72 weeks there are ~260 events, giving roughly 70-80% power at HR 0.70. Risks: low relapse rates in modern placebo arms and laquinimod-style weak clinical translation. Primary completion Nov 2026 points to a topline in early 2027.

assumptions.claim: Teriflunomide 14 mg, a DHODH inhibitor, reduced the annualized relapse rate by about 31% vs placebo.
Vidofludimus calcium 30 mg and 45 mg reduced cumulative combined unique active MRI lesions vs placebo through week 24.
Laquinimod met its relapse-rate primary endpoint in ALLEGRO but missed it in BRAVO.
assumptions.source: ALLEGRO, Comi et al. NEJM 2012; BRAVO, Vollmer et al. J Neurol 2014

reason: Type I interferon blockade may add only a few points of complete renal response on top of MMF and steroids, below what about 360 patients can detect at week 52.
rationale: TULIP-LN missed its UPCR primary, but intensified-regimen anifrolumab gave about 14 points more complete renal response than placebo at week 52 in ~45 patients per arm; phase 2 effects usually shrink, so I expect ~9 points here. With ~181 per arm and placebo CRR near 28%, power is about 50%. Add-on biologics in lupus nephritis have a mixed record (belimumab, obinutuzumab positive; abatacept, rituximab negative). Primary completion Feb 2027 makes an AstraZeneca topline by June 2027 roughly a coin flip.

assumptions.claim: In TULIP-LN the primary endpoint (UPCR change at week 52) was not met, while complete renal response at week 52 was numerically higher with intensified-regimen anifrolumab than placebo.
assumptions.source: TULIP-LN, Jayne et al. Ann Rheum Dis 2022 (NCT02547922)

assumptions.claim: Obinutuzumab added to standard therapy increased complete renal response at week 76 vs placebo (about 46% vs 33%).
Abatacept added to MMF and steroids did not improve complete renal response vs placebo.
assumptions.source: ALLURE, Furie et al. Arthritis Rheumatol 2022

reason: With about 37 patients per arm over 24 weeks, a realistic 40-60 mL FVC benefit has well under 50% power, and dose B may be the lower dose.
rationale: HEC585 is an oral pirfenidone-like antifibrotic tested in a small Chinese PF-ILD phase 2b with about 37 patients per arm over 24 weeks. Placebo FVC loss in PF-ILD is roughly 70-90 mL per 24 weeks with between-patient SD near 190 mL, so even a pirfenidone-sized benefit (~50 mL) gives power around 25-35%. It is unclear whether dose B is the higher dose. Still recruiting in Oct 2026 despite a Dec 2026 primary completion date, so results by mid-2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In INBUILD, placebo patients with progressive fibrosing ILD lost about 188 mL FVC over 52 weeks.
Pirfenidone in progressive unclassifiable ILD reduced site-spirometry FVC decline over 24 weeks by about 95 mL vs placebo.
assumptions.source: Maher et al. Lancet Respir Med 2020 (NCT03099187)

reason: Two primary endpoints (HbA1c and fasting triglycerides) in only about 35 patients per arm, with modest expected metreleptin effects in partial lipodystrophy, leave limited power to win both.
rationale: Metreleptin's open-label benefits in partial lipodystrophy were modest and concentrated in patients with severe metabolic derangement and low leptin; FDA did not approve it for PL. This 69-patient placebo-controlled trial lists two primary endpoints (HbA1c and fasting TG at month 6), and both must be met. I expect an HbA1c effect near -0.6 points with SD ~1.1, about 50% power alone and ~35% jointly with TG. Primary completion July 2026; results may come at ENDO/ADA in June 2027 or via CT.gov posting due July 2027.

assumptions.claim: The US metreleptin label states that safety and effectiveness in partial lipodystrophy have not been established.

In NIH open-label data, metabolic improvements with metreleptin in partial lipodystrophy were smaller than in generalized lipodystrophy and seen mainly in patients with severe baseline hypertriglyceridemia or hyperglycemia.
assumptions.source: Diker-Cohen et al. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2015

reason: Stage Two face/neck arms will be small, and a dose-finding phase 2 may report only descriptive IGA changes rather than a formal significant comparison with vehicle PDT.
rationale: Hemoporfin PDT is approved in China after a placebo-PDT-controlled phase 3 showing a large efficacy advantage in port-wine stains, so an IGA improvement over vehicle PDT at the higher light doses is plausible in Stage Two. But Stage Two arms are small, the PWB-IGA scale is non-standard, and a dose-finding study may report without a formal test. Still recruiting with a Jan 2027 primary completion and up to 44 weeks of follow-up, so results by June 2027 are very unlikely.
evidence: Zhao et al. PLoS One 2016 (hemoporfin phase 3, China)

assumptions.claim: Hemoporfin PDT showed a large efficacy advantage over placebo PDT for port-wine stains in a randomized Chinese phase 3 trial.

reason: Enrolment of 66 is complete and the primary outcome is measured at 24 hours, so primary completion by Dec 2026 is likely; FDAAA posting falls due around Dec 2027, so posting by Aug 2027 is less likely.
rationale: Small two-part phase 2 by a Taiwanese sponsor, active not recruiting with primary completion Dec 2026. With enrolment done and a 24-hour safety primary, slippage beyond March 2027 is unlikely; termination after enrolment is rare. A US site makes posting required within a year of completion, so posting before end Aug 2027 is possible but not expected.

reason: A DHODH inhibitor with mild lymphocyte effects may cut relapses by only about 20%, which roughly 255 events over 72 weeks cannot reliably detect, especially if modern placebo relapse rates run low.
rationale: Twin of ENSURE-1. Vidofludimus calcium (IMU-838) is a DHODH inhibitor whose phase 2 MRI lesion reduction resembled teriflunomide, which cut relapses about 30% vs placebo. I expect HR ~0.70; with 1,100 treatment-naive patients and ~30% placebo relapse by 72 weeks there are ~255 events, roughly 70-80% power at HR 0.70. Risks: low modern placebo relapse rates, sites in war-affected countries, and laquinimod-style weak clinical translation. Topline likely early 2027.

assumptions.claim: Teriflunomide 14 mg, a DHODH inhibitor, reduced the annualized relapse rate by about 31% vs placebo.
Vidofludimus calcium 30 mg and 45 mg reduced cumulative combined unique active MRI lesions vs placebo through week 24.
Laquinimod met its relapse-rate primary endpoint in ALLEGRO but missed it in BRAVO.
assumptions.source: ALLEGRO, Comi et al. NEJM 2012; BRAVO, Vollmer et al. J Neurol 2014

reason: Carisbamate showed only modest efficacy in focal epilepsy and its LGS evidence is open-label; drop-seizure percent change is noisy and placebo arms vary, so a 15-point median difference may not reach significance.
rationale: Recent LGS phase 3s of active broad-spectrum ASMs (cannabidiol, fenfluramine, rufinamide, clobazam) mostly succeeded with 15-25 point median differences in drop seizures, but soticlestat failed. Carisbamate has modest efficacy in focal epilepsy (one of two phase 3s positive) and only open-label LGS data. With about 250 patients the trial is reasonably powered for a 15-20 point difference. Slow recruitment since 2022 suggests the record is still recruiting, delaying readout. I put success near 50%.

assumptions.claim: In GWPCARE4, median drop-seizure reduction was 43.9% with cannabidiol 20 mg/kg vs 21.8% with placebo.
In fenfluramine Study 1601, median drop-seizure reduction was 26.5% at 0.7 mg/kg/day vs 7.8% with placebo.
Takeda's soticlestat phase 3 in LGS (SKYWAY) did not meet its primary endpoint.

reason: COAST's PFS gain came from a small phase 2 whose durvalumab arm did far worse than PACIFIC; IO add-ons to PD-(L)1 consolidation (tiragolumab in SKYSCRAPER-03) have failed, and CD73 blockade has no phase 3 win.
rationale: The trial rests on COAST (HR 0.44 for durvalumab plus oleclumab), but COAST was small, investigator-assessed and had an unusually poor durvalumab arm (median PFS 6.3 vs 16.8 months in PACIFIC), a classic setup for phase 3 regression. Adding a second immunomodulator to PD-(L)1 consolidation after chemoradiation failed with tiragolumab, and oleclumab has shown little activity elsewhere. With about 700 patients in the comparison, a true HR near 0.85 would still give a fair chance, so I put success near 18%.

assumptions.claim: In COAST, durvalumab plus oleclumab improved PFS vs durvalumab alone (HR 0.44), with a durvalumab-alone median PFS of 6.3 months.
assumptions.source: Herbst et al., J Clin Oncol 2022

assumptions.claim: In PACIFIC, median PFS by BICR with durvalumab after chemoradiation was 16.8 months.
SKYSCRAPER-03 (atezolizumab plus tiragolumab vs durvalumab after chemoradiation) did not meet its PFS primary endpoint.

reason: Even intravitreal complement inhibitors only slow geographic atrophy growth by 15-20%, and it is unproven that oral factor B inhibition prevents iRORA; with about 146 eyes the trial can only detect a large effect.
rationale: Complement genetics support the target, but local C3/C5 inhibition gave only modest effects on GA growth and no proven prevention of conversion from intermediate AMD. Systemic factor B inhibition may not reach enough choroidal suppression to matter, and a proof-of-concept with about 146 patients and roughly 55 events can detect only a hazard ratio near 0.5. Novartis has not advanced iptacopan in AMD publicly. I put success near 18%.

assumptions.claim: Monthly intravitreal pegcetacoplan reduced geographic atrophy lesion growth by about 17-22% over 24 months.
Avacincaptad pegol reduced GA growth by about 14-18% at 12 months in GATHER2.

reason: Only 64 men across three arms (about 21 per arm) with two co-primary outcomes (IIEF and EHS) that must both separate from placebo, against a sizeable placebo response in erectile function questionnaires.
rationale: Sponsor-run nutraceutical trials often report favourable results, and earlier Testofen studies reported improved libido and androgen-decline symptoms. But here about 21 men per arm must show between-group significance on both IIEF and EHS, and placebo responses on sexual-function questionnaires are large. Two doses give two chances. Publication from this Australian CRO typically comes 1-2 years after completion, so a result by mid-2027 is uncertain. I put success near 30%.
evidence: Steels et al., Phytother Res 2011 (Testofen libido)
Rao et al., Aging Male 2016 (Testofen androgen decline)

assumptions.claim: A 6-week trial of Testofen 600 mg in 60 healthy men reported improved libido on DISF-SR vs placebo.

reason: With about 82 patients per arm the 95% interval on the remission difference spans roughly plus or minus 15 points, so even a true tie could breach a 20-25 point margin by chance; the 26-week dosing interval may also give less trough suppression than monthly mepolizumab 300 mg.
rationale: Depemokimab and mepolizumab share the IL-5 mechanism; depemokimab binds IL-5 with higher affinity and suppressed eosinophils over 26 weeks in SWIFT. MANDARA showed benralizumab non-inferior to mepolizumab in a similar relapsing/refractory EGPA population (59% vs 56%) with a -25 point margin. If OCEAN uses a similar margin, a true difference near zero gives about 75-85% power. GSK reports Phase 3 headline results promptly. I put success near 76%.

assumptions.claim: In MANDARA, remission at both weeks 36 and 48 occurred in 59% with benralizumab vs 56% with mepolizumab.
In MIRRA, 32% on mepolizumab vs 3% on placebo were in remission at both weeks 36 and 48.
Depemokimab every 26 weeks reduced annualized asthma exacerbations by about 54% vs placebo in pooled SWIFT-1/2.

reason: Completed sponsor-run paediatric study designed with FDA; results will likely be posted around the 12-month deadline, possibly delayed if AstraZeneca certifies a pending US filing for this use.
rationale: Status is completed (primary completion August 2026), so termination is very unlikely. AstraZeneca usually posts results within 12 months, which falls around 10 August 2027, just before the read date; the US label lacks this indication, so a delayed-posting certification tied to a supplemental filing is possible. Primary outcome edits at results posting are usually wording only.

reason: Absolute sputum neutrophil counts are highly skewed and variable between visits, and nebulized ensifentrine's anti-inflammatory effect in COPD airways is unproven; 56 patients in a crossover may not show a significant change.
rationale: Ensifentrine inhibits PDE4 as well as PDE3, and oral roflumilast cut sputum neutrophils by about a third in COPD, which gives biological plausibility. But inhaled ensifentrine's anti-inflammatory signal in patients is thin, background maintenance therapy dilutes effects, and sputum counts are noisy. The crossover design helps power. Merck's acquisition of Verona means the result is more likely to appear as a congress abstract or paper than a press release, probably after mid-2027. I put success near 35%.
evidence: Franciosi et al., Lancet Respir Med 2013 (RPL554)

assumptions.claim: Roflumilast 500 ug for 4 weeks reduced absolute sputum neutrophils by about 36% vs placebo in COPD.
Nebulized ensifentrine 3 mg BID increased average FEV1 AUC0-12h by about 87-94 mL vs placebo at week 12 in ENHANCE-1/2.
assumptions.source: Anzueto et al., Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2023

reason: The phase 2 VIRO-15 signal comes from 27 selected, single-arm patients; platinum rechallenge in heavily pretreated platinum-resistant disease often fails, and the control of chemotherapy plus bevacizumab is not trivial.
rationale: Olvi-Vec's case rests on single-arm VIRO-15 (ORR 54%, median PFS 11.4 months in 27 patients), and single-arm signals in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer rarely hold up in randomized phase 3. The experimental arm does add platinum rechallenge, which may itself help some patients. With about 186 patients and open-label BICR-assessed PFS, an HR near 0.65 is needed. Still recruiting in late 2026, so readout probably slips past mid-2027. I put success near 30%.

assumptions.claim: In VIRO-15, intraperitoneal Olvi-Vec followed by platinum-based chemotherapy with or without bevacizumab gave ORR 54% and median PFS 11.4 months in 27 PRROC patients.
In MIRASOL, investigator's-choice chemotherapy gave a median PFS of 3.98 months in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.

reason: Small NIH-funded device feasibility study, active not recruiting, whose 24-month post-implant safety follow-up may push primary completion past the registered November 2026 date.
rationale: Enrolment is closed and follow-up is the 24-month post-implant window, so the registered November 2026 date is plausible but could slip if late implants extend it. Device feasibility studies are generally not applicable clinical trials, but NIH funding requires posting within a year of primary completion, which falls after the read date. Termination is unlikely with enrolment complete.

reason: CCTA percent change in total atheroma volume is noisy and includes calcified plaque that LDL lowering barely shrinks, so a true 3-4 point benefit may not reach significance with about 280 evaluable patients per arm.
rationale: Inclisiran adds about 50% LDL-C lowering on statins; every PCSK9 plaque-imaging trial (GLAGOV, PACMAN-AMI, HUYGENS) met its IVUS/OCT primary. Here the endpoint is CCTA total atheroma volume percent change over 24 months in non-obstructive CAD, which is noisier and less LDL-sensitive than IVUS PAV; expected difference around -3 to -4 points against an SE near 1.5. Novartis sized 610 patients for this, so moderate odds of significance. Readout likely ESC/AHA 2027, with some chance of an earlier pipeline statement.

assumptions.claim: Evolocumab on top of statins reduced percent atheroma volume by about 1.0 percentage point vs placebo over 76 weeks.
Inclisiran lowered LDL-C by about 50% vs placebo on top of maximally tolerated statins.
Alirocumab added to high-intensity statin reduced percent atheroma volume vs placebo at 52 weeks after AMI.

reason: The composite needs no rejection, no DSA, Breg of at least 3% and steroid-free reduced immunosuppression; MIC patients may fail one criterion, and any statement by mid-2027 would more likely be an early stop than a final read.
rationale: Standard-of-care controls stay on steroids and full-dose mycophenolate, so almost none can meet criterion 4; the comparison therefore hinges on how many MIC patients achieve the whole tolerance-like phenotype. The phase 1 TOL-1 study showed Breg induction and feasible immunosuppression reduction, so a sizeable MIC responder rate is plausible. But the trial was still recruiting in October 2026 with one-year follow-up, so any result before mid-2027 is unlikely and would probably be an early stop or interim, which pulls p_met down.
evidence: TOL-1 phase 1, Morath et al., J Clin Invest 2020
Morath et al., J Am Soc Nephrol 2023 (MIC and regulatory B cells)

assumptions.claim: Donor-derived MIC infusion before living-donor kidney transplant was feasible and allowed reduced immunosuppression in a phase 1 study.
assumptions.source: Morath et al., J Clin Invest 2020

assumptions.claim: MIC-treated recipients showed long-lasting increases in regulatory B cells.
assumptions.source: Morath et al., J Am Soc Nephrol 2023

reason: Surgery already saves over 90% of limbs at 30 days, so if the trial is judged as superiority there is no room to win; the sponsor most likely framed it as non-inferiority, which it has met in every prior Fortelyzin trial.
rationale: Supergene ran FRIDOM, FRIDA and FORPE as non-inferiority trials and reported each as met, publishing within roughly a year. Historical thrombolysis-vs-surgery trials (STILE, TOPAS) showed similar amputation rates, so a non-inferiority claim on 30-day amputation-free rate with 85 per arm is likely if that is the hypothesis. If the published hypothesis is superiority, success is unlikely because both arms should sit near 90-95%. I weight a non-inferiority framing at about 75%.

assumptions.claim: Intra-arterial thrombolysis and surgery gave similar amputation-free survival in acute arterial occlusion.
Non-immunogenic staphylokinase was non-inferior to alteplase in acute ischaemic stroke.

reason: The agitation hypothesis for masupirdine rests on a post hoc analysis of a failed cognition trial, and agitation trials carry large placebo responses that swamp modest drug effects.
rationale: Masupirdine (5-HT6 antagonist) missed its phase 2 cognition endpoint; the agitation signal came from post hoc subgroup analysis. The 5-HT6 class has a near-uniform record of phase 3 failure. Agitation trials show large placebo improvements (brexpiprazole beat placebo by only about 5 CMAI-total points). With about 125 per arm and either dose counting, I expect a small, likely non-significant difference. Suven should disclose topline via a stock-exchange filing in H1 2027.
evidence: Brexpiprazole Trial 213, Lee et al., JAMA Neurology 2023

assumptions.claim: Masupirdine did not meet its primary ADAS-Cog endpoint in the phase 2 Alzheimer's trial.
Brexpiprazole 2-3 mg reduced CMAI total by about 5.3 points more than placebo at week 12.

reason: One-time subretinal gene therapy plus vitrectomy may let vision drift 1-3 letters below fixed aflibercept dosing by week 54, and a lower CI bound beyond a roughly 4-5 letter margin would fail non-inferiority.
rationale: Phase 1/2a subretinal RGX-314 kept BCVA roughly stable over 2 years with large cuts in injection burden, and supplemental anti-VEGF is allowed, which protects mean BCVA. The population is anti-VEGF responders, so aflibercept gains are small, limiting room for a deficit. With about 240 per arm the SE is near 1.1 letters, so a true difference of -1 to -2 letters passes a 4-5 letter margin; either dose suffices. Sustained-delivery precedents (Archway) met NI, though others (KSI-301 DAZZLE) failed.
evidence: RGX-314 phase 1/2a, Campochiaro et al., Lancet 2024

assumptions.claim: Subretinal RGX-314 maintained stable BCVA with reduced anti-VEGF injections over 2 years in previously treated nAMD.
The Port Delivery System was non-inferior to monthly ranibizumab on BCVA change at weeks 36-40.

reason: 64 patients spread over ascending TS23 doses against heparin, which already lowers RV/LV over 48 hours, leaves little power, and low-dose cohorts dilute any pooled effect.
rationale: TS23 inactivates alpha2-antiplasmin to boost endogenous fibrinolysis; first-in-patient efficacy data. Heparin alone lowers RV/LV modestly by 48 hours, while lytic approaches cut it by about 0.2-0.3 extra. TS23 is probably weaker than full-dose lysis, and the ascending-dose design with about 32 treated patients split across doses gives limited power. A small sponsor may report descriptively or at ISTH/AHA 2027.

assumptions.claim: In ULTIMA, heparin alone reduced RV/LV by about 0.03 at 24 hours vs about 0.30 with ultrasound-assisted thrombolysis.

reason: An uncharacterised oral add-on in a single-site 120-patient trial must beat placebo on both ADAS-Cog and CDR-SB at 28 weeks, a bar almost no symptomatic Alzheimer's agent has cleared.
rationale: EX039 has no published efficacy data; add-on symptomatic agents in AD have a very poor success record. Both co-primaries (ADAS-Cog and CDR-SB) must be met; with about 60 per arm the SE for ADAS-Cog is about 1 point, while plausible effects are under 1 point. The trial was still recruiting in October 2026 with 28-week follow-up, so a result by mid-2027 is unlikely.

reason: No antifibrotic or metabolic drug has yet reduced clinical events in compensated NASH cirrhosis; resmetirom's fat and stiffness reductions may not translate into fewer decompensations within about three years, and a modest event count with 3:1 allocation limits power.
rationale: Resmetirom improves steatosis, fibrosis and liver stiffness in F2-F3 NASH and open-label F4c data showed falling stiffness, but every prior outcome or histology trial in NASH cirrhosis (simtuzumab, selonsertib, emricasan, belapectin, obeticholic acid REVERSE) failed. The enrichment for portal hypertension (MRE, ELF, platelets) raises event rates, but I expect only around 100-120 composite events with 3:1 randomization, so the trial needs a hazard ratio near 0.65 to reach significance. Madrigal guided a 2027 readout; primary completion is December 2026.
evidence: STELLAR-4 selonsertib, Harrison et al. J Hepatol 2020
Simtuzumab NASH cirrhosis, Harrison et al. Gastroenterology 2018

assumptions.claim: Resmetirom 100 mg gave fibrosis improvement of at least one stage in 25.9% vs 14.2% with placebo at week 52 in F1B-F3 NASH.
Selonsertib did not improve fibrosis versus placebo at week 48 in compensated NASH cirrhosis.
assumptions.source: STELLAR-4, Harrison et al. J Hepatol 2020

assumptions.claim: Non-selective beta blockers reduced decompensation or death in compensated cirrhosis with clinically significant portal hypertension (HR about 0.51).

reason: NMDAR encephalitis often improves after first-line immunotherapy, so a high placebo responder rate at week 24 with about 30 patients per arm leaves little room to show an add-on IL-6 receptor benefit; the separate LGI1 cohort primary adds a further hurdle.
rationale: Most NMDAR encephalitis patients improve by at least one mRS point over six months on standard immunotherapy, so placebo responders (without rescue) should be near half. Evidence for IL-6 blockade is retrospective tocilizumab series in refractory autoimmune encephalitis. With roughly 30 per arm, a difference near 25 points is needed for significance. The basket design lists NMDAR and LGI1 cohort primaries; if both must be met, the bar is higher still. Roche/Chugai would likely disclose topline in H1 2027 pipeline updates or congresses.
evidence: Titulaer et al., Lancet Neurol 2013 (NMDAR encephalitis treatment and outcomes)
Lee WJ et al., Neurotherapeutics 2016 (tocilizumab in autoimmune encephalitis)

assumptions.claim: About 53% of NMDAR encephalitis patients improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy and 81% reached mRS 0-2 by 24 months.
Tocilizumab was associated with better mRS outcomes than continued rituximab or no further therapy in rituximab-refractory autoimmune encephalitis in a retrospective series.

reason: Forty neonates give power only for a very large drop in death or disability; with a 24-month endpoint the trial is unlikely to finish on time, and any early report would rest on interim or partial follow-up.
rationale: Neuroprotective add-ons in HIE (erythropoietin in HEAL, others) have not reduced death or disability, and in South Asian centres hypothermia itself failed in HELIX with about half of infants dying or disabled. Sovateltide's evidence is preclinical plus sponsor-run Indian stroke trials. With 20 per arm a difference near 40 points is needed. The trial is still recruiting with a 24-month primary, so a result by mid-2027 would be an early sponsor report, which Pharmazz tends to frame positively.
evidence: HELIX, Thayyil et al. Lancet Glob Health 2021
Sovateltide phase 3 in acute ischaemic stroke, Gulati et al. Drugs 2024

assumptions.claim: In the HELIX trial in India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, death or disability at 18 months occurred in about half of infants and hypothermia did not reduce it.
assumptions.source: Thayyil et al., Lancet Glob Health 2021

assumptions.claim: High-dose erythropoietin added to hypothermia did not reduce death or neurodevelopmental impairment in neonatal HIE.

reason: PVd is an active comparator sharing the bortezomib-dexamethasone backbone, so mezigdomide must beat pomalidomide head to head; neutropenia-driven dose reductions could erode the potency advantage seen in early-phase studies.
rationale: Mezigdomide is a more potent CELMoD than pomalidomide, active even in pomalidomide-refractory disease, and MeziVd gave high response rates in early lines in phase 1/2; iberdomide already beat DVd in EXCALIBER-RRMM. PVd in lenalidomide-exposed, often anti-CD38-exposed patients gives median PFS around 11-13 months (OPTIMISMM, DREAMM-8). With 810 patients the trial is powered for a hazard ratio near 0.75; I expect around 0.68. BMS has guided a readout around 2026-2027.
evidence: OPTIMISMM, Richardson et al. Lancet Oncol 2019

assumptions.claim: The PVd control arm had a median PFS of 12.7 months in lenalidomide-exposed RRMM after at least one prior line.
PVd gave median PFS 11.2 vs 7.1 months for Vd (HR 0.61) in lenalidomide-exposed RRMM.
assumptions.source: OPTIMISMM, Richardson et al. Lancet Oncol 2019

assumptions.claim: Mezigdomide plus dexamethasone produced an overall response rate of about 41% in triple-class-refractory myeloma.

reason: Renal sinus fat is a small MRI compartment with noisy segmentation; measurement variability and missing scans could blur an otherwise large weight-loss-driven reduction.
rationale: Tirzepatide produces 15-20% weight loss and large reductions in visceral and ectopic fat (SURPASS-3 MRI), and renal sinus fat behaves like visceral fat, so a 52-week placebo-controlled difference of 20% or more is likely; with about 67 per arm this should be highly significant despite MRI noise. The trial is completed (July 2026); Lilly usually posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov near the 12-month deadline (July 2027), and ADA or ERA 2027 are plausible venues before then.
evidence: SURPASS-3 MRI substudy, Gastaldelli et al. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2022

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide reduced liver fat content and visceral adipose tissue volume significantly more than insulin degludec in type 2 diabetes over 52 weeks.
assumptions.source: SURPASS-3 MRI, Gastaldelli et al. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2022

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide 15 mg produced mean weight loss of about 20.9% vs 3.1% with placebo at 72 weeks.

reason: With 11 versus 6 patients and spontaneous or biopsy-related HSIL regression in the placebo arm, only a very large difference in histologic response would reach p<0.05.
rationale: Topical artesunate showed histologic regression of cervical HSIL in about two-thirds of women in an uncontrolled phase 1, and the sponsor's phase 1 suppository study suggested activity in anal HSIL. But placebo regression of anal HSIL at 18 weeks (partly from diagnostic biopsies) is likely 15-30%, and with 17 patients randomized 2:1 a difference of 50+ points is needed. A small LLC sponsor may report late or only at a specialty meeting.
evidence: Trimble CL et al., Clin Cancer Res 2020 (artesunate vaginal inserts for CIN2/3)
Artesunate suppositories phase 1 in anal HSIL, NCT03100045

assumptions.claim: Artesunate vaginal inserts were followed by histologic regression of CIN2/3 in about two-thirds of treated women in a phase I study.
assumptions.source: Trimble et al., Clin Cancer Res 2020

reason: Most overdose patients given IV NAC early never develop hepatotoxicity, so percent ALT change at day 3 is near zero for many and huge for a few; with 12 per arm this skewed outcome will rarely separate.
rationale: IV N-acetylcysteine given within 8-10 hours largely prevents hepatotoxicity, so the placebo arm will mostly have stable ALT with a few large rises, making percent change highly skewed. An add-on oral agent must reduce injury in the minority who develop it, which 24 patients cannot show reliably. The single-centre trial has been recruiting since 2023 and is likely to run late, so a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Smilkstein et al., NEJM 1988 (oral NAC timing and hepatotoxicity)
Chiew et al., Cochrane Review 2018 (interventions for paracetamol overdose)

assumptions.claim: Hepatotoxicity after acetaminophen overdose is uncommon when N-acetylcysteine is started within 8-10 hours of ingestion.

reason: Cardiac gene therapy has failed before (CUPID 2), and with about 50 patients per arm and only a handful of cardiovascular deaths, the listed primaries cannot all reach significance unless a hierarchical composite carries a large benefit.
rationale: AB-1002 (AAV inhibitor-1c gene therapy) has only small phase 1 data. Four primaries are listed: CV death, NYHA class, LVEF and 6MWT. If they form a hierarchical win-ratio composite, a phase 2 of about 150 could show significance only with a large functional effect; if each must be met, CV death alone (about 5% at 52 weeks) cannot be significant. CUPID 2's failure with SERCA2a gene therapy sets a low prior. Bayer/AskBio will likely present at a 2027 congress.

assumptions.claim: Intracoronary AAV1/SERCA2a gene therapy did not reduce recurrent heart failure events versus placebo.

reason: LAG-3 blockade added to PD-1 failed to improve RFS in the analogous adjuvant RELATIVITY-098 trial; an active pembrolizumab control leaves little room for an incremental effect large enough to detect.
rationale: The experimental arm swaps pembrolizumab for cemiplimab (equivalent PD-1 blockade) and adds the LAG-3 antibody fianlimab. The closest precedent, RELATIVITY-098 (relatlimab plus nivolumab vs nivolumab after resection), failed on RFS, suggesting LAG-3 adds little once PD-1 controls micrometastatic disease. Fianlimab is dosed higher and gave high response rates in metastatic phase 1 cohorts, but the trial needs an HR near 0.8 against a strong active control, which I think is unlikely. Extra immune toxicity and discontinuations may further erode any benefit.
evidence: Fianlimab plus cemiplimab phase 1 melanoma cohorts (Hamid, 2023)

assumptions.claim: In KEYNOTE-054, 12-month RFS with adjuvant pembrolizumab in resected stage III melanoma was 75.4%.
In KEYNOTE-716, 12-month RFS with adjuvant pembrolizumab in resected stage IIB/IIC melanoma was about 90%.
RELATIVITY-098, adding relatlimab (anti-LAG-3) to adjuvant nivolumab in resected stage III-IV melanoma, did not meet its RFS primary endpoint.

reason: A high and variable placebo SRI(4) response on stable background therapy can erase a modest TYK2 effect, as when baricitinib and anifrolumab each missed in one of their two phase 3 trials.
rationale: Phase 2 PAISLEY showed a 24-point SRI(4) gain at week 32 for 3 mg BID, but with an inverted dose-response that suggests some noise, and SLE phase 3 programmes routinely shrink phase 2 effects (anifrolumab TULIP-1, baricitinib BRAVE-II). With placebo responses near 40-45% at week 52, I expect a true gain of about 10 points; with about 258 per arm, power is roughly 60-70% at that effect. TYK2 inhibition blocks type I interferon and IL-12/23 signalling, a validated SLE axis, which supports a real but modest effect.

assumptions.claim: In phase 2 PAISLEY, SRI(4) response at week 32 was 58.2% with deucravacitinib 3 mg BID vs 34.4% with placebo.
In SLE-BRAVE-II, baricitinib 4 mg did not improve week-52 SRI-4 response over placebo (both about 46-47%).
Anifrolumab did not meet its week-52 SRI(4) primary endpoint in TULIP-1 despite a positive phase 2.

reason: Placebo SRI(4) responses can reach 45-55% in trials with many Latin American and Asian sites on background therapy, leaving a modest TYK2 effect short of significance at 257 per arm.
rationale: This is the twin of POETYK SLE-1 with the same design and timing. Phase 2 PAISLEY gave a 24-point SRI(4) gain for 3 mg BID, but phase 2 SLE effects typically shrink by half or more in phase 3, and twin-trial programmes often split (anifrolumab, baricitinib, tabalumab). I expect a true gain near 10 points on a placebo response in the mid-40s, giving roughly even odds of significance with about 257 per arm. Heavy Latin American enrolment may raise placebo response slightly.

assumptions.claim: In phase 2 PAISLEY, SRI(4) response at week 32 was 58.2% with deucravacitinib 3 mg BID vs 34.4% with placebo.
In SLE-BRAVE-I, week-52 SRI-4 response was 57% with baricitinib 4 mg vs 46% with placebo, while SLE-BRAVE-II showed no significant difference.
assumptions.source: Morand et al. and Petri et al., Lancet 2023

reason: With 31 patients per arm and a noisy patient-reported percent-change endpoint, a modest true regenerative effect may not reach significance against a placebo intracordal injection.
rationale: Recombinant HGF injected into scarred vocal folds improved VHI and mucosal wave in an open-label phase I/II study, but no randomized data exist. A 62-patient trial with a subjective patient-reported endpoint and an intracordal placebo injection (which itself may help through expectation and minor tissue remodelling) has limited power, and percent-change outcomes vary widely. Established scar and sulcus are hard to reverse, and regenerative effects may still be small at 24 weeks. I put success near one in three.
evidence: Hirano et al., phase I/II intracordal HGF for vocal fold scar and sulcus, 2018

assumptions.claim: An open-label phase I/II study of intracordal recombinant HGF in vocal fold scar and sulcus reported improvement in voice handicap and mucosal wave without serious adverse events.
assumptions.source: Hirano et al., J Tissue Eng Regen Med 2018

reason: About 145 patients per arm gives limited power for the 10-12 point SRI-4 gain typical of successful SLE biologics, and a high, variable placebo response at week 60 can push the difference below significance.
rationale: Ianalumab depletes B cells and blocks BAFF-R, combining two validated SLE mechanisms (belimumab's BAFF blockade; obinutuzumab's B-cell depletion in lupus nephritis). Its SLE phase 2 was supportive, and it met phase 3 primaries in Sjogren's disease and ITP. But SRI-4 at week 60 with steroid tapering carries a placebo response near 40%, and with about 145 per arm the trial has roughly 50-60% power for a 12-point gain. Rituximab's EXPLORER failure shows B-cell depletion does not guarantee an SRI benefit.

assumptions.claim: Belimumab improved week-52 SRI response over placebo by about 14 points in BLISS-52 (57.6% vs 43.6%) and about 10 points in BLISS-76 (43.2% vs 33.5%).
assumptions.source: Navarra et al., Lancet 2011; Furie et al., Arthritis Rheum 2011

assumptions.claim: Rituximab added to background therapy did not improve major or partial clinical response over placebo in non-renal SLE (EXPLORER).

reason: Enrolment across four age cohorts, the youngest last, has run since April 2023 and is still open; the March 2027 completion date will more likely be extended than the study stopped.
rationale: Pediatric antibiotic PK trials enrol slowly; 3.5 years in, this 48-child study is still recruiting and the 9-month-to-2-year cohort is typically enrolled last. The March 2027 primary completion is likely to slip; termination risk is modest because the study fulfils pediatric regulatory obligations for an approved antibiotic, and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

reason: Sixty adolescents per arm gives little power for the 8-13 point gain seen in adults, and pediatric functional GI trials often show high placebo responses.
rationale: In adults, tenapanor 50 mg BID raised the combined 6/12-week responder rate by 8-13 points (T3MPO-1 and -2). This adolescent trial uses a different SBM+2 based composite and only about 60 patients per arm, giving low power for an adult-sized effect; pediatric functional GI trials often see high placebo response, and some (lubiprostone in pediatric constipation) failed. Two doses are tested, which helps slightly. The study largely serves pediatric regulatory requirements, so it may be sized for feasibility rather than power.

assumptions.claim: In adult T3MPO-1, the 6/12-week combined responder rate was 27.0% with tenapanor 50 mg BID vs 18.7% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Chey et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2020

assumptions.claim: In adult T3MPO-2, the 6/12-week combined responder rate was 36.5% with tenapanor vs 23.7% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Chey et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2021

assumptions.claim: In the adult phase 3 trials, about 6-8% of tenapanor patients discontinued for diarrhoea vs under 1% on placebo.

reason: The comparator inhibits the same target; if alpelisib keeps its efficacy when toxicity is managed, inavolisib's advantage may be too small (HR near 0.8) to reach significance.
