rationale: Both arms target PI3K-alpha with fulvestrant after CDK4/6 inhibition, so the gain must come from inavolisib's mutant selectivity, mutant p110-alpha degradation and better tolerability. Alpelisib loses dose intensity to hyperglycaemia and rash (25% stopped for AEs in SOLAR-1), while inavolisib was well tolerated with a large benefit in INAVO120 (PFS HR 0.43). A plausible HR near 0.7 with about 290 events gives good power, but a same-target active comparator could narrow the gap; open-label conduct is mitigated by BICR.

assumptions.claim: In BYLieve cohort A, alpelisib plus fulvestrant after a CDK4/6 inhibitor gave a median PFS of 7.3 months.
In SOLAR-1, 25% of patients discontinued alpelisib because of adverse events.
In INAVO120, adding inavolisib to palbociclib-fulvestrant gave a PFS hazard ratio of 0.43 vs placebo.

reason: Phase 3 rests on a dose and subgroup signal from a phase 2b that missed its primary analysis; S1P1 modulation may not move SRI-4 beyond a placebo response near 40%.
rationale: Cenerimod, an S1P1 receptor modulator, did not show a significant dose-response in its phase 2b CARE primary analysis; the phase 3 programme rests on a signal for the 4 mg dose and in higher-activity or interferon-high patients. Lymphocyte-trafficking modulation has no validated record in SLE, and SRI-4 at month 12 carries placebo responses near 40%. With about 235 per arm the trial can detect roughly 12 points; I expect a true gain nearer 5.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2b CARE study, cenerimod did not show a statistically significant dose-response on mSLEDAI-2K change at month 6 in the primary analysis; a signal was seen for the 4 mg dose.
Placebo SRI(4) response at week 52 in TULIP-1 was about 40%.

reason: If B cells recover by month 12, the off-treatment remission gap may shrink below the roughly 18 points detectable with about 75 patients per arm.
rationale: Adding B-cell depletion to first-line steroids raises durable remission: rituximab plus dexamethasone lifted sustained response from about 36% to about 60% in newly diagnosed ITP. Ianalumab adds BAFF-R blockade and already met its primary endpoint in VAYHIT2. SROT-12 (response off treatment in months 12-15) fits that mechanism, and steroid-only durable remission is around 25%. With about 75 per arm and two doses, a 20-point gain gives good power. Risks are the May 2026 endpoint switch and B-cell recovery eroding the gap by month 12.

assumptions.claim: Adding rituximab to dexamethasone in newly diagnosed ITP raised sustained response at 6 months from 36% to 63%.
Ianalumab plus eltrombopag met its primary endpoint of time to treatment failure in previously treated ITP (VAYHIT2).
The primary endpoint was changed in May 2026 from time to treatment failure to SROT-12.

reason: TTFields added only a modest OS gain over gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel in LAPC in PANOVA-3 (HR about 0.82, p=0.039); with 512 patients the trial has roughly coin-flip power for an effect of that size, and device adherence is uncertain.
rationale: PANOVA-3 showed TTFields plus gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel improved OS in LAPC (16.2 vs 14.2 months, HR 0.82), a modest effect barely significant with 556 patients. This Chinese device-maker trial (512 patients, 5 sites) replicates the design; power for HR ~0.8 is about 50-60%. Chinese sponsors may achieve better adherence and tend to report favourably, but the true effect is small. Still recruiting in late 2026 with an event-driven OS endpoint, so a public result before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In PANOVA-3, TTFields plus gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel improved median OS in locally advanced pancreatic cancer to 16.2 vs 14.2 months (HR 0.82).
PFS was not significantly improved by TTFields in PANOVA-3.

reason: Bevacizumab biosimilar trials nearly always show ORR equivalence; the main way this fails is chance or slow, uneven accrual pushing the ORR difference interval past the margin.
rationale: Biosimilar bevacizumab equivalence trials in first-line non-squamous NSCLC with carboplatin-paclitaxel (Pfizer, Amgen, mAbxience, Biocad and others) have almost all met their ORR equivalence margins, as analytically similar antibodies behave the same clinically. Risks are manufacturing quality of a newer Russian producer and statistical noise with 620 patients. The trial was still recruiting in late 2026, so a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely; Russian sponsors rarely publish promptly.

assumptions.claim: Bevacizumab biosimilar equivalence trials in non-squamous NSCLC with carboplatin-paclitaxel have generally met their ORR equivalence margins.
assumptions.source: Reinmuth et al. 2019 (PF-06439535); Thatcher et al. 2019 (ABP 215)

reason: Acute gout flares improve quickly on their own and placebo patients get paracetamol rescue, so the placebo pain drop at 72 hours is large and can swamp a moderate NLRP3-inhibitor effect.
rationale: IL-1 blockade is validated in gout flares (canakinumab, anakinra), and dapansutrile's open-label phase 2a showed large day-3 pain reductions. But that study had no placebo; here rescue paracetamol and the natural resolution of flares give the placebo arm a big VAS drop. With 200 vs 100 patients and SD ~27 mm, an effect near 9-10 mm is needed for significance. Recruitment has dragged since 2023 at a small private sponsor, so results by mid-2027 are unlikely.
evidence: Kluck et al. 2020, Lancet Rheumatol (dapansutrile phase 2a)

assumptions.claim: In an open-label phase 2a, dapansutrile reduced target-joint pain by about half or more from baseline by day 3 in acute gout flare.
assumptions.source: Kluck V et al., Lancet Rheumatol 2020

reason: Cenerimod's phase 2b signal was a small mSLEDAI-2K difference (about 1.2 points), and SLE phase 3 trials with SRI-4 at month 12 often fail against high placebo response on background therapy.
rationale: The CARE phase 2b showed cenerimod 4 mg reduced mSLEDAI-2K by only about 1.2 points more than placebo at month 6, with stronger signals in high interferon-signature subsets. SLE phase 3 programmes (anifrolumab TULIP-1, baricitinib SLE-BRAVE-II, others) frequently miss SRI-4 because placebo response on background therapy runs 40-50%. With ~225 per arm, about 9-10 points of difference are needed. Viatris should press-release topline in 1H 2027 after December 2026 primary completion.

assumptions.claim: In the CARE phase 2b, cenerimod 4 mg reduced mSLEDAI-2K at month 6 by 1.19 points more than placebo.
Placebo SRI-4 response at week 52 in belimumab phase 3 trials was about 34-44%.

reason: Only 100 adolescents (67 vs 33) and three co-primary endpoints (UAS7, ISS7, HSS7) must all reach significance; a higher placebo response in teenagers could leave one component short.
rationale: In adult REMIX-1 and REMIX-2, remibrutinib improved UAS7 at week 12 by about 8 points over placebo (about -20 vs -11), with consistent ISS7 and HSS7 gains. CSU biology is similar in adolescents, and BTK inhibition works fast. With SD ~12.5 and 67 vs 33 patients, power for an 8-point gap is ~85%, but three correlated co-primaries must all succeed. Novartis typically shows paediatric data at congresses or posts on ClinicalTrials.gov within 12 months, so mid-2027 publication is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: In adult REMIX-1/REMIX-2, UAS7 change at week 12 was about -20 with remibrutinib vs about -11 to -12 with placebo.
assumptions.source: Metz et al., NEJM 2025 (REMIX-1/2; NCT05030311, NCT05032157)

reason: Sunitinib is a weak comparator in papillary-dominant nccRCC (PFS about 5-6 months), so failure would mostly need zanzalintinib plus nivolumab to underperform the cabozantinib-nivolumab benchmark in a mixed histology population.
rationale: Sunitinib performs poorly in non-clear cell RCC: PAPMET showed cabozantinib beat it in papillary RCC (PFS 9.0 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.60). Cabozantinib plus nivolumab gave ORR 47% and PFS 12.5 months in papillary/unclassified/translocation RCC. Zanzalintinib, a related multi-kinase VEGFR/MET/TAM inhibitor, plus nivolumab should reach HR ~0.55 for PFS and a large ORR gap, so both co-primaries are likely met. Exelixis press-releases toplines, expected around early 2027.

assumptions.claim: In PAPMET, sunitinib median PFS in papillary RCC was 5.6 months vs 9.0 months with cabozantinib (HR 0.60).
Cabozantinib plus nivolumab produced ORR 47% and median PFS 12.5 months in papillary, unclassified or translocation-associated RCC.
assumptions.source: Lee et al., J Clin Oncol 2022 (NCT03635892)

reason: With only 94 children and an event-driven design that may close with about 40-50 exacerbations, even a true hazard ratio near 0.6 gives under 50% power.
rationale: Benralizumab cuts exacerbations in adults with eosinophilic asthma by about 30-50%, and anti-IL-5 works in children (mepolizumab MUPPITS-2 rate ratio 0.73). Eosinophil depletion should translate to a hazard ratio around 0.5-0.6 here. But enrolment stopped at 94 and the event-driven double-blind period may end with roughly 45 events, so power is near 45-50%. AstraZeneca rarely press-releases paediatric trials; results more likely at ERS 2027 or on ClinicalTrials.gov by end of 2027.

assumptions.claim: Mepolizumab reduced asthma exacerbations in urban children with eosinophilic asthma (rate ratio 0.73).
Benralizumab reduced annual exacerbation rates by 28-51% versus placebo in adults with eosinophilic asthma.

reason: Factor XIa inhibition must add meaningful protection on top of antiplatelets; LIBREXIA-ACS was stopped for futility, though asundexian's positive OCEANIC-STROKE supports the stroke setting.
rationale: Bayer's OCEANIC-STROKE, a near-identical design with asundexian in about 12,300 patients, met its ischemic stroke endpoint in late 2025 (about 26% relative reduction) without more major bleeding, validating FXIa inhibition after non-cardioembolic stroke/TIA. AXIOMATIC-SSP showed milvexian lowered symptomatic ischemic stroke by about 30% at mid doses. With roughly 800 events, an HR near 0.8 is detectable. LIBREXIA-ACS futility tempers confidence. Primary completion October 2026, so topline likely early 2027.

assumptions.claim: Asundexian reduced ischemic stroke vs placebo after non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk TIA in OCEANIC-STROKE without increasing major bleeding.
In AXIOMATIC-SSP, milvexian at 25-100 mg twice daily was associated with about a 30% relative reduction in symptomatic ischemic stroke vs placebo, without a clear dose response.
LIBREXIA-ACS was stopped early because it was unlikely to meet its primary efficacy endpoint.

reason: Still recruiting in late 2026 in a rare FGFR2-fusion cholangiocarcinoma population, so the December 2026 primary completion date will very likely be pushed back, with results posted only well after the read date.
rationale: FOENIX-CCA4 is an FDA post-marketing confirmatory dose-comparison study for futibatinib in a rare biomarker-selected population; recruitment of 120 patients has run since July 2023 and was still open in October 2026, while the primary ORR needs follow-up after the last patient enrols. Taiho maintains its records, so the primary completion date will probably be moved into late 2027 or beyond. Termination is possible but unlikely for a regulatory commitment; results posting before August 2027 is very unlikely.

reason: Factor XIa inhibition may not prevent cardioembolic stroke as well as factor Xa inhibition; asundexian was clearly inferior to apixaban in OCEANIC-AF, and with about 850 events a tight margin needs milvexian to match apixaban almost exactly.
rationale: OCEANIC-AF stopped with asundexian about 3.8-fold worse than apixaban on stroke or systemic embolism, which casts doubt on the class in AF. Against that, milvexian 100 mg twice daily gives deeper, sustained FXIa inhibition. The IDMC let LIBREXIA-AF continue after OCEANIC-AF and again when the lower-dose ACS trial stopped for futility in 2025, which argues against gross inferiority. A sample of about 20,000 suggests a tight non-inferiority margin (about 1.2-1.3), so success needs a hazard ratio near 1.0. Overall the outcome is close to a coin flip.

assumptions.claim: In OCEANIC-AF, asundexian 50 mg daily was inferior to apixaban for stroke or systemic embolism (HR about 3.8) and the trial was stopped early.
Apixaban had a stroke or systemic embolism rate of 1.27% per year in ARISTOTLE.
LIBREXIA-ACS was stopped in 2025 after an interim analysis showed it was unlikely to meet its primary endpoint, while LIBREXIA-AF continued.
assumptions.source: Johnson & Johnson / BMS press release, November 2025

reason: It is unproven that an SSTR2 antagonist restores glucagon counterregulation well enough to cut nocturnal hypoglycemia in long-standing type 1 diabetes, and placebo-period counts are noisy and overdispersed with only about 62 participants per dose.
rationale: ZT-01 blocks somatostatin receptor 2 to release the glucagon response that is suppressed during hypoglycemia in type 1 diabetes. Rodent and early clamp data show more glucagon, but no controlled efficacy data exist on real-world hypoglycemic events. A crossover design with within-patient comparison gives reasonable power if the event rate falls by about 30%, and one of three doses (or a pooled analysis) can succeed. Counts of nocturnal events below 54 mg/dL are low and overdispersed, and alpha-cell dysfunction in long-standing type 1 diabetes may limit the effect. The trial was still recruiting in late 2026.
evidence: Karimian et al., Diabetes 2013 (SSTR2 antagonism in diabetic rats)

assumptions.claim: SSTR2 antagonism improved glucagon counterregulation to hypoglycemia in diabetic rats.

reason: Restoring gut microbiota diversity has to translate into a mortality benefit at 12 months, with only about 90 deaths; a realistic effect (HR about 0.8) is far below what this phase 2b can detect.
rationale: Observational data link low microbiota diversity to death after alloHCT, and MaaT013 showed activity in steroid-refractory gut GvHD. But no prophylactic FMT trial has shown a survival benefit, and 12-month overall survival is a hard endpoint driven by relapse, infection and GvHD. With about 387 patients and 12-month mortality of about 25%, there will be roughly 90 deaths, so the trial has power only for an HR near 0.6. The record still shows recruiting, so a readout by mid-2027 most likely means an early stop.
evidence: Taur et al., Sci Transl Med 2018 (auto-FMT after alloHCT)

assumptions.claim: Lower intestinal microbiota diversity around engraftment was associated with higher mortality after allogeneic HCT across several centers.

reason: Sham and placebo injections into the anal sphincter produce large reductions in incontinence episodes, so a one-time autologous cell injection has to beat a strong placebo response at 12 months with only 100 patients per arm.
rationale: Iltamiocel has a track record of disappointing controlled results: its phase 3 in stress urinary incontinence did not separate from placebo overall, and earlier fecal incontinence data were mainly uncontrolled. Placebo responses in fecal incontinence trials are large (about 30% or more of patients halve their episodes), and diary-based episode frequency is highly variable. With 200 patients and a single injection, the trial can show only a moderate effect. The sponsor is a small private subsidiary, so the readout and any filing are likely to be slow.
evidence: Graf et al., Lancet 2011 (NASHA Dx vs sham)

assumptions.claim: In the sham-controlled NASHA Dx trial, 31% of sham-treated patients had at least a 50% reduction in incontinence episodes at 6 months, versus 52% with active treatment.

reason: The adjuvant CDK4/6 class record is mixed: abemaciclib and ribociclib succeeded, but palbociclib failed twice. If TQB3616 has weaker exposure, tolerability or adherence, or the population is low-risk with few events, IDFS may not separate.
rationale: Adding a continuous-dosing CDK4/6 inhibitor to adjuvant endocrine therapy reduced IDFS events by about 25-30% in monarchE and NATALEE, while intermittent palbociclib failed in PALLAS and PENELOPE-B. TQB3616 is a newer CDK4/6 inhibitor with positive data in advanced breast cancer, and this large trial (1,946 patients, 2:1) should have good power for an HR of about 0.75 at an event-driven analysis. A readout by mid-2027 would most likely be a positive interim analysis, which raises p_met for earlier deadlines.
evidence: monarchE (Johnston et al., JCO 2020; Lancet Oncol 2023)

assumptions.claim: In NATALEE, ribociclib plus a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor improved IDFS versus endocrine therapy alone (HR about 0.75; 3-year IDFS 90.4% vs 87.1%).
In PALLAS, adding palbociclib to adjuvant endocrine therapy did not improve IDFS.
In monarchE, adding abemaciclib to endocrine therapy reduced the risk of IDFS events by about 30% in high-risk node-positive early breast cancer.

reason: SLE phase 3 trials often fail because of high placebo response on background therapy and heterogeneity between regions; baricitinib succeeded in one replicate trial and failed in the other, and here both replicate studies need to succeed.
rationale: In the phase 2 SLEek trial, upadacitinib 30 mg gave large improvements in BICLA, SRI-4, LLDAS and flares versus placebo. With about 250 patients per arm in each replicate study, a 10-point BICLA gain would be significant. But the phase 2 effect is likely inflated, and SLE phase 3 trials fail often (TULIP-1, SLE-BRAVE-II). The probability is about 0.75 per study, with high correlation between the two, so both succeed with probability about 0.6. Topline results are expected around mid-2027.
evidence: SLEek phase 2 (Merrill et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2024)
SLE-BRAVE-I and -II (Morand et al.; Petri et al., Lancet 2023)

assumptions.claim: In TULIP-2, BICLA response at week 52 was 31.5% with placebo versus 47.8% with anifrolumab.
Baricitinib 4 mg met the SRI-4 primary endpoint in SLE-BRAVE-I but not in SLE-BRAVE-II.
assumptions.source: Morand et al. and Petri et al., Lancet 2023

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 SLEek trial, upadacitinib 30 mg improved BICLA and SRI-4 responses versus placebo at week 48.

reason: Novartis stopped enrolment at 49 and set study completion equal to primary completion (Dec 2026), which points to a planned close-out on schedule; results posting is likely near the 12-month deadline, after August 2027.
rationale: Active, not recruiting with only 49 participants in a 36-month design; primary and study completion both 23 Dec 2026, which suggests a truncated study heading for close-out rather than an extension. Novartis keeps records updated and usually posts results close to the 12-month deadline (Dec 2027), so posting by Aug 2027 is less likely than not. Some chance the record is switched to terminated (business decision) given the small enrolment. Primary outcome changes are unlikely this late.

reason: Oral JAK1 inhibition has no proven lung-function benefit in asthma and the population is not selected for type-2 inflammation; with about 62 per arm and an SD near 380 mL the highest dose needs roughly 140 mL over placebo to reach significance.
rationale: Povorcitinib blocks JAK1 signalling downstream of IL-4/13, IL-5 and TSLP, so a lung-function signal is plausible, but inhaled JAK programmes failed and there is no oral JAK asthma precedent. Placebo FEV1 gains in biologic trials run 90-200 mL from regression to the mean. With ~62 per arm (SE of difference ~70 mL) a significant result needs a ~140 mL effect, above what I expect (~80 mL). Exacerbations are badly underpowered at this size. Incyte usually discloses phase 2 outcomes in pipeline updates, so a statement by mid-2027 is plausible.

assumptions.claim: In NAVIGATOR, pre-bronchodilator FEV1 rose about 0.09 L from baseline at week 52 in the placebo arm versus 0.23 L with tezepelumab.
In QUEST, placebo improved FEV1 by about 0.18-0.21 L at week 12 versus 0.32-0.34 L with dupilumab.

reason: A PD-1/LAG-3 bispecific must beat an active pembrolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel arm on PFS in only 83 patients; tobemstomig showed no advantage over pembrolizumab in other phase 2 head-to-head studies and Roche has deprioritised it.
rationale: Superiority on PFS against pembrolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel, an effective control (median PFS ~7.5-9.7 months in PD-L1+ TNBC), with only ~83 patients and maybe 45 events; even a true HR of 0.75 would rarely reach significance. Tobemstomig did not beat pembrolizumab in its NSCLC phase 2 and Roche has pulled back the programme, so a true benefit is unlikely. Results will most likely appear only as a CT.gov posting near the October 2027 deadline.

assumptions.claim: In KEYNOTE-355, median PFS with pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in CPS>=10 TNBC was 9.7 months versus 5.6 months with chemotherapy.
In IMpassion130, median PFS with atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel in PD-L1-positive TNBC was 7.5 months.

reason: A dose-optimisation study tied to the adagrasib accelerated approval; BMS will run it to completion, with results posting probably near the 12-month deadline in late 2027.
rationale: Active, not recruiting with primary completion Oct 2026 and study completion Nov 2026; as a post-marketing dose-optimisation study it is unlikely to be terminated. BMS/Mirati generally post within 12 months of actual primary completion, which puts the deadline around Oct 2027, after the Aug 2027 read date, so posting by then is less likely than not. The descriptive ORR primary is unlikely to change.

reason: Older small trials of OM-85 showed ~35-40% fewer wheezing episodes, but modern multicentre trials of bacterial lysates usually show smaller effects; with overdispersed episode counts in 296 children, a 20% reduction gives under 50% power.
rationale: OM-85 has supportive meta-analyses and Razi 2010 (38% fewer attacks), but that evidence comes from small, single-country trials and larger rigorous studies tend to shrink the effect. I expect a rate ratio near 0.8. With ~1.8 episodes per child over 6 months and negative-binomial overdispersion, the SE of the log rate ratio is ~0.14, so power is ~40% at RR 0.8. Severe episodes are rarer and less likely to separate. The trial is completed; OM Pharma is private, so disclosure will likely come through CT.gov posting or a 2027 congress.

assumptions.claim: In children aged 1-6 with recurrent wheezing, OM-85 reduced wheezing attacks by 37.9% versus placebo over 6 months.
assumptions.source: Razi et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2010

reason: CDK4/6 rechallenge after progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor gives modest ORR gains (about 5-10 points), which 127 per arm barely detects, and both ORR and PFS primaries must be met.
rationale: Post-CDK4/6 rechallenge trials gave mixed results: MAINTAIN (HR 0.57) and postMONARCH (HR 0.73) were positive on PFS, PACE was negative, and objective response gains were small. Placebo plus endocrine therapy ORR in this setting is ~5-8%. An 8-point ORR difference with 127 per arm is ~50% powered, and the co-primary PFS must also be significant. The trial was still recruiting in Oct 2026, so a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely; a Chinese sponsor without US sites rarely posts on CT.gov.

assumptions.claim: Switching to ribociclib plus a different endocrine therapy after CDK4/6 progression improved PFS with HR about 0.57.
assumptions.source: Kalinsky et al., J Clin Oncol 2023 (MAINTAIN)

assumptions.claim: Abemaciclib plus fulvestrant after CDK4/6 inhibitor progression improved PFS with HR about 0.73.
assumptions.source: postMONARCH, Kalinsky et al., ASCO 2024 / J Clin Oncol 2025

reason: Pharmacological prevention of cardiac-surgery AKI has a long record of failures, and LSALT peptide has no human AKI efficacy data; a 120-per-arm trial needs about a 15-point absolute reduction to be significant.
rationale: LSALT (DPEP-1 inhibitor) has only preclinical and COVID-19 phase 2 data. Many agents (sodium bicarbonate, statins, remote ischaemic preconditioning, ANG-3777) failed to prevent post-cardiac-surgery AKI. KDIGO with urine output in high-risk CKD patients gives a placebo AKI rate near 35-40%; I expect at most a ~6-point reduction, well short of the ~15 points detectable with 120 per arm. The micro-cap sponsor was still recruiting at 9 sites, so completion slips and a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Acute kidney injury occurs in roughly a fifth to a third of adults after cardiac surgery, higher in those with pre-existing CKD.
assumptions.source: Hu et al., J Cardiothorac Vasc Anesth 2016 (meta-analysis)

reason: The hot-flash co-primary should be clearly met, but non-inferiority on 18-month rPFS rests on few events in good-prognosis PSA responders, so a wide confidence interval could cross the margin even with no true difference.
rationale: Randomised patients reached PSA <0.2 on apalutamide plus ADT, a group with excellent short-term prognosis (18-month rPFS ~85-90%), and both arms keep apalutamide, so a large rPFS penalty from pausing ADT is unlikely. Testosterone recovery should make the hot-flash co-primary near-certain. The risk is the NI test: with ~40 events or a rate-difference margin, the interval may be too wide. Both co-primaries must be met. Janssen will likely present at ASCO or ESMO 2027.

assumptions.claim: In TITAN, apalutamide plus ADT improved rPFS versus ADT alone in mCSPC with HR 0.48.
SWOG 9346 could not show non-inferiority of intermittent versus continuous ADT for overall survival in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer.

reason: Superiority over placebo is very likely with 208 versus 104 patients, but 24 weeks is short for minoxidil, the strict 0.01 level and any co-primary non-inferiority test against topical 2% minoxidil add risk.
rationale: Low-dose oral minoxidil grows hair in women: Ramos 2020 found 1 mg oral comparable to topical 5% at 24 weeks, and topical 2% beats placebo by ~10 hairs/cm2. I expect ~9 hairs/cm2 over placebo with SD ~16; with 208 vs 104 the SE is ~1.9, so significance at 0.01 is very likely. The main risks are a large placebo response, imaging noise, or the trial's own hypothesis also requiring non-inferiority to topical 2%. A Spanish private sponsor with EU-only sites will likely disclose at a congress or via CTIS, not quickly.

assumptions.claim: In women with female pattern hair loss, oral minoxidil 1 mg daily and topical 5% minoxidil gave similar increases in hair density at 24 weeks.
assumptions.source: Ramos et al., J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol 2020

assumptions.claim: Topical 2% and 5% minoxidil increased non-vellus hair counts in women substantially more than placebo at 48 weeks.
assumptions.source: Lucky et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2004

reason: PI3K blockade may add less in HER2-driven disease than in HR+/HER2- (INAVO120), and long maintenance with inavolisib toxicity (hyperglycaemia, diarrhoea, stomatitis) could erode dose intensity in a modest 230-patient trial.
rationale: Still recruiting in Oct 2026 with PFS follow-up of up to ~40 months, so a primary readout by mid-2027 is unlikely and any early statement would probably be an interim analysis or a stop. Inavolisib gave PFS HR 0.43 in INAVO120 (HR+/HER2-), and PI3K activation drives trastuzumab resistance, so benefit in PIK3CA-mutated HER2+ maintenance is plausible; HER2CLIMB-05 shows maintenance add-ons can reach HR ~0.64. Risks: smaller effect in HER2-driven disease, tolerability over long maintenance and a modest sample of 230.

assumptions.claim: Inavolisib plus palbociclib and fulvestrant improved PFS with a hazard ratio of about 0.43 versus placebo in PIK3CA-mutated HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer.
PIK3CA mutation was associated with shorter PFS among HER2+ metastatic patients treated with pertuzumab, trastuzumab and docetaxel.
assumptions.source: CLEOPATRA biomarker analysis, Baselga et al. JCO 2014

assumptions.claim: Adding tucatinib to trastuzumab-pertuzumab maintenance after first-line induction improved PFS with a hazard ratio of about 0.64.

reason: Biosimilars rarely fail; the residual risk is a PK geometric-mean ratio CI or the ratio of near-zero GdE lesion counts falling outside the protocol margins through chance or a manufacturing difference.
rationale: Celltrion's biosimilar phase 3 programmes (infliximab, rituximab, trastuzumab, tocilizumab and others) have consistently shown equivalence. Ocrelizumab suppresses GdE lesions almost completely, so counts are low in both arms and ratio margins are usually set wide; the PK part is a standard AUC comparison. The main uncertainty is timing: the trial was still recruiting in Oct 2026 with a 24-week endpoint, so primary results are unlikely before mid or late 2027.

assumptions.claim: Ocrelizumab reduced the number of GdE T1 lesions by about 94-95% versus interferon beta-1a.
assumptions.source: OPERA I/II, Hauser et al. NEJM 2017

assumptions.claim: Celltrion's earlier antibody biosimilar phase 3 trials met their equivalence endpoints.

reason: Enrolment stopped at 21 after Roche moved afimkibart into phase 3, so the study is likely closed around end-2026 as completed or terminated, with results posting due only after the read date.
rationale: Only 21 participants were enrolled, enrolment is closed and the registry lists primary and study completion at end-2026, so the study most likely closes on schedule as completed or is marked terminated after early truncation; posting would be due by end-2027.

reason: PFS should be met, but OS counts as a co-primary here and may not cross its interim boundary at the first readout, since post-progression enfortumab vedotin in the chemotherapy arm dilutes the OS difference in a global population.
rationale: RC48-C016 (disitamab vedotin plus toripalimab vs gemcitabine-platinum in HER2-expressing first-line UC) showed PFS HR 0.36 and OS HR 0.54, and EV-302 shows an ADC plus PD-1 beats chemotherapy on both endpoints. PFS success is very likely. Because the round counts OS as a co-primary, the main risk is OS not yet significant at the first readout, especially with post-progression EV in the control arm diluting OS globally.

assumptions.claim: Disitamab vedotin plus toripalimab improved PFS (HR about 0.36) and OS (HR about 0.54) versus gemcitabine-platinum in previously untreated HER2-expressing urothelial carcinoma.
Median PFS with platinum-gemcitabine chemotherapy was about 6.3 months in previously untreated advanced urothelial carcinoma.
Enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab met both PFS and OS at the first interim analysis versus chemotherapy.

reason: Agomelatine has small antidepressant effects and little adjunctive evidence, and a biomarker-defined subgroup primary in an adjunctive MDD trial with high placebo response leaves little room to separate.
rationale: ALTO-300 is agomelatine given adjunctively, with the primary analysis in a pre-defined biomarker subgroup. Agomelatine monotherapy effects are small (roughly 1.5-2.5 MADRS points), adjunctive evidence is thin, and Alto's similar biomarker-guided ALTO-100 phase 2b failed in 2024. Adjunctive MDD trials carry large placebo responses, and a subgroup primary reduces the analysed sample. Phase 2 success rates for such precision-psychiatry approaches are around 25%.
evidence: ALTO-100 phase 2b MDD topline (Alto Neuroscience), Oct 2024
Agomelatine meta-analysis, Taylor et al. BMJ 2014

assumptions.claim: Alto's biomarker-guided ALTO-100 phase 2b trial in MDD did not meet its primary endpoint.
Agomelatine's mean advantage over placebo on depression rating scales is small, under about 2 HAM-D points.

reason: Type I IFN blockade has no randomized efficacy data in SSc, and background mycophenolate drives placebo improvement in a demanding multi-domain composite, so a difference of about 11 points with 157 per arm may not be reached.
rationale: No randomized phase 2 of anifrolumab in SSc preceded this phase 3; the rationale rests on the type I IFN signature in SSc and lupus efficacy (TULIP-2). SSc trials have often failed (tocilizumab focuSSced on mRSS, lenabasum RESOLVE-1, abatacept ASSET) because background MMF drives placebo improvement on composites. Revised CRISS-25 is a demanding multi-domain composite, and with about 157 per arm roughly an 11-point difference is needed for significance.
evidence: focuSSced tocilizumab, Khanna Lancet Respir Med 2020

assumptions.claim: Tocilizumab did not meet its primary mRSS endpoint in early diffuse SSc.
assumptions.source: focuSSced, Khanna et al. Lancet Respir Med 2020

assumptions.claim: Lenabasum failed its ACR-CRISS primary endpoint, with high placebo response in patients on background immunosuppression.
Anifrolumab improved lupus disease activity versus placebo in a phase 3 trial.

reason: A naked EGFRxHER3 bispecific added to docetaxel in EGFR-wild-type NSCLC after immunochemotherapy is likely to give only a modest OS gain, and both OS and BICR-PFS must reach significance.
rationale: SI-B001 is a naked EGFRxHER3 bispecific; earlier naked anti-EGFR or anti-VEGFR2 add-ons to chemotherapy in NSCLC produced only modest OS gains (REVEL HR 0.86, SQUIRE HR 0.84), and phase 2 combination data were modest. Both OS and BICR-PFS must be met. Sponsor-run trials in China succeed fairly often, and a result announced by mid-2027 is more likely to be positive, which partly offsets the weak prior; the sponsor's ADC iza-bren may also lower its priority.

assumptions.claim: Ramucirumab plus docetaxel improved OS versus docetaxel in second-line NSCLC with a hazard ratio of about 0.86.
Necitumumab added to gemcitabine-cisplatin improved OS in squamous NSCLC with a hazard ratio of about 0.84.
assumptions.source: SQUIRE, Thatcher et al. Lancet Oncol 2015

reason: Without phase 2 data in Sjogren's, TYK2 inhibition may give at most a 1-point ESSDAI benefit, which a large placebo improvement and between-patient variability can easily mask.
rationale: Deucravacitinib blocks TYK2 (type I IFN, IL-12/23), a pathway active in Sjogren's, and showed lupus activity in PAISLEY, but there is no phase 2 in Sjogren's and the JAK1 inhibitor filgotinib failed there. Recent Sjogren's phase 3s (ianalumab NEPTUNUS-1/2) met ESSDAI with roughly 1-point differences; with about 258 per arm and two doses, a true effect of about 1 point gives roughly even odds. High placebo response is the main threat.

assumptions.claim: Ianalumab met the ESSDAI primary endpoint in two phase 3 Sjogren's trials with placebo-adjusted differences of about 1 point.
Filgotinib did not significantly improve outcomes versus placebo in a phase 2 Sjogren's trial.
Deucravacitinib improved SLE responder rates versus placebo in phase 2.
assumptions.source: PAISLEY, Morand et al. Arthritis Rheumatol 2023

reason: Resistance to a prior FGFR inhibitor is heterogeneous (off-target bypass as well as kinase-domain mutations), so tinengotinib's phase 1/2 activity may not hold across a broader randomized Part B population.
rationale: Tinengotinib inhibits FGFR1-3 including gatekeeper and molecular-brake resistance mutants and showed responses in FGFR-inhibitor-refractory FGFR2-fusion cholangiocarcinoma in phase 1/2. The control, physician's-choice chemotherapy after chemotherapy and an FGFR inhibitor, has short PFS (about 2-3 months), so a 2:1 trial with BICR PFS has good power if phase 2 activity holds. Risks are heterogeneous resistance mechanisms and a small Part B.
evidence: ABC-06 FOLFOX second-line BTC, Lamarca Lancet Oncol 2021

assumptions.claim: FOLFOX gave median PFS of about 4 months in second-line biliary tract cancer, before any FGFR inhibitor.
assumptions.source: ABC-06, Lamarca et al. Lancet Oncol 2021

assumptions.claim: Tinengotinib produced objective responses in FGFR2-fusion cholangiocarcinoma that had progressed on prior FGFR inhibitors.

reason: With a 1-year TLF rate near 5%, a tight absolute non-inferiority margin or higher-than-expected event rates in an all-comer population could leave the upper confidence bound above the margin even with equivalent stents.
rationale: Modern thin-strut DES compared with Xience in all-comer non-inferiority trials almost always meet non-inferiority on 1-year TLF (TALENT, BIOSCIENCE, BIOFLOW-V). Angiolite already showed non-inferior late lumen loss versus Xience in the ANGIOLITE randomized trial. With about 2300 patients and roughly 5% event rates the trial should have enough power unless the margin is tight. Results are more likely at ESC or TCT 2027 than by June.

assumptions.claim: The Angiolite sirolimus-eluting stent was non-inferior to Xience on in-stent late lumen loss in a randomized trial.
A thin-strut sirolimus-eluting stent was non-inferior to Xience on 1-year target-lesion failure in an all-comer trial with event rates around 5%.

reason: Intradermal saline injections themselves produce visible scar improvement from needle trauma and assessor optimism, so the saline responder rate could be high enough to shrink the gap on a stringent both-cheeks responder definition.
rationale: Space-occupying injectable gels for atrophic acne scars have generally beaten saline controls on investigator-rated scar scales (Bellafill pivotal about 64% vs 33%). With 118 vs 39 patients, a 20-25 point difference is detectable. AbbVie advanced ELAPR002f (tropoelastin-based) to a pivotal device trial, implying a phase 2 signal. Risk is a high saline response on a both-cheeks 1-grade rule. Results will likely surface mainly via registry posting near the July 2027 deadline or aesthetics congresses.

assumptions.claim: In the Bellafill pivotal acne scar trial about two thirds of PMMA-collagen subjects versus about one third of saline-control subjects were responders at 6 months.
assumptions.source: Karnik et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2014

assumptions.claim: Allocation is 3:1 gel to saline (1 in 4 chance of saline).

reason: A herbal tablet has no proven anti-inflammatory potency in axial spondyloarthritis, and after an NSAID washout the placebo arm may still post 25-35% ASAS20 at week 8, leaving a small difference.
rationale: With 204 per arm, a 12-15 point ASAS20 difference would be significant. Placebo ASAS20 in axSpA trials runs around 25-40% at weeks 12-16, likely a bit lower at week 8 after NSAID washout. Chinese TCM phase 3 programs that reach publication are usually reported as positive, and the selected TCM-syndrome population is enriched. Still recruiting at the registered completion date, so a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Placebo ASAS20 response at week 16 was 28% in MEASURE 2.
Placebo ASAS40 response at week 16 was 18% in COAST-V.
assumptions.source: van der Heijde et al., Lancet 2018 (COAST-V)

reason: The tremelimumab benefit in STK11/KEAP1/KRAS-mutant disease comes from exploratory POSEIDON subgroups, mostly on OS, and against an active pembrolizumab-chemo control a 100-patient trial needs a PFS HR near 0.6 to reach significance.
rationale: TRITON tests whether adding CTLA-4 blockade overcomes immune resistance of STK11/KEAP1-mutant tumours. POSEIDON subgroups showed OS gains versus chemo, not versus pembrolizumab-chemo, and PFS differences were small. With about 80 events, only HR below about 0.64 is significant; a true HR around 0.85 gives roughly 20% power. Phase 2b estimation design may be reported descriptively. Results most likely at a late-2027 congress.

assumptions.claim: In POSEIDON, durvalumab plus tremelimumab plus chemo improved OS versus chemo in exploratory STK11-, KEAP1- and KRAS-mutant non-squamous subgroups.
assumptions.source: Peters et al., ESMO 2022 / Skoulidis et al., Nature 2024

assumptions.claim: Median PFS with platinum-pemetrexed-pembrolizumab in KEYNOTE-189 overall was about 9 months, lower in KEAP1/STK11-mutant disease.

reason: The FAK-inhibitor add-on effect rests on single-arm phase 1b data; if the true PFS gain over PLD is modest, about 115 events with 2:1 allocation may not reach significance by BICR.
rationale: PLD alone in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer gives median PFS about 3.5-4 months. Ifebemtinib plus PLD showed high response rates and PFS around 6 months in single-arm phase 1b and earned China breakthrough designation. A true HR near 0.65 with about 115 events gives reasonable power. Chinese sponsors announce positive registrational data quickly and stay quiet on misses, so a public readout skews positive. Still recruiting late 2026, so readout timing is late.

assumptions.claim: Single-agent chemotherapy in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer gave median PFS 3.4 months in AURELIA.
assumptions.source: Pujade-Lauraine et al., J Clin Oncol 2014

assumptions.claim: Investigator's-choice chemotherapy (including PLD) gave median PFS about 4 months in MIRASOL.

reason: CLE placebo arms can improve with background topicals and seasonal variation, and scarring discoid lesions respond slowly, which could compress the CLASI-70 difference at week 24.
rationale: Type I interferon drives cutaneous lupus; anifrolumab doubled CLASI-50 response versus placebo in SLE patients with active skin disease in TULIP, and anti-BDCA2 litifilimab confirmed the pathway in CLE. With about 170 per arm, a 15-point CLASI-70 gap suffices. AstraZeneca reports phase 3 readouts in quarterly results, so a statement by mid-2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: In TULIP-2, among patients with baseline CLASI-A of at least 10, CLASI-50 at week 12 was 49% with anifrolumab versus 25% with placebo.
Litifilimab significantly reduced CLASI-A versus placebo at week 16 in CLE in LILAC part B.

reason: TPL2 inhibition is unvalidated in UC; the earlier tilpisertib molecule needed a prodrug reformulation, and in an advanced-therapy-refractory population with roughly 44 patients per dose arm a moderate effect would miss significance.
rationale: Novel oral mechanisms in UC phase 2 succeed about a third of the time. Population is advanced-therapy experienced, where placebo clinical response is about 20-30% and drug effects are smaller. The dose-ranging design leaves about 44 per arm, so the highest dose needs roughly a 20-point gain. Gilead replaced tilpisertib with a prodrug, suggesting exposure limits. Gilead may disclose topline via earnings or a late-2027 congress.

assumptions.claim: Placebo clinical response at week 8 in U-ACHIEVE induction (mixed bio-naive and bio-exposed) was 27%.
Gilead earlier tested tilpisertib (GS-4875), a TPL2 inhibitor, in a phase 2 UC study.

reason: Pediatric heart transplants are rare and enrolment across three German centres is slow, so the registered January 2027 completion will probably slip or recruitment will continue past March 2027.
rationale: Fifteen pediatric heart transplant recipients at three German centres, recruiting since 2023, with organ allocation dependent on donor availability; extensions are typical. A European device/solution sponsor is unlikely to post results on ClinicalTrials.gov. The single safety primary outcome is unlikely to change.

reason: A single-site feasibility pilot with perhaps 15-30 PTSD patients per arm against an active conjoint therapy may not test CAPS-5 formally or reach significance even with a real 10-point effect.
rationale: MDMA-assisted therapy cut CAPS-5 about 10-12 points more than therapy with placebo in MAPP1/MAPP2, and an uncontrolled MDMA-CBCT pilot showed large drops. Here the comparator is active CBCT, open label, and the trial is a feasibility pilot whose PTSD sample may be about 15 per arm; a 10-point difference with SD about 12 is borderline. Recruitment is ongoing, so results by mid-2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In MAPP1, MDMA-assisted therapy reduced CAPS-5 by about 11-12 points more than therapy with placebo at 18 weeks.
An uncontrolled pilot of MDMA-assisted CBCT in dyads reported large reductions in clinician-rated PTSD severity.
assumptions.source: Monson et al., J Trauma Stress 2020

reason: With about 22 patients per arm, a strict single-timepoint remission (BVAS 0, prednisolone <=4 mg) and a placebo arm partly on background mepolizumab/benralizumab, a JAK1 effect would need to exceed roughly 25-30 points to reach p<0.05.
rationale: NS-229 is an oral JAK1 inhibitor; JAK inhibition lowers eosinophils and case series suggest activity in refractory EGPA, but there is no randomized evidence. The population needs >=7.5 mg prednisolone despite optional anti-IL-5 biologics, so it is refractory. Placebo remission under OGC taper in MIRRA was low (single digits for sustained remission), and a single week-28 look may run 10-20%. With 45 patients, power is modest unless the effect is large. Nippon Shinyaku may disclose the result only in pipeline updates.

assumptions.claim: In MIRRA, remission (BVAS 0 and prednisolone <=4 mg/day) at both weeks 36 and 48 occurred in about 3% of placebo patients.
In MANDARA, about 59% of benralizumab and 56% of mepolizumab patients were in remission at weeks 36 and 48, so background anti-IL-5 is active in many EGPA patients.

reason: Topical patidegib may not deliver enough hedgehog inhibition in the skin; the earlier 2% gel phase 3 missed overall, and this trial rests on a post hoc PTCH1-mutation subgroup whose effect may shrink on replication.
rationale: Systemic hedgehog inhibition (vismodegib) almost abolishes new BCCs in Gorlin syndrome, so the target is validated; the question is topical delivery. PellePharm's earlier patidegib 2% phase 3 missed its primary endpoint overall, but Sol-Gel redesigned around a PTCH1-confirmed, high-burden (>=10 facial BCCs) population where a post hoc reduction was seen, and switched to counting all new BCCs by central photo review, which raises event counts. With about 56 per arm and an overdispersed count, a true 35-50% reduction gives reasonable power; a 25% reduction does not.
evidence: Tang et al., NEJM 2012 (vismodegib in basal cell nevus syndrome)

assumptions.claim: The earlier patidegib gel 2% phase 3 in Gorlin syndrome did not meet its primary endpoint in the overall population.
Oral vismodegib reduced the rate of new surgically eligible BCCs in basal cell nevus syndrome by about 90% versus placebo.

reason: As-needed fluticasone propionate via a dry-powder inhaler (including children) may deliver less anti-inflammatory effect per rescue use than budesonide-albuterol did in MANDALA, shrinking the hazard ratio toward 0.85 or above.
rationale: This is a near copy of MANDALA (ICS-SABA rescue vs SABA on top of maintenance therapy in patients with a recent severe exacerbation), where high-dose budesonide-albuterol cut first severe exacerbation by about 26% and the low dose narrowly missed. Pairing an ICS with every rescue puff is a well-validated mechanism (also BATURA, SYGMA). With about 924 per arm and an event-driven design (roughly 400+ events), power for HR 0.78 is high. Risks are a weaker high dose of fluticasone propionate, DPI technique in children, and adherence.

assumptions.claim: In MANDALA, budesonide-albuterol 180/160 mcg as needed reduced the risk of a first severe asthma exacerbation versus albuterol alone, HR about 0.74.
In MANDALA, the lower 180/80 mcg dose had HR about 0.83 and did not reach significance.

reason: With 18 vs 9 patients, Fisher's exact test needs about 8 of 18 complete histologic responses against 0 of 9 on placebo for p<0.05; a plausible 20-35% complete response rate on topical artesunate falls short.
rationale: Artesunate showed histologic regression in small open-label studies of HPV-associated intraepithelial neoplasia, and spontaneous complete regression of vulvar HSIL in 18 weeks is rare (placebo near 0% in imiquimod trials). But complete histologic clearance is a strict endpoint and the trial is tiny (2:1, 27 patients), so even a real effect is likely to miss two-sided significance. The trial is still recruiting after nearly three years, so a result by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: van Seters et al., NEJM 2008 (imiquimod for VIN)
Trimble et al., Clin Cancer Res 2020 (artesunate for CIN2/3, phase 1)

assumptions.claim: In a placebo-controlled trial of imiquimod for vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia, no placebo patient had a complete response at 20 weeks.

reason: Enrolling 54 patients with Acinetobacter HABP/VABP in Greece and Israel within about 10 months of a May 2026 start is ambitious; the March 2027 primary completion will probably slip.
rationale: Omnix's OMN6 phase 2a is a safety/PK dose-ranging study in a hard-to-recruit ICU population (APACHE II 10-24, no septic shock or ARDS, confirmed ABC). Such trials usually run behind schedule, and small sponsors carry funding risk. Results are not due on ClinicalTrials.gov before 2028, and the trial may not be an applicable US trial. PK and safety primaries are seldom changed in substance.

reason: Total eGFR change at 24 months mixes any acute hemodynamic dip with the chronic benefit; endothelin antagonists slow decline modestly (about 1 mL/min/yr), so the 24-month difference may be only 1-1.5 units against an SE near 0.5.
rationale: In ZENITH-CKD, zibotentan 0.25 mg plus dapagliflozin lowered UACR about 27% beyond dapagliflozin, and endothelin antagonism improved kidney outcomes in SONAR. In high-proteinuria CKD the control arm declines fast, which gives room for benefit. But ERA eGFR effects have been marginal (PROTECT total slope borderline, DUPLEX missed), and the primary is total change at month 24 including any acute dip. With about 1,800 patients, power is around 50-70% for a 1.3-unit difference. A positive result is more likely to be press-released by June.

assumptions.claim: In ZENITH-CKD, zibotentan 0.25 mg plus dapagliflozin reduced UACR by about 27% versus dapagliflozin alone at week 12.
In SONAR, atrasentan reduced the composite kidney endpoint versus placebo with HR about 0.65 in UACR responders.
In PROTECT, the 2-year total eGFR slope difference for sparsentan versus irbesartan was about 1 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr and narrowly missed significance.

reason: IL-6 blockade mainly calms orbital inflammation; its effect on proptosis (the primary) is likely smaller than IGF-1R inhibition, and about 26 patients per arm cannot reliably detect a 20-25 point difference.
rationale: Tocilizumab improved clinical activity and gave some proptosis reduction in steroid-resistant TED, and pacibekitug is a long-acting anti-IL-6. Placebo proptosis response in TED trials runs 10-20%. A 20-25 point gain is plausible but not assured, and power is limited at about 26 per arm (better if both doses are pooled). After the Novartis takeover the focus is cardiovascular, so disclosure may come late or only through pipeline updates; an early disclosure is more likely if positive.
evidence: Perez-Moreiras et al., Am J Ophthalmol 2018 (tocilizumab RCT in TED)

assumptions.claim: In OPTIC, the proptosis response rate at week 24 was about 10% with placebo versus 83% with teprotumumab.
In a placebo-controlled trial of tocilizumab in corticosteroid-resistant TED, tocilizumab improved CAS response versus placebo.
assumptions.source: Perez-Moreiras et al., Am J Ophthalmol 2018

reason: Gilead's PURPOSE 3 hit primary completion in July 2026 with lenacapavir PrEP already approved, so results are due on ClinicalTrials.gov by July 2027 with no reason to delay; Gilead usually posts on time.
rationale: Active not recruiting phase 2 PK/safety/acceptability study run with HPTN; primary completion 22 July 2026 makes results due around July 2027. Lenacapavir for PrEP is approved, so a delay certification is unlikely, and Gilead is generally compliant, though posting often lands near the deadline. Termination is very unlikely this late. Seven primary outcomes add slight risk of a substantive edit.

reason: PK/safety phase 2 run by Gilead with HPTN; follow-up past primary completion (July 2026) is routine, so stopping is very unlikely and results posting by the one-year deadline (July 2027) is likely given Gilead's posting record.
rationale: Primary completion passed in July 2026 with status active, not recruiting; Gilead usually posts ClinicalTrials.gov results close to the 12-month deadline, which falls before the read date. Lenacapavir PrEP is approved, so there is no safety reason to stop. Primary outcomes are simple PK and safety measures, unlikely to be changed in substance.

reason: Patients already on BTKi for at least a year progress slowly when BTKi is simply continued, so PFS events accrue slowly and the trial may need long follow-up before a significant difference can be shown.
rationale: Adding a BCL2 inhibitor to BTKi produces deep responses and much lower progression (venetoclax-ibrutinib data), so a true HR well below 0.6 is plausible. The main problem is timing: the trial was still recruiting in October 2026, so a primary result by June 2027 most likely means a positive interim. Lisaftoclax activity in R/R CLL supports the mechanism.

assumptions.claim: Lisaftoclax was approved in China in 2025 for previously treated CLL/SLL.
Fixed-duration venetoclax plus ibrutinib achieved high undetectable MRD rates in CLL.

reason: Unproven oral agent in alopecia areata tested over only 12 weeks with about 36 patients per arm; even JAK inhibitors show modest SALT change at week 12, so a significant separation from placebo is unlikely.
rationale: NXC736 has no prior efficacy data in alopecia areata. Twelve weeks is early for hair regrowth: in the baricitinib and ritlecitinib phase 3 trials, separation from placebo was modest at week 12 and grew by weeks 24-36. With about 36 per arm and SD near 30 points of percent change, only a large effect would reach significance. The trial was still recruiting after its registered primary completion date, so a readout by mid-2027 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Placebo SALT improvement in moderate-to-severe AA trials is small at early time points.

reason: Aflibercept rarely lets patients lose 15 or more letters (about 2-4%), so an eye drop cannot be shown superior on vision loss; at best it shows comparable rates, which is not superiority.
rationale: KHK4951 is a topical VEGFR inhibitor (tivozanib eye drops); topical anti-VEGF agents have not matched intravitreal injections in DME. Loss of 15 or more letters on aflibercept is rare (about 1-4% in VIVID/VISTA), so the experimental arm cannot do significantly better. A formal non-inferiority claim is not stated in the record, and Kyowa Kirin may report the phase 2 only briefly in pipeline updates.

assumptions.claim: In VIVID/VISTA, few aflibercept-treated DME eyes (under 5%) lost 15 or more letters by week 52.

reason: Anti-inflammatory therapy after acute MI has mixed results (CANTOS positive, CLEAR SYNERGY colchicine null); an IL-6 effect around HR 0.85-0.9 could miss significance even with about 1000 events.
rationale: Ziltivekimab cuts hsCRP by about 80-90% (RESCUE), and IL-1beta blockade cut MACE 15% in CANTOS. However, colchicine after MI was null in CLEAR SYNERGY, and ARTEMIS does not enrich for persistent inflammation. With about 1000 events, power for HR 0.85 is around 70%, so success is close to a coin flip. Novo usually announces CVOT toplines promptly after primary completion in January 2027.

assumptions.claim: Canakinumab reduced MACE with a hazard ratio of about 0.85 in post-MI patients with hsCRP of at least 2 mg/L.
Colchicine started after MI did not reduce cardiovascular events (HR about 0.99).
Ziltivekimab lowered hsCRP by 77-92% versus placebo in phase 2.

reason: 24-week safety/PK phase 2a by BMS, no longer recruiting, with primary completion December 2026; it should complete on schedule, and results may be posted near the one-year deadline, after the read date.
rationale: Enrollment is closed and treatment lasts 24 weeks, so the December 2026 primary completion date is achievable. BMS usually posts results within 12 months, which is after the August 2027 read date in most cases. Safety-only primary outcomes are rarely changed.

reason: A pirfenidone-like agent in about 100 patients per arm needs a reduction in FVC decline of at least 60 mL/year to reach significance; the effect may be smaller or diluted by the interim dose selection.
rationale: Sufenidone is a pirfenidone analogue; pirfenidone and nintedanib roughly halve FVC decline relative to placebo (about -200 mL/year). With about 105 per arm and SD around 200 mL/year, a true effect of 80-100 mL/year would be detected, but an unproven analogue may be weaker. The trial was still recruiting in October 2026 with a 52-week endpoint, so a primary readout by mid-2027 is very unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Placebo FVC decline was about 220 mL/year in the INPULSIS trials.
Pirfenidone reduced the proportion of patients with significant FVC decline at 52 weeks versus placebo.

reason: Placebo response in dementia-related psychosis trials is large and variable, and elderly patients may not tolerate doses giving the muscarinic effect seen in schizophrenia; a modest drug-placebo gap of about 1-1.5 NPI-C points could be lost in noise.
rationale: Xanomeline reduced hallucinations and delusions in a 1997 AD trial, giving a mechanistic rationale, and KarXT works in acute schizophrenia. Against that, ADP trials show heavy placebo response (pimavanserin's benefit faded by week 12), KarXT's ARISE adjunctive schizophrenia trial failed, and ADEPT-2 was enlarged to 500, hinting at a smaller effect than planned. About an even chance. Still recruiting at launch, so primary completion and topline likely slip toward mid-2027.
evidence: Bodick et al. 1997 Arch Neurol (xanomeline in AD)

assumptions.claim: Xanomeline reduced psychotic symptoms (hallucinations, delusions) versus placebo in patients with Alzheimer's disease.
Pimavanserin's phase 2 AD psychosis trial showed a significant psychosis benefit at week 6 that was no longer significant at week 12.
KarXT did not meet the primary endpoint as adjunctive therapy in the ARISE schizophrenia trial.

reason: If ZP5-9676 is a new benzimidazole, its single-dose hookworm efficacy is unproven in humans; a cure rate only modestly above placebo would be the main threat, though even 40% versus ~12% would be significant with ~114 evaluable hookworm cases.
rationale: Benzimidazoles (albendazole 400 mg) cure roughly 70-80% of hookworm infections in one dose, while placebo cure by Kato-Katz at day 14 is around 10-15%, so a placebo-controlled test of a benzimidazole-class 600 mg chewable should show superiority with ~114 evaluable hookworm cases. Main uncertainties are the compound's identity and potency, and whether a small sponsor with one Brazilian site, still recruiting at launch, reports anything by June 2027.
evidence: Moser et al. 2017 BMJ (network meta-analysis of STH drugs)

assumptions.claim: Single-dose albendazole 400 mg cures roughly 70-80% of hookworm infections.
assumptions.source: Keiser & Utzinger 2008, JAMA; Moser et al. 2017, BMJ

reason: With 40 patients per arm, a 12-month Barthel Index difference needs about 11 points to reach significance and the mRS co-primary must also be met; placebo-controlled IV cell-therapy stroke trials (MASTERS, TREASURE) have not shown efficacy.
rationale: Large placebo-controlled cell-therapy stroke trials (MASTERS, TREASURE) were negative; positive signals come mostly from small single-centre studies. Here 80 patients, two co-primaries (Barthel Index and mRS) and large natural recovery in both arms make significance on both unlikely, though sponsor-run single-centre trials sometimes report favourable results, and an early report would more likely be positive. Reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely: still recruiting at launch with 12-month follow-up.
evidence: MASTERS, Hess et al. 2017 Lancet Neurol
Law et al. 2021 Stem Cell Res Ther (Malaysian MSC stroke trial)

assumptions.claim: The MASTERS phase 2 trial of IV MultiStem cells in acute ischemic stroke did not improve 90-day outcomes versus placebo.
The TREASURE trial of MultiStem in Japanese ischemic stroke patients did not meet its primary endpoint.

reason: Crizotinib could do better than expected by BICR, or too few PFS events could accrue in a 190-patient trial with long PFS, but repotrectinib's 35.7-month TKI-naive PFS leaves a wide margin.
rationale: Repotrectinib's TRIDENT-1 TKI-naive cohort had ORR 79% and median PFS 35.7 months, versus crizotinib's 15.9-19.3 months in PROFILE 1001 and OO-1201, plus better CNS activity. An HR around 0.5 with ~100 events gives high power. Risks: open-label design, event-driven timing slipping, and smaller-than-expected separation. Reporting by June 2027 depends on events maturing on time; BMS may disclose via earnings or a congress.
evidence: PROFILE 1001, Shaw et al. 2019 Ann Oncol

assumptions.claim: In TRIDENT-1, TKI-naive ROS1-positive NSCLC patients on repotrectinib had median PFS of 35.7 months and ORR 79%.
Crizotinib gave median PFS of 19.3 months in ROS1-positive NSCLC in PROFILE 1001.
Crizotinib gave median PFS of 15.9 months by independent review in East Asian ROS1-positive NSCLC.

reason: Pembrolizumab-chemotherapy could outperform its modest historical PFS in HER2-mutant NSCLC and narrow the gap, though zongertinib's high first-line response rate makes failure unlikely.
rationale: Zongertinib produced ORR ~71% in pretreated and ~77% in untreated HER2 TKD-mutant NSCLC (Beamion LUNG-1) with low discontinuation, while chemo-immunotherapy in HER2-mutant disease gives median PFS around 6-8 months in retrospective series. Targeted TKIs have consistently beaten chemotherapy in oncogene-driven NSCLC, and immunotherapy adds little in such tumours. An expected HR ~0.5 with ~230 events gives high power; the main uncertainty is timing of the event-driven readout.
evidence: Beamion LUNG-1, Heymach et al. 2025 NEJM
Saalfeld et al. 2021 J Thorac Oncol

assumptions.claim: Zongertinib achieved an objective response rate of about 71% in previously treated HER2 TKD-mutant NSCLC.
assumptions.source: Beamion LUNG-1, Heymach et al. 2025, NEJM

assumptions.claim: Immune checkpoint inhibitors with chemotherapy give short PFS in ERBB2-mutant NSCLC in retrospective cohorts.
assumptions.source: Saalfeld et al. 2021, J Thorac Oncol

assumptions.claim: In KEYNOTE-189, 27.7% of the pembrolizumab-chemotherapy arm discontinued any treatment component for adverse events.

reason: LAG-3 blockade has added little in NSCLC so far, and a ~195-patient phase 2 needs roughly a 10-12 point pCR gain over a ~20% chemo-immunotherapy control to reach significance.
rationale: Neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy gives pCR around 17-25% (CheckMate 816, KEYNOTE-671, AEGEAN). LAG-3 blockade is validated only in melanoma (relatlimab), and nivolumab plus relatlimab in NEOpredict-Lung gave modest pathological gains. Adding fianlimab may raise pCR by ~5 points; with ~97 per arm, a 10+ point gain is needed. A phase 2 may use a looser one-sided alpha, which raises the chance slightly.

assumptions.claim: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus chemotherapy produced a pCR rate of 24.0% in resectable NSCLC.
Perioperative pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy produced a pCR rate of 18.1% in resectable NSCLC.

reason: Pfizer's long-term extension is fully enrolled with a fixed 52-week treatment, so it should complete close to its March 2027 date; results posting before August 2027 is unlikely.
rationale: Active, not recruiting; primary completion is fixed by the last rollover participant's 52 weeks plus 30 days of follow-up. Pfizer keeps the registry current and usually posts results near the one-year deadline, after the read date. Stopping is unlikely while ritlecitinib's vitiligo programme continues, and the safety-only primary outcomes are stable.

reason: M108's benefit could be smaller than zolbetuximab's if the CLDN18.2 cutoff is broad and low expressers are enrolled, diluting the PFS hazard ratio.
rationale: Claudin 18.2 targeting with an antibody plus chemotherapy is validated: zolbetuximab improved PFS in SPOTLIGHT (HR 0.75) and GLOW (HR 0.69 with CAPOX). M108 is an Fc-enhanced anti-CLDN18.2 antibody tested in a 486-patient Chinese trial with IRC-assessed PFS, giving good power for HR ~0.7. Risks are a broader biomarker cutoff, chemotherapy-limiting nausea and vomiting, and a single-country sponsor. Still recruiting at launch, so results by mid-2027 are unlikely; an early disclosure would most likely follow a positive interim.
evidence: GLOW, Shah et al. 2023 Nat Med

assumptions.claim: Zolbetuximab plus CAPOX improved PFS versus placebo plus CAPOX with HR 0.687, control median PFS 6.8 months.
assumptions.source: GLOW, Shah et al. 2023, Nature Medicine

assumptions.claim: Zolbetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 improved PFS with HR 0.75 versus placebo plus mFOLFOX6.

reason: LAG-3 blockade adds only a modest increment over PD-1 alone (RELATIVITY-047 HR 0.75), and with about 75 patients per arm a pCR gain under ~18 points is unlikely to reach two-sided significance.
rationale: Neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 monotherapy gives pCR around 20-30%; nivolumab+relatlimab single-arm gave 57% pCR, suggesting LAG-3 combos may roughly double pCR, but that was a small single-centre study and randomized LAG-3 data in metastatic disease show only modest added benefit. With 76 vs 75 patients, power is about 50% for a 15-point and about 80% for a 23-point difference. Uncertainty about fianlimab's added activity (phase 3 metastatic data mixed/unclear) keeps the estimate below 50%.
evidence: Amaria et al., Nature 2022 (neoadjuvant nivolumab+relatlimab, NCT02519322)
Amaria et al., Nat Med 2018 (neoadjuvant nivolumab vs nivo+ipi)
SWOG S1801, Patel et al., NEJM 2023

assumptions.claim: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus relatlimab produced a pathologic complete response rate of 57% in resectable stage III/oligometastatic melanoma.
Neoadjuvant nivolumab monotherapy produced a pCR rate of about 25% in high-risk resectable melanoma.
Adding relatlimab to nivolumab in untreated metastatic melanoma gave a PFS hazard ratio of about 0.75.

reason: Multi-target VEGFR/AXL TKIs in ESCC have improved PFS against placebo but have not shown convincing OS gains, and beating active chemotherapy on OS in heavily pretreated patients with post-progression crossover to other agents is a high bar.
rationale: Third-line chemotherapy in ESCC after PD-1 failure yields median OS around 6 months, so the bar is low, and KC1036 showed ORR near 30% in single-arm phase 2. But angiogenic TKIs in ESCC (anlotinib, apatinib) improved PFS without clear OS benefit, open-label OS endpoints are diluted by subsequent therapy, and a ~0.75 HR is needed for 490 patients. Still recruiting in late 2026, so an early public readout would most likely be a positive interim.
evidence: ESCORT, Huang et al., Lancet Oncol 2020
ATTRACTION-3, Kato et al., Lancet Oncol 2019

assumptions.claim: Investigator's-choice docetaxel or irinotecan in second-line ESCC gave a median overall survival of about 6.2 months.
assumptions.source: ESCORT, Huang et al., Lancet Oncol 2020

assumptions.claim: Anlotinib versus placebo in previously treated ESCC improved PFS but did not significantly improve OS.

reason: Small biotech phase 2a with sequential dose cohorts at a single site, started July 2026 and aiming to finish 90 participants by December 2026; slippage and an unrefreshed record are both likely, and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.
rationale: Operations only: an ambitious six-month timeline for three sequential dose cohorts with demanding vaginal-cytology screening at one site suggests the primary completion date will be pushed out if the record is updated; a small sponsor rarely posts results quickly; outcomes are standard safety/PK and unlikely to change.

reason: With 32 vs 16 patients, only a difference of roughly 35 points or more would reach significance, and placebo arms in anal HSIL can show sizeable regression (biopsy removal of small lesions, spontaneous clearance, and partial responses counted).
rationale: Topical artesunate showed histologic regression in about two-thirds of CIN2/3 patients in a phase 1 cervical study, and early anal studies were encouraging, but these were uncontrolled. Placebo partial-plus-complete response in anal HSIL over 18 weeks may be 15-30%. With 48 patients randomized 2:1, power is modest unless the true difference exceeds about 35 points. The trial has been recruiting slowly since 2024, so a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Trimble et al., Clin Cancer Res 2020 (vaginal artesunate in CIN2/3)

assumptions.claim: Vaginal artesunate inserts produced histologic regression of CIN2/3 in about two-thirds of treated women in a phase 1 study.
assumptions.source: Trimble et al., Clin Cancer Res 2020

reason: Anti-CLDN18.2 antibodies have only been proven on top of chemotherapy alone; their incremental PFS benefit on a PD-1 plus chemotherapy backbone is untested, and a broader CLDN18.2 cutoff could dilute the effect.
rationale: Zolbetuximab added to chemotherapy gave PFS HRs of 0.69-0.75 in SPOTLIGHT and GLOW, and ASKB589 with CAPOX+PD-1 showed high response rates in phase 1/2. With 780 patients and roughly 480 PFS events, the trial has high power for HR 0.75. Main uncertainty is whether the effect persists on a PD-1 backbone and with a possibly lower CLDN18.2 threshold. Enrolment is complete, and a Chinese listed sponsor would likely announce topline in 2027.
evidence: GLOW, Shah et al., Nat Med 2023

assumptions.claim: Zolbetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 improved PFS in CLDN18.2-positive HER2-negative gastric cancer with a hazard ratio of about 0.75.
Zolbetuximab plus CAPOX improved PFS with a hazard ratio of about 0.69.
assumptions.source: GLOW, Shah et al., Nat Med 2023

assumptions.claim: Tislelizumab plus chemotherapy in first-line gastric cancer gave a median PFS of about 7 months.

reason: With about 33 patients and a patient-reported symptom-resolution endpoint dominated by lingering fatigue, a significant hazard ratio would need a very large benefit over standard atovaquone plus azithromycin in low-risk patients.
rationale: Tafenoquine has anti-Babesia activity in case reports of relapsing disease, but this trial adds it to effective standard therapy in low-risk hospitalized patients, where most improve anyway and residual fatigue drives time to sustained resolution. Thirty-three patients give little power for a hazard ratio below about 2. Babesiosis enrolment is seasonal and has been slow, and the small sponsor has limited cash, so delays and a possible early stop are plausible.
evidence: IDSA babesiosis guideline, Krause et al., Clin Infect Dis 2021

assumptions.claim: The 2020 IDSA guideline recommends atovaquone plus azithromycin as first-line treatment for babesiosis.
assumptions.source: Krause et al., Clin Infect Dis 2021

reason: Large-sponsor long-term extension with enrolment closed and a completion date consistent with the parent studies' timeline; likely to finish near the registered date, with results posting probably near the 12-month deadline after the read date.
rationale: Operations only: rollovers from the two parent phase 3 studies ended by about early 2026, so 56 weeks of extension treatment ends around the registered December 2026 date; Incyte maintains its records, rarely stops a supportive LTE, and typically posts results near the one-year deadline (December 2027), after the August 2027 read date.

reason: Completed GSK vaccine study; GSK reliably submits results within about 12 months of primary completion (August 2026), so posting by end of August 2027 is likely, though QC review can push it past the read date.
rationale: Operations only: already completed, so termination is essentially impossible; GSK has a strong disclosure record and the 12-month window from August 2026 ends just before the read date, leaving some risk of QC lag; outcome measures sometimes change when results are entered for a study with 44 cohort-specific primary outcomes.

reason: Both co-primaries must be met; the antihypertensive component should clearly beat placebo on SBP, so the residual risk is mainly the HbA1c comparison or a high placebo/regression effect in a 12-week office-BP trial.
rationale: This is a factorial fixed-dose combination trial: each co-primary tests an approved-class drug against its matched placebo on its own target (an ARB-type agent on systolic BP, an antidiabetic on HbA1c). Standard-dose antihypertensives lower office SBP about 9-12 mmHg more than placebo, and oral antidiabetics lower HbA1c about 0.5-0.8%, both well detectable with about 92 per arm. Korean FDC phase 3 trials of this kind almost always succeed; the main uncertainty is whether results become public quickly.
evidence: Law, Morris and Wald, BMJ 2009 (BP-lowering drug meta-analysis)
Ferrannini et al., Diabetes Care 2010 (dapagliflozin monotherapy)

assumptions.claim: A standard dose of one antihypertensive drug lowers systolic blood pressure by about 9 mmHg more than placebo on average.
assumptions.source: Law MR, Morris JK, Wald NJ, BMJ 2009

assumptions.claim: SGLT2 inhibitor monotherapy lowers HbA1c by about 0.5-0.6% more than placebo at 24 weeks.

reason: The phase II part has about 30 patients per arm and may be analysed descriptively; even a 25-point ORR gain is borderline significant at that size, and the record also lists phase III PFS and OS as primary outcomes that cannot be met by mid-2027.
rationale: Disitamab vedotin plus PD-1 blockade has given ORRs around 40-50% in HER2-expressing gastric cancer, against roughly 15-20% for second-line paclitaxel, so a sizeable ORR gain is likely. But only about 30 patients per arm, inclusion of HER2 IHC 1+ disease, prior PD-1 exposure, and a phase II that may be reported without a formal test reduce the chance of a declared significant primary result. Phase III primaries cannot read out by mid-2027.
evidence: RAINBOW, Wilke et al., Lancet Oncol 2014

assumptions.claim: Second-line paclitaxel alone gave an objective response rate of about 16% in the RAINBOW trial.
assumptions.source: RAINBOW, Wilke et al., Lancet Oncol 2014

assumptions.claim: Disitamab vedotin monotherapy gave an ORR of about 25% in HER2-overexpressing gastric cancer after two or more prior lines.

reason: Selective TYK2 inhibition has already failed in IBD (deucravacitinib LATTICE-CD and LATTICE-UC); zasocitinib's higher exposure may help, but week-12 endoscopic response with 67 per arm needs roughly a 20-point gain over placebo.
rationale: IL-23 blockade works in Crohn's (risankizumab, guselkumab, mirikizumab), and zasocitinib blocks IL-23/IL-12/IFN signalling with strong psoriasis efficacy, so a signal is plausible. But the TYK2 class failed in IBD with deucravacitinib, oral small molecules have less exposure in gut than IV biologics, and week-12 endoscopic response is a hard, early endpoint. Placebo endoscopic response in biologic-experienced CD runs about 10-15%. With 67 per arm, one of three doses must show about 18-20 points of separation. I put it a bit below even.

assumptions.claim: Placebo endoscopic response at week 12 was about 12% in the ADVANCE risankizumab induction trial.
Deucravacitinib did not meet its primary endpoints in moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease in phase 2.

reason: First-in-human inhaled CFTR mRNA study from a small private biotech, already active not recruiting; likely to finish near its date, but registry updates and results posting are slow.
rationale: Enrollment is closed and the registered primary completion (Nov 2026) is near, so a large slip past Feb 2027 is less likely than not, though Part 3 with ivacaftor and 24-week follow-up could push it. A small venture-backed sponsor could stop for funding reasons. Results posting is due only about Nov 2027, so posting by Aug 2027 is unlikely. Safety-only primary outcomes are rarely changed.

reason: Methotrexate acts slowly and modestly in atopic dermatitis; at week 16 its EASI-75 rate may be only 25-35%, so the margin over a 10-15% placebo rate is real but not large.
rationale: Methotrexate has consistent efficacy in AD from randomized comparisons with azathioprine and cyclosporine, with mean SCORAD reductions near 40% by 12-20 weeks. Placebo EASI-75 at week 16 in AD phase 3 trials without topical steroids runs 10-15%. A 15-20 point gap with about 138 per arm gives over 90% power. Risks are the slow onset by week 16, dropouts counted as non-responders, and modest SC dosing. The trial is still recruiting, so a public result before mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Schram et al. 2011 methotrexate vs azathioprine in AD (MAcAD)
Goujon et al. 2018 methotrexate vs cyclosporine in adult AD

assumptions.claim: Placebo EASI-75 response at week 16 was about 12-15% in the SOLO 1 and SOLO 2 trials of dupilumab monotherapy.
Methotrexate gave a mean SCORAD reduction of about 42% after 12 weeks in adults with severe AD.
assumptions.source: Schram et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2011

reason: With about 83 patients and maybe 55 PFS events, even a true hazard ratio near 0.6 has only moderate power, and TIL activity after prior immunotherapy may be lower than early single-arm data suggest.
rationale: Single-agent gemcitabine after prior systemic therapy in cervical cancer yields low response rates and median PFS near 2-3 months. TIL therapy (lifileucel) showed about 44% ORR in previously treated cervical cancer, and GT101 reported meaningful early activity. Measuring PFS from first study treatment rather than randomization further favours the TIL arm. The main risks are small size, manufacturing dropouts and lower TIL activity after checkpoint inhibitors. Still recruiting, so early publication is unlikely.
evidence: C-145-04 lifileucel in cervical cancer (Jazaeri, ASCO 2019)

assumptions.claim: Lifileucel produced an objective response rate of about 44% in previously treated recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer.
Investigator's-choice chemotherapy (including gemcitabine) had a median PFS of about 2.9 months in second-line cervical cancer.

reason: Symptom endpoints in Sjogren's carry a large placebo response over 48 weeks, and both ESSPRI and DASPRI must separate; the phase 2 symptom-population effect is likely to shrink in a 26-country phase 3.
rationale: Dazodalibep's phase 2 met its ESSPRI primary in the high-symptom, low-ESSDAI population with roughly a 1.2-point placebo-adjusted gain, a rare positive symptom result in Sjogren's. Patient-reported symptom endpoints have failed for many drugs, and phase 3 placebo responses over 48 weeks tend to be larger, so I expect the effect to shrink toward 0.4-0.5 points. With about 217 per arm and an SD near 2, that gives power around 60-70% for ESSPRI. DASPRI must also be met, which lowers the joint probability. Amgen should report topline in early 2027.
evidence: Dazodalibep phase 2 Sjogren's (St Clair et al., Nat Med 2024)

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial, dazodalibep met the ESSPRI primary endpoint in the population with high symptom burden and low systemic activity (ESSPRI >=5, ESSDAI <5).
assumptions.source: St Clair et al., Nature Medicine 2024 (NCT04129164)

reason: Opdualag already gives about 43-45% ORR; phase 1 fianlimab-cemiplimab response rates near 57-61% will likely shrink in phase 3, and with 280 per arm a gap under 8 points will not be significant.
rationale: Relatlimab-nivolumab had a BICR ORR of about 43% in RELATIVITY-047. Fianlimab plus cemiplimab reached about 57-61% ORR in first-line melanoma phase 1 cohorts, but expansion cohorts usually overstate phase 3 results. If the true ORR is about 50%, the expected gap of about 5 points is below the roughly 8 points needed with 280 per arm. Two LAG-3/PD-1 combinations are mechanistically very similar, so superiority is a hard bar. Still recruiting, so results by mid-2027 are unlikely.
evidence: Fianlimab + cemiplimab phase 1 first-line melanoma (Hamid, ESMO 2023)

assumptions.claim: Relatlimab plus nivolumab produced an objective response rate of about 43% by BICR in first-line advanced melanoma.
Fianlimab plus cemiplimab produced an objective response rate of about 57-61% in PD-1-naive advanced melanoma cohorts in phase 1.
