reason: A novel-mechanism oral antidepressant in a 4-week, 50-site US trial faces high placebo response; most phase 2 MDD programs fail, and silence months after completion hints at a weak result.
rationale: SP-624 is a first-in-class SIRT6 activator from a small private sponsor; the earlier phase 2 was not convincing overall. Phase 2 MDD trials with new mechanisms succeed perhaps a quarter of the time, and multi-site US trials have placebo MADRS drops near 9-11 points even at 4 weeks. The trial completed in July 2026 with no topline yet, which leans negative. With about 249 per arm and SD near 9, a true 2-point effect would be needed for good power.
evidence: GEMINI AXS-05 MDD trial (Iosifescu, J Clin Psychiatry 2022)

assumptions.claim: In the 6-week GEMINI trial of AXS-05 in MDD, the placebo arm improved by about 12 MADRS points.
assumptions.source: GEMINI, Iosifescu et al., J Clin Psychiatry 2022

reason: The trial most likely tests non-inferiority to dulaglutide, which an exendin-4 Fc fusion should pass; if superiority is the primary hypothesis, a weekly exenatide-based agent is unlikely to beat dulaglutide by a significant margin.
rationale: Chinese phase 3 trials of new GLP-1 agents against dulaglutide are usually designed for non-inferiority with a 0.3-0.4% margin, and exendin-4 based weekly agents generally match dulaglutide. Dulaglutide lowers HbA1c by about 1.5-1.9% at 26 weeks in Chinese metformin-treated patients with baseline near 8.3%. I give about 75% that the trial's own hypothesis is non-inferiority (about 90% met) and about 25% that it is superiority (about 35% met).
evidence: Ecnoglutide vs dulaglutide phase 3 in China (2024)

assumptions.claim: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg lowered HbA1c by about 1.5-1.9 percentage points at 26 weeks in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes on metformin.

reason: Large-sponsor pediatric phase 3 already closed to enrollment; primary completion at week 56 should land close to the registered February 2027 date, with results posting due only in 2028.
rationale: Enrollment is closed, so the week-56 primary completion follows from the last patient's start and Janssen tends to keep dates realistic; a slip beyond May 2027 is possible but not likely. Guselkumab is approved for adult UC and the drug's safety profile gives little reason to stop. Results posting is due 12 months after primary completion, so posting by Aug 2027 is unlikely. Pediatric primary endpoints are agreed with regulators and rarely change late.

reason: No anti-tau antibody has yet shown a robust, significant slowing of tau PET accumulation in a randomized trial; the MTBR epitope is better motivated than the N-terminus but BMS-986446 has no human efficacy data yet.
rationale: N-terminal anti-tau antibodies (semorinemab, gosuranemab, tilavonemab) did not slow tau PET accumulation. Mid-region bepranemab missed its clinical primary but reportedly slowed tau PET spread, which supports antibodies that bind the mid-domain/MTBR and block seeding. BMS-986446 (formerly PRX005) binds MTBR with high affinity. With about 155 per arm over 76 weeks, a 25-30% slowing of tau PET accumulation would likely be significant, but efficacy is unproven. Primary completion is March 2027, so most readouts fall after June 2027.

assumptions.claim: Semorinemab did not reduce tau PET accumulation versus placebo in prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease over 73 weeks.
assumptions.source: TAURIEL, Teng et al. JAMA Neurol 2022 (NCT03289143)

assumptions.claim: Gosuranemab did not slow clinical decline in early Alzheimer's disease in the phase 2 TANGO study.
Bepranemab missed its CDR-SB primary endpoint but slowed tau PET accumulation in the phase 2 TOGETHER study.

reason: 100 vs 50 patients give only ~60-70% power for a ~1-point NRS difference against a saline injection that itself produces a large placebo response in shoulder pain.
rationale: Extended-release triamcinolone beat saline by about 1 NRS point at week 12 in the knee OA phase 3, and intra-articular steroids relieve glenohumeral OA pain. With 100 vs 50 patients and an SD near 2.4, power for a 1-point difference is roughly 60-70%. Saline injections give large placebo responses, the endpoint is worst rather than average daily pain, and glenohumeral injection accuracy varies. A sponsor-run phase 3 built on a positive knee program puts success slightly above even.

assumptions.claim: In the knee OA phase 3, ZILRETTA reduced week-12 average daily pain versus saline by about 1 NRS point.
assumptions.source: Conaghan et al. J Bone Joint Surg Am 2018 (NCT02357459)

reason: With 30 open-label patients per arm and a binary wound-closure endpoint, only a ~30-point difference would reach p<0.05, and the record frames the aim as effect-size estimation rather than a hypothesis test.
rationale: This open-label trial has 30 per arm and a binary wound-closure endpoint. The record frames the aim as estimating effect size, so a significant superiority claim at 0.05 would need about a 30-point difference. Local antibiotic-loaded calcium sulfate may reduce residual osteomyelitis and flap breakdown, but standard flap closure already succeeds in most patients. Recruitment is still open, so a late readout and a small-company report with descriptive statistics are likely.

reason: Glycemic efficacy is near certain; the only realistic threat is high GI-driven discontinuation in an older renal-impaired population, which would shrink but not erase the HbA1c difference.
rationale: In the phase 2 T2D trial, retatrutide lowered HbA1c by about 2 points versus placebo at 36 weeks, and GLP-1-based agents keep their glycaemic effect in CKD. On background basal insulin, which may be titrated, placebo improves modestly. A 320-patient, 52-week trial is heavily powered. The only realistic threats are heavy dropout or poor tolerability in renal patients, which would not overturn significance. Lilly usually announces pivotal T2D readouts in earnings releases or at ADA.
evidence: Retatrutide phase 2 T2D, Rosenstock et al. Lancet 2023 (NCT04867785)

assumptions.claim: Retatrutide 12 mg reduced HbA1c by about 2.0 percentage points from baseline at 36 weeks in T2D, versus essentially no change with placebo.
In SURPASS-5, placebo added to titrated insulin glargine reduced HbA1c by about 0.9 points at 40 weeks.

reason: Still recruiting in late 2026 with a 24-week primary window, so the December 2026 primary completion cannot hold and the date will likely slip well into 2027 or later.
rationale: This small Chinese phase 2 of an oral HIF-PH inhibitor in beta-thalassemia is still recruiting as of October 2026. Every patient needs 24 weeks of follow-up, so completion in December 2026 is impossible and a slip past March 2027 is very likely if the record is updated. Termination is possible for a small sponsor but not the base case. Chinese sponsors rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov, and the safety primary outcome is unlikely to be redefined.

reason: Single-site Chinese phase 2 still recruiting in late 2026 with a 24-week response window, so the December 2026 primary completion will almost certainly slip.
rationale: This is an open-label, dose-ranging, single-site Chinese phase 2 of AND017 in lower-risk MDS anemia. It is still recruiting in October 2026 and response is assessed up to week 25, so primary completion must move past March 2027 if the record is updated. Termination is possible for a small sponsor. Posting results on ClinicalTrials.gov is unlikely for this sponsor type and timeframe, and the response definition looks settled.

reason: Phase 1/2 still recruiting in late 2026 with an ORR endpoint needing follow-up, so primary completion is likely to slip; small-biotech funding adds some termination risk.
rationale: This is a multi-stage phase 1/2 of the AKT1 antisense LNP WGI-0301 with sorafenib in second-line HCC. It is still recruiting in October 2026, includes a randomized expansion, and ORR needs repeated scans, so the December 2026 primary completion is very likely to move. Second-line sorafenib combinations face a moving standard of care, and the small Chinese sponsor adds some stop risk. Results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by mid-2027 is unlikely.

reason: Kv7 opening works in focal epilepsy, but BHV-7000 has no published efficacy data yet, failed in mood disorders, and 75 mg may sit low on its dose-response curve against a 20% placebo reduction.
rationale: Kv7.2/7.3 opening is clinically validated in focal epilepsy: ezogabine worked, and azetukalner's X-TOLE showed a 53% vs 18% median seizure reduction. BHV-7000 is a potent, more selective Kv7 activator, but it failed in bipolar mania and depression and has no public epilepsy efficacy data. The 75 mg dose may be modest. Placebo responses at multinational sites and an 8-week double-blind phase add risk. With 130 per arm, power for a 15-20 point median difference is good, and Biohaven announces topline quickly.
evidence: X-TOLE azetukalner (NCT03796962), French et al. JAMA Neurol 2023
Ezogabine RESTORE 1, French et al. Neurology 2011

assumptions.claim: Azetukalner 25 mg reduced median monthly focal seizure frequency by 52.8% versus 18.2% with placebo in the phase 2b X-TOLE trial.

reason: BI 764524 is an anti-semaphorin 3A antibody aimed at ischaemia, not an anti-VEGF agent, so a ≥2-step DRSS improvement over sham with about 35 eyes per arm is unlikely; earlier non-VEGF drugs in NPDR failed this endpoint.
rationale: Only anti-VEGF drugs have reliably produced ≥2-step DRSS improvement (PANORAMA: 65-80% vs 15% sham at week 52). Sema3A blockade targets reperfusion and permeability, and the HORNBILL phase 1/2 in ischaemic DR showed safety but no clear anatomical gain. Non-VEGF agents (APX3330 ZETA-1, oral and other mechanisms) have missed DRSS endpoints. With about 35 per arm, even a 15-20 point gain is borderline, though three regimens give some multiplicity benefit. The record still said recruiting in October 2026, so a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In PANORAMA, 15% of sham eyes with moderately severe to severe NPDR had a ≥2-step DRSS improvement at week 52, versus 65-80% with aflibercept.
assumptions.source: PANORAMA, Brown et al., JAMA Ophthalmol 2021

assumptions.claim: BI 764524 is a monoclonal antibody against semaphorin 3A, developed for diabetic retinopathy with macular ischaemia.

reason: With 24 patients per arm, two biopsy co-primaries (fibrosis improvement and NASH resolution) both have to reach significance, and HSD17B13 silencing has so far shown ALT and NAS trends rather than large histological effects.
rationale: VSA006 appears to be the Greater China version of Arrowhead's ARO-HSD (GSK4532990). Human genetics support HSD17B13, but the early data show ALT and NAS falls, little liver-fat change and no proven fibrosis benefit; GSK's larger phase 2b is still under way. Placebo fibrosis response in F2-F3 runs at 14-22%, so 24 per arm would need about a 35-point gain on both co-primary histology endpoints. A small single-site Chinese phase 2 may also report descriptively.

assumptions.claim: In MAESTRO-NASH, 14.2% of placebo patients had ≥1-stage fibrosis improvement with no NAS worsening at week 52.
ARO-HSD lowered hepatic HSD17B13 mRNA and ALT in patients with suspected NASH over 12 weeks.

reason: Anti-IL-5 biologics reliably halve severe exacerbations in eosinophilic asthma, so the main risk is a low placebo exacerbation rate in Chinese patients (often under 1 per year), which shrinks the event count and power.
rationale: 610 is an anti-IL-5 antibody from Sunshine Guojian (3SBio). Its class has a strong record: mepolizumab cut exacerbations about 50% in MENSA and DREAM, and benralizumab cut them about 70% in Asian patients (MIRACLE). A 480-patient, 52-week trial has ample power for a rate ratio near 0.5 even at a placebo rate of about 0.8/year. The remaining risks are execution (the record still says recruiting) and a low placebo event rate.

assumptions.claim: In MENSA, subcutaneous mepolizumab reduced clinically significant exacerbations by about 53% versus placebo.
In DREAM, mepolizumab reduced exacerbation rates by 39-52% across doses versus placebo.

reason: With 100 patients and maybe 20-25 dropouts in 24 weeks, a retention hazard ratio would need to be about 0.4 to reach significance, and the second primary (take-home doses) must also be met.
rationale: Sonara is a digital tool for video-observed take-home methadone. It will likely raise take-home doses, which is what it is built for, but retention is already moderate in usual take-home care, and about 50 per arm with few dropout events gives little power for a time-to-dropout difference. Under the round's rule both primaries must be met, which compounds the risk. An SBIR phase II at one site is unlikely to report before mid-2027.

reason: IL-4/IL-13 blockade has given only modest or inconsistent nasal-symptom benefit in allergic rhinitis (dupilumab did not cut TNSS after allergen challenge). With INCS background and the usual large placebo response, the TNSS difference may stay under the ~0.5 points needed.
rationale: Lebrikizumab blocks IL-13, a central allergic cytokine, and lowers IgE over time. In AR, though, type-2 biologics have shown modest effects: omalizumab lowers nasal scores by small margins, and dupilumab improved RQLQ in asthmatics with PAR but did not clearly lower TNSS in challenge studies. Placebo improvement in AR trials is large (2-3 of 12 points). With 225 per arm and SD about 2.7, a difference of about 0.5 points is needed, which is near my central estimate. Lilly went straight to phase 3, which signals some confidence.
evidence: Weinstein 2018 dupilumab asthma with PAR (JACI Pract)

assumptions.claim: Dupilumab improved rhinitis quality of life (RQLQ) in patients with uncontrolled asthma and comorbid perennial allergic rhinitis.
assumptions.source: Weinstein et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol Pract 2018

assumptions.claim: In ADvocate1/2, lebrikizumab discontinuation for adverse events was low (a few percent) and similar to placebo.

reason: The record is a placeholder (start and primary completion both 2026-12) for a 40-patient, 6-month safety study, so any updated record will show a later completion. A small sponsor raises the risk of withdrawal.
rationale: Start and primary completion are both listed as December 2026, but patients take drug for 6 months and the primary safety window is 12 months, so a realistic primary completion falls in 2027-2028, well past March 2027. Sound Pharmaceuticals is small, and the trial depends on Med-El implant scheduling, so withdrawal or suspension is a real possibility. No results can be posted by August 2027. The primary outcome is safety-only and might be revised when the record is updated.

reason: Adding a VEGFR2 antibody to paclitaxel reliably improves PFS (RAINBOW HR 0.64). The risk is the OS dual primary: OS benefit after PD-1 failure is uncertain (RAINBOW-Asia OS null) and may be immature or not met when PFS is reported.
rationale: Pulocimab (AK109) is an anti-VEGFR2 antibody like ramucirumab, which with paclitaxel gave a PFS HR of 0.64 in RAINBOW and 0.77 in RAINBOW-Asia against a paclitaxel mPFS of about 3 months. Cadonilimab may add some benefit after PD-1 failure. PFS by BICR is very likely met. OS is also primary: RAINBOW-Asia showed no OS gain, and OS may be immature at the PFS readout, so a strict co-primary reading lowers the estimate. Akeso announces positive toplines quickly.

assumptions.claim: In RAINBOW, ramucirumab plus paclitaxel improved PFS (HR 0.635; median 4.4 vs 2.9 months) and OS (HR 0.807) over paclitaxel alone.
In RAINBOW-Asia, ramucirumab plus paclitaxel improved PFS (HR 0.765; paclitaxel median about 3.2 months) without a significant OS benefit.
assumptions.source: Xu et al., Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2021 (RAINBOW-Asia)

reason: Anti-TIGIT add-ons have failed in phase 3 across tumours. With 39 patients per arm and both ORR and PFS as primaries, a significant gain over PD-1 plus bevacizumab is unlikely, and the phase 2 may report descriptively.
rationale: PD-1 plus bevacizumab gives an ORR of about 25-30% by RECIST in first-line HCC (IMbrave150, ORIENT-32). MORPHEUS-Liver suggested a higher ORR when tiragolumab was added, but the class then failed repeatedly in phase 3 and Roche stopped tiragolumab. A 3-arm phase 2 with 39 per arm needs an ORR gain of about 25 points and a PFS gain on top under the co-primary rule. The trial is still recruiting, so a readout before mid-2027 is unlikely, and deprioritisation is possible.

assumptions.claim: In IMbrave150, atezolizumab plus bevacizumab gave an ORR of about 27-30% by RECIST 1.1 on independent review.
Tiragolumab plus atezolizumab failed to improve PFS/OS over atezolizumab in PD-L1-high NSCLC in SKYSCRAPER-01.

reason: No tau-directed therapy has slowed PSP clinically, OGA inhibition lacks human efficacy evidence, and a significant PSPRS difference over 52 weeks needs a 20-30% slowing against a placebo decline of about 10 points with SD near 7.5.
rationale: FNP-223 (ASN120290) is an O-GlcNAcase inhibitor meant to reduce tau aggregation. Every PSP disease-modification trial so far (davunetide, tideglusib, gosuranemab, tilavonemab, salsalate) failed on PSPRS, and the OGA inhibitor ceperognastat did not succeed in Alzheimer's disease. Placebo decline in early PSP-RS is about 9-11 PSPRS points per year with SD around 7-8, so 120 per arm detects only a 20-30% slowing. With no human efficacy signal, the prior for a first-in-class PSP disease modifier is low.

assumptions.claim: Placebo PSPRS worsened by about 10 points over 52 weeks in the gosuranemab PASSPORT trial.
assumptions.source: Dam et al., Nat Med 2021; NCT03068468

assumptions.claim: Tilavonemab did not slow PSPRS progression versus placebo over 52 weeks in PSP.
assumptions.source: Hoglinger et al., Lancet Neurol 2021; NCT02985879

reason: Unselected TROP2 ADC monotherapy has modest activity in gastric cancer (ORR near 20%), and topoisomerase-I payload cross-resistance after prior irinotecan may blunt the OS gain over physician's-choice chemotherapy.
rationale: Sac-TMT showed about 20% ORR in heavily pretreated gastric cancer in early Kelun studies. TROP2 ADCs have mixed OS records: Dato-DXd and sacituzumab govitecan failed OS against docetaxel in NSCLC, while sac-TMT won several Chinese phase 3s. Third-line TPC gives median OS of only 5-6 months, leaving room for benefit, and about 380 events give good power for HR near 0.78. No TROP2 selection and payload cross-resistance temper the odds, so I put success near a coin flip.

assumptions.claim: Trifluridine-tipiracil gave median OS of 5.7 months in third-line or later gastric cancer.
assumptions.source: TAGS, Shitara et al., Lancet Oncol 2018

assumptions.claim: Physician's-choice paclitaxel or irinotecan gave median OS of about 5 months in third-line gastric cancer.
assumptions.source: JAVELIN Gastric 300, Bang et al., Ann Oncol 2018

assumptions.claim: Datopotamab deruxtecan did not significantly improve OS over docetaxel in pretreated NSCLC.
assumptions.source: TROPION-Lung01, Ahn et al., J Clin Oncol 2025

reason: Placebo responses on a symptom-relief endpoint in acute HAE attacks can be high and 62 per arm leaves limited margin; operationally the trial is still recruiting, so an early public outcome is disproportionately likely to be a stop or delay rather than efficacy results.
rationale: Plasma-derived C1-INH is a proven acute HAE therapy: Berinert (IMPACT1) and Cinryze (CHANGE) beat placebo on time to relief, and OCTA-C1-INH at standard doses should behave similarly, so if completed the chance of success is about 85%. But the trial was still recruiting in late 2026 against a December 2026 primary completion, with a paediatric phase to follow. Any public outcome by mid-2027 has a material chance of being a termination rather than efficacy data, which pulls the conditional p_met down, most at the March deadline.
evidence: IMPACT1 Berinert (Craig, J Allergy Clin Immunol 2009)
CHANGE nanofiltered C1-INH acute trial (Zuraw, NEJM 2010)
Recombinant human C1-INH RCT (Riedl, Ann Allergy Asthma Immunol 2014)

assumptions.claim: In IMPACT1, 20 U/kg C1-INH shortened median time to onset of symptom relief to 0.5 h versus 1.5 h on placebo.
assumptions.source: Craig et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2009

assumptions.claim: In the acute nanofiltered C1-INH trial, median time to unequivocal relief was 2 h versus more than 4 h with placebo.

reason: Enrollment is closed and the primary window is 18 weeks, so a February 2027 primary completion looks achievable; AbbVie usually posts results close to the 12-month deadline, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely, and termination is improbable for an approved drug's mitigation study.
rationale: Randomized safety study of steroid versus vasoconstrictor eye-drop prophylaxis during mirvetuximab treatment. Status is active, not recruiting with 108 enrolled and an 18-week primary window, so the registered February 2027 primary completion is plausible. AbbVie maintains records consistently and has no commercial reason to stop. Results are due by about February 2028, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. The primary safety count is simple and unlikely to be changed.

reason: TROP2 ADCs failed to beat docetaxel on OS in post-immunotherapy NSCLC (Dato-DXd, sacituzumab govitecan), so higher response rates with an EGFRxHER3 ADC may not translate into survival, and heavy hematologic toxicity can erode the benefit.
rationale: Iza-bren (BL-B01D1) showed objective responses in roughly a third or more of EGFR wild-type NSCLC in phase 1, and Baili's other Chinese phase 3s have read out positively at interim analyses. Docetaxel OS in Chinese post-immunotherapy patients is about 9-10 months, and 698 patients give ample power for HR near 0.78. Against that, TROPION-Lung01 and EVOKE-01 failed OS versus docetaxel. Chinese sponsor disclosure skews toward positive results, nudging the conditional p_met up.
evidence: BL-B01D1 first-in-human phase 1 (Ma et al., Lancet Oncol 2024)

assumptions.claim: Docetaxel median OS was 10-12 months after prior immunotherapy and platinum in EVOKE-01 and TROPION-Lung01.
assumptions.source: Paz-Ares et al., J Clin Oncol 2024; Ahn et al., J Clin Oncol 2025

assumptions.claim: BL-B01D1 produced objective responses in about a third or more of EGFR wild-type NSCLC patients in its first-in-human study.

reason: An open-label phase 2 with about 120 patients randomized 2:1 and roughly 65 deaths expected cannot reliably show a significant OS hazard ratio unless the true effect is near 0.6, and CD70 blockade has no randomized proof in AML.
rationale: Venetoclax plus azacitidine gives median OS of about 14.7 months (VIALE-A), and add-on agents such as magrolimab (ENHANCE-3) failed to improve OS. Cusatuzumab's CD70 blockade showed encouraging early remissions with azacitidine but has no randomized evidence. With about 65 events and 2:1 allocation, power for a true HR of 0.75 is roughly 25%. Results will likely come at EHA or ASH 2027. I put success near 15%.
evidence: Cusatuzumab with azacitidine phase 1/2 (Riether et al., Nat Med 2020)

assumptions.claim: Venetoclax plus azacitidine gave median OS of 14.7 months and a CR rate of 36.7% in VIALE-A.
Adding magrolimab to venetoclax-azacitidine did not improve OS in unfit AML.

reason: Gene-agnostic NR2E3 modifier gene therapy rests on uncontrolled phase 1/2 data, and pooling RHO with other genotypes dilutes any effect on a noisy maze test, although unmasked patients and untreated controls bias toward a positive read.
rationale: OCU400 delivers NR2E3 to reset photoreceptor gene networks across RP genotypes. The phase 1/2 claimed LDNA gains in treated versus untreated eyes but was small and not rigorously controlled. The phase 3 uses assessor-blinded LDNA against untreated controls (2:1), pooled across RHO and gene-agnostic cohorts, which dilutes a genotype-specific effect. Patients know their assignment, which can inflate maze performance, and Ocugen frames results favourably. I estimate about 38%.
evidence: Voretigene neparvovec phase 3 (Russell et al., Lancet 2017)

assumptions.claim: The OCU400 phase 1/2 trial was a small open-label dose-escalation study without randomized controls.
Voretigene neparvovec met a multi-luminance mobility test primary endpoint against untreated controls.

reason: A 130-patient open-label phase 2 framed around preliminary efficacy is unlikely to be powered to show a significant ORR gain over ruxolitinib, which already produces high response rates in newly diagnosed chronic GVHD.
rationale: Axatilimab (anti-CSF-1R) gave 74% ORR in refractory chronic GVHD (AGAVE-201) and ruxolitinib about 50% at week 24 in REACH3. In newly diagnosed disease both work, and adding axatilimab may add 5-10 points of ORR at 6 months; with 65 per arm the SE of the difference is about 8 points. The stated aim of preliminary efficacy and assessing axatilimab's contribution suggests a descriptive analysis, which lowers the chance of a formally met primary.

assumptions.claim: Axatilimab 0.3 mg/kg gave a 74% response rate within the first six months in refractory chronic GVHD.
Ruxolitinib gave a 49.7% overall response rate at week 24 in steroid-refractory chronic GVHD.

reason: Dupilumab inadequate responders may be more refractory to upadacitinib than biologic-naive patients, shrinking the week-8 EASI 90 gain; still, continued dupilumab in failing patients should give very low EASI 90, so failure needs an unexpectedly weak JAK response.
rationale: Patients enter with EASI >=12 despite at least 4 months of dupilumab, so continuing dupilumab should yield few new EASI 90 responses by week 8 (about 5%). Upadacitinib is fast and potent (Heads Up, Measure Up), and response-based escalation to 30 mg after week 2 maximises week-8 response; even a refractory population should reach 30-40% EASI 90. With about 92 per arm, a 20+ point gap is easily significant. Open-label design with blinded assessor adds little bias risk. AbbVie usually press-releases head-to-head data, so publication in H1 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: Upadacitinib 30 mg reached EASI 90 at week 16 in about 61% vs 39% for dupilumab.
assumptions.source: Heads Up, Blauvelt et al. JAMA Dermatol 2021

assumptions.claim: Upadacitinib 15 mg reached EASI 90 at week 16 in roughly 42-53% of patients in the monotherapy phase 3 trials.
assumptions.source: Measure Up 1/2, Guttman-Yassky et al. Lancet 2021

reason: Dose-optimisation phase 2 now owned by AstraZeneca, fully enrolled; the primary completion date should hold or be confirmed as actual, with results posting due only about a year after primary completion.
rationale: Status is active, not recruiting with primary completion December 2026, so the date is plausible, but one primary outcome runs through long-term follow-up and AstraZeneca may reset the data-cut date, giving a moderate lateness risk. Termination is unlikely while the actinium programme is being advanced. ClinicalTrials.gov results are due about December 2027, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. Amendment risk is modest given multi-part design changes.

reason: A gamma-secretase modulator lowers new Abeta42 production but does not actively clear plaque; over 72 weeks the separation from slowly accumulating placebo may be only a few Centiloids, which may not reach significance or may be reported only descriptively.
rationale: RO7269162 is an oral gamma-secretase modulator that cut CSF Abeta42 in phase 1. BACE inhibitors with large production cuts (verubecestat, lanabecestat) produced small but significant amyloid PET reductions over 1.5-2 years, so a modest decline relative to placebo (+2 to +4 CL) is plausible. With about 128 per arm and an SD near 12 CL, a 5 CL effect would be significant, but the effect size of a modulator is uncertain and a phase 2a may report descriptively. Roche typically discloses at AAIC/CTAD, mostly after June 2027.

assumptions.claim: Placebo amyloid PET rose about 3.6 Centiloids over 18 months in early AD.
assumptions.source: Clarity AD, van Dyck et al. NEJM 2023

assumptions.claim: Verubecestat reduced amyloid PET relative to placebo in prodromal AD despite no clinical benefit.

reason: Neuroprotectants have almost uniformly failed to improve 90-day mRS on top of reperfusion; nerinetide failed overall in ESCAPE-NA1 and ESCAPE-NEXT, so a modest or null shift is the most likely outcome.
rationale: NoNO-42 is a next-generation PSD-95-targeted neuroprotectant given with thrombolysis, presumably designed to avoid the plasmin degradation that blunted nerinetide with alteplase. Still, the neuroprotection field has a long record of null phase 2/3 trials, and an ordinal shift benefit of the size detectable with 600 patients is uncertain. Still recruiting at 9 Canadian sites with primary completion listed as December 2026, so a 2027 H1 readout is unlikely unless an adaptive interim stops early.

assumptions.claim: Nerinetide did not improve 90-day mRS overall; benefit appeared only in patients not given alteplase.
Nerinetide in thrombectomy patients without thrombolysis was neutral on 90-day mRS.

reason: Placebo response in binge eating disorder is large (binge frequency often halves on placebo), compressing the drug-placebo difference; solriamfetol's DNRI/TAAR1 effect on binge eating is untested in a large trial.
rationale: Stimulant-like catecholaminergic drugs work in BED: lisdexamfetamine beat placebo by about 1.3 binge days/week, and dasotraline had one positive phase 3. Solriamfetol is a DNRI with TAAR1 activity and two doses give two chances, but Axsome's solriamfetol programme is mixed (ADHD positive at one dose, MDD failed) and BED placebo responses are high. Still recruiting in October 2026 against a December 2026 completion suggests a slip; Axsome press-releases toplines promptly, so mid-2027 disclosure is roughly even odds.

assumptions.claim: In lisdexamfetamine phase 3 BED trials, binge-eating days per week fell by about 3.9 on drug versus 2.5 on placebo at week 12.

reason: With 45 children and about 30 events, only a hazard ratio near 0.5 would be significant at two-sided 0.05; CDK4/6 inhibition has no randomized evidence of benefit in paediatric high-grade glioma.
rationale: Paediatric high-grade glioma after radiotherapy progresses fast on temozolomide maintenance (median EFS roughly 6 months from post-RT randomisation). Adding agents has repeatedly failed (HERBY bevacizumab). Abemaciclib has CNS penetration and some rationale in CDK pathway-altered tumours, but the trial is a small randomized estimation study, likely run for a paediatric investigation plan, so formal significance is improbable. Lilly rarely publicises such results quickly; ClinicalTrials.gov posting around early 2028 is more likely.

assumptions.claim: Adding bevacizumab to RT/temozolomide in paediatric HGG did not improve EFS (HR about 0.86, not significant).
assumptions.source: HERBY, Grill et al. J Clin Oncol 2018

reason: About 21 patients per arm over 21 days give little power for a QMG difference of about 2 points with an SD near 3.5; symptomatic benefit seen after single doses may attenuate or be dose-limited by tolerability.
rationale: NMD670 is a ClC-1 chloride channel inhibitor that enhances neuromuscular transmission; single doses improved QMG in a phase 1/2a crossover in MG. A 21-day symptomatic effect of about 2 QMG points is plausible, but with only about 21 patients per arm and placebo improvement of about 1 point, significance at the highest dose is close to a coin flip; dose-response testing across three doses helps somewhat. Still recruiting in October 2026, so topline likely mid-2027; NMD Pharma would press-release it.

assumptions.claim: Single oral doses of NMD670 improved QMG total score versus placebo in AChR+ MG patients in a phase 1/2a crossover study.

reason: Platinum-pemetrexed is a reasonable post-osimertinib comparator (median PFS about 4-5.5 months); failure would require Dato-DXd plus osimertinib to give much less than the ORR and PFS seen in TROPION-Lung05 and ORCHARD, or ILD-related dropouts.
rationale: After osimertinib, platinum-pemetrexed gives BICR median PFS of about 4.2-5.4 months (MARIPOSA-2, HERTHENA-Lung02). TROP2 ADCs are active in EGFR-mutant NSCLC: Dato-DXd ORR about 44% in TROPION-Lung05, and sac-TMT beat platinum chemotherapy with HR 0.49 in OptiTROP-Lung04. Adding continued osimertinib should help CNS control. With about 512 patients in this comparison and a large expected effect, power is high. AstraZeneca press-releases toplines; readout around Q1-Q2 2027.

assumptions.claim: Platinum-pemetrexed after osimertinib gave a BICR median PFS of 4.2 months in MARIPOSA-2.
assumptions.source: MARIPOSA-2, Passaro et al. Ann Oncol 2024

assumptions.claim: Sacituzumab tirumotecan improved PFS versus platinum chemotherapy after EGFR-TKI failure with HR about 0.49.
Dato-DXd achieved an ORR of about 44% in pretreated EGFR-mutant NSCLC.
assumptions.source: TROPION-Lung05, Ahn et al. J Clin Oncol 2025

reason: Only 19 patients across two parts; raising hepcidin cuts iron absorption but also traps iron in tissue, so LIC may fall only slowly over 24 weeks and the difference is unlikely to reach significance.
rationale: REGN7999 blocks TMPRSS6 to raise hepcidin and limit intestinal iron absorption, the main driver of iron overload in NTDT. Without chelation, LIC changes slowly (placebo +0.4 mg/g over a year in THALASSA), and hepcidin also restricts hepatic iron export, so 24-week LIC falls may be small. Enrolment of only 19 suggests the trial was curtailed, leaving very little power. Regeneron rarely publicises small phase 2 results quickly; ClinicalTrials.gov posting around December 2027 is the likeliest disclosure.

assumptions.claim: In NTDT patients on placebo, LIC rose by about 0.38 mg Fe/g dw over 52 weeks.

reason: Pharmacokinetic variability in patients (target-mediated clearance, anti-drug antibodies, weight differences) with about 80 per arm could push a 90% CI for one of the two AUC ratios outside the margin, even if the products are similar.
rationale: Amgen has a long record of successful biosimilar PK-similarity studies, and pembrolizumab has predictable linear PK at 200 mg Q3W. Testing in adjuvant NSCLC patients adds variability, and two co-primary AUC endpoints must both pass, but with 163 patients a 90% CI around a ratio near 1.0 should sit inside 80-125%. Amgen tends not to press-release biosimilar PK results, so disclosure by mid-2027 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks after resection and platinum chemotherapy is an approved Keytruda regimen in stage IB-IIIA NSCLC.
assumptions.source: KEYNOTE-091, O'Brien et al. Lancet Oncol 2022

reason: B013's mechanism is not disclosed; unless it is an anti-angiogenic agent (which reliably extends PFS with weekly paclitaxel in platinum-resistant disease), a 90-patient trial needs an HR near 0.62 to reach significance, which most add-ons to paclitaxel do not deliver.
rationale: Weekly paclitaxel alone gives median PFS near 3.5-4 months in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Bevacizumab added to paclitaxel roughly halved the hazard in AURELIA, so an anti-angiogenic B013 could succeed; the ascites-drainage and cardiovascular exclusions hint at that class but do not confirm it. With about 65 events, significance needs HR below about 0.62. Mechanism uncertainty puts p_met near 0.4. The trial was still recruiting two months before its registered primary completion, so an early readout is unlikely.
evidence: APPROVE 2021 (apatinib + PLD in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer)

assumptions.claim: In AURELIA, chemotherapy alone gave median PFS of 3.4 months and bevacizumab plus chemotherapy 6.7 months (HR about 0.48) in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.
assumptions.source: Pujade-Lauraine et al., J Clin Oncol 2014 (AURELIA)

assumptions.claim: In the AURELIA weekly paclitaxel cohort, median PFS was about 3.9 months without bevacizumab and 10.4 months with it.
assumptions.source: Poveda et al., J Clin Oncol 2015 (AURELIA cohort analysis)

reason: The China phase 3 had an unusually small placebo response (-0.9); a global placebo arm typically improves 2-2.5 MG-ADL points by week 24, shrinking the observed difference, though about 95 per arm still detects a gap near 1 point.
rationale: Telitacicept (BLyS/APRIL blockade) cut MG-ADL by 5.74 vs 0.91 points at week 24 in RemeGen's China phase 3 and is approved in China for gMG. Global gMG trials show placebo MG-ADL changes near -2 (MINT, RAISE), so I expect a difference of about -2.5. With 191 patients and SD near 3.6, the trial can detect a difference of about 1 point. Belimumab's failure in MG is the main reason for doubt, but APRIL co-blockade and the strong China data support p_met around 0.85. Topline likely Q2 2027.

assumptions.claim: In RemeGen's China phase 3 of telitacicept in gMG, MG-ADL fell by 5.74 points with telitacicept vs 0.91 with placebo at week 24.
assumptions.source: RemeGen telitacicept China phase 3 gMG results (2024-2025)

assumptions.claim: In MINT, placebo MG-ADL change in AChR-positive patients at week 26 was about -2.2 and the inebilizumab difference about -1.9.
assumptions.source: Nowak et al., Lancet Neurology 2025 (MINT, NCT04524273)

reason: Obefazimod's large ulcerative colitis effect may not carry over to Crohn's disease (as with S1P modulators), and placebo CDAI drops of about 80 points at week 12 leave room for only a modest separation at about 70 per arm.
rationale: Obefazimod, a miR-124 enhancer, was clearly positive in two UC phase 3 induction trials (ABTECT 1 and 2), with about 16-19 points placebo-adjusted remission. No Crohn's data exist yet, and UC-to-CD translation fails for some mechanisms (ozanimod). The card's primary is continuous CDAI change at week 12, which is more sensitive than remission, and any dose meeting it counts. Placebo CDAI change is about -80 with SD about 100, so a -35 difference is near the significance threshold. Abivax reports promptly; topline is likely in H1 2027.
evidence: Obefazimod phase 2b UC 2023 (Vermeire, Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol)

assumptions.claim: Obefazimod 50 mg once daily achieved placebo-adjusted clinical remission of about 16% (ABTECT-1) and about 19% (ABTECT-2) at week 8 in moderately to severely active UC.
assumptions.source: Abivax ABTECT induction topline press release, July 2025

assumptions.claim: Ozanimod, effective in UC (True North), failed its induction primary endpoints in Crohn's disease.
assumptions.source: YELLOWSTONE induction trials, Bristol Myers Squibb 2023-2024

reason: Platinum rechallenge plus continued ICI should beat docetaxel modestly regardless of the virus, but with about 95 BICR events the HR must fall below about 0.67, and Olvi-Vec has no randomized evidence of re-sensitizing NSCLC to chemotherapy.
rationale: Docetaxel after chemo-immunotherapy gives median PFS near 3.7-4.5 months (TROPION-Lung01, EVOKE-01, CONTACT-01). The experimental arm combines platinum rechallenge with continued ICI, which alone often outperforms docetaxel in patients who progressed on maintenance. Olvi-Vec's platinum re-sensitization evidence comes from single-arm ovarian data (VIRO-15). With 142 patients, the HR must reach about 0.67. Genelux is small and enrolment has been slow, so an early report would most likely be an interim or a stop.

assumptions.claim: Docetaxel gave median PFS of about 3.7 months in previously treated NSCLC in TROPION-Lung01.
assumptions.source: Ahn et al., J Clin Oncol 2025 (TROPION-Lung01, NCT04656652)

assumptions.claim: In VIRO-15, Olvi-Vec followed by platinum-based chemotherapy gave median PFS of about 11 months in platinum-resistant or refractory ovarian cancer (single arm).

reason: Compensated MASH cirrhosis often carries little residual liver fat, which compresses absolute PDFF reductions; even so a GLP-1/glucagon co-agonist should separate clearly from placebo with about 42 per arm.
rationale: Efinopegdutide reduced liver fat by about 73% relative in non-cirrhotic NAFLD, beating semaglutide. Glucagon receptor co-agonism acts directly on the liver, and survodutide also cut liver fat in cirrhosis. Even with a lower baseline PDFF (about 10%), an absolute reduction near 6 points against near-zero placebo change is far beyond the detectable difference at 85 patients. The trial is completed; Merck may delay CT.gov posting for an unapproved drug, so EASL 2027 is the likeliest public venue.
evidence: Efinopegdutide vs semaglutide phase 2a NAFLD 2023 (Romero-Gomez, J Hepatol)

assumptions.claim: Efinopegdutide 10 mg weekly reduced liver fat content by about 72.7% relative vs about 42.3% with semaglutide at week 24 in NAFLD.
assumptions.source: Romero-Gomez et al., Journal of Hepatology 2023

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in MASH liver-fat trials typically change MRI-PDFF by less than 1 absolute percentage point over 6 months.
assumptions.source: Resmetirom MAESTRO-NASH and efruxifermin HARMONY placebo arms (2023-2024)

reason: Still recruiting in October 2026 with 7 biweekly infusions and 24 weeks of follow-up, so last-patient week 36 lands after mid-2027; a small private sponsor makes a registry update late and adds some funding-stop risk.
rationale: Any patient enrolled after October 2026 reaches week 36 no earlier than mid-2027, past the 2027-06-29 threshold, so the registered March 2027 date is unlikely to hold if the record is updated. Walden is a venture-funded private biotech running a five-disease adaptive basket, which carries some risk of trimming or stopping. Results posting by August 2027 is very unlikely. A safety-only primary is rarely amended.

reason: Anti-CD20 beats cyclosporine on remission mainly at 24 months, after cyclosporine is withdrawn and patients relapse; if the primary is read at 12 months (as the short registered timeline suggests), remission rates are similar and superiority fails.
rationale: In MENTOR, rituximab and cyclosporine gave similar remission at 12 months (60% vs 52%), but rituximab was far better at 24 months (60% vs 20%). B007 is a humanized anti-CD20 that should act like rituximab. Whether the trial succeeds depends on the timepoint and on whether the hypothesis is superiority or non-inferiority, and the record gives neither. The registered dates are inconsistent with 2-year follow-up while still recruiting, so an early report is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In MENTOR, complete or partial remission at 24 months was 60% with rituximab vs 20% with cyclosporine.
In MENTOR, remission at 12 months was 60% with rituximab vs 52% with cyclosporine, meeting non-inferiority only.

reason: With 20 patients per arm and an active triple-therapy control that already resolves many acute HSK episodes and suppresses viral shedding by day 70, a significant cure-rate difference needs about 30 points or more.
rationale: BD111 (Cas9 lentiviral-like particles against HSV-1) was safe in a three-patient investigator-initiated study with no recurrences. Its likely advantage is preventing recurrence, which shows up later than day 70. Antiviral plus steroid therapy cures many stromal keratitis episodes and clears tear qPCR within 10 weeks. The single-center, single-blind 40-patient design gives only about 30% power for a plausible 20-point gain. A small Chinese sponsor makes an early public readout unlikely.
evidence: NCT04560790 (BD111 investigator-initiated trial in refractory HSK)
Yin et al. 2021, Nature Biotechnology (HELP preclinical)

assumptions.claim: In an investigator-initiated study, three patients with refractory HSK treated with BD111 had no recurrence and no serious adverse events over about 18 months of follow-up.

reason: SVR35 add-on benefit is plausible, but TSS50 is a second primary and add-on agents to ruxolitinib (navitoclax, pelabresib) have repeatedly improved spleen response without a significant symptom benefit against a strong blinded placebo response.
rationale: Navtemadlin (MDM2 inhibitor) showed SVR35 15% vs 5% as monotherapy in BOREAS, so an SVR35 gain over placebo plus continued ruxolitinib in TP53WT suboptimal responders is likely. Both SVR35 and TSS50 are registered primaries; symptom co-primaries failed for navitoclax (TRANSFORM-1) and pelabresib (MANIFEST-2) add-ons despite strong spleen results, and navtemadlin GI toxicity can blunt symptom gains. Still recruiting in October 2026 with a run-in plus 24-week endpoint, so the December 2026 completion date is unrealistic and a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Navtemadlin monotherapy achieved SVR35 of about 15% vs about 5% with best available therapy at week 24 in relapsed/refractory myelofibrosis.
Navitoclax plus ruxolitinib improved SVR35 versus placebo plus ruxolitinib but did not significantly improve TSS50 at week 24.
Pelabresib plus ruxolitinib roughly doubled SVR35 versus placebo plus ruxolitinib while the symptom endpoint was not significant.

reason: Adjunctive GAD trials have a large placebo response on HAM-A (about 10 points in 6 weeks), and prior adjunctive antipsychotic trials in GAD (risperidone, quetiapine) failed to separate; a 1-2 point true effect gives modest power even with about 235 per arm.
rationale: ITI-1284 is deuterated lumateperone, whose 42 mg adjunctive MDD trials were positive, so some anxiolytic signal is plausible. But adjunctive antipsychotics have a poor record in GAD, placebo response in 6-week HAM-A trials is large and site-driven (Eastern Europe plus US), and phase 2 power for a 1.5-2 point effect is only moderate; either dose counts, which helps slightly. J&J rarely press-releases phase 2 results, and with March 2027 primary completion a disclosure before July 2027 earnings is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Lumateperone 42 mg adjunctive to antidepressants significantly reduced MADRS versus placebo in major depressive disorder.
Risperidone augmentation did not separate from placebo on HAM-A in GAD patients with inadequate response to anxiolytics.

reason: SGLT inhibition has no proven mechanism in HCM; in HFpEF the KCCQ gain is about 2-3 points at 6-8 months, below what 250 per arm can reliably detect against SD about 17, and a sizeable placebo KCCQ response further dilutes the signal.
rationale: Sotagliflozin is first tested in HCM here; evidence for SGLT2 inhibitors on KCCQ comes from HFpEF, where DELIVER and EMPEROR-Preserved showed 1.5-3 point gains and PRESERVED-HF about 5.8 points. HCM symptoms are driven by obstruction and diastolic dysfunction that SGLT inhibition addresses only indirectly, unlike myosin inhibitors (+7 to +9 points). With about 250 per arm and SD about 17, a true 2.5-point effect gives under 50% power. Enrollment is closed and Lexicon, a small listed company, should report topline in H1 2027.

assumptions.claim: Dapagliflozin improved KCCQ-CSS by about 5.8 points versus placebo at 12 weeks in HFpEF.
assumptions.source: PRESERVED-HF, Nassif et al. Nat Med 2021

assumptions.claim: Aficamten improved KCCQ-CSS by about 7 points versus placebo at week 24 in obstructive HCM.
Dapagliflozin improved KCCQ total symptom score by about 2.4 points versus placebo at 8 months in HFpEF.

reason: Two-site Taiwanese MSC trial still recruiting 90 COPD patients in October 2026 with a December 2026 primary completion date; small cell-therapy sponsors usually extend timelines and seldom post results on ClinicalTrials.gov.

A TKI implant dosed every 6 months could lose a few letters against aflibercept every 8 weeks in partly loaded naive eyes; if the mean deficit approaches the likely 4.5-letter margin, non-inferiority fails, though rescue rules and loading doses limit this.
rationale: SOL-R tests axitinib implant re-dosed about every 24 weeks against aflibercept q8w for BCVA non-inferiority at week 48. Sustained-release TKIs (EYP-1901 in DAVIO 2) and port delivery (Archway) stayed within 1-2 letters of aflibercept, and rescue plus aflibercept loading keeps deficits small, so non-inferiority against a 4-5 letter margin is likely. Enrollment is complete, primary completion January 2027, and Ocular Therapeutix guided topline for H1 2027 as its NDA basis.

assumptions.claim: Aflibercept 2 mg every 8 weeks gained about 8 letters at week 52 in treatment-naive nAMD.
The vorolanib intravitreal insert EYP-1901 was within about 1-2 letters of aflibercept q8w in BCVA in previously treated nAMD.

reason: Anti-TSLP antibodies reliably lower blood eosinophils, so the main risks are the small arms (about 36 each) in an unselected asthma population with modest baseline counts, and a private sponsor reporting only descriptive reductions without a stated test.
rationale: Solrikitug is an anti-TSLP antibody; tezepelumab lowered blood eosinophils by roughly 50% versus placebo in PATHWAY and NAVIGATOR, an effect of about 3 standard errors even with 36 per arm. The PD endpoint makes success likely; residual risk is a non-eosinophilic population with low baseline counts and vague private-company reporting. The trial completed July 2026, so an ATS 2027 abstract or press release is plausible but not assured.

assumptions.claim: Tezepelumab substantially reduced blood eosinophil counts versus placebo over 52 weeks in severe asthma.
Tezepelumab reduced blood eosinophils versus placebo across doses in the phase 2b PATHWAY trial.

reason: Eosinophil lowering by an anti-TSLP antibody in COPD selected for high eosinophils is near certain; the residual risk is noise in about 60 patients per arm and reporting without a formal statistical statement.
rationale: Patients were selected for elevated blood eosinophils, so baseline counts are high and anti-TSLP blockade should lower them by about 200 cells/uL against placebo, a large signal with about 60 per arm. FEV1 at 12 weeks is less certain: biologics in eosinophilic COPD give 50-160 mL gains, near this trial's detection limit. Primary completion was September 2026; a private sponsor may disclose at ATS 2027 or ERS 2027.

assumptions.claim: Dupilumab improved pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by about 83 mL versus placebo at week 12 in COPD with eosinophils of at least 300 cells/uL.
Tezepelumab lowered blood eosinophils in COPD but did not significantly reduce exacerbations overall in the phase 2a trial.

reason: With 16 patients per arm, a significant PFS-6 difference needs an absolute gain of roughly 45 points, far beyond what focused-ultrasound BBB opening with bevacizumab plausibly delivers, since bevacizumab penetration is not the main limit in rGBM.
rationale: Bevacizumab alone gives PFS-6 of roughly 15-45% across rGBM trials (BELOB, BRAIN). Focused-ultrasound BBB opening is unproven to improve efficacy, and bevacizumab acts largely on vasculature, so added delivery may add little. With 32 patients, only an implausibly large difference would reach p<0.05. Still recruiting in October 2026 with a December 2026 completion date and a 6-month endpoint, so a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Bevacizumab alone achieved a 6-month PFS of about 43% in recurrent glioblastoma.
assumptions.source: BRAIN trial, Friedman et al. JCO 2009

assumptions.claim: Bevacizumab monotherapy achieved a 6-month PFS of about 16% in recurrent glioblastoma.
assumptions.source: BELOB, Taal et al. Lancet Oncol 2014

reason: Topoisomerase-I ADCs show high response rates in SCLC, but heavy myelosuppression and post-progression therapies could dilute the OS gain over topotecan; an OS effect smaller than response data suggest is the main way this fails.
rationale: BL-B01D1 (EGFRxHER3 bispecific ADC with topo-I payload) showed about 50-60% ORR in previously treated SCLC in phase 2, and other novel agents beat chemotherapy on OS in 2L SCLC (tarlatamab HR 0.60). Topotecan in this setting gives median OS of about 7-8 months, leaving room for a clear gain with 722 patients. Baili has announced several phase 3 interim OS successes for this drug and files quickly in China, so an interim or final readout in 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: Tarlatamab improved overall survival versus chemotherapy in 2L SCLC (HR about 0.60; control median OS about 8.3 months).
The topotecan/CAV control arm had a median OS of about 7.6 months in relapsed SCLC.
assumptions.source: ATLANTIS, Aix et al. Lancet Respir Med 2023

assumptions.claim: BL-B01D1 showed an objective response rate around 50% or higher in previously treated SCLC in early-phase trials.

reason: Roughly 14 patients per active arm in an exploratory phase 2a umbrella; a significant week-12 UPCR difference needs a very large effect, and Sanofi may report descriptively without a formal test.
rationale: Frexalimab (anti-CD40L) has a plausible mechanism in immune-mediated podocytopathy (anti-nephrin antibodies, T-B cell help), and enrolling steroid-responsive patients enriches for it. But the arm is tiny, percent UPCR change is highly variable (SD ~45 points), placebo patients on low-dose steroids can remit spontaneously, and phase 2a umbrella studies often report descriptively. Still recruiting in late October 2026 against a December 2026 primary completion, so an early readout is unlikely; any early public statement is more likely an arm drop than a significant win.
evidence: Hengel et al., NEJM 2024 (anti-nephrin autoantibodies in podocytopathies)
Vermersch et al., NEJM 2024 (frexalimab phase 2 in relapsing MS)

assumptions.claim: Anti-nephrin autoantibodies are present in a substantial share of adults and children with minimal change disease.
Frexalimab significantly reduced new gadolinium-enhancing T1 lesions versus placebo at week 12 in relapsing MS.

reason: Enrolment is closed and the 48-week single-arm biomarker endpoint is fixed; UCB usually keeps dates close, so a modest slip is the main operational risk and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.
rationale: Open-label phase 3b mechanistic biomarker study of an approved drug from a large sponsor, already active not recruiting with a March 2027 primary completion; low risk of termination or primary-outcome change. Results would normally be posted around a year after primary completion, i.e. after the August 2027 read date.

reason: Oral TPO-receptor agonists reliably raise platelets before procedures while placebo rarely reaches >=50 with a >=20 rise; the main residual risk is an operational or reporting issue (Part A/B split shrinking arms) rather than efficacy.
rationale: Every TPO-receptor agonist tested pre-procedure in CLD (avatrombopag ADAPT-1/2, lusutrombopag L-PLUS 1/2) beat placebo by wide margins. The composite here also requires a >=20x10^9/L rise, which placebo patients almost never achieve without transfusion, so placebo response should be single digits. Herombopag (hetrombopag) is an approved eltrombopag-like agonist in China. Even with Part A patients reducing Part B arms to ~50 each, power is very high. Hengrui typically discloses via sNDA acceptance or congress abstracts.
evidence: ADAPT-1 and ADAPT-2, Terrault et al., Gastroenterology 2018

assumptions.claim: In ADAPT-1/2, avatrombopag responders (no platelet transfusion or rescue) were about 66-88% versus 23-38% with placebo.
In L-PLUS 1, 79% of lusutrombopag patients versus 13% of placebo patients avoided pre-procedure platelet transfusion.

reason: Anti-CD38 plus Pd is a proven doublet-to-triplet gain, but Chinese patients with prior daratumumab exposure (only primary refractoriness is excluded) could blunt the benefit, and a novel anti-CD38 may be less potent than daratumumab or isatuximab.
rationale: Adding an anti-CD38 antibody to pomalidomide-dexamethasone after lenalidomide and a PI improved PFS with HR ~0.6 in both APOLLO and ICARIA-MM, with control medians of 6.5-6.9 months. SG301 is a novel anti-CD38 with single-agent activity in phase 1. Risks: possible inclusion of anti-CD38-exposed patients, an unproven molecule, and an event-driven primary analysis that is still recruiting, so a public result by June 2027 would most likely be an early efficacy stop, which favours 'met' conditionally.

assumptions.claim: In APOLLO, daratumumab-Pd versus Pd gave median PFS 12.4 vs 6.9 months, HR 0.63.
In ICARIA-MM, isatuximab-Pd versus Pd gave median PFS 11.5 vs 6.5 months, HR 0.596.

reason: With about 36 patients per arm, a teduglutide-sized gain (~30 points) gives only ~70-80% power, and placebo responder rates rise when PN is actively weaned during the double-blind period.
rationale: PJ009 is a daily weight-based GLP-2 analogue, a class with repeated phase 3 success on the same >=20% PN-volume responder endpoint (teduglutide STEPS 63% vs 30%; apraglutide and glepaglutide also positive). The trial copies the STEPS design but is smaller (72 patients), leaving meaningful chance of a miss if placebo response is high or the dose is suboptimal, as happened to teduglutide 0.10 mg/kg in its first phase 3. A quick public statement from a small Chinese sponsor is likelier after a win.

assumptions.claim: In STEPS, 63% of teduglutide 0.05 mg/kg/day patients versus 30% of placebo patients achieved >=20% PN volume reduction at weeks 20 and 24.
In the first teduglutide phase 3, the 0.05 mg/kg dose was superior to placebo (46% vs 6%) but the 0.10 mg/kg dose was not.

reason: The composite requires both a 4-point itch response and near-clear nodules at week 24; lesion clearance lags itch relief, so the absolute composite gain could be smaller than expected, though sample size gives ample power.
rationale: Povorcitinib (oral JAK1) showed large, dose-dependent itch NRS4 and nodule responses over placebo in its phase 2 PN trial, and JAK/IL-31/IL-4R agents have all succeeded in PN phase 3 with placebo composite rates around 10%. With ~175 per arm, even a 15-point difference is highly significant. Primary completion was October 2026, and Incyte usually press-releases phase 3 toplines within a few months, so a public result by mid-2027 is very likely.
evidence: PRIME and PRIME2 (dupilumab, Yosipovitch Nat Med 2023)

assumptions.claim: In PRIME, 60% of dupilumab versus 18% of placebo patients achieved Itch NRS4 at week 24.
Povorcitinib phase 2 in prurigo nodularis showed significantly higher Itch NRS4 rates than placebo at week 16.

reason: The composite of itch NRS4 plus IGA-CPG-S 0/1 at week 24 is demanding because nodule clearance lags itch relief; a regional mix including Japan could raise placebo response, but power remains high.
rationale: Twin of STOP-PN1 with the same design and size (~173 per arm). Povorcitinib phase 2 in PN showed robust itch and lesion benefits, and every recent PN phase 3 of a targeted agent (dupilumab, nemolizumab) separated from placebo on itch and IGA endpoints. A 10-15 point composite gain would already be significant. Incyte is likely to release both STOP-PN toplines together in early 2027, shortly after the October 2026 primary completion.
evidence: PRIME and PRIME2 (dupilumab, Yosipovitch Nat Med 2023)

assumptions.claim: In PRIME2, dupilumab improved Itch NRS4 at week 24 versus placebo (about 58% vs 20%).
In OLYMPIA 2, nemolizumab achieved Itch NRS4 at week 16 in about 56% versus 21% with placebo.

reason: PFS is very likely positive, but OS is a dual primary; if the first report has immature OS without significance, the round's all-primaries rule could score the trial as not met.
rationale: Trop-2 ADCs have beaten single-agent chemotherapy in pretreated TNBC by large margins (ASCENT PFS HR 0.41; OptiTROP-Breast01 sac-TMT HR 0.32 with OS also significant at interim), and control chemotherapy PFS by BICR is only ~2-3 months. FDA018-ADC is a similar Trop-2 ADC, so PFS success is highly probable. The main discount is the OS dual primary: if OS is immature at first disclosure, the round's co-primary rule may count it as not met.

assumptions.claim: In ASCENT, sacituzumab govitecan improved PFS versus chemotherapy (5.6 vs 1.7 months, HR 0.41) in brain-metastasis-negative patients.
In OptiTROP-Breast01, sacituzumab tirumotecan improved BICR PFS versus chemotherapy (HR about 0.32) and OS at interim in Chinese TNBC patients.

reason: Injectable VLP norovirus vaccines have not proven protective in young children (HIL-214 failed in infants), immunity is strain-specific and short-lived, and genotype shifts (GII.17, GII.4 variants) may cut efficacy.
rationale: No norovirus vaccine has yet shown efficacy in a pediatric phase 3; HilleVax's bivalent VLP (HIL-214) showed essentially no efficacy in infants. Zhifei's quadrivalent Pichia VLP covers the main circulating Chinese genotypes including GII.17 and is given in three doses, and older children may respond better, but efficacy is highly uncertain. With about 100 cases across 6,600 children, a VE near 40% would only borderline reach significance. Primary completion is March 2027, so a public result by June 2027 would be fast.
evidence: Takeda NoV VLP adult field study (Sherwood, Vaccine 2020)

assumptions.claim: HilleVax's HIL-214 bivalent VLP vaccine did not meet its primary efficacy endpoint (VE about 5%) against moderate-to-severe norovirus AGE in infants.
GII.17 norovirus re-emerged as a leading genotype in China during 2024-2025 seasons.

reason: Plain bupivacaine paravertebral block already gives strong early analgesia, and small dose arms (~24 patients) after thoracoscopy, with multimodal rescue analgesia, often leave liposomal-vs-plain differences non-significant.
rationale: Liposomal bupivacaine extends block duration, which should help a 72-hour AUC, and Hengrui's liposomal bupivacaine has beaten plain bupivacaine in its infiltration programme in China. But head-to-head nerve-block RCTs of liposomal versus plain bupivacaine (including paravertebral and intercostal blocks in thoracic surgery) are mixed, the dose-finding arms are small, and phase 2 results may be reported descriptively. Hengrui seldom publicises phase 2 data quickly.
evidence: Hussain et al., Anesthesiology 2021 (meta-analysis liposomal vs plain bupivacaine peripheral nerve block)

assumptions.claim: A meta-analysis of RCTs found liposomal bupivacaine in peripheral nerve blocks gave no clinically important analgesic benefit over plain bupivacaine.

reason: Small-biotech multi-part phase 2 still recruiting toward 178 patients with a December 2026 primary completion date that looks unrealistic; date extension is likely and a funding-driven stop is a real possibility.
rationale: Still recruiting in late 2026 with an optional randomized Part 3, so primary completion will almost surely move past March 2027. Ryvu is cash-constrained, adding stop risk. European-only sites and a non-US sponsor make CT.gov results posting very unlikely. A multi-part design leaves some chance of primary outcome edits (e.g., dropping Part 3).

reason: Fully enrolled 46-patient phase 2 with a 17-week primary period; topline guided for around end-2026, so the primary completion date should hold and posting by August 2027 is unlikely for a small biotech.
rationale: Active, not recruiting with a short primary safety window, so completion near December 2026 is plausible. Dianthus is likely to report topline but post CT.gov results near the 12-month deadline (December 2027). Low stop and amendment risk.

reason: The composite needs serum calcium of 8.0-10.0 mg/dL on half the elemental calcium without raising active vitamin D; if amorphous calcium does not fully compensate, many AMOR-1 patients will be titrated up or fall below range, shrinking the responder rate.
rationale: The endpoint requires a 50% cut in calcium dose, which the control arm by design keeps unchanged, so control responders should be near zero. Even 25-30% responders on AMOR-1 (10-12 of 41) would beat 0-1 of 21 by Fisher's test. The main risk is that half-dose amorphous calcium fails to hold serum calcium at 8.0 or above in hypoparathyroid patients who often run low-normal. The key secondary (calcium in range) compares like with like and is unlikely to show superiority.

assumptions.claim: Control patients keep their initial elemental calcium intake throughout the study.
AMOR-1 patients are planned to receive about 50% of their prior elemental calcium intake after the replacement phase.

reason: The randomized phase 1 signal (HR about 0.5 vs enzalutamide) came from roughly 80 patients and will likely shrink; a control arm that includes docetaxel is stronger than enzalutamide alone, so the true HR may sit near 0.75-0.8.
rationale: EZH2 inhibition to restore AR-inhibitor sensitivity has a randomized phase 1 rPFS signal (14.3 vs 6.2 months, HR about 0.51) in post-abiraterone mCRPC. Pfizer launched multiple phase 3s on it. Post-abiraterone controls do poorly (rPFS 4-6 months on ARPI switch), and with 600 patients the trial is powered for HR near 0.7. Regression from the small phase 1 and the docetaxel option in control are the main threats. OS will likely be immature at the rPFS readout.
evidence: NCT03460977 mevrometostat phase 1 randomized expansion (ASCO GU 2025)

assumptions.claim: In the randomized phase 1 expansion in post-abiraterone mCRPC, mevrometostat plus enzalutamide gave median rPFS of about 14.3 months vs 6.2 months for enzalutamide alone (HR about 0.51).
In PSMAfore, the ARPI-change control arm had median rPFS of about 5.6 months by central review.

reason: Pediatric dose-escalation study with about 10 patients per dose cohort and only 12 pooled placebo patients; results will likely be descriptive, and any test would have very low power against a sizable pediatric placebo response.
rationale: This is a safety and PK dose-ranging study in 6-11 year olds, randomized 5:1 per cohort, built for dose selection rather than hypothesis testing. Results most likely surface as CT.gov postings with descriptive statistics, which count as not met. Adult tenapanor effects on bowel movements are moderate, and pediatric placebo responses are large, so significance with 10 vs 12 patients is improbable.

assumptions.claim: Each cohort randomizes 12 patients 5:1 tenapanor to placebo across up to 6 sequential dose cohorts.

reason: Simulated inadvertent gluten exposure may cause only modest mucosal damage in placebo patients over 28 weeks, leaving little Vh:Cd decline to prevent; with about 38 per arm and noisy biopsy morphometry, a real but small protective effect may miss significance.
rationale: Anti-OX40L blockade of gluten-specific T cell responses is plausible but untested in celiac; prior immunomodulators (AMG 714 anti-IL-15) failed Vh:Cd endpoints, while only the transglutaminase inhibitor ZED1227 showed clear mucosal protection. Low-level gluten exposure may produce small placebo declines, limiting the detectable effect at about 38 per arm. Sanofi reports phase 2 outcomes in pipeline updates, so a public verdict is likely by mid-2027.
evidence: AMG 714 celiac phase 2a (Lahdeaho, Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2019)

assumptions.claim: ZED1227 significantly attenuated gluten-induced decline in Vh:Cd vs placebo in a 6-week gluten challenge.
AMG 714 did not significantly attenuate gluten-induced Vh:Cd decline vs placebo in a gluten-challenge phase 2a.
assumptions.source: Lahdeaho et al., Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2019

reason: Non-depleting B-cell inhibition gave only a non-significant trend in an earlier SLE phase 2, and BICLA placebo responses near 35% mean the trial needs a roughly 14-point gain to reach significance with 95 patients per arm.
rationale: Obexelimab (CD19 x FcgammaRIIb) failed to reach significance in a 2018 SLE phase 2 (42% vs 29%, p=0.18). SLE phase 2 trials succeed at most about a third of the time, and background-therapy placebo BICLA rates of 30-40% demand large effects. With 95 per arm, a true 8-10 point difference gives under 40% power. Zenas will publicize topline promptly, likely early 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the earlier phase 2 of obexelimab (XmAb5871) in SLE, the primary endpoint was not statistically significant (about 42% vs 29%, p=0.18).
Placebo BICLA response in TULIP-2 was about 31.5%.

reason: Seltorexant's adjunctive antidepressant effect is small (about 2-3 MADRS points), so placebo-response variability across 16 mostly ex-US countries could erase significance; a required Part 2 relapse result would also come late.
rationale: A prior phase 3 (MDD3001) and the phase 2b showed 20 mg seltorexant beat placebo by about 2.5-3 MADRS points in MDD with insomnia. Part 1 should have several hundred patients, giving good power for a 2.5-point effect, but the effect is small and placebo response is high in Latin American and Eastern European sites. The trial is still recruiting, so a public Part 1 result by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In phase 3 MDD3001, adjunctive seltorexant 20 mg significantly improved MADRS total score vs placebo at day 43 in MDD with insomnia symptoms.

reason: Psychological support plus high expectancy can drive large placebo MADRS drops in a US-only psychedelic trial; if the placebo arm improves 12+ points, the margin over CYB003 could narrow to a non-significant 3-4 points.
rationale: CYB003 phase 2 showed a very large MADRS separation (about 14 points at week 3), and psilocybin phase 3 (COMP005) met its week-6 endpoint with about 3.6 points. Functional unblinding with an inert placebo favours the drug. With about 110 per arm and SD near 11, an effect of 4 points or more gives high power. Cybin guided topline for Q4 2026 after the trial completed, so a public result is near certain.

assumptions.claim: In the CYB003 phase 2, a single 12 mg dose reduced MADRS by about 14 points more than placebo at 3 weeks.
COMP005 psilocybin 25 mg showed a MADRS difference of about -3.6 vs placebo at week 6.

reason: An unvalidated NET-targeting mechanism tested over only 6 weeks in about 24 patients per arm on background csDMARDs; placebo DAS28-CRP drops of 0.7-1.0 points leave little room for a modest effect to reach significance.
rationale: CIT-013, an anti-citrullinated histone antibody that blocks NETs, has phase 1 biomarker data but no controlled efficacy in RA. Six weeks is short for a non-cytokine mechanism, and early placebo DAS28-CRP changes in csDMARD-inadequate responders run around -0.7 to -1.0 with SD about 1.1. With 24 per arm, a true 0.4-point difference has roughly 25% power; three doses give several chances, lifting p_met slightly. EU-only sites mean no ClinicalTrials.gov posting duty; a private sponsor would likely announce topline or present at EULAR 2027.

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in csDMARD-inadequate-response RA trials show mean DAS28-CRP improvements of about 1 point by week 12.

reason: PD-1 blockade adds little in MMRp/MSS colon cancer; with 60 per arm, a plausible 5-10 point gain in major pathological response over neoadjuvant CAPEOX is unlikely to reach two-sided significance.
rationale: MMRp/MSS colon cancer is largely resistant to PD-1 inhibitors, and chemo-immunotherapy data show only modest gains in deep pathological response. FOxTROT and OPTICAL put neoadjuvant oxaliplatin-fluoropyrimidine pCR at about 4-7% with major regression in a minority, so control mPR near 15%. With 60 per arm the SE of the difference is about 7 points, so a likely 5-10 point effect is underpowered, though a randomized phase 2 may use a lenient alpha. Still recruiting at its registered completion, so readout most likely late 2027 or beyond.

assumptions.claim: In FOxTROT, 6 weeks of neoadjuvant FOLFOX/CAPOX gave pathological complete response in about 4% of patients overall, lower in pMMR tumours.
assumptions.source: FOxTROT, Morton et al. J Clin Oncol 2023

assumptions.claim: In NICHE, only about a quarter of pMMR colon tumours showed pathological response to neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab.
assumptions.source: NICHE, Chalabi et al. Nat Med 2020

reason: Both co-primaries must succeed for one dose; the CGI-S co-primary in a heterogeneous shift-worker population with high placebo response, plus night-time MWT variability and dropouts, is the weaker link despite solriamfetol's large wake-promoting effect.
rationale: Solriamfetol produced large MWT gains in narcolepsy and OSA (300 mg about 10-12 minutes over placebo on the 40-minute MWT in TONES 2 and 3), and modafinil and armodafinil met MSLT and clinical global endpoints in shift work disorder. About 173 per arm gives ample power for MWT; the main risk is the CGI-S co-primary and noise from night-shift testing and dropouts. Axsome issues topline press releases promptly; still recruiting at launch suggests topline around mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: In TONES 3 (OSA), solriamfetol 300 mg improved MWT sleep latency by about 12.8 minutes vs about 0.2 minutes with placebo at week 12.
assumptions.source: Schweitzer et al. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2019

assumptions.claim: Armodafinil 150 mg in shift work disorder improved night-time MSLT by 3.1 minutes vs 0.4 minutes with placebo.
assumptions.source: Czeisler et al. Mayo Clin Proc 2009

reason: Complete debridement should clearly beat gel vehicle, but the record lists time to complete wound closure within 12 weeks as a second primary; showing faster closure versus vehicle with about 108 per arm is uncertain and both must succeed.
rationale: EscharEx's phase 2 ChronEx trial showed complete debridement in about 63% vs 13% with gel vehicle within 14 days, a robust effect a 216-patient phase 3 should reproduce. The risk lies in the second registered primary, time to complete wound closure by 12 weeks, where phase 2 showed only trends; under the co-primary rule success hinges on closure unless it is framed as a secondary or non-inferiority test. Adaptive sample-size design and still recruiting at launch point to topline in the second half of 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the ChronEx phase 2 trial, complete debridement within 14 days occurred in about 63% of EscharEx patients vs 13% with gel vehicle.

reason: As a non-inferiority comparison with imipenem-cilastatin, failure needs HRS-8427's composite cure to fall more than the margin (likely 10 points) below control, which is uncommon for new beta-lactams in cUTI.
rationale: HRS-8427 is reportedly a Hengrui siderophore cephalosporin. New beta-lactams tested against carbapenems or piperacillin-tazobactam in cUTI have consistently met non-inferiority on the composite at test of cure and often shown numerical superiority (APEKS-cUTI 73% vs 55%, CERTAIN-1 71% vs 58%). With about 290 per arm and a typical 10-point margin, power exceeds 90% if true rates are equal. Completed September 2026; Hengrui usually discloses through NMPA filing announcements or publications, with uncertain timing.

assumptions.claim: In APEKS-cUTI, composite cure at test of cure was 72.6% with cefiderocol vs 54.6% with imipenem-cilastatin.
assumptions.source: Portsmouth et al. Lancet Infect Dis 2018

assumptions.claim: In CERTAIN-1, composite success was 70.6% with cefepime-taniborbactam vs 58.0% with meropenem.
assumptions.source: Wagenlehner et al. N Engl J Med 2024

reason: Anti-TFPI prophylaxis versus on-demand treatment gives very large bleed reductions; the only realistic threats are thrombotic events forcing a dosing pause, as happened with concizumab, or heavy dropout in a small Part A.
rationale: Every anti-TFPI antibody tested against on-demand therapy has cut treated ABR by about 80-90% (marstacimab BASIS, concizumab explorer8), and entry required at least 6 treated bleeds in 26 weeks, so on-demand controls should bleed about 25-40 times per year. With 2:1 randomization and over 40 patients on KN057, significance is near-certain unless safety interrupts dosing. Alphamab, HKEX-listed, announces milestones; with primary completion in October 2026 a topline or China NDA announcement in 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: In BASIS, marstacimab prophylaxis reduced treated ABR by about 92% versus prior on-demand therapy (about 3.2 vs 38 bleeds per year).

reason: FGF21 analogues reliably improve NASH resolution, but potency varies by construct (pegbelfermin underwhelmed); with about 40 per arm a less potent Fc-FGF21 or a high placebo response could miss significance.
rationale: Fc-fused FGF21 analogues efruxifermin (HARMONY: NASH resolution 47-76% vs 15% placebo) and pegozafermin (ENLIVEN: 23-37% vs 2%) produced large histological effects, and the primary allows success on either NASH resolution or fibrosis improvement, with two doses. At about 40 per arm a 20-25 point gain is detectable with roughly 75% power. Construct potency is unknown and pegbelfermin was weaker. Started 2023 and still recruiting in late 2026 with 48-week biopsies, so readout likely 2028 and early public results unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In ENLIVEN, NASH resolution without fibrosis worsening occurred in 23-37% of pegozafermin groups vs 2% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Loomba et al. N Engl J Med 2023

assumptions.claim: In HARMONY, NASH resolution occurred in 47% (28 mg) and 76% (50 mg) of efruxifermin patients vs 15% with placebo at week 24.
assumptions.source: Harrison et al. Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2024

reason: Against active hyaluronate rather than saline, MSC injections in knee OA have shown only small WOMAC differences, and the MRI cartilage co-primary at 24 weeks must also succeed, a bar few cell therapies have cleared.
rationale: Randomized MSC trials in knee OA show modest pain and function gains with inconsistent structural effects, and here an MRI cartilage co-primary at 24 weeks must also be met. The comparator is active hyaluronate, whose own WOMAC improvements narrow the gap. Earlier AlloJoin phase 1/2 data from China were encouraging but small. Still recruiting in late 2026 with 48-week follow-up, so primary completion will slip well past March 2027 and a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Lamo-Espinosa 2016 MSC plus HA vs HA

assumptions.claim: A small randomized trial found bone-marrow MSC plus HA improved WOMAC only modestly versus HA alone at 12 months.
assumptions.source: Lamo-Espinosa et al. J Transl Med 2016

reason: China-only phase 2 still recruiting past its registered October 2026 primary completion; expect the dates to be pushed back rather than termination, no ClinicalTrials.gov results posting, and little change to the ORR primary.
rationale: Single-country Chinese sponsor trials rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov and usually extend dates rather than terminate; Avistone is actively developing vebreltinib, so a stop is unlikely within the window. ORR primary outcomes in such phase 2 records are seldom changed in substance, though occasional switches to PFS happen.

reason: Sclerostin-pathway antibodies reliably raise spine BMD by 10%+ in a year against a flat placebo; the only realistic failure is an unexpectedly weak or poorly tolerated highest-dose regimen.
rationale: AGA2118 is a sclerostin/DKK1 bispecific antibody; single sclerostin blockade already gives about +11% lumbar spine BMD at 12 months versus about 0% on placebo (romosozumab phase 2), and blosozumab gave up to ~18%. With ~54 per arm and a between-patient SD near 4.5%, even a third of that effect would be significant at the highest dose. Total hip BMD should also separate clearly. The main uncertainty is timing of disclosure by a private sponsor rather than the result.

assumptions.claim: Romosozumab 210 mg monthly increased lumbar spine BMD by 11.3% at 12 months versus -0.1% with placebo.
Blosozumab 270 mg every 2 weeks increased lumbar spine BMD by about 17.7% at 52 weeks in postmenopausal women with low BMD.
assumptions.source: Recker et al., J Bone Miner Res 2015

reason: Atropine is an active, proven myopia-control comparator; a first-in-class antisense eye drop with no controlled human efficacy data is unlikely to beat it on refraction change with 70 children per arm.
