rationale: The comparator is atropine, which in low dose slows spherical-equivalent progression by roughly a third to a half in children, so SHJ002 must not only work but beat an active drug. With ~70 per arm and an SD near 0.5 D, the trial can detect only a difference of about 0.25 D, larger than plausible for a novel antisense drop. An exploratory phase 2 relative to atropine more likely shows comparability, which under the round's rules does not count as met.

assumptions.claim: Children on 0.01% atropine in LAMP progressed by about -0.59 D in spherical equivalent over one year.
SHJ002 is an antisense oligonucleotide against a microRNA and is compared with atropine rather than placebo in this phase 2.

reason: Shingrix produces a CD4+ T-cell response in roughly 90% of recipients, leaving almost no room for a statistically superior response rate; the trial is mainly a safety comparison with no stated efficacy hypothesis.
rationale: The card takes the CD4+ T-cell response rate as the efficacy primary, but the record states no hypothesis, and the comparator is AS01-adjuvanted Shingrix, which gives CD4 responses in about 90% of adults over 50 one month after dose 2. A ceiling-bound response rate makes statistical superiority very unlikely even if the srRNA vaccine is as immunogenic; most mRNA zoster candidates have aimed only for comparable cellular responses with better reactogenicity. A report of comparability would count as not met.

assumptions.claim: Over 90% of adults aged 50+ had a gE-specific CD4+ T-cell vaccine response one month after the second Shingrix dose.
assumptions.source: Cunningham et al., J Infect Dis 2018 (ZOE-50/70 immunogenicity)

reason: Dementia-related psychosis trials have large placebo responses and noisy clinician ratings, so a real but modest muscarinic effect of about 2 points can be swamped; tolerability-limited dosing in frail elderly adds risk.
rationale: Xanomeline reduced hallucinations and delusions in Alzheimer's patients in the 1990s, and KarXT showed a robust antipsychotic effect in schizophrenia, so the mechanism is credible. But AD psychosis trials have repeatedly been eroded by placebo responses (pimavanserin's effect shrank over time), KarXT's adjunctive schizophrenia trial ARISE failed, and elderly patients may not tolerate full dosing. With ~200 per arm and SD near 8.5, an effect of about 2 points gives roughly 70% power; my prior on the true effect is centred a little below that. The trial was still recruiting at launch, so primary completion will slip.

assumptions.claim: Xanomeline monotherapy reduced hallucinations, delusions and agitation versus placebo in patients with Alzheimer's disease.
Pimavanserin reduced NPI-NH psychosis by about 1.8 points versus placebo at week 6 in AD psychosis, with no significant difference at week 12.
KarXT improved PANSS total by about 9.6 points versus placebo at week 5 in acute schizophrenia.

reason: Anti-TL1A antibodies have shown 20-25 point placebo-adjusted remission gains in phase 2; failure would need the phase 3 effect to shrink drastically against a placebo rate near 9%, which is unlikely with ~175 per arm.
rationale: Three anti-TL1A antibodies (afimkibart in TUSCANY-2, tulisokibart in ARTEMIS-UC, duvakitug in RELIEVE UCCD) all beat placebo on clinical remission by roughly 20-25 points or more in phase 2. Phase 3 effects usually shrink, but a 10-15 point gain over a ~9% placebo rate with ~175 per arm is still highly significant. Roche will likely disclose the induction readout in early-to-mid 2027, possibly alongside Ametrine-1.

assumptions.claim: Tulisokibart achieved clinical remission at week 12 in 26% versus 1% with placebo in ARTEMIS-UC.
Placebo clinical remission at week 12 by modified Mayo score was 13.3% in a large phase 3 UC induction trial.
Afimkibart (RVT-3101) significantly increased week-14 clinical remission versus placebo in the TUSCANY-2 phase 2b UC trial.

reason: Both week-12 and week-52 remission must be met; the class effect is large and treat-through placebo remission at week 52 is usually below 10%, so failure needs a much weaker drug than phase 2 suggested.
rationale: Same anti-TL1A class evidence as Ametrine-2, with a strong week-12 induction effect expected over a ~9% placebo rate. The co-primary week-52 remission in a treat-through design compares continued afimkibart against continued placebo, where placebo remission is typically about 5-8% (etrasimod ELEVATE UC 52: 32% vs 7%), so the second endpoint should also be met. Primary completion is January 2027; Roche may announce in Q2 2027 or wait for its half-year results in July.

assumptions.claim: In a treat-through UC trial, week-52 clinical remission was 32% with etrasimod versus 7% with placebo.
assumptions.source: ELEVATE UC 52, Sandborn et al., Lancet 2023

assumptions.claim: Tulisokibart achieved clinical remission at week 12 in 26% versus 1% with placebo in ARTEMIS-UC.

reason: The same 2 mg daily dose given once rather than twice may lose some mucosal contact time and histological effect; with a remission rate near 90% and ~154 per arm, a 3-5 point deficit could push the lower bound past a 10-point margin.
rationale: Budesonide orodispersible tablet 1 mg twice daily produced histological remission in over 90% of adults after 6 weeks in EOS-1. The once-daily arm gives the same total daily dose, so outcomes should be close; the risk is a modest loss from a single daily mucosal exposure. With high response rates and ~154 per arm the confidence interval is narrow (about +/-7 points), so a typical 10-15 point margin is probably cleared. Superiority on symptom remission is not expected. Falk usually presents at UEGW, so disclosure before July 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Budesonide orodispersible tablet 1 mg twice daily for 6 weeks gave histological remission in about 93% of adults with active EoE versus 0% on placebo.

reason: Blocking neutrophil-recruiting CXC chemokines is unproven in UC, and with about 48 per arm only a remission gain of 15+ points would reach significance as monotherapy; the combination with mirikizumab, not monotherapy, is the more likely winner.
rationale: Eltrekibart neutralises ELR+ CXC chemokines (CXCL1-8), a neutrophil-trafficking mechanism without clinical validation in UC. Monotherapy at the highest dose vs placebo with ~48 per arm has power only for large effects (about 15+ points over a ~9% placebo remission), larger than I expect from a novel mechanism. Only 143 patients enrolled across 207 sites suggests the adaptive design narrowed or stopped early. Lilly will likely disclose at DDW/UEGW 2027 or through ClinicalTrials.gov posting near the August 2027 deadline.

assumptions.claim: Placebo clinical remission at week 12 by modified Mayo score was 13.3% in a phase 3 UC induction trial run by the same sponsor.

reason: OS is a hard endpoint against pembrolizumab, which has a durable tail in PD-L1+ HNSCC; the anti-CD47 component has no proven OS benefit in solid tumours and VEGF blockade has not improved OS in HNSCC before.
rationale: Ivonescimab beat pembrolizumab on PFS in PD-L1+ NSCLC (HARMONi-2) and the ivonescimab+ligufalimab phase 2 in first-line PD-L1+ HNSCC showed ORR around 60% versus roughly 19% for pembrolizumab monotherapy historically. OS superiority over pembrolizumab is harder, and CD47 agents have repeatedly disappointed. Still recruiting in Oct 2026, so any readout by mid-2027 would be an early interim that Akeso would publicise mainly if positive, which lifts the conditional probability to about 0.6.
evidence: Ivonescimab plus ligufalimab phase 2 in 1L PD-L1+ R/M HNSCC (Akeso, 2024)

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab monotherapy gave median OS of about 12.3 months in PD-L1 CPS>=1 recurrent/metastatic HNSCC.
Ivonescimab improved PFS over pembrolizumab in PD-L1-positive advanced NSCLC with a hazard ratio of about 0.51.

reason: Enrolment is complete and the 12-week double-blind period should end on schedule; results posting is not due until about a year after primary completion, and the OLE continues to 2028.
rationale: Status is active, not recruiting with a 12-week double-blind primary period, so a March 2027 primary completion is consistent with enrolment ending in 2026. Denali keeps records current, so slippage beyond 90 days is unlikely. Results posting is due about March 2028, making posting by August 2027 unlikely. Termination risk exists from Biogen/Denali portfolio decisions on BIIB122, but the trial continued through Oct 2026. A safety-only primary outcome is rarely amended.

reason: Lecanemab itself lowers CSF MTBR-tau243, so the incremental reduction from an anti-MTBR antibody could be smaller than expected and a dose-response test in roughly 105 patients across several arms may lack power.
rationale: The primary endpoint is a proximal target-engagement biomarker: E2814 binds the microtubule-binding region and has lowered CSF MTBR-tau243 in dominantly inherited AD participants. Biomarker dose-response primaries in phase 2 succeed at high rates. The main uncertainty is the add-on effect over lecanemab, which also lowers tau biomarkers, and small arms if several doses are tested. CDR-SB at 24 months is unpowered and unlikely to be significant or public by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: E2814 reduced CSF MTBR-tau243 in dominantly inherited Alzheimer's disease participants in an open-label study.
In Clarity AD, adverse events led to lecanemab discontinuation in 6.9% vs 2.9% on placebo.

reason: PACAP-pathway blockade is less validated than CGRP: an anti-PAC1 receptor antibody failed, and only one anti-PACAP ligand antibody has shown about a 2-day benefit, so the effect may be too small in a hard-to-treat population.
rationale: MEDI0618 targets the PACAP pathway. Lu AG09222 (anti-PACAP) cut migraine days about 2 days more than placebo in a phase 2a in patients with prior preventive failures, while AMG 301 (anti-PAC1R) failed. Placebo response over 12 weeks in such populations runs about -1.5 to -2.5 days. With about 100-150 per arm, a true difference near 1.3 days gives roughly even odds of significance. Mixed aCGRP-naive and inadequate-responder cohorts may dilute the effect.

assumptions.claim: The anti-PACAP antibody Lu AG09222 reduced monthly migraine days by about 2 days more than placebo in a phase 2a in patients with 2-4 prior preventive failures.
assumptions.source: HOPE trial, Ashina et al., NEJM 2024

assumptions.claim: The anti-PAC1 receptor antibody AMG 301 did not separate from placebo in migraine prevention.

reason: Only 90 patients randomised 2:1 with about 30 controls; even a real hepatic PFS benefit may miss significance, and any readout by mid-2027 would be an immature early look.
rationale: Melphalan/HDS gives high hepatic response rates in uveal melanoma (FOCUS), and hepatic-only progression favours a liver-directed arm. Control trifluridine-tipiracil plus bevacizumab had median PFS 5.6 months in SUNLIGHT, so hepatic PFS might run 6-7 months. A true HR near 0.55 with about 55 events gives modest power. The trial started in Aug 2025 and is still recruiting, so the December 2026 primary completion is unrealistic and a public result by June 2027 is improbable.
evidence: FOCUS melphalan/HDS in uveal melanoma (Zager, Ann Surg Oncol 2024)

assumptions.claim: Trifluridine-tipiracil plus bevacizumab gave a median PFS of 5.6 months in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.

reason: A patient-reported hand function and pain score at 24 weeks is noisy and driven by many factors besides axonal fusion; with 49 per arm a modest PEG-fusion benefit is unlikely to reach significance.
rationale: PEG-fusion has shown early sensory recovery gains in small digital-nerve series, but evidence for durable functional benefit on a patient-reported scale is thin. The composite MHQ ADL plus pain score at 24 weeks is a noisy, indirect endpoint, and 98 patients give limited power. The sponsor is a small company and the trial was still recruiting in Oct 2026 with a 24-week endpoint, so the March 2027 primary completion will likely slip and a public result by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Bamba et al., PEG fusion of digital nerves (J Trauma Acute Care Surg 2016)

assumptions.claim: In a small controlled study, PEG-fusion of digital nerve injuries improved early sensory recovery versus standard repair.
assumptions.source: Bamba et al., J Trauma Acute Care Surg 2016

reason: The primary analysis is limited to the CpcPH subgroup, roughly 45-50 patients per arm, and PVR change by catheterisation is variable; an effect under about 0.7 Wood units could miss significance.
rationale: Relaxin is a vasodilator that lowers pulmonary pressures and raises cardiac output; Tectonic's phase 1b hemodynamic cohort of TX45 in PH-HFpEF showed PVR reductions after a single dose. Sustained 24-week dosing should keep some effect, and the CpcPH subgroup has the most pulmonary vascular component to reduce. The constraint is power: about 45-50 CpcPH patients per arm with a change-score SD near 1.8 Wood units. Placebo PVR should be flat. A small biotech will report a clear topline in early 2027.
evidence: RELAX-AHF hemodynamic substudy (Ponikowski, Eur Heart J 2014)

assumptions.claim: Serelaxin infusion reduced pulmonary capillary wedge and pulmonary artery pressures in acute heart failure patients.
assumptions.source: Ponikowski et al., Eur Heart J 2014

assumptions.claim: A single dose of TX45 reduced pulmonary vascular resistance in PH-HFpEF patients in the phase 1b study.

reason: Adding CTLA-4 blockade to PD-(L)1 consolidation after chemoradiotherapy has not improved PFS before (nivolumab plus ipilimumab in BTCRC LUN 16-081), so cadonilimab may not beat an active PD-L1 comparator.
rationale: Head-to-head versus an active PD-L1 antibody (sugemalimab, GEMSTONE-301 median PFS 9-10.5 months) requires the CTLA-4 arm of cadonilimab to add benefit, which consolidation trials of nivolumab plus ipilimumab did not show. Cadonilimab's lower toxicity and Akeso's strong record in Chinese head-to-head trials offset this somewhat. The trial was still recruiting in Oct 2026, so any readout by mid-2027 would be an interim that Akeso would mostly disclose if positive. Net about even odds.

assumptions.claim: Sugemalimab consolidation after chemoradiotherapy gave median PFS of about 9.0 months versus 5.8 months for placebo in stage III NSCLC.
assumptions.source: GEMSTONE-301, Zhou et al., Lancet Oncol 2022

assumptions.claim: Adding ipilimumab to nivolumab consolidation after chemoradiotherapy did not improve PFS and increased toxicity.

reason: Pregabalin is an effective active comparator in DPN pain; NaV1.8 inhibition (suzetrigine) only matched pregabalin in a similar phase 2, and VX-993 already failed in acute pain, so superiority over pregabalin is very unlikely.
rationale: There is no placebo arm; the comparator is pregabalin, which reduced NPRS about 2.1 points in Vertex's suzetrigine DPN phase 2, where suzetrigine merely matched it. VX-993 did not separate from placebo in acute pain and was deprioritised. Superiority over pregabalin is near-impossible, but the trial's own primary may be within-arm change from baseline, which would likely be significant; that ambiguity in how labellers read Vertex's statement lifts p_met to about 0.3.

assumptions.claim: In Vertex's phase 2 DPN study, pregabalin reduced weekly average NPRS by about 2 points at week 12, similar to suzetrigine.
assumptions.source: Vertex press release on suzetrigine DPN phase 2, Dec 2023

assumptions.claim: VX-993 did not show a statistically significant improvement over placebo in a phase 2 acute pain bunionectomy study.

reason: In ARSi-naive disease enzalutamide alone is very effective (rPFS about 20 months), so EZH2 inhibition may add less than in the post-abiraterone setting where the randomized signal was seen.
rationale: In a randomized phase 1 expansion in post-abiraterone mCRPC, mevrometostat plus enzalutamide roughly doubled rPFS versus enzalutamide (HR about 0.51), with a mechanistic rationale (EZH2 blockade restoring AR-inhibitor sensitivity). ARSi-naive patients have a stronger control arm (enzalutamide rPFS about 20-22 months in PREVAIL and TALAPRO-2), so the effect may shrink to HR about 0.65-0.7, still well powered with 900 patients. An early public readout would most likely be a positive interim.
evidence: Mevrometostat + enzalutamide randomized phase 1 expansion (ASCO GU 2025)

assumptions.claim: In post-abiraterone mCRPC, mevrometostat plus enzalutamide improved rPFS versus enzalutamide alone with a hazard ratio of about 0.51.
Enzalutamide plus placebo gave a median rPFS of 21.9 months in first-line mCRPC.

reason: Autologous whole-cell cancer vaccines have repeatedly failed to change recurrence in prostate cancer, and with about 100 patients and perhaps 25 DFS events only a very large effect would be significant.
rationale: High-risk pT3+ Gleason 8-10 disease with undetectable PSA after prostatectomy: biochemical recurrence by about 22 months is perhaps 25-35% without adjuvant therapy. Irradiated autologous tumour-cell vaccines (GVAX, others) have not shown clinical benefit, and sipuleucel-T did not delay biochemical failure. A small sponsor, 3 sites, still recruiting with a registered primary completion of Feb 2027, so the timeline is unrealistic and an early report is very unlikely. Expected events are too few to detect a moderate hazard ratio; open-label PSA surveillance adds noise.

assumptions.claim: Phase 3 trials of the allogeneic GVAX whole-cell prostate cancer vaccine (VITAL-1, VITAL-2) were stopped without showing survival benefit.
Sipuleucel-T did not significantly prolong time to biochemical failure in men with biochemical recurrence after prostatectomy.
assumptions.source: PROTECT, Beer et al. Clin Cancer Res 2011

reason: IRC-assessed CR/CRi needs marrow confirmation, so missing biopsies or a strict month-16 window could cap the combination's CR rate; the gap over zanubrutinib alone should still be large.
rationale: Continuous BTK inhibitor monotherapy rarely produces CR/CRi in the first 16 months (single digits in SEQUOIA by IRC). BCL2 plus BTK combinations give CR/CRi rates around 35-55% (GLOW, CAPTIVATE), and sonrotoclax plus zanubrutinib in first-line CLL showed deep responses and high uMRD in the phase 1/2. A 30+ point difference with 47 per arm gives very high power. This is a contribution-of-components study for registration, so the endpoint is chosen to be met. The main uncertainty is when it reports (EHA June 2027 or ASH 2027).

assumptions.claim: Ibrutinib plus venetoclax produced an IRC-assessed CR/CRi rate of about 39% in first-line CLL.
Zanubrutinib monotherapy in first-line CLL gave a CR/CRi rate below 10% at about 2 years of follow-up.

reason: IL-17A/F blockade reliably beats placebo on ACR50 in TNF-IR PsA; the only plausible failure is sonelokimab underperforming as it did versus expectations in HS, which still would likely leave a significant gap over a ~9% placebo rate.
rationale: In TNF-inadequate-responder PsA, placebo ACR50 at week 16 is low (5-10%), while IL-17 inhibitors reach 35-45% (bimekizumab 43% vs 7% in BE COMPLETE). Sonelokimab's phase 2 ARGO showed ACR50 near 46% vs 20%. With about 150 per arm, even a 15-point difference would be significant. Primary completion January 2027 and an active, small-cap sponsor make a topline press release by mid-2027 likely; the residual risk is corporate (financing, strategy after the VELA HS readout) rather than efficacy.

assumptions.claim: Bimekizumab achieved ACR50 of 43% vs 7% with placebo at week 16 in TNF-IR psoriatic arthritis.
Sonelokimab in phase 2 ARGO achieved ACR50 of roughly 46% vs about 20% for placebo at week 12.

reason: Menstrual migraine trials have large placebo responses on a short 5-day window with few migraine days at baseline, so a modest gepant effect (about 0.3 days per period) could be lost in noise.
rationale: Short-term perimenstrual prophylaxis works with long-acting triptans (frovatriptan, naratriptan), and rimegepant has proven preventive activity (every-other-day dosing beat placebo by about 0.8 monthly migraine days). Intermittent daily dosing across the perimenstrual window should cut migraine days, but the baseline is only about 2-3 migraine days per window and placebo improvement is large. With about 240 per arm and SD near 1.1, a 0.3-day effect gives roughly 75-80% power. Still recruiting near its registered primary completion, so results by mid-2027 are unlikely.
evidence: Silberstein et al. Neurology 2004 (frovatriptan MM prophylaxis)
Mannix et al. Obstet Gynecol 2007 (naratriptan MM prevention)

assumptions.claim: Every-other-day rimegepant 75 mg reduced monthly migraine days by 4.3 vs 3.5 with placebo in episodic migraine prevention.
Perimenstrual frovatriptan 2.5 mg twice daily significantly reduced the incidence of menstrual migraine vs placebo.

reason: With about 45 patients per arm, a 15-20 point gain in remission over cyclosporine at week 76 has only about even odds of reaching p<0.05, and the exploratory phase 2 may not formally test superiority at all.
rationale: Anti-CD20 therapy outperforms calcineurin inhibitors in primary membranous nephropathy once relapses after cyclosporine withdrawal accumulate (MENTOR: 60% vs 20% at 24 months, but similar at 12 months). Week 76 sits in between, so the expected gap is perhaps 15-20 points. Zuberitamab is a rituximab-like anti-CD20. With 45 per arm, power is near 50%; two zuberitamab doses help slightly. The phase 2 explicitly aims to explore phase 3 design, so a formal superiority claim is uncertain, and a Chinese sponsor is unlikely to publish by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: In MENTOR, complete or partial remission was 60% with rituximab vs 52% with cyclosporine at 12 months, and 60% vs 20% at 24 months.

reason: Weight loss drives AHI reduction; orforglipron gives roughly 9-11% placebo-adjusted weight loss, which should still reduce AHI by about 10-15 events/h, far beyond what 178 per arm needs to detect.
rationale: Tirzepatide in SURMOUNT-OSA reduced AHI by 25.3 vs 5.3 events/h at week 52 (difference about 20) with about 16% placebo-adjusted weight loss. Orforglipron produced about 11-12% placebo-adjusted weight loss in ATTAIN-1, implying an AHI difference near 12-14 events/h. With roughly 178 per arm and SD about 18, power exceeds 99%. The trial completed in July 2026 and Lilly routinely press-releases phase 3 toplines and presents at ATS/SLEEP/ADA, so a public result by mid-2027 is very likely.

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide reduced AHI by 25.3 events/h vs 5.3 with placebo at week 52 in participants not using PAP.
Orforglipron 36 mg produced mean weight loss of about 12.4% vs 0.9% with placebo at 72 weeks in adults with obesity.

reason: SSc autoantibodies are not clearly pathogenic, so IgG lowering by FcRn blockade may not soften skin; mRSS also improves spontaneously on placebo, and 58 vs 29 patients cannot detect a small difference.
rationale: mRSS-based SSc trials have a long record of failure: placebo arms improve by 2-4 points through regression to the mean (focuSSced, faSScinate, RISE-SSc), and even active immunomodulators rarely separate significantly at 24 weeks. FcRn blockade lowers IgG, but SSc autoantibodies are mainly markers, with no human proof of concept. The trial is small (2:1, 87 patients), giving low power for an effect below about 2.5 points. argenx usually discloses proof-of-concept toplines, though perhaps after week 48.

assumptions.claim: In focuSSced, mRSS change at week 48 was -6.1 with tocilizumab vs -4.4 with placebo, not statistically significant.
assumptions.source: Khanna et al., Lancet Respir Med 2020

assumptions.claim: In RISE-SSc, riociguat did not significantly improve mRSS vs placebo at week 52 in early diffuse SSc.
assumptions.source: Khanna et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2020

reason: A topical amyloid-aggregation inhibitor must reach the retina at active levels to slow GA; eye-drop and oral approaches have consistently failed here, and 55 per arm detects only a large effect on lesion growth.
rationale: Only intravitreal complement inhibitors (pegcetacoplan, avacincaptad) have slowed GA growth, by about 15-20%. Topical and oral GA candidates (emixustat, brimonidine-type approaches, others) have failed, and eye drops rarely achieve meaningful posterior-segment exposure. GAL-101 targets amyloid-beta aggregation, a weakly validated GA mechanism. With 55 per arm and between-patient SD of growth around 0.75 mm2/year, only an effect beyond 25% would be significant. Still recruiting with 12-24 month treatment, so the March 2027 completion date will slip and early results are very unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Oral emixustat did not reduce GA lesion growth vs placebo over 24 months.
Monthly intravitreal pegcetacoplan reduced GA growth by roughly 20% vs sham over 24 months.

reason: Selective 5-HT2C agonism may capture less of fenfluramine's anti-seizure effect than PACIFIC's small Dravet subset suggested; a weaker drug plus a variable placebo response could leave the difference non-significant with about 48 per arm.
rationale: Bexicaserin is a selective 5-HT2C agonist. Fenfluramine, which acts partly through 5-HT2C, gives large effects in Dravet (median convulsive seizure reduction 75% vs 19%). In PACIFIC, bexicaserin reduced countable motor seizures by a median of about 53% vs 21% for placebo across DEEs, with the Dravet subset responding well. Dravet trials show large, consistent drug-placebo separation (fenfluramine, cannabidiol, stiripentol). With roughly 48 per arm and an expected 30-35 point median difference, power is about 85-90%. Lundbeck, which acquired Longboard, should announce topline in H1 2027.

assumptions.claim: Fenfluramine 0.7 mg/kg/day gave median convulsive seizure frequency reduction of 74.9% vs 19.2% with placebo in Dravet syndrome.
Bexicaserin in the phase 1b/2a PACIFIC study reduced countable motor seizures by a median of about 53% vs about 21% with placebo across DEEs.

reason: Neuroprotectants added to reperfusion have almost uniformly failed in phase 3 stroke trials, and otaplimastat's phase 2 showed safety but no clear efficacy signal, so a true effect of a few points on mRS 0-1 is unlikely to be detected.
rationale: Otaplimastat is an MMP-inhibiting neuroprotectant with only preclinical efficacy and a small phase 2 (SAFE-TPA) that was mainly a safety study without a significant functional benefit. Adjunctive neuroprotection on top of thrombolysis/EVT has a long record of phase 3 failures (e.g., nerinetide ESCAPE-NA1 overall). With 426 per arm and a placebo mRS 0-1 rate near 38%, the trial can only detect about 9-10 point differences, far above any plausible effect. Probability of a significant mRS 0-1 benefit is low; results are unlikely by mid-2027 because recruitment was still ongoing at launch.

assumptions.claim: In ESCAPE-NA1, nerinetide did not improve the proportion with mRS 0-2 at 90 days versus placebo overall (about 61% vs 59%).
In the phase 2 SAFE-TPA trial, otaplimastat with rtPA did not increase parenchymal hematoma and showed no significant difference in 90-day mRS versus placebo.

reason: DPP1 inhibition gave only about a 20% exacerbation-rate reduction in ASPEN with 1,700 patients; with 669 patients and overdispersed exacerbation counts, a similar effect would leave power near 60-70%, so a modest true effect could miss significance.
rationale: HSK31858 is a DPP1 inhibitor, the class validated by brensocatib (ASPEN: rate ratios about 0.79-0.81 versus placebo, placebo rate 1.29/yr). Haisco's Chinese phase 2 reportedly reduced exacerbations, and the phase 3 enrols patients with at least two exacerbations in the prior year, giving a decent event rate. With about 335 per arm, a rate ratio of 0.75 gives roughly 80% power, but 0.80 gives about 60%. The class mechanism is proven, which supports a moderately favourable probability. Timing is uncertain because the record still said recruiting at launch.
evidence: WILLOW (brensocatib phase 2, Chalmers et al., NEJM 2020)

assumptions.claim: In ASPEN, brensocatib 10 mg and 25 mg reduced the annualized pulmonary exacerbation rate versus placebo with rate ratios of about 0.79 and 0.81, and a placebo rate of about 1.29 per year.
In WILLOW, brensocatib prolonged time to first exacerbation versus placebo in bronchiectasis.

reason: Retatrutide's weight loss clearly exceeds tirzepatide's in cross-trial data, so the main threat is higher retatrutide discontinuation for GI events or excess weight loss diluting the treatment-regimen difference; even so the trial is heavily powered.
rationale: Retatrutide 12 mg gave 24.2% weight loss at 48 weeks in phase 2 and about 28-29% at 68 weeks in TRIUMPH-4, versus about 20-22% for tirzepatide at maximum dose at 72 weeks (SURMOUNT-1, SURMOUNT-5). An expected difference of about 6-8 points with an SD of about 10% and 400 per arm gives z well above 5. Higher retatrutide dropout and dose-escalation intolerance narrow but are very unlikely to erase superiority. Lilly reliably announces phase 3 toplines within weeks to a few months of completion (primary completion Nov 2026).
evidence: Retatrutide phase 2 obesity (Jastreboff et al., NEJM 2023)
TRIUMPH-4 topline (Eli Lilly press release, Dec 2025)

assumptions.claim: Retatrutide 12 mg produced a mean 24.2% reduction in body weight at 48 weeks in the phase 2 obesity trial.
Tirzepatide at maximum tolerated dose produced about 20.2% weight loss at 72 weeks in SURMOUNT-5.

reason: The AUEC primary is near-certain given the albuterol component, but if the trial's hypothesis requires trough FEV1 superiority over the albuterol-alone arm after only 4 weeks, the fluticasone contribution (about 100 mL) could fall short of significance with about 160 per arm.
rationale: Fp/ABS versus placebo (or versus FP) on post-dose FEV1 AUEC0-6h is driven by albuterol bronchodilation, about 200-300 mL, so that comparison is essentially assured. The binding risk is the trough FEV1 co-primary, usually tested against the albuterol-alone arm to show the ICS contribution; in DENALI the higher-dose budesonide/albuterol met it at 12 weeks while the lower dose was borderline. Four weeks of FP QID in partly ICS-naive patients should give about 80-130 mL, adequately but not overwhelmingly powered. Combined probability of all primaries met is about 0.85.

assumptions.claim: In DENALI, budesonide/albuterol 160/180 ug significantly improved FEV1 AUC0-6h versus budesonide and trough FEV1 versus albuterol at 12 weeks.
assumptions.source: DENALI, Chipps et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol Pract 2023

reason: For mild (VIBe 1) soft-tissue bleeding, oxidized cellulose already achieves hemostasis within 3 minutes in most patients, so the margin left for TachoSil may be too small for 58 patients per arm to show significance.
rationale: TachoSil, a fibrinogen/thrombin collagen patch held under pressure, has repeatedly beaten standard topical methods on early hemostasis (e.g., liver resection versus argon beam). Active biologic hemostats usually achieve about 85-95% success within 3-4 minutes versus about 55-75% for passive ORC in mild-to-moderate soft-tissue bleeding. A roughly 20-point difference with 58 per arm gives about 80% power, lower if the mix skews toward mild bleeding. Results are unlikely to be public by mid-2027 given a private sponsor and recruitment still ongoing at launch.
evidence: TachoSil vs argon beam coagulator in liver resection (Fischer et al., 2011)
EVARREST fibrin sealant patch soft-tissue trial (2013)
Grifols fibrin sealant vs Surgicel soft-tissue phase 3 (2018)

assumptions.claim: TachoSil achieved a higher rate of hemostasis within a few minutes than argon beam coagulation in a randomized liver resection trial.

reason: Omidenepag lowers IOP slightly less than latanoprost (about 0.6 mmHg in AYAME, upper CI 1.26 against a 1.5 margin), so a slightly larger gap in Chinese patients could push the upper confidence bound past the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: This is a China bridging study of omidenepag isopropyl 0.002%, already approved in Japan and the US. In Japan's AYAME, omidenepag lowered mean diurnal IOP by 5.93 versus 6.56 mmHg for latanoprost at week 4, meeting non-inferiority (margin 1.5 mmHg) with an upper CI of about 1.26. With about 115 per arm and SD near 2.3 mmHg, the upper bound would sit near 1.2 mmHg if the gap repeats, giving about 80% chance of meeting a 1.5 margin. A tighter margin or a larger gap in Chinese patients is the main risk. Superiority on percent change is very unlikely.
evidence: AYAME (Aihara et al., Am J Ophthalmol 2020)
PEONY phase 3 in Asian patients (omidenepag vs latanoprost)

assumptions.claim: In AYAME, omidenepag isopropyl 0.002% reduced mean diurnal IOP by 5.93 mmHg versus 6.56 mmHg for latanoprost 0.005% at week 4, meeting the 1.5 mmHg non-inferiority margin.
assumptions.source: AYAME, Aihara et al., Am J Ophthalmol 2020

reason: The relugolix responder effect in LIBERTY was more than 50 points, so failure would need an implausibly high placebo response or major dropout in this small 80-vs-40 trial.
rationale: Relugolix combination therapy achieved MBL responder rates of 73% and 71% versus 19% and 15% for placebo in LIBERTY 1 and 2, with amenorrhea also strongly improved. Even 80 versus 40 patients gives near-total power for a difference of about 50 points. GnRH antagonism reliably suppresses menstrual bleeding regardless of population. The main uncertainty is operational: Qilu rarely publicises results and recruitment was still listed as ongoing at launch.
evidence: LIBERTY 1 and LIBERTY 2 (Al-Hendy et al., NEJM 2021)
Relugolix monotherapy phase 3 in Japanese fibroid patients (Osuga et al., 2019)

assumptions.claim: In LIBERTY 1, 73% of women on relugolix combination therapy versus 19% on placebo met the MBL responder endpoint (<80 mL and at least 50% reduction).
In LIBERTY 2, the responder rates were 71% versus 15% for placebo.

reason: Anti-IL-5 antibodies improve pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by only about 100-160 mL with an SD near 400 mL, so about 75 patients per arm gives roughly 40-60% power per dose, and placebo improvement at week 52 can shrink the difference.
rationale: Choosing FEV1 rather than exacerbations as the primary is a weak spot for IL-5 blockade: mepolizumab gave about 100 mL (MENSA) and benralizumab 116-159 mL (CALIMA/SIROCCO), significant only with about 400 per arm. With about 75 per arm, a 130 mL true effect gives about 50% power for one dose; two doses, with one enough, raise the chance modestly, offset by possible multiplicity adjustment. The exacerbation inclusion bar (at least 1 in 12 months) is low, which lowers the event rate for the key secondary.

assumptions.claim: In MENSA, subcutaneous mepolizumab increased pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by about 98 mL versus placebo at week 32.
In SIROCCO, benralizumab every 8 weeks increased pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by about 159 mL versus placebo at week 48 in patients with eosinophils of at least 300 cells/uL.

reason: AstraZeneca phase 2 closed at 24 patients with induction done; open-label maintenance runs to Sept 2027, so it likely continues unless AZD7798 is deprioritised, and results posting falls right around the 12-month mark.
rationale: Enrolment closed at 24 of about 30 planned and the registered primary completion (Aug 2026) has passed. AstraZeneca usually posts summary results about 12 months after primary completion, which lands right at the Aug 2027 read date, and registry QC can push posting later; non-US sites make it a likely non-applicable trial. Termination risk comes mainly from a portfolio decision during open-label maintenance. Safety-only primary outcomes rarely change in substance.

reason: Biopsy sampling variability and regression to the mean can produce spontaneous histologic resolution on placebo (20% in phase 2), shrinking the margin, especially if central Banff reading is strict and many patients have chronic active lesions.
rationale: Phase 2 (n=22) showed resolution of morphologic AMR at week 24 in 82% vs 20% with placebo, with lower MVI scores and dd-cfDNA; CD38 depletion of NK and plasma cells suits MVI-driven late AMR. With 66 per arm, power stays above 90% even if the effect halves. Risks: stricter central Banff reading, higher spontaneous resolution, less reversible chronic active lesions. Enrolment is closed; Biogen treats felzartamab as a key asset, so a topline press release in 2027 is likely, around mid-year.
evidence: Mayer et al., NEJM 2024 (felzartamab phase 2 in late AMR)

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial, morphologic AMR activity resolved at week 24 in 9 of 11 felzartamab patients versus 2 of 10 placebo patients.
assumptions.source: Mayer KA et al., N Engl J Med 2024

reason: A small real PK difference versus one of the reference products (EU or US Keytruda), or a chance ORR difference that lands outside the equivalence margin, is the most plausible way this biosimilar study fails.
rationale: Comparative biosimilar trials of monoclonal antibodies almost always show equivalence once analytical similarity is established. With 726 patients, ORR equivalence around the ~48% response seen with pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum (KEYNOTE-189) is well powered. Both AUC bioequivalence (80-125%) and ORR equivalence must pass, and the three-way EU/US comparison adds a small extra failure chance. Private sponsor mAbxience may announce topline by press release in 2027, but timing is uncertain and congress presentation could come after June.
evidence: Bevacizumab and trastuzumab biosimilar comparative efficacy trials (2017-2019)

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum gave an objective response rate of 47.6% in first-line non-squamous NSCLC.
assumptions.source: KEYNOTE-189, Gandhi L et al., N Engl J Med 2018

reason: Still recruiting in late Oct 2026 with 181-day safety follow-up, so the registered Nov 2026 completion cannot hold and should move to mid-2027; GSK updates records and usually posts results about a year after completion.
rationale: Because every participant needs follow-up to Day 181, a trial still enrolling in Oct 2026 cannot reach primary completion before roughly May 2027, well after the 2027-02-21 threshold; GSK maintains its records, so the date will likely be updated rather than left stale. Results posting by Aug 2027 is therefore unlikely. Termination is rare for a safety study of a vaccine in an active programme.

reason: Placebo response in functional dyspepsia is high (often 30-40%), so an herbal granule with a modest true effect may not separate at 171 per arm.
rationale: Chinese TCM phase 3 trials that report usually report success, and 171 per arm gives about 80% power for a 14-15 point difference. The responder definition (both fullness and early satiety halved in more than half of weeks) is strict, which lowers placebo response somewhat, but functional dyspepsia placebo rates remain high and variable. Still recruiting in Oct 2026, so a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely; Tasly may disclose it only alongside an NMPA filing.
evidence: Ford et al., placebo response in functional dyspepsia meta-analysis (2015)

assumptions.claim: The pooled placebo response rate in randomized trials of functional dyspepsia is around 40%.
assumptions.source: Ford AC et al., meta-analysis of placebo response in functional dyspepsia, 2015

reason: With only 15 untreated controls and an undefined BCVA response threshold, a modest gene-therapy gain in visual acuity could miss significance even if real.
rationale: Early VGR-R01 and other AAV-CYP4V2 studies in China reported visual acuity gains in most treated eyes, while untreated BCD eyes decline slowly and rarely gain letters over a year. The open-label untreated control (no sham) favours the treated arm on BCVA. Main limits are the 30 vs 15 size and an unspecified responder threshold; a 40% vs 5% split would be significant, 30% vs 5% might not. Vitalgen will likely disclose results around an NMPA filing in 2027.
evidence: ZVS101e AAV-CYP4V2 first-in-human study in BCD (2023-2024)

assumptions.claim: Untreated eyes with Bietti crystalline dystrophy show slow progressive loss of visual function rather than spontaneous improvement over one year.
assumptions.source: BCD natural history literature (CYP4V2 cohort studies in Chinese patients)

reason: Placebo plus topical corticosteroids can reach 25-35% EASI-75 in well-managed Japanese children, but even then the upadacitinib effect should remain large enough with about 50 per arm.
rationale: Upadacitinib plus TCS roughly tripled EASI-75 versus placebo plus TCS in adults and adolescents (AD Up, Rising Up), and JAK inhibition works similarly in children; dupilumab paediatric trials show placebo+TCS EASI-75 of 11-27%. A ~45-point difference with 50 vs 49 patients gives near-certain significance. Main uncertainty is timing: a Japan-only paediatric study is unlikely to get a press release, so results probably surface via registry posting or a congress around early 2028.
evidence: LIBERTY AD PEDS (Paller et al., JAAD 2020)

assumptions.claim: In AD Up, EASI-75 at week 16 was 26.4% with placebo plus TCS versus 64.6% with upadacitinib 15 mg plus TCS.
assumptions.source: Reich K et al., Lancet 2021 (AD Up)

assumptions.claim: In children 6-11 years with severe AD, EASI-75 at week 16 was about 27% with placebo plus TCS versus about 70% with dupilumab every 4 weeks plus TCS.
assumptions.source: Paller AS et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2020 (LIBERTY AD PEDS)

reason: Topical wound-healing agents added to compression rarely beat standard care in phase 3, because good compression already closes 35-50% of ulcers by week 16 and the add-on effect is small.
rationale: Phase 3 trials of topical agents for venous leg ulcers have mostly failed (e.g. HP802-247), as standard care with compression heals a large share within 16 weeks and screening run-ins only partly remove fast healers. 156 per arm detects about 15 points, more than a topical gel typically adds. Still recruiting at 12 sites in Oct 2026, so the Dec 2026 completion will slip and a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Apligraf VLU pivotal trial (Falanga et al., 1998)

assumptions.claim: Smith & Nephew's HP802-247 failed its phase 3 venous leg ulcer trials against vehicle and standard care.

reason: About 100-130 exacerbations over 24 weeks give little power for the 15-30% reduction anti-TSLP achieved in COPD; tezepelumab's COURSE missed with a 17% reduction over 52 weeks.
rationale: TQC2731 is an anti-TSLP antibody. Tezepelumab cut COPD exacerbations by only 17% overall in COURSE (not significant), more in eosinophil-high patients; no eosinophil cutoff is visible here. A 24-week phase 2 with 258 patients yields roughly 100-130 events, giving about 30-40% power for a 25% reduction. Chinese sponsors rarely publish phase 2 results before mid-year; disclosure may come in Sino Biopharm reports or at ERS 2027.
evidence: BOREAS dupilumab COPD (Bhatt et al., NEJM 2023)
NOTUS dupilumab COPD (Bhatt et al., NEJM 2024)

assumptions.claim: In COURSE, tezepelumab reduced moderate or severe COPD exacerbations by about 17% versus placebo over 52 weeks, which was not statistically significant.
In BOREAS, the placebo arm's annualized moderate or severe exacerbation rate was about 1.1 per year in eosinophilic COPD on triple therapy.
assumptions.source: Bhatt SP et al., N Engl J Med 2023 (BOREAS)

reason: Small Chinese sponsor's two-dose oral phase 2 in DME is already completed; status should stay completed, and posting of results on ClinicalTrials.gov is unlikely without US sites.
rationale: The trial is marked completed, so a change to terminated or withdrawn is very unlikely. EnnovaBio has no US sites and no apparent FDAAA obligation; Chinese small biotechs rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov. Record edits after completion seldom change the CRT primary outcome in substance.

reason: Only about 24 patients per arm over 8 weeks; phosphate change is noisy (SD ~1.4 mg/dL) and regression to the mean after binder washout lowers placebo too, so a real ~1 mg/dL effect can still miss significance.
rationale: AP306 is a pan-phosphate transporter inhibitor (NaPi2b/PiT1/PiT2), mechanistically stronger than tenapanor, with a positive China phase 2. Tenapanor lowered phosphate ~1-1.4 mg/dL vs placebo in short trials. At the top dose (375 mg/day) a placebo-adjusted drop of ~1.2 mg/dL gives roughly 75-80% power with 24/arm, and six dose arms give extra chances. Main uncertainties: small arms, variability after washout, and whether a dose-ranging phase 2b reports formal per-arm tests.

assumptions.claim: In a placebo-controlled tenapanor dose-ranging trial in hemodialysis patients after binder washout, placebo serum phosphate fell by about 0.5 mg/dL while the top dose fell by about 2 mg/dL.
Tenapanor fixed-dose 8-week treatment lowered serum phosphate by roughly 1.0-1.2 mg/dL from baseline in hemodialysis patients.

reason: Failure is very unlikely; the only plausible route is an unusually large placebo response in a Chinese monotherapy population combined with high dropout, which would shrink but almost certainly not erase a ~1.9-point HbA1c gap.
rationale: BGM0504 is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist similar to tirzepatide. Incretin agonists in drug-naive T2D with baseline HbA1c ~8.5% consistently beat placebo by ~1.7-2.1 points (SURPASS-1, DREAMS-1 mazdutide in China). With ~69 per arm and SD ~1.0, the trial is massively powered for superiority. Uncertainty is mainly about timing and the size of the placebo response, not the outcome.

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide 15 mg monotherapy lowered HbA1c by 2.07 points vs +0.04 with placebo at 40 weeks.
Mazdutide monotherapy in Chinese T2D reduced HbA1c by about 2 points more than placebo at 24 weeks.

reason: Semaglutide 1 mg is a strong comparator (~1.8-1.9 point HbA1c drop in Chinese patients); non-inferiority is very likely, but if the trial's actual primary hypothesis is superiority, a 10 mg dose may not separate significantly.
rationale: Dual GLP-1/GIP agonists beat semaglutide 1 mg on HbA1c by ~0.4 points (SURPASS-2), so non-inferiority with a typical 0.3-0.4 margin is near certain with ~179 per arm. I discount a little for the chance the protocol's primary hypothesis is superiority at 10 mg, where power is good but not certain, and for open-label conduct.

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide 10 mg reduced HbA1c by 2.24 points vs 1.86 with semaglutide 1 mg at 40 weeks (difference -0.39).
Semaglutide 1 mg lowered HbA1c by about 1.8 points over 30 weeks in a predominantly Chinese population.
assumptions.source: SUSTAIN China, Ji et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2021

reason: A selective 5-HT2C agonist may not reproduce fenfluramine's multi-receptor efficacy in a heterogeneous DEE population; the small, partly unblinded-feeling PACIFIC effect could shrink substantially in a 367-patient phase 3 with a sizeable placebo response.
rationale: Bexicaserin (LP352) showed a large median seizure reduction in the small PACIFIC phase 1b/2a (~53% vs ~21% placebo). Fenfluramine, which works partly through 5-HT2C, beat placebo by ~19 points in LGS. With ~184 per arm, a true ~20-point median difference gives high power, but DEE trials (soticlestat SKYWAY/SKYLINE) have failed on heterogeneity and placebo response. Lundbeck must disclose topline promptly, so a readout in H1 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: Fenfluramine 0.7 mg/kg/d reduced drop-seizure frequency by a median 26.5% vs 7.8% with placebo in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.
assumptions.source: Knupp KG et al., JAMA Neurol 2022

assumptions.claim: In PACIFIC, bexicaserin reduced countable motor seizure frequency by a median of about 53% vs about 21% with placebo.

reason: A single-site NIDA-funded inpatient dose-escalation study that is still recruiting past its registered completion date; it will most likely simply run late, with dates pushed out rather than results posted by August 2027.
rationale: Small 40-patient single-site phase 2 with an IV enzyme against methamphetamine, still recruiting after its registered primary completion, so completion will slip and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely. NIH-funded trials face some funding risk, giving a modest stop probability. Primary outcomes are safety counts and urine PK, which are rarely changed in substance.

reason: An ultra-rare pediatric crossover study with 32 weeks of blinded dose escalation; with only 6 patients the timeline depends on a few individuals, and the small sponsor updates the record irregularly, so slippage past March 2027 is plausible.
rationale: Six MVID children each go through a 32-week placebo-crossover escalation across three dose levels; any late-enrolled participant pushes primary completion past the registered December 2026. Napo/Jaguar is a small company, so results posting by August 2027 is unlikely, and with safety-only primary outcomes substantive amendment is unlikely. Termination risk is low but nonzero given corporate finances.

reason: Beating an active complement inhibitor that already slows GA growth ~20% would need a further large effect; with ~67 eyes per arm over 56 weeks, superiority over pegcetacoplan is very hard even for an active drug.
rationale: Pegcetacoplan reduces GA growth by ~20% vs sham; square-root growth in similar populations is ~0.39 mm/yr untreated (GATHER2 sham), so ~0.30 mm/yr on pegcetacoplan. Showing a significant further reduction with ~67 per arm needs ~0.06 mm/yr extra, a large incremental effect for a novel agent. Phase 2 head-to-head designs often aim at comparability rather than superiority, which would score as not met. BI usually presents at congresses later in the year.

assumptions.claim: Monthly pegcetacoplan reduced GA lesion growth by roughly 20% vs sham over 24 months in pooled OAKS/DERBY.
In GATHER2, the sham arm's square-root GA growth was about 0.39 mm/year at 12 months vs about 0.34 with avacincaptad pegol.

reason: With about 20 patients per arm, significance on both ORR and PFS is nearly impossible, and anti-TIGIT add-on effects to PD-1 plus chemotherapy have repeatedly failed in phase 3, so the experimental arm is unlikely to separate at all.
rationale: Enrollment stopped at 39, far below a typical randomized phase 2, suggesting the substudy was curtailed. Co-primary ORR and PFS both need to be significant; with ~20 per arm that requires an implausibly large effect. Anti-TIGIT antibodies added to PD-(L)1 have failed in multiple phase 3s (SKYSCRAPER-01, KEYVIBE program), and domvanalimab's own development has been under pressure. The PD-1 plus carboplatin/paclitaxel control should give an ORR around 35-45%.

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab plus platinum and 5-FU achieved an ORR of about 36% in first-line recurrent/metastatic HNSCC.
Tiragolumab plus atezolizumab did not significantly improve PFS or OS over atezolizumab in first-line PD-L1-high NSCLC.

reason: A first-in-class anti-S100A8/A9 antibody in IPF has no clinical proof of mechanism; most novel IPF mechanisms fail in phase 2, and with background antifibrotics shrinking placebo decline, a 28-week trial of 150 patients needs a ~60 mL effect.
rationale: Placebo FVC decline over 28 weeks with mixed antifibrotic background is ~70-100 mL; with SD ~190 mL and 75 per arm the trial needs ~60 mL benefit for significance. Successful IPF phase 2s (nerandomilast, nintedanib) showed effects of that size, but many novel mechanisms (ziritaxestat, pamrevlumab, GLPG1205) failed. Base rate for a novel IPF mechanism at phase 2 is about 25%. A small venture-backed biotech will likely announce topline in H1 2027.

assumptions.claim: In INPULSIS, placebo FVC fell by about 223 mL over 52 weeks without antifibrotic background.
Ziritaxestat failed to slow FVC decline in phase 3 IPF despite an encouraging phase 2a.

reason: All objectives must succeed: three-lot GMC consistency plus seroresponse and GMC non-inferiority against Varivax; a live attenuated vaccine with somewhat lower gE antibody response than Varivax could miss one GMC margin.
rationale: Lot-to-lot consistency trials run by major manufacturers usually succeed, and GSK chose the 12-15 month Varivax comparison after earlier phase 3 work on this candidate, as it did with Priorix vs M-M-R II. The added non-inferiority against Varivax on both seroresponse and GMC is the main risk, since all primary objectives must pass. GSK rarely press-releases such results, so a public primary result by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Priorix vs M-M-R II US phase 3 program (GSK, 2019-2021)

assumptions.claim: GSK's MMR vaccine Priorix met non-inferiority to M-M-R II in US phase 3 trials, supporting its 2022 FDA approval.

reason: Single-arm PK bridging study of the registrational Q4M cabotegravir formulation; ViiV runs such studies to completion and usually posts close to the 12-month deadline, which falls just after the read date.
rationale: Large sponsor, priority asset (Q4M CAB-ULA PrEP), enrolment complete, so stopping is very unlikely. Registered primary completion 2026-09-09 means the FDAAA posting deadline is about 2027-09, just after the 2027-08-31 read date; GSK/ViiV usually post near the deadline, and the month 13-25 trough window may push the primary completion date later. Some chance the trough time frame or targets are edited.

reason: Superiority against active IVIg maintenance in IVIg-responsive patients is a high bar; with 77 per arm the trial needs empasiprubart to improve grip strength clearly beyond the IVIg-maintained baseline, not just preserve it.
rationale: Phase 2 ARDA showed empasiprubart largely removed the need for IVIg retreatment and suggested grip-strength gains beyond the on-IVIg baseline at the higher dose, which is why argenx chose a head-to-head design. Complement C2 blockade gives steady exposure without IVIg end-of-cycle wear-off, and a 4-week average grip strength reduces noise. Still, beating an effective active comparator with 154 patients is roughly a coin flip. Readout expected around the turn of 2026/27.
evidence: Leger et al. IVIg in MMN crossover, Brain 2001

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 ARDA study, empasiprubart reduced the risk of needing IVIg retreatment by about 91% versus placebo.
IVIg is the only established effective maintenance therapy for MMN and maintains grip strength in responders.
assumptions.source: Leger et al., Brain 2001 (IVIg crossover in MMN)

reason: Open-label single-site Chinese dose-optimisation study of a priority ADC; likely to keep running past its stale completion date, with little chance of CT.gov posting.
rationale: HLX43 is Henlius's lead ADC, so the HCC cohort is likely to complete, though HCC could be deprioritised versus lung indications. Chinese sponsors rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov. Primary outcomes (ORR, PFS by investigator) may be edited if the dose-optimisation design is restructured, but most such records stay unchanged.

reason: Anti-TSLP reliably lowers FeNO, so the main risk is that the first public statement is a pipeline note calling the data positive without a formal primary-endpoint result, or that the posted analysis lacks a significance test.
rationale: TSLP blockade with tezepelumab cut FeNO by roughly 10-15 ppb versus placebo, a large and consistent biomarker effect; a long-acting anti-TSLP at its top dose should reproduce this with about 75 patients per arm. FEV1 at 26 weeks is less certain (tezepelumab about +0.13 L, near the power limit here). GSK posts results promptly, but the CT.gov deadline is mid-July 2027, so a June 2027 public result depends on a congress or pipeline disclosure.

assumptions.claim: Tezepelumab reduced FeNO by about 10 ppb or more versus placebo at week 52 in NAVIGATOR.
Tezepelumab improved pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by about 0.13 L versus placebo at week 52 in NAVIGATOR.

reason: With 130 patients over 48 weeks only about 80-90 exacerbations are expected; a realistic rate ratio near 0.6 against an active high-dose ICS comparator gives well under 60% power for a negative-binomial test.
rationale: Benralizumab cuts exacerbations by roughly 40-50% versus placebo in eosinophilic asthma (SIROCCO, ANDHI), less at eosinophils 150-300. Escalating to high-dose ICS adds a modest benefit, so the true ratio against this control is probably about 0.6. The small sample makes significance uncertain, and SGRQ, tested hierarchically, is less likely still. AstraZeneca tends to present phase 3b data at ATS or ERS and posts near the 12-month deadline (September 2027).

assumptions.claim: In ANDHI, benralizumab reduced the annualized exacerbation rate by about 49% versus placebo in patients with eosinophils of 150/uL or more.
assumptions.source: Harrison et al., Lancet Respir Med 2021 (ANDHI)

assumptions.claim: In SIROCCO, benralizumab every 8 weeks reduced exacerbations by about 51% versus placebo in patients with eosinophils of 300/uL or more.

reason: Biosimilar equivalence on ORR with about 400 per arm is usually well powered; failure would come from chance imbalance or a real quality difference shifting the ratio outside the margin.
rationale: Monoclonal biosimilar comparative trials in China and elsewhere almost always show equivalence when analytics match; pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum gives ORR near 48-55%, so 808 patients give tight confidence limits. The main uncertainty is timing: the trial was still recruiting in October 2026 with a 24-week ORR endpoint, and Qilu is private and rarely publishes trial results quickly, so a public statement by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum produced an objective response rate of about 48% in non-squamous NSCLC.

reason: Congenital hypothalamic obesity (SOD, ONH, PSIS) is a different mechanism from acquired injury; if the MC4R pathway deficit is less central, setmelanotide's effect could be smaller than in TRANSCEND, and 39 patients leave little room.
rationale: In acquired HO (TRANSCEND), setmelanotide gave about a 20-point placebo-adjusted BMI reduction at 52 weeks; even half that effect at 26 weeks would be highly significant with 20 versus 19 patients and an SD near 8%. Uncertainty is whether congenital HO responds as well. Still recruiting in October 2026 with titration plus 26 weeks of treatment, so primary completion and topline will likely slip to the second half of 2027.
evidence: Roth et al., setmelanotide phase 2 in HO, NCT04966741 (Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2024)

assumptions.claim: In TRANSCEND, setmelanotide reduced BMI by about 16.5% versus a 3.3% increase on placebo at 52 weeks in acquired hypothalamic obesity.
In the open-label phase 2 HO study, most patients achieved at least 5% BMI reduction by week 16.
assumptions.source: Roth et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2024, NCT04966741

reason: Small US single-arm two-stage study by a small sponsor, still recruiting 120 brain-metastasis patients at 12 sites in late 2026; very likely to run past its January 2027 primary completion date.
rationale: Brain-metastasis breast cancer trials accrue slowly, and with 12 months of intracranial follow-up after the last patient the January 2027 date is unrealistic, so the record will most likely show a later date or still be recruiting. A small sponsor raises some risk of stopping for funding or strategy. Posting before the read date is very unlikely.

reason: PFS benefit is likely, but OS is a second primary endpoint that will be immature by mid-2027; under the co-primary rule a PFS-only announcement may not count as meeting all primary outcomes.
rationale: Adding anti-angiogenic plus PD-1 activity to nab-paclitaxel in first-line TNBC should beat nab-paclitaxel alone: PD-(L)1 agents gave ITT PFS HR about 0.8, and bevacizumab with paclitaxel about 0.6. Ivonescimab phase 2 in TNBC showed high response rates. A PFS HR near 0.6 against a control median near 5.5 months is very likely significant. The discount is for the co-primary OS rule and Akeso reporting only a PFS interim.

assumptions.claim: In IMpassion130, placebo plus nab-paclitaxel had a median PFS of 5.5 months, and atezolizumab gave an ITT PFS HR of 0.80.
In E2100, adding bevacizumab to paclitaxel in first-line metastatic breast cancer roughly halved the hazard of progression.

reason: Novel GA mechanisms mostly fail in phase 2, and even approved complement inhibitors slow square-root growth by only about 0.05 mm/yr, which about 37 patients per arm over 50 weeks cannot reliably detect.
rationale: Placebo square-root GA growth in recent trials is about 0.35-0.40 mm/yr; pegcetacoplan and avacincaptad cut it by about 15-20%. Detecting that with about 37 patients per arm needs a larger effect than any approved agent shows, and the phase 2 GA failure rate (lampalizumab, emixustat, danicopan, brimonidine) is high. Boehringer may use a dose-response (MCP-Mod) test, which helps somewhat. Results most likely come via CT.gov near December 2027.
evidence: Chroma and Spectri lampalizumab, NCT02247479 (JAMA Ophthalmol 2018)

assumptions.claim: In GATHER2, square-root GA growth was about 0.39 mm/yr on sham versus about 0.34 mm/yr on avacincaptad pegol at 12 months.
Lampalizumab failed to slow GA growth versus sham in two phase 3 trials despite a positive phase 2 subgroup signal.

reason: Unvalidated new compound in a 14-subject crossover split across two doses; EEG spike-wave counts are noisy, and an exploratory study reporting mean and median differences may give no formal test of the primary.
rationale: Small single-center proof-of-concept crossover of an unknown-mechanism ASM in GGE with EEG-defined absence seizures. Effective absence drugs (ethosuximide, valproate) suppress spike-wave bursts strongly, so a truly active drug could show a large within-subject effect even with 14 subjects. Most novel ASMs fail early, though, and with two doses the higher-dose comparison may include only part of the cohort. The primary is descriptive (mean and median), so a significance statement may be missing. A small private sponsor is more likely to publicize a positive result.

assumptions.claim: Ethosuximide gave freedom from treatment failure in about 53% of children with absence epilepsy at 16 weeks, versus 29% with lamotrigine.

reason: Both co-primaries compare the combination against the component that lacks the active ingredient (dapagliflozin for HbA1c, rosuvastatin for LDL-C), so each should succeed; the remaining risk is execution or reporting.
rationale: Korean factorial FDC registration trial. The HbA1c co-primary tests dapagliflozin's add-on effect over rosuvastatin alone. Dapagliflozin 10 mg on metformin lowers HbA1c by about 0.5-0.6 points more than placebo, and statins nudge HbA1c slightly up, so with 80 per arm the power is high. The LDL-C co-primary (rosuvastatin vs no statin) gives a 40-50% difference and is near certain. Similar Korean FDC trials almost always meet. Recruitment was still open at launch, so the readout is probably late.
evidence: Bailey 2010 Lancet, dapagliflozin add-on to metformin

assumptions.claim: Dapagliflozin 10 mg added to metformin lowered HbA1c by about 0.54 percentage points more than placebo at 24 weeks.

reason: An anti-galectin-3 antibody with no validated mechanism in PD, tested over only 28 weeks in 62 levodopa-treated early-PD patients, where MDS-UPDRS change is small and noisy.
rationale: Disease-modifying antibodies in early PD (prasinezumab, cinpanemab) missed their MDS-UPDRS primaries even with larger samples and longer follow-up. TB006 is an anti-galectin-3 antibody whose Alzheimer's phase 2 gave no convincing primary win. With 31 per arm, a 28-week window and symptomatic levodopa background, a significant MDS-UPDRS difference is unlikely. The sponsor may describe the result as encouraging without a significant primary, which counts as not met.

assumptions.claim: Prasinezumab did not significantly change MDS-UPDRS parts I-III versus placebo over 52 weeks in early PD.
Cinpanemab showed no benefit over placebo on MDS-UPDRS in early PD.

reason: A full-dose long-acting GLP-1 agonist against placebo in drug-naive T2D almost always gives a large, significant HbA1c difference; failure would need a trial-conduct or reporting problem.
rationale: GZR18 (bofanglutide) is a biweekly GLP-1 receptor agonist that showed strong HbA1c and weight effects in phase 2. Placebo-controlled monotherapy trials of GLP-1 agonists in Chinese T2D (PIONEER 11, DREAMS-1 with mazdutide) show placebo-adjusted HbA1c reductions of 1-2 points. With 137 per arm, the primary is near certain. The open questions are timing and whether Gan & Lee discloses topline by June 2027 (listed company; ADA 2027 is a plausible venue).

assumptions.claim: Full-dose GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce HbA1c by more than 1 percentage point versus placebo in Chinese drug-naive T2D.

reason: Semaglutide 1 mg is a strong comparator (about -1.8 HbA1c points in Chinese patients); superiority needs a clear dose advantage, though the trial's own hypothesis is probably non-inferiority first, which is very likely met.
rationale: A head-to-head GLP-1 trial against semaglutide in Chinese T2D on metformin-based therapy. Registration trials like this usually test non-inferiority (margin about 0.3-0.4) with superiority second. GZR18 at high dose has high exposure and phase 2 efficacy near tirzepatide's, so non-inferiority is very likely and superiority on HbA1c is plausible with about 1,100 patients. If the sponsor's own primary is superiority only, p_met falls to roughly 0.6. Topline is expected in H1 2027 at the earliest.

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide 1.0 mg lowered HbA1c by about 1.8 percentage points at 30 weeks in Chinese-predominant T2D patients on metformin.
Tirzepatide was superior to semaglutide 1 mg on HbA1c with differences of 0.15-0.45 points.

reason: Phase 2a compares only about 26 patients per arm, and the full 2a+2b analysis is unlikely by mid-2027. A placebo arm counting response at any time during GC taper can be high, so significance is fragile.
rationale: JAK inhibition, especially ruxolitinib, is the most active steroid-sparing approach in retrospective VEXAS cohorts, and pacritinib adds IRAK1 inhibition, so a real effect is plausible. But VEXAS is rare: phase 2b was still recruiting at launch, and any result public by mid-2027 would likely be a small phase 2a dose-selection readout with limited power or only descriptive statistics. Older, frail patients and pacritinib's GI toxicity raise discontinuation risk.
evidence: Heiblig 2022 Blood, JAK inhibitors in VEXAS

assumptions.claim: In a retrospective French VEXAS cohort, ruxolitinib gave higher clinical response rates than other JAK inhibitors.

reason: With about 128 per arm, a 24-week window and around 100 exacerbations, a realistic 20-30% rate reduction is often not significant; phase 2 trials of TSLP and IL-33 biologics in COPD have missed similar endpoints.
rationale: COPD biologic phase 2 trials with exacerbation primaries often miss: tezepelumab COURSE had a rate ratio of 0.83 and missed, and IL-33 programmes are mixed. Dupilumab worked only in eosinophil-selected patients (rate ratio about 0.70). The eligibility shown does not clearly enrich for type-2 inflammation. A 24-week exacerbation endpoint with 256 patients has limited power. Primary completion is March 2027, so a public readout by June 2027 is unlikely from this Chinese sponsor.

assumptions.claim: Tezepelumab phase 2 COURSE in COPD did not meet its primary moderate-severe exacerbation endpoint (rate ratio about 0.83).
assumptions.source: Singh et al., Lancet Respir Med 2025

assumptions.claim: Dupilumab reduced moderate-severe COPD exacerbations by about 30% in patients with blood eosinophils of at least 300.

reason: MG-ADL responder rates on placebo at a single time point are often 30-45%, and the phase 2b effect came from a small sample; a 64-per-arm trial needs a 20-25 point difference to reach significance.
rationale: Descartes-08, an mRNA CAR-T given without lymphodepletion, beat placebo in the small MG-001 phase 2b (most treated patients reached a 5-point MG Composite improvement at month 3, versus about a third on placebo), and the AURORA design was agreed with FDA. MG trials of effective drugs usually succeed, but phase 2b estimates from about 30 patients tend to shrink, and placebo MG-ADL responder rates are sizable. Enrollment is complete and month-4 data should read out in early-to-mid 2027 via press release from a listed sponsor.

assumptions.claim: In the MG-001 phase 2b, a larger share of Descartes-08 than placebo patients achieved a 5-point or greater MG Composite improvement at month 3.
In ADAPT, about 30% of placebo patients were MG-ADL responders (2-point or greater sustained improvement) in the first cycle.

reason: Aripiprazole is an effective active comparator; if the trial's hypothesis is superiority, a new 3-6 mg antipsychotic is unlikely to beat it by a significant PANSS margin, whereas a non-inferiority design (usual for Chinese registration trials) would very likely succeed.
rationale: Chinese phase 3 of an antipsychotic against aripiprazole with no placebo arm; such registration trials are usually non-inferiority designs, which nearly always succeed because efficacy differences between antipsychotics are small. If the hypothesis is superiority, success is unlikely. Weighting roughly 65% non-inferiority gives about 0.66. I expect PANSS change near -27 in both arms with a near-zero difference. Qilu rarely publicizes results quickly, and results that do appear early skew positive.
evidence: Leucht et al., Lancet 2013 antipsychotic network meta-analysis
Huhn et al., Lancet 2019 antipsychotic network meta-analysis
Kane et al. 2002 aripiprazole acute schizophrenia trial

assumptions.claim: Head-to-head efficacy differences between most second-generation antipsychotics, including aripiprazole, are small (standardized mean differences mostly under 0.2).
Aripiprazole 10-30 mg separates from placebo on PANSS total in 4-6 week acute schizophrenia trials.
assumptions.source: Kane et al., J Clin Psychiatry 2002

reason: If JMKX003142 is a vasopressin V2 antagonist (thirst and diuretic exclusions suggest an aquaretic), a tolvaptan-like TKV effect should be detectable; failure would come from insufficient potency or dose, or dilution by aquaresis-driven dropouts in a 52-week trial of ~67 per arm.
rationale: Exclusions for inability to feel thirst and planned diuretic use point to an aquaretic V2 receptor antagonist. Tolvaptan cut annual TKV growth roughly in half (about -2.7 points per year) in TEMPO 3:4, with a larger first-year effect. In a rapidly progressive population with placebo growth near 6% per year and SD near 6, 67 per arm gives good power for a comparable effect. Uncertainty on mechanism, dose arms and potency keeps p_met at 0.7. The 52-week endpoint and ongoing recruitment make a public result by mid-2027 very unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In TEMPO 3:4, tolvaptan reduced annual total kidney volume growth to 2.8% versus 5.5% with placebo over 3 years.
Vasopressin V2 antagonists cause an early reversible eGFR decline, so 1-year eGFR change is not expected to favour drug.

reason: ONO-2020 is a novel non-antipsychotic mechanism with no prior agitation efficacy data; with 45 patients per arm and a substantial placebo response on CMAI in inpatients, a significant difference requires an effect larger than brexpiprazole's.
rationale: Phase 2a proof-of-concept of a first-in-class compound (reported as an epigenetic modulator) in AD agitation, a field where even approved brexpiprazole gives only about a 5-point CMAI advantage with a large placebo response. With 45 per arm and SD near 14, power for a 5-point effect is under 50%, and a novel mechanism probably has a smaller true effect. Recruitment of hospitalized patients is slow, so results by mid-2027 are unlikely.
evidence: Brexpiprazole agitation trial (Lee et al., JAMA Neurol 2023, NCT03548584)
Grossberg et al. 2020 brexpiprazole agitation trials

assumptions.claim: In the brexpiprazole 2-3 mg agitation trial, CMAI fell about 22.6 points on drug versus 17.3 on placebo at week 12 (difference about -5.3).

reason: Icotrokinra has no published PsA phase 2; if the oral IL-23R peptide gives less joint efficacy than injectable IL-23 blockers, ACR20 separation could shrink, though 375 per arm leaves ample power even for a 10-point gap.
rationale: IL-23 pathway blockade reliably improves ACR20 in PsA (guselkumab and risankizumab about 20-30 points over placebo), and icotrokinra matched injectable-class skin efficacy in ICONIC-LEAD. With 750 patients, even a modest 10-point gain would be significant. Mixing biologic-experienced patients lowers response slightly. Placebo ACR20 at week 16 is expected near 28%. J&J usually issues topline press releases for icotrokinra, so a result around mid-2027 is plausible.

assumptions.claim: Guselkumab every 4 weeks achieved ACR20 at week 24 in 64% versus 33% with placebo in biologic-naive PsA.
Icotrokinra achieved IGA 0/1 at week 16 in about 65% versus 8% with placebo in moderate-to-severe psoriasis.
Risankizumab achieved ACR20 at week 24 in 57% versus 34% with placebo in PsA.
assumptions.source: Kristensen et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2022 (KEEPsAKE-1)

reason: Still recruiting a month before its registered primary completion, so the 8-week dose-finding study will likely finish in early-to-mid 2027; Takeda keeps records current and posts results near the 12-month deadline.
rationale: Recruitment is open at launch with 96 targeted, so the last 8-week visit falls in 2027; whether it lands before or after 28 Feb 2027 is close to even. Takeda updates records reliably, making a void unlikely. Results posting usually comes about a year after primary completion, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. Orexin agonists have shown tolerability issues, but TAK-360 is not known to have a safety stop.

reason: Selective endothelin-A antagonism reliably lowers proteinuria in IgAN (atrasentan about -36% vs placebo); failure would need SC0062 10 mg to be much less potent than in phase 2 or fluid-retention dropouts to dilute the effect.
rationale: SC0062 is a selective endothelin-A receptor antagonist; the class has a robust, reproducible antiproteinuric effect on top of RAS blockade (ALIGN: atrasentan -36% vs placebo at 36 weeks), and SC0062's phase 2 in IgAN showed a dose-related UPCR reduction of similar size. With 180 per arm and SD near 40%, power for a 30-point difference is essentially complete. Placebo on optimized RASi/SGLT2i should change little. Biocity's disclosure habits make timing, not the result, the main uncertainty.

assumptions.claim: Atrasentan reduced 24-hour UPCR by 36.1% versus placebo at week 36, with placebo near -3%.
SC0062 reduced proteinuria versus placebo at 12 weeks in its phase 2 IgAN cohort.

reason: An oral small-molecule GLP-1 agonist over 36 weeks should clearly separate on weight; the main residual risk is GI-driven discontinuation and missing data diluting a treatment-policy estimate in an older HFpEF population.
rationale: HRS-7535 is Hengrui's oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist, which produced substantial weight loss in Chinese obesity trials; GLP-1 agonists reliably cut weight in HFpEF with obesity (STEP-HFpEF: -13.3% vs -2.6% at 52 weeks). Over 36 weeks with 112 per arm, a 4-5 point placebo-adjusted loss would already be highly significant. Still recruiting at launch with a 36-week endpoint, the trial is unlikely to report before late 2027.
evidence: HRS-7535 phase 2 obesity trial in China (Hengrui)

assumptions.claim: In STEP-HFpEF, semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced body weight by 13.3% versus 2.6% with placebo at 52 weeks.
Oral small-molecule GLP-1 agonist orforglipron produced 9-15% weight loss versus about 2% with placebo at 36 weeks.

reason: Ruxolitinib cream has shown large EASI75 gains in every vehicle-controlled AD trial; the only plausible failure is an unusually high vehicle response in a small (~80 per arm) moderate-AD sample.
rationale: Ruxolitinib 1.5% cream beat vehicle on EASI75 by roughly 35-50 points in TRuE-AD1, TRuE-AD2 and the pediatric TRuE-AD3. Here the population has failed topical steroids or calcineurin inhibitors, which may lower both arms, but the effect remains far beyond what 80 per arm needs. Primary completion passed in August 2026, so a congress abstract, earnings mention or CT.gov posting by mid-2027 is plausible.

assumptions.claim: In TRuE-AD1 and TRuE-AD2, EASI75 at week 8 was 62.1% and 61.8% with ruxolitinib 1.5% cream versus 24.6% and 14.4% with vehicle.
assumptions.source: Papp et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2021

assumptions.claim: In children aged 2-11 (TRuE-AD3), ruxolitinib cream achieved IGA treatment success at week 8 far more often than vehicle (about 56% vs 11%).

reason: Both primaries must be met; weight loss is likely, but a 6-month WOMAC pain co-primary faces a large placebo response and only modest weight-mediated pain relief at that point, unlike semaglutide's 68-week STEP 9 result.
rationale: KBP-336 is a long-acting dual amylin and calcitonin receptor agonist; amylin agonists give 5-8% placebo-adjusted weight loss by 6 months, so the weight primary is likely met (about 0.9). The WOMAC pain co-primary is harder: STEP 9 showed pain benefit with about 10 points of placebo-adjusted weight loss over 68 weeks, while here the loss is smaller and only 6 months long, and oral calcitonin failed in OA. I put pain at about 0.5, giving 0.42 overall.
evidence: Oral salmon calcitonin knee OA phase 3 (Karsdal 2015)

assumptions.claim: In STEP 9, semaglutide reduced WOMAC pain by 41.7 versus 27.5 points with placebo at 68 weeks, with weight loss of 13.7% versus 3.2%.
Cagrilintide 4.5 mg weekly reduced body weight by 10.8% versus 3.0% with placebo at 26 weeks.

reason: Enrolment is closed and the registered primary completion is close, so the trial should finish near schedule; Sanofi posts results near the 12-month deadline, which falls after the read date.
rationale: Active, not recruiting, with infant follow-up ending around the December 2026 date; Sanofi keeps records current, so a modest slip risk remains (the SAE window to day 517 hints at possible extension). Posting results is due roughly December 2027, after the August 2027 read date. No known safety signal for PCV21 makes a stop unlikely.

reason: With 60 patients per arm and a Day-14 mortality near 10-12%, no plausible antibiotic effect could show significant superiority on mortality against meropenem; the phase 2 is likely descriptive.
rationale: Phase 2, 120 patients, active meropenem control, all-cause mortality primary. Day-14 mortality with meropenem in HABP/VABP trials is about 12% (APEKS-NP), so the trial cannot detect a mortality difference; new beta-lactams match rather than beat meropenem on mortality. Any report is likely descriptive or a non-inferiority-style claim, which does not count as meeting a superiority objective. Hengrui rarely publicizes phase 2 anti-infective results quickly.

assumptions.claim: In APEKS-NP, Day-14 all-cause mortality was 11.6% with meropenem and 12.4% with cefiderocol in HABP/VABP.
assumptions.source: Wunderink et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021 (APEKS-NP)

assumptions.claim: In ASPECT-NP, 28-day all-cause mortality was about 24-25% in both ceftolozane-tazobactam and meropenem arms in ventilated HABP/VABP.
assumptions.source: Kollef et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2019 (ASPECT-NP)

reason: Plasma kallikrein blockade is validated (lanadelumab, garadacimab); the only realistic risk is that the extended Q3M/Q6M dosing loses coverage late in the interval, but even a 60% reduction would be significant here.
rationale: Navenibart is a long-acting anti-plasma-kallikrein antibody; phase 1b/2 ALPHA-STAR showed roughly 90-95% attack reductions from baseline.
