Lanadelumab (HELP) and garadacimab (VANGUARD) achieved about 87% reductions vs placebo with placebo rates near 2 attacks/month. With ~78 placebo patients and a large expected effect, power is near certain. Astria guided topline in early 2027, so a public result by mid-2027 is very likely.

assumptions.claim: In HELP, the placebo arm had a mean attack rate of 1.97 attacks/month and lanadelumab 300 mg q2w reduced attacks by 87%.
In VANGUARD, garadacimab reduced the mean monthly attack rate by about 87% vs placebo (placebo about 2.0 attacks/month).
In ALPHA-STAR, navenibart reduced mean monthly attack rates by about 90% or more from baseline.

reason: Functional upper-abdominal pain responds strongly to placebo over four weeks, so a modest choleretic/spasmolytic effect may not separate on VAS.
rationale: 4-MUST appears to be a 4-methylumbelliferone (hymecromone-related) product; hymecromone is a modest choleretic/antispasmodic. Placebo responses in functional biliary/dyspeptic pain are large, so separation of 6-10 mm on VAS is plausible but uncertain. Russian sponsor trials that become public early tend to be reported as positive, which lifts the conditional probability. Public results by mid-2027 are unlikely since the trial was still recruiting in late 2026.

assumptions.claim: Hymecromone (4-methylumbelliferone) is marketed in Russia as a choleretic/antispasmodic for biliary dyskinesia.

reason: Idiopathic hypersomnia patients have intact orexin signalling, so an orexin-2 agonist may give a smaller ESS benefit than in narcolepsy, and a 30-patient-per-arm design leaves little margin.
rationale: Alixorexton (ALKS 2680) is an orexin-2 agonist with strong ESS and MWT effects in NT1 (Vibrance-1) and positive data in NT2 (Vibrance-2). IH lacks orexin deficiency, so effects should be smaller, but orexin agonism is wake-promoting broadly. With about 30 per arm and an ESS SD near 5, a 4-5 point placebo-adjusted difference at the top dose would be significant; one dose suffices. Alkermes reports topline promptly.

assumptions.claim: Alixorexton showed statistically significant ESS and MWT improvements vs placebo in narcolepsy type 1 in Vibrance-1.
The ALKS 2680 phase 1b study included an idiopathic hypersomnia cohort with dose-related MWT improvements.

reason: Adjunctive GAD trials have large placebo-plus-antidepressant HAM-A responses (around 10 points in 6 weeks), which swamp modest add-on effects; many adjunct trials have failed.
rationale: Adjunctive treatment of GAD after inadequate antidepressant response is a hard setting: quetiapine XR adjunct failed, pregabalin adjunct gave small gains. Placebo HAM-A drops near 10 points at 6 weeks. ABBV-932 has no public efficacy data. Power is reasonable for a 2.5-point difference, but true effects are often smaller. The trial was still recruiting in late October 2026, so timing slips and AbbVie rarely publicizes phase 2 psychiatry readouts quickly.

assumptions.claim: Adjunctive pregabalin added to SSRI/SNRI in GAD non-responders produced a statistically significant but small HAM-A advantage over placebo.
assumptions.source: Rickels et al., Am J Psychiatry 2012

assumptions.claim: Adjunctive quetiapine XR did not separate from placebo on HAM-A in GAD patients with inadequate SSRI/SNRI response.

reason: A potent URAT1 inhibitor against placebo cannot plausibly miss on serum urate; the only risk is heavy dropout from gout flares counted as non-response, which would shrink but not erase the difference.
rationale: AR882 (pozdeutinurad) is a potent URAT1 inhibitor; phase 2b showed most patients on 75 mg reaching sUA below 6 mg/dL. URAT1 inhibitors (lesinurad, verinurad, dotinurad) all beat placebo on sUA targets. Placebo response stays low, even with background allopurinol (about 28% in CLEAR 1). With about 289 per arm the trial is massively powered. The trial is complete, so a topline release in early 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: In CLEAR 1, placebo plus allopurinol reached sUA below 6 mg/dL at month 6 in about 28% of patients.
In the AR882 phase 2b trial, a large majority of patients on 75 mg reached sUA below 6 mg/dL.
assumptions.source: Arthrosi AR882 phase 2b results, ACR Convergence 2022

reason: Three-arm PK similarity with about 60 patients per arm across two AUC intervals; higher-than-expected between-patient variability or a small manufacturing difference could push a 90% CI outside the margin.
rationale: Biosimilar PK equivalence studies by experienced developers succeed in most cases; Sandoz has a strong biosimilar track record, including the natalizumab biosimilar. Ocrelizumab PK is moderately variable, and three pairwise comparisons over two AUC intervals add some failure risk. Sandoz rarely press-releases PK similarity results; disclosure more likely at a late-2027 congress or with a filing.

assumptions.claim: Sandoz's natalizumab biosimilar showed equivalence to Tysabri in relapsing MS in the Antelope trial.

reason: If enrolled patients were largely prior PPI non-responders, acid suppression with vonoprazan may induce histologic remission in few of them, shrinking the gap to placebo.
rationale: Acid suppression induces histologic remission in about half of patients with esophageal eosinophilia (PPI meta-analysis), and vonoprazan is a stronger acid suppressor; Japanese series suggest similar or better responses. Placebo histologic response in EoE trials is typically under 10%. With ~48 per arm, a 25-30 point difference gives high power. Main uncertainty is whether the population is enriched for PPI non-responders.

assumptions.claim: PPIs induce histologic remission in about 50% of patients with esophageal eosinophilia.
assumptions.source: Lucendo et al., Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2016

assumptions.claim: In LIBERTY EoE TREET Part A, about 5% of placebo patients reached peak eosinophils of 6/hpf or fewer at week 24.

reason: B7-H4 is not used to select patients, so if responses concentrate in high expressers the unselected PFS benefit could fall short, though chemotherapy controls in platinum-resistant disease are weak.
rationale: Single-agent chemotherapy in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer gives median PFS of only 3.5-4 months (AURELIA, MIRASOL). HS-20089, a B7-H4 ADC with a topoisomerase-1 payload, showed objective responses in roughly a third or more of heavily treated ovarian patients in phase 1. ADCs like mirvetuximab beat chemo with PFS HR 0.65. With about 468 patients and BICR PFS, a HR near 0.6 would be clearly significant.

assumptions.claim: In MIRASOL, investigator's-choice chemotherapy gave a median PFS of 3.98 months and mirvetuximab reduced the hazard of progression with HR 0.65.
In AURELIA, chemotherapy alone gave a median PFS of 3.4 months in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.
assumptions.source: Pujade-Lauraine et al., J Clin Oncol 2014 (AURELIA)

reason: A single Ixo-vec dose plus as-needed aflibercept may trail fixed q8w aflibercept by one to two letters, especially in treatment-naive eyes, and with about 155 per arm the lower confidence bound can cross an unstated margin of roughly 4 to 5 letters.
rationale: Non-inferiority versus aflibercept with about 155 per arm gives a standard error near 1.4 letters. Phase 2 LUNA and phase 1 OPTIC showed BCVA roughly maintained with a large cut in injection burden, but maintenance driven by supplemental injections tends to lag fixed dosing by 1-2 letters, and treatment-naive eyes are new territory for Ixo-vec. With a likely margin of 4-4.5 letters and a true difference near -1.5, non-inferiority is about a coin flip. Lilly's purchase of Adverum suggests some confidence; steroid-drop prophylaxis should limit inflammation-related vision loss.

assumptions.claim: Ixo-vec 6E10 kept mean BCVA within a few letters of baseline at about one year while cutting supplemental anti-VEGF injections by over 80%.
Aflibercept 2 mg every 8 weeks gains about 7 letters at week 48 in treatment-naive nAMD.
Recent nAMD non-inferiority trials versus aflibercept used a 4-letter margin.

reason: Only failure path is QCZ484 knocking down angiotensinogen less than zilebesiran or the highest-dose arm being small enough that a modest drop in 24-hour ABPM misses significance.
rationale: QCZ484 is a twice-yearly angiotensinogen siRNA. The same mechanism (zilebesiran) cut 24-hour ambulatory SBP by 14-17 mmHg versus placebo at month 3 in KARDIA-1 with a similar washout design, and placebo arms in such trials drift upward. Even with ~70-80 patients in the top-dose arm and an SD near 13 mmHg, a placebo-adjusted fall of 8 mmHg or more is highly significant. Novartis moved it into a 396-patient phase 2b, implying good phase 1 knockdown.

assumptions.claim: Zilebesiran reduced 24-hour mean ambulatory SBP by about 14 to 17 mmHg versus placebo at month 3.
The placebo arm's 24-hour SBP rose by several mmHg at month 3 after antihypertensive washout.

reason: Superiority over placebo is near certain with about 1,900 per arm; the only realistic threat is GI-driven discontinuation diluting the treatment-policy estimate, which affects the size of the effect, not significance.
rationale: MariTide (GIPR antagonist plus GLP-1 agonist, monthly) gave up to about 20% weight loss at 52 weeks in phase 2 without plateau, versus about 2-3% on placebo. A 72-week phase 3 with dose escalation and 3,853 patients has essentially full power for superiority; the open question is only the magnitude (treatment-policy placebo-adjusted loss of roughly 15-19%).

assumptions.claim: MariTide produced up to about 20% mean weight loss at 52 weeks in adults with obesity without type 2 diabetes, with no plateau.
Placebo arms in 72-week obesity trials lost about 2.4-3.1% of body weight.

reason: With about 550 per arm, superiority on weight is near certain; GI-related discontinuation could shrink the treatment-policy effect but not remove significance.
rationale: In phase 2, MariTide gave up to about 17% weight loss at 52 weeks in type 2 diabetes with large HbA1c falls. People with diabetes lose less, so I expect a placebo-adjusted 72-week difference near 12-13%, similar to tirzepatide in SURMOUNT-2. With 1,105 patients the trial is massively powered for superiority.

assumptions.claim: MariTide produced up to about 17% mean weight loss at 52 weeks in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes.
Tirzepatide 15 mg gave 14.7% vs 3.2% weight loss with placebo at 72 weeks in type 2 diabetes.

reason: Placebo PFS after VEGFR TKI failure is about 2 months, so any active multikinase/MET inhibitor should separate; failure needs AL2846 to have little activity in TKI-refractory disease.
rationale: Second-line RAIR-DTC versus placebo is a favourable setting: in COSMIC-311 cabozantinib cut PFS risk by about 78% against a placebo median of 1.9 months. AL2846 is a MET/VEGFR-family TKI from the anlotinib originator, and CTTQ's placebo-controlled phase 3s in refractory settings have mostly succeeded. With 144 patients and a likely HR near 0.3-0.4, power is high; residual risk is weaker-than-expected activity after anlotinib or lenvatinib.

assumptions.claim: Placebo median PFS after prior VEGFR TKI in RAIR-DTC was 1.9 months.
Cabozantinib gave a PFS hazard ratio of about 0.22 versus placebo after prior VEGFR TKI.

reason: With about 47 per arm and KCCQ-CSS change SD near 17-19, a true 7-point gain gives only about 50% power per dose; weight is sure to be met, so the KCCQ co-primary decides.
rationale: Incretin weight loss improved KCCQ-CSS by about 7-8 points versus placebo in STEP-HFpEF and SUMMIT. Mazdutide 6 mg gives similar or greater weight loss, so a 6-8 point gain is plausible, but with 47 per arm the standard error is about 3.7 points. Both primaries (KCCQ-CSS and weight) must be met; weight is certain. Two doses each get a chance, and Innovent is more likely to publicise early if KCCQ is significant, lifting the conditional probability to about 0.6.

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide improved KCCQ-CSS by 7.8 points versus placebo at 52 weeks in obesity-related HFpEF.
Tirzepatide improved KCCQ-CSS by about 6.9 points versus placebo in HFpEF with obesity.
Mazdutide 6 mg produced about 14% weight loss at 48 weeks in Chinese adults with obesity.

reason: A coarse 4-point pain scale in a 72-patient trial leaves little room: by day 8 most attacks resolve on etoricoxib alone, so any steroid benefit shows only at day 2, if at all.
rationale: Adding a corticosteroid to an NSAID should speed relief of acute gout, but steroids and NSAIDs are similarly effective alone, so the add-on gain is modest. With 36 per arm and a 4-point Likert scale, a day-2 difference is plausible but day-8 pain will be near floor in both arms. Small sponsor trials that get published tend to report the combination as superior, which lifts the conditional estimate to about even.
evidence: Rainer, Ann Intern Med 2016 (prednisolone vs indomethacin)

assumptions.claim: Oral prednisolone and indomethacin give similar pain relief in acute gout.
Etoricoxib 120 mg matched indomethacin for pain relief in acute gout over 8 days.

reason: Fully enrolled small-sponsor phase 2 with 53-week follow-up; likely to finish near its March 2027 date, with results posting and record updates lagging.
rationale: Status is active, not recruiting, so the last patient's week-53 visit should fall around the registered March 2027 date; a small sponsor may slip a little or leave the date estimated (void). Results posting by August 2027 is unlikely given the 12-month window and small-company habits. The odd safety-only primary (CTCAE toxicity) could be rewritten toward efficacy at completion, a small amendment risk.

reason: ePRO monitoring effects on global QoL at 3 months are small (a few points) and diluted by usual-care symptom management in French and German centres and by missing questionnaires, so even 1,458 patients may not show significance.
rationale: Remote symptom monitoring improved HRQoL in Basch 2016 and PRO-TECT, but mean differences were small and later trials (eRAPID, CAPRI) were mixed. With about 729 per arm and an SD near 20, a 3-point gain is detectable, but missing QLQ-C30 data and a broad all-stage population dilute it. The sponsor-run design and large sample keep the chance near even. Still recruiting with a January 2027 registered date, results by mid-2027 are unlikely.
evidence: Denis, JAMA 2019 (web-based follow-up in lung cancer)

assumptions.claim: Electronic PRO symptom monitoring improved HRQoL at 3 months versus usual care in community oncology practices.
Weekly ePRO reporting improved QoL and survival in a single-centre randomized trial.

reason: Dupilumab with a 600 mg loading dose may act faster in CSU than its slow week-24 curves suggest, narrowing the week-4 gap below what 205 per arm can detect.
rationale: Remibrutinib, a BTK inhibitor, acts within days: in REMIX-1/2 UAS7 separated from placebo by week 1-2 and was near its plateau by week 4. Dupilumab's CSU benefit builds slowly over 12-24 weeks, so at week 4 its arm should resemble a modestly enhanced placebo. A gap of about 4-5 UAS7 points with an SD near 11 and 205 per arm gives over 90% power. Novartis chose the early time point deliberately; the main risk is a quicker dupilumab onset.

assumptions.claim: Remibrutinib 25 mg twice daily reduced UAS7 significantly versus placebo from week 1-2 onward.
Dupilumab reduced UAS7 by about 20.5 versus 12.0 points with placebo at week 24 in omalizumab-naive CSU.

reason: Phase 1/2a seizure reductions were open-label on top of multiple ASMs; against a sham procedure the true week-28 effect of a slowly building Nav1.1 upregulation could be smaller than the open-label signal suggested.
rationale: Zorevunersen upregulates Nav1.1 from the wild-type SCN1A allele; open-label MONARCH/ADMIRAL and extensions showed ~40-50% median convulsive seizure reductions on top of multiple ASMs, deepening over time, with Vineland gains. Dravet placebo responses run about -10 to -20%, so a ~30-point median difference is plausible and 85 per arm gives good power for a rank-based test. Risks: open-label inflation, sham-procedure response, week 28 possibly early for a slowly building effect. Topline likely waits for week-52 data (2H 2027), so few results by June 2027.

assumptions.claim: In GWPCARE1 the placebo arm's median convulsive-seizure frequency fell by about 13% versus about 39% with cannabidiol.
Fenfluramine 0.7 mg/kg/day reduced mean monthly convulsive seizure frequency 62.3% more than placebo in Dravet syndrome.
In phase 1/2a, two or three 70 mg doses of zorevunersen gave a median reduction in convulsive seizure frequency of about 43% at 3 months after the last dose.

reason: The open-label phase 2 portion (24 children rolled over from ACCEL) runs to its 26-week AHV readout, but the record also covers a placebo-controlled phase 3 portion that will likely extend dates and enrollment.
rationale: The record is a combined phase 2/3 protocol whose registered dates and 24-patient enrollment reflect only the open-label phase 2 part; folding in the double-blind phase 3 portion (ages 3-17) would push primary completion well past May 2027 and may add a placebo-comparison primary. BridgeBio is well funded and committed to infigratinib in achondroplasia and hypochondroplasia, so stopping is unlikely; results posting before primary completion plus a year is unlikely.

reason: QLM3003's mechanism and phase 2 data are not public; if it behaves like a weak PDE4-type topical, an emollient ointment vehicle with a 20-25% EASI-75 rate could leave a gap too small to separate.
rationale: Vehicle-controlled phase 3 trials of topicals in mild-to-moderate AD (ruxolitinib, tapinarof, roflumilast, crisaborole) nearly all met their primaries, with vehicle EASI-75 rates of about 14-25% and drug-vehicle gaps of 20-45 points. Even a modest 15-point gap is well powered at 120 per arm. Risks are an unknown, possibly weak molecule and an ointment vehicle that raises the control rate. Qilu is unlisted and rarely issues toplines, so a public statement by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Crisaborole AD-301/302, Paller et al., JAAD 2016

assumptions.claim: In TRuE-AD1/2, vehicle EASI-75 at week 8 was about 14-25% versus about 62% with ruxolitinib 1.5% cream.
In ADORING 1/2, tapinarof 1% cream gave week-8 EASI-75 of about 56-59% versus 21-23% with vehicle.
In crisaborole 2% ointment phase 3 trials, ISGA success was about 31-33% versus 18-25% with vehicle ointment.

reason: A first-in-class oral epigenetic regulator with only phase 1 data must beat placebo on ADAS-cog12 within 26 weeks, when placebo decline is only 1-2 points and most novel AD mechanisms have shown no cognitive separation.
rationale: Novel-mechanism oral candidates in mild-to-moderate AD have a poor phase 2 record, and a 26-week ADAS-cog12 comparison at ~87 per arm only detects differences of about 2.5 points, larger than most agents produce. Placebo decline over 6 months is small, limiting room for benefit, and ONO-2020 has no published efficacy signal. The trial completed in July 2026; Ono may disclose via pipeline updates or AD/PD/AAIC, and ClinicalTrials.gov results fall due around July 2027.
evidence: Atri et al., JAMA 2018 (idalopirdine phase 3 trials)
Cummings et al., Alzheimer's disease drug development pipeline 2024

assumptions.claim: In three 24-week idalopirdine phase 3 trials in mild-to-moderate AD on cholinesterase inhibitors, placebo ADAS-cog change was small and no dose separated from placebo.

reason: Semaglutide 2.4 mg is a strong comparator for both weight and liver fat; the liver-fat co-primary could show a smaller-than-expected gap, and open-label dropout could dilute differences, though both risks look small.
rationale: Mazdutide 9 mg (GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist) lowered weight ~18% at 48 weeks in Chinese studies versus ~12% for semaglutide 2.4 mg in STEP 7's mainly Chinese population, so ~5-6 points superiority at 240 per arm is near-certain on weight. The glucagon component adds hepatic fat oxidation and mazdutide cut liver fat by roughly 70-80% in earlier studies, making liver-fat superiority over semaglutide very likely too. Both co-primaries must be met. Innovent reports toplines promptly, likely in 1H 2027.
evidence: STEP 7, Mu et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2024

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly reduced body weight by about 12% at week 44 in STEP 7, a mainly Chinese population.
assumptions.source: Mu et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2024 (STEP 7)

assumptions.claim: In GLORY-1, mazdutide 6 mg reduced body weight by about 13-14% at week 48 versus little change with placebo.
Mazdutide 9 mg reduced body weight by about 18% at week 48 in a Chinese phase 2 study of adults with obesity.

reason: Part B (90 patients) depends on process-2 drug and is still recruiting with a 52-week safety primary, so the November 2026 primary completion date cannot hold and will be pushed into 2027-2028.
rationale: Still recruiting in October 2026 with a 52-week primary safety window means primary completion cannot come before late 2027, so the registered 2026-11 date will be revised (or voided if left as estimated). Pacira is committed to PCRX-201 as its main gene-therapy asset, though manufacturing dependency adds some risk of a pause or termination. No results posting expected before primary completion.

reason: With 25 per arm and a noisy 24-week ICARS change in a slowly progressive, heterogeneous disease, only a ~4-point difference is detectable, larger than a metabolic-substrate therapy is likely to produce in six months.
rationale: GLM101 delivers mannose-1-phosphate to bypass PMM2 deficiency; earlier open-label work showed glycosylation biomarker effects but no controlled clinical efficacy. ICARS change over 24 weeks has an SD near 5 points, and 25 per arm detects only ~4-point differences, while practice and placebo improvements narrow the gap. Rare-disease phase 2b trials by small sponsors with clinician-rated scales succeed infrequently. Primary completion was August 2026, so a topline from this private sponsor is plausible in late 2026 to mid-2027.
evidence: AZATAX acetazolamide in PMM2-CDG, Martinez-Monseny et al., Genet Med 2019

assumptions.claim: In the open-label AZATAX trial, acetazolamide improved ICARS scores in PMM2-CDG patients over 6 months.

reason: Both DIAMOND phase 3 trials failed because placebo PANSS improvements of 14-19 points matched ulotaront; stricter enrolment may help but a 3-5 point true effect leaves this trial near coin-flip power.
rationale: Ulotaront's positive phase 2 (-7.5 PANSS vs placebo at week 4) was not replicated in DIAMOND 1 and 2, where placebo responses of -14 to -19 points swamped 50-100 mg effects of at most ~4 points. This trial adds hospitalised patients with prior good response and Japanese sites, which may temper placebo response, but a plausible 100 mg effect of 3-5 points gives roughly 40-60% power at ~179 per arm with two-dose multiplicity. TAAR1 class evidence (ralmitaront) is also weak. Sumitomo/Otsuka should announce topline by early 2027.
evidence: Sumitomo Pharma/Otsuka DIAMOND topline release, July 2023

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 SEP361-201 trial, PANSS total fell 17.2 points with ulotaront versus 9.7 with placebo at week 4.
In DIAMOND 1 the placebo arm improved by about 19.3 PANSS points at week 6, similar to or more than ulotaront 50 mg (16.9) and 75 mg (19.6).
In DIAMOND 2, ulotaront 100 mg improved PANSS by about 18.1 versus 14.3 with placebo at week 6, not statistically significant.

reason: The study was closed out early with only 7 of the planned patients and its completion date has passed, so the record will likely be closed as terminated (or completed under the amended protocol) with Novartis posting safety results around the one-year deadline.
rationale: Enrollment stopped at 7 and the protocol was cut back to a safety-only primary; with primary and study completion both on 2026-10-15, the next status update is likely Terminated (early closure) though Novartis sometimes marks amended early closures as Completed. Novartis reliably posts results near the 12-month deadline (October 2027), so posting by end of August 2027 is possible but less likely than not. The safety primary is unlikely to change further.

reason: Enrollment is complete and the booster-response primary falls in early 2027, so the US-government-funded trial should finish close to schedule, with results posted only after the one-year window.
rationale: Active, not recruiting with a February 2027 primary completion two weeks after the third vaccination; vaccine immunogenicity trials by Bavarian Nordic with DoD JPM CBRN funding usually run to schedule, though two-stage designs can slip a few months. Termination is unlikely given government funding. Results posting is due about a year after primary completion, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

reason: Placebo durable response in refractory chronic ITP is near zero, so the only real risk is that TQB3473 gives a weak durable response at the dose chosen.
rationale: TQB3473 is understood to be an oral SYK inhibitor; the same class (sovleplenib, ESLIM-01) gave 48% vs 0% durable response in Chinese chronic ITP with the same weeks 14-24, 4-of-6-visits endpoint. Placebo durable response in pretreated ITP with platelets under 30 is 0-3% across fostamatinib, rilzabrutinib and TPO-RA trials, so even a modest drug effect (15-20 points) is significant with about 100 per arm. The trial is still recruiting, so the March 2027 completion will probably slip and a readout before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In ESLIM-01, the SYK inhibitor sovleplenib gave a durable response (weeks 14-24) of 48.4% vs 0% with placebo in Chinese adults with chronic ITP.
assumptions.source: ESLIM-01, Hu et al., Lancet Haematol 2024

assumptions.claim: In the pooled fostamatinib FIT1/FIT2 trials, stable platelet response was 18% vs 2% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Bussel et al., Am J Hematol 2018

reason: Vadadustat usually leaves hemoglobin a little lower than ESA, and three-times-weekly dosing may lose some potency, so the lower confidence bound could cross a non-inferiority margin; a true superiority test would almost surely fail.
rationale: This pragmatic open-label trial is most likely a non-inferiority test (Akebia wants three-times-weekly dosing on the label), though the record gives no margin. In INNO2VATE, vadadustat was non-inferior to darbepoetin with Hb differences of -0.17 to -0.31 g/dL. With about 175 per arm the SE is about 0.11 g/dL, so a margin of -0.5 or -0.75 is likely met unless TIW dosing underperforms. I give about 20% weight to a superiority hypothesis that would fail. The trial completed in August 2026, so a topline release in late 2026 or early 2027 is likely.
evidence: Haase et al. vadadustat QD/TIW phase 2 in hemodialysis (Nephrol Dial Transplant 2019)

assumptions.claim: In INNO2VATE's prevalent dialysis cohort, the difference in mean Hb change for vadadustat minus darbepoetin was about -0.17 g/dL, within a -0.75 g/dL non-inferiority margin.
In a 16-week phase 2 study, hemodialysis patients converted from ESA to vadadustat three times weekly kept mean Hb near baseline.
assumptions.source: Haase et al., Nephrol Dial Transplant 2019

reason: The control arm is untreated at week 12 and will have almost no responders, so failure would need the strict undetectable-plus-ALT-normal response at week 48 to fall far below phase 2 levels.
rationale: In phase 2 SOLSTICE, monthly tobevibart plus elebsiran suppressed HDV RNA below LLOQ in most participants by week 48, often with ALT normalization. Untreated controls almost never reach HDV RNA undetectability with normal ALT (2% in the MYR301 delayed arm at week 48). Even if the strict composite reaches only 30-45%, the gap against roughly 0-2% at week 12 is highly significant with 62 per arm. Enrollment is complete with primary completion at end-2026, and Vir is likely to release topline data in the first half of 2027.

assumptions.claim: In MYR301, the combined response in the delayed-treatment arm at week 48 was about 2%.
In phase 2 SOLSTICE, a majority of participants on monthly tobevibart plus elebsiran had HDV RNA below LLOQ at week 48.

reason: With about six patients per arm and two efficacy primaries (PS volume and stool volume) that would both need significance, a formal win is very unlikely even if crofelemer reduces losses somewhat.
rationale: The trial has 18 patients split three ways, and it calls its efficacy outcomes 'preliminary'. Both efficacy primaries (PS volume and stool volume) would need significance at 6 vs 6, which is implausible given SDs of about 3 L/week in PS-volume trials. Crofelemer's support comes from small open-label proof-of-concept reports of 10-25% PS reductions. Jaguar/Napo is likely to describe the results as 'positive' without a formal significance statement. Still recruiting in a rare population, so completion will probably slip past mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: In STEPS, placebo-treated SBS-IF patients reduced PS volume by about 2.3 L/week at week 24 under a protocolized weaning algorithm, vs 4.4 L/week with teduglutide.

reason: Placebo plus standard skincare cuts lesion counts substantially in acne trials, and all three co-primaries (inflammatory count, total count, ISGA 0/1) must be significant, with the ISGA success-rate endpoint the most fragile.
rationale: Combined oral contraceptives consistently beat placebo on acne lesion counts, by about 4-5 inflammatory lesions at cycle 6 in drospirenone, norgestimate and levonorgestrel trials, and cyproterone acetate is the most antiandrogenic progestin. With 354 vs 177 patients, a 4-5 lesion difference is highly significant for both count endpoints. ISGA success (about 20% vs 10% in past COC trials) is likely but less certain, so the three co-primaries lower the probability. Started August 2026, so the February 2027 completion is unrealistic and a public result by mid-2027 is very unlikely.
evidence: Koltun et al. DRSP/EE20 acne trial (Contraception 2008)
Maloney et al. DRSP/EE20 acne (Obstet Gynecol 2008)
Arowojolu et al. Cochrane review of COCs for acne (2012)

assumptions.claim: In placebo-controlled acne trials of drospirenone 3 mg/EE 20 ug, the pill reduced inflammatory lesions by roughly 4-5 more than placebo at cycle 6, with ISGA success about 15-21% vs 4-9%.
assumptions.source: Koltun et al., Contraception 2008; Maloney et al., Obstet Gynecol 2008

reason: Faricimab after four monthly loading doses already gives about 9-10 letters by week 16, so a bispecific VEGF/complement drug is very unlikely to show statistically superior vision gains in 50 vs 50 patients.
rationale: Head-to-head anti-VEGF trials in DME almost never show superior BCVA at matched loading, because the VEGF pathway drives the gain and complement has little role in DME. Faricimab gains about 9 letters by week 16. With about 50 per arm and a between-patient SD near 8.5 letters, a difference above about 3.4 letters would be needed for significance, but the expected difference is close to zero. This phase 2 is most likely meant to show comparability, which counts as not met under a superiority reading.

assumptions.claim: In YOSEMITE and RHINE, faricimab gave mean BCVA gains of about 10-11 letters at one year in DME, most of it reached during the monthly loading phase.

reason: Single-injection safety trial, fully enrolled, with a 6-month endpoint; it should complete around end-2026, but a small cell-therapy sponsor could slow follow-up or results posting.
rationale: The trial is active, not recruiting, with 31 patients and a 6-month primary endpoint, so a primary completion around December 2026 is realistic. US results posting is due about 12 months after completion, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. Safety primary outcomes rarely change.

reason: Insulin optimization in the placebo arm and insulin down-titration on tirzepatide (to avoid hypoglycemia) could shrink the HbA1c gap in type 1 diabetes, though about 450 per arm leaves a large safety margin.
rationale: Incretin drugs lower HbA1c less in type 1 than in type 2 diabetes (liraglutide about 0.2 points vs placebo in ADJUNCT ONE). Tirzepatide is more potent and causes weight loss of about 15%, and observational T1D data show HbA1c falls of about 0.5 points. With about 905 patients and an SD near 0.9, the trial can detect a 0.2-point difference with near certainty. Primary completion is November 2026, and Lilly usually reports topline results by its Q1 earnings or ADA.
evidence: ADJUNCT ONE liraglutide in T1D (Diabetes Care 2016)

assumptions.claim: In ADJUNCT ONE, liraglutide 1.8 mg reduced HbA1c by about 0.2 percentage points more than placebo in type 1 diabetes at 52 weeks.
assumptions.source: Mathieu et al., Diabetes Care 2016 (ADJUNCT ONE)

assumptions.claim: Added to basal insulin in type 2 diabetes, tirzepatide reduced HbA1c by 2.1-2.4 percentage points vs 0.9 with placebo at 40 weeks.

reason: Small 4-site phase 2 still recruiting with a 30-day post-transplant safety endpoint; the remaining enrollment by early 2027 is tight for a small sponsor, so completion may slip.
rationale: The trial is still recruiting at 4 US sites toward 49 patients, with primary completion registered for March 2027. Each patient's endpoint is short (day 30 after transplant), so finishing on time depends only on enrollment, which often slips at small sponsors. Results posting is unlikely before the read date.

reason: Curettage, seton removal and closure with saline give combined remission rates of 35-45% in control arms, which wiped out the stem-cell effect in ADMIRE-CD II.
rationale: The best evidence for this setting comes from darvadstrocel. ADMIRE-CD met its endpoint narrowly (50% vs 34%), but the larger ADMIRE-CD II failed (48.8% vs 46.2%) because the surgical control arm responded strongly. TH-SC01 is a mesenchymal cell product with no published phase 3 benchmark, and 114 per arm only detects differences of about 18 points or more. I allow some uplift for Chinese single-sponsor trials. The trial is still recruiting with a December 2026 completion date, so results before mid-2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In ADMIRE-CD, combined remission at week 24 was 50% with darvadstrocel vs 34% with placebo (p=0.024).
In ADMIRE-CD II, combined remission at week 24 was 48.8% vs 46.2% with placebo, not significant.

reason: Completed Boehringer phase 2 with a short 16-week design; the main uncertainty is whether results are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov before the 31 Aug 2027 read date, about 12.5 months after primary completion.
rationale: Status is already completed (primary completion 14 Aug 2026), so termination is very unlikely. Boehringer generally complies with the 12-month FDAAA results window for multinational trials, but posting often lands near the deadline and CT.gov quality-control review can push the public posting date past 31 Aug 2027. Primary outcome changes after completion are uncommon; minor restructuring at results entry is possible.

reason: The rationale rests on a post hoc signal of reduced coronary FAI in high-inflammation psoriasis patients; an anti-oxLDL antibody may not move a noisy perivascular imaging score significantly within 24 weeks in 120 per arm.
rationale: Orticumab's evidence for lowering coronary inflammation comes from a subgroup of a psoriasis phase 2a, which often fails to replicate. FAI-score is prognostic, but drug-induced change is not well characterised beyond biologics in psoriasis. Still recruiting in Oct 2026 with a 24-week endpoint, so the Feb 2027 primary completion will slip and topline is unlikely before late 2027. Small sponsor adds funding risk, and a phase 3 by end-2027 is implausible.
evidence: Elnabawi et al., JAMA Cardiology 2019 (biologics and FAI in psoriasis)

assumptions.claim: Perivascular fat attenuation index around coronary arteries predicts cardiac mortality independently of standard risk factors.
Biologic therapy for psoriasis was associated with a reduction in coronary perivascular FAI after one year.

reason: APRIL-only blockade spares BAFF, the main driver of B-cell activity in Sjogren's, and ESSDAI trials show large placebo responses; with about 40 per arm, a modest 1-2 point difference is unlikely to reach significance.
rationale: Recent Sjogren's agents (ianalumab, dazodalibep, nipocalimab) separated from placebo on ESSDAI by roughly 1-2.5 points, with placebo improving 2-4 points. Sibeprenlimab lowers immunoglobulins but targets APRIL alone, so a smaller effect is likely. An 83-patient proof-of-concept trial has power only for a large effect (about 3 points with SD 4.5). ESSPRI rarely separates. Otsuka seldom press-releases phase 2 toplines, so disclosure by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Telitacicept phase 2 in primary Sjogren's, China, 2024

assumptions.claim: Ianalumab improved ESSDAI over placebo by only about 1 point in its phase 3 programme.
Placebo arms in recent Sjogren's ESSDAI trials improved by roughly 2-4 points at about 6 months.

reason: CRR is likely to improve, as with polatuzumab-R-GemOx, but OS is a second primary outcome that will be immature at any 2027 readout, and the round requires all primary outcomes met.
rationale: Adding a CD79b ADC or bispecific to R-GemOx raised complete response rates substantially in POLARGO, STARGLO and SUNMO; R-GemOx alone gave about 25-41% CR. A 20-point gain with 141 per arm gives over 85% power for CRR. The main discount is the dual OS primary, which will be immature, and possible scoring as not met. Hengrui typically discloses via NDA-acceptance filings and congress abstracts, so disclosure by June 2027 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: In STARGLO the complete response rate was about 58.5% with glofitamab-GemOx versus about 25.3% with R-GemOx.
Adding polatuzumab to R-GemOx improved overall survival in transplant-ineligible relapsed/refractory DLBCL.

reason: Fully enrolled 16-week safety study now under Sanofi after the Blueprint acquisition; likely to complete on or near schedule, with results posting near the 12-month deadline in late 2027.
rationale: Active, not recruiting with a 16-week primary window and primary completion on 31 Dec 2026, so a slip of more than 90 days needs late enrolment or an added cohort. Sanofi cited BLU-808 as a rationale for buying Blueprint, so termination is unlikely. Results for a December 2026 primary completion are due by December 2027, and large sponsors usually post near the deadline, so posting by 31 Aug 2027 is unlikely.

reason: GLP-1/glucagon co-agonists produce large MASH-resolution effects; failure would need an unusually high placebo histology response or biopsy-reading noise in about 60 patients per arm.
rationale: Incretin and glucagon co-agonists have shown 30-50 point gains in MASH resolution over placebo (tirzepatide in SYNERGY-NASH, survodutide, pemvidutide). Mazdutide's glucagon component cuts liver fat strongly. With 60 per arm, even a 25-point effect is highly significant. Fibrosis improvement is less certain at this size. Innovent publicises mazdutide data actively, and primary completion was Sept 2026, so a topline or an EASL 2027 presentation by June 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: In SYNERGY-NASH, MASH resolution without fibrosis worsening at week 52 was 44-62% with tirzepatide versus about 10% with placebo.
In ESSENCE, fibrosis improvement without worsening of steatohepatitis was about 37% with semaglutide versus about 22% with placebo at week 72.

reason: Botulinum toxins reliably beat placebo on TWSTRS at week 4, so the risk is that this engineered long-acting toxin is under-dosed in a first dose-finding study in cervical dystonia.
rationale: Pivotal trials of abobotulinum-, incobotulinum-, rimabotulinum- and daxibotulinumtoxin showed 7-10 point TWSTRS gains over placebo at week 4, with SD about 10. With 44 per arm, a 7-point effect gives about 90% power. IPN10200 is a novel recombinant toxin and the doses are exploratory, so the highest dose could fall short. Still recruiting in Oct 2026 against a March 2027 primary completion, and Ipsen tends to disclose at results events, so a readout by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Comella et al. 2011 incobotulinumtoxinA in cervical dystonia
Truong et al. 2005 abobotulinumtoxinA in cervical dystonia

assumptions.claim: Approved botulinum toxin type A products improved TWSTRS total score by roughly 7-10 points more than placebo at week 4-6 in pivotal cervical dystonia trials.
assumptions.source: ASPEN-1 (Comella et al., 2022); Comella et al., Neurology 2011

reason: Endothelin antagonism on top of SGLT2i has a well-replicated albuminuria-lowering effect; failure would need an unexpectedly small effect in this high-proteinuria regional population.
rationale: ZENITH-CKD showed zibotentan 1.5 mg plus dapagliflozin lowering UACR by about a third versus dapagliflozin alone at 12 weeks, and ERAs consistently cut albuminuria 30-40%. With 112 per arm and log-UACR SD about 0.8, a 30% reduction gives z above 3. UPCR tracks UACR closely. This is a regional bridging study for the Eurasian Economic Union, so no press release is expected; public disclosure would mostly come from CT.gov posting around Sept 2027 or a congress abstract.

assumptions.claim: In ZENITH-CKD, zibotentan 1.5 mg plus dapagliflozin reduced UACR by about 34% versus dapagliflozin alone at week 12.

reason: Sham-surgery placebo responses in Parkinson's cell and gene therapy trials have repeatedly erased open-label gains, and diary ON-time is noisy with only 34 sham patients; no readout is possible before 2028.
rationale: Still recruiting in Oct 2026 with a 78-week endpoint, so efficacy data cannot appear before 2028. Any public statement by June 2027 would most likely be a stop, which counts as not met. On the eventual outcome, the open-label phase 1 showed about 2-3 h more good ON-time in the high-dose cohort. Sham-controlled fetal graft and AAV-neurturin trials failed against strong placebo responses, so true success is roughly 35-40%.
evidence: exPDite phase 1 bemdaneprocel, Tabar et al., Nature 2025
Freed et al., NEJM 2001 fetal transplant sham-controlled trial
CERE-120 phase 2, Marks et al., Lancet Neurol 2010

assumptions.claim: Sham-controlled trials of fetal dopaminergic tissue transplantation in Parkinson's disease did not meet their primary endpoints.
assumptions.source: Freed et al., NEJM 2001; Olanow et al., Ann Neurol 2003

assumptions.claim: In the open-label phase 1 of bemdaneprocel, the high-dose cohort showed improvement in ON-time without troublesome dyskinesia at 18 months.

reason: Fully enrolled 76-patient PK study of subcutaneous nivolumab; week-18 trough sampling should finish near the registered February 2027 date, with results posted on the registry only about a year after that.
rationale: Enrollment is complete (active, not recruiting) and the last primary PK sample is at Cycle 7 Day 1 (week 18), so primary completion in early 2027 is achievable. BMS updates its records regularly but usually posts results close to the 12-month deadline, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. Pure PK endpoints rarely change, and termination is unlikely for a sponsor-driven formulation study extending subcutaneous nivolumab to the ipilimumab-chemotherapy regimen.

reason: First-line pembrolizumab already gives roughly 45-55% confirmed responses in Merkel cell carcinoma, so with 59 patients per arm a single-lesion intralesional injection must add about 18 points to reach significance, which is unlikely for an unproven innate-immune plasmid.
rationale: Control pembrolizumab ORR in checkpoint-naive advanced MCC is about 56% in KEYNOTE-017 and 40-50% for avelumab/retifanlimab; strict BICR confirmation persisting to week 24 lowers it to about 45%. IFx-Hu2.0 evidence is small phase 1b data, mostly in checkpoint-refractory patients. A 118-patient trial needs an ~18-point gain. Enrolling 118 first-line MCC patients at 18 US sites by March 2027 is ambitious for a micro-cap sponsor, so an early public result would more likely be a stop than a win.

assumptions.claim: First-line pembrolizumab in advanced Merkel cell carcinoma gave an objective response rate of about 56-58%.
First-line avelumab gave a confirmed ORR of about 40% by independent review in advanced Merkel cell carcinoma.

reason: Ivonescimab's VEGF arm only matches bevacizumab, so the trial depends on PD-1 blockade adding PFS benefit in a mostly microsatellite-stable colorectal population, where CheckMate 9X8 failed and only AtezoTRIBE succeeded.
rationale: Ivonescimab swaps bevacizumab for a PD-1/VEGF bispecific, so benefit hinges on immunotherapy in MSS mCRC: AtezoTRIBE was positive (HR 0.69), CheckMate 9X8 negative. Akeso's China phase 3s have repeatedly beaten active controls (HARMONi-2, HARMONi-6) and early phase 2 ORR with chemotherapy was high. Akeso tends to announce only positive interims promptly, which lifts the conditional probability. Still recruiting in October 2026, so a 2027 H1 readout would need an early interim.

assumptions.claim: Adding atezolizumab to FOLFOXIRI-bevacizumab improved PFS in first-line mCRC (HR about 0.69).
Adding nivolumab to mFOLFOX6-bevacizumab did not improve PFS in first-line mCRC (median about 11.9 months in both arms).
Ivonescimab improved PFS over pembrolizumab in PD-L1-positive advanced NSCLC (HR 0.51).

reason: A muscarinic agonist has no proven antimanic effect, and KarXT's titration and GI side effects may blunt separation within a 3-week inpatient trial where placebo arms often improve 10 or more YMRS points.
rationale: KarXT works in schizophrenia (EMERGENT-2/3, PANSS gains of 8-10 points vs placebo) and M4 agonism lowers striatal dopamine, the target antipsychotics use against mania; the cholinergic hypothesis of mania adds support. But no mania data exist, ARISE failed, titration over the first week cuts into a 3-week window, and mania placebo responses are large (brexpiprazole mania trials failed). Powered for about 4.5 points with SD 11; I give roughly even odds.

assumptions.claim: KarXT improved PANSS total by about 9.6 points more than placebo at week 5 in acute schizophrenia.
Placebo arms in 3-week acute mania trials typically improve YMRS by about 6-12 points.
Discontinuation for adverse events with KarXT was about 6-7% vs 5-6% on placebo in 5-week schizophrenia trials.

reason: Multinational inpatient mania trials with sites in India, China and Eastern Europe often show placebo YMRS drops above 10 points, which can swamp a modest effect from a non-dopamine-blocking drug titrated over the first week.
rationale: Same design and drug as BALSAM-1: KarXT's M4-mediated reduction of striatal dopamine release and schizophrenia efficacy (EMERGENT-2/3) argue for an antimanic effect, but there is no mania data, ARISE failed, titration eats into a 3-week trial and mania placebo responses are high. Broader geography (China, India, Western Europe) adds heterogeneity. Still recruiting in October 2026 with a November 2026 completion date, so the date will likely slip past January 2027.

assumptions.claim: KarXT improved PANSS total by about 9.6 points more than placebo at week 5 in acute schizophrenia.
Placebo arms in 3-week acute mania trials typically improve YMRS by about 6-12 points.

reason: Biosimilar PK equivalence usually holds; the residual risk is a formulation difference (e.g. the hyaluronidase co-formulation or absorption) pushing an AUC ratio interval outside the margin.
rationale: Comparative PK studies of monoclonal antibody biosimilars from experienced developers like Celltrion almost always meet the 80-125% equivalence margins. Daratumumab has relatively low PK variability at the 1800 mg SC dose, and 473 patients give ample precision for the week 0-1 and week 8-10 AUCs. Enrollment is complete, so the week-24 PK window closes on time. Celltrion tends to present results at congresses rather than issuing early toplines, so a public result by June 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Subcutaneous daratumumab 1800 mg showed non-inferior Ctrough to IV daratumumab in COLUMBA.

reason: Still recruiting a month before its registered November 2026 completion date, so Takeda will likely push primary completion into 2027; results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.
rationale: An 88-patient adaptive dose-finding study in narcolepsy type 2, a hard-to-recruit population across 7 countries, still recruiting in late October 2026 against a November 2026 primary completion date, so slippage past February 2027 is likely. Takeda keeps records current, so the late date would show. Orexin agonists remain a priority class for Takeda, making termination unlikely; posting comes about a year after completion.

reason: Oral SERDs beat fulvestrant in all-comers only when ESR1-mutant tumours drive the effect; this Chinese population is largely ESR1 wild-type and partly CDK4/6-naive, so an all-patient PFS benefit is likely too small.
rationale: Among oral SERDs vs fulvestrant or standard endocrine therapy, only elacestrant (EMERALD, HR 0.70) won in all patients; imlunestrant, vepdegestrant, giredestrant and amcenestrant missed the ITT endpoint, succeeding at most in ESR1-mutant subsets. D-0502 has only phase 1 data. Started 2022 and still recruiting in late 2026, the trial is slow, so results by mid-2027 are unlikely; a small sponsor would publicise a positive result faster, which slightly lifts the conditional chance.

assumptions.claim: Elacestrant improved PFS vs standard endocrine therapy in all patients (HR 0.70) in EMERALD.
Imlunestrant monotherapy did not significantly improve PFS vs standard endocrine therapy in all patients (HR about 0.87).
Amcenestrant did not improve PFS vs physician's choice endocrine therapy.

reason: If remigromig's VEGF blockade is weaker than ranibizumab's at matched monthly dosing, a BCVA deficit of 2-3 letters could break a 4-letter non-inferiority margin; otherwise non-inferiority with ~350 per arm is very likely.
rationale: Both arms are dosed every 4 weeks in year 1, so a VEGF-blocking Wnt-agonist antibody should match ranibizumab on BCVA; new agents vs anti-VEGF in DME (faricimab, aflibercept 8 mg) have landed within about 1.5 letters. With ~350 per arm and SD about 9.5 letters, the CI half-width is ~1.4 letters, so non-inferiority holds unless the true deficit exceeds ~2.5 letters, and either dose suffices. Merck's acquisition and the move to a 3-arm pivotal suggest supportive AMARONE data.

assumptions.claim: Monthly ranibizumab 0.5 mg gave about +10 to +12 ETDRS letters at 1 year in DME.
assumptions.source: RISE/RIDE, Nguyen Ophthalmology 2012; DRCR Protocol T, Wells NEJM 2015

assumptions.claim: Faricimab was non-inferior to aflibercept on BCVA at year 1 in DME using a 4-letter margin.

reason: In mild HS with as few as 4 lesions, a 75% count drop can happen by chance or with emollient vehicle, so a high vehicle HiSCR75 rate could shrink the gap below significance, as happened in one of the two prurigo nodularis trials of the same cream.
rationale: Incyte's phase 2 in Hurley I/II HS showed a significant reduction in AN count versus vehicle at week 16, prompting twin phase 3s with the stricter HiSCR75. With 287 per arm the trial has about 85% power for a 12-point gain over a ~25% vehicle rate. Ruxolitinib cream has a strong but not perfect phase 3 record (AD and vitiligo positive; one prurigo nodularis trial missed). Primary completion was October 2026, so Incyte topline is likely in early 2027.

assumptions.claim: In a phase 2 vehicle-controlled study, ruxolitinib cream 1.5% reduced abscess and inflammatory nodule count more than vehicle at week 16 in Hurley I/II HS.
Placebo HiSCR75 at week 16 was about 15-25% in moderate-to-severe HS biologic phase 3 trials.
assumptions.source: BE HEARD I/II bimekizumab, Kimball Lancet 2024

reason: About 33 patients per arm in a mixed conventional- and advanced-therapy-experienced CD population gives roughly 50-65% power even for a 20-25 point gain in centrally read endoscopic response.
rationale: Brivekimig combines an anti-TNF nanobody with OX40L blockade; TNF blockade is validated in CD and brivekimig was positive in a phase 2 HS trial. Placebo endoscopic response with central reading at week 12-16 runs around 10-15%. A plausible 15-25 point gain at the top dose is near the detection threshold with 33 per arm, and prior anti-TNF failures dilute the effect. Still recruiting at launch, so the readout likely slips past mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Placebo endoscopic response at week 12 in a central-read CD induction trial was about 12%.
Brivekimig met its primary endpoint versus placebo in a phase 2 hidradenitis suppurativa trial.

reason: In mild-moderate HS with low AN counts (as few as 4), small fluctuations give a high vehicle HiSCR75 rate, which can shrink a topical drug's margin.
rationale: Ruxolitinib cream beat vehicle on AN count in a phase 2 Hurley I/II HS trial, and Incyte moved to two phase 3s with HiSCR75. With 290 per arm, a 10-point difference gives about 85% power, but vehicle responses in mild HS with low lesion counts are high and HiSCR75 is a demanding threshold for a topical. Effect around 12 points is the central case; failure of one of two twin trials is a real possibility.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial, ruxolitinib cream 1.5% reduced AN count significantly more than vehicle at week 16 in Hurley I/II HS.

reason: In type 1 diabetes, insulin dose reductions to avoid hypoglycaemia can absorb much of an incretin's glucose effect, as with liraglutide in ADJUNCT ONE, leaving a small HbA1c difference.
rationale: With about 233 per arm and an HbA1c SD near 0.85, the standard error of the difference is about 0.08, so even a 0.2-point reduction would be significant. Liraglutide gave about -0.2 versus placebo in T1D, and tirzepatide is a stronger glucose and weight agent; real-world T1D series report about 0.5-point falls. Insulin titration may blunt the effect, but failure needs a near-null result.

assumptions.claim: Liraglutide 1.8 mg added to insulin in type 1 diabetes lowered HbA1c by about 0.2 percentage points versus placebo at 52 weeks.
assumptions.source: ADJUNCT ONE, Mathieu et al., Diabetes Care 2016

reason: TDF already suppresses HBV DNA in many patients by week 48, and superiority must hold in both HBeAg-positive and HBeAg-negative parts with about 50 per arm each.
rationale: ALG-000184, a potent capsid assembly modulator, gave deep and fast HBV DNA declines in phase 1b. In HBeAg-positive patients with high viral loads, TDF reaches <10 IU/mL at week 48 in perhaps 35-55%, which leaves room for superiority. Both part-specific primaries must succeed, though. In HBeAg-negative disease, TDF suppression is high, even with a target-not-detected bar. With about 50 per arm, a 20-point gain gives only moderate power.

assumptions.claim: In HBeAg-positive patients, 67% on TDF had HBV DNA <29 IU/mL at week 48.
assumptions.source: GS-US-320-0110, Chan et al., Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2016

reason: Daily latanoprost drops are the gold-standard IOP lowerer; a sustained-release latanoprost implant is unlikely to beat it with 25 eyes per arm, and the trial likely aims at comparability, not superiority.
rationale: PA5108 delivers latanoprost from an intracameral implant; intracameral prostaglandin implants such as bimatoprost SR roughly match, rather than beat, topical comparators. Latanoprost lowers diurnal IOP by about 7-8 mmHg from an unmedicated baseline. With 25 per arm and an SD near 3 mmHg, superiority over the active control is unlikely. A sponsor claim of meeting its objective would most likely rest on comparability, which the card does not register as superiority.

assumptions.claim: Bimatoprost SR implant lowered IOP by a similar amount to timolol over 12 weeks, showing non-inferiority but not superiority.

reason: Continued nusinersen keeps pretreated type 2 SMA patients stable or slightly improving, so switching to intrathecal gene therapy may add only about 1 HFMSE point, too little to detect with 25 per arm.
rationale: Intrathecal OAV101 at the same 1.2E14 vg dose beat sham by only about 1.9 HFMSE points in treatment-naive patients (STEER). Gains were about 1 point in nusinersen- or risdiplam-pretreated patients (STRENGTH). Here the control keeps active nusinersen. With an SD around 3.5 and 25 per arm, a 1-point difference has under 20% power. Open-label assessment and younger children add some upside. The trial is still recruiting, so a readout by mid-2027 is very unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Intrathecal OAV101 improved HFMSE by 2.39 points versus 0.51 with sham at 52 weeks in treatment-naive SMA patients aged 2 to under 18.

reason: IL-1 blockade has historically had modest efficacy in RA, and in a biologic-refractory population with about 30 per arm a 10-15 point ACR50 gain would not reach significance.
rationale: Anakinra and canakinumab showed only modest ACR responses in RA, and bDMARD-IR placebo ACR50 at week 12 is about 10-12%. Dual IL-1 alpha/beta blockade with lutikizumab may do somewhat better, but a substudy of about 30 per arm needs a roughly 20-point ACR50 gain to reach significance. AbbVie rarely publicises phase 2 platform readouts quickly, so public results by mid-2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In bDMARD-inadequate responders on csDMARDs, placebo ACR50 at week 12 was about 12%.

reason: Percent change in AHI is noisy and skewed, and a sizeable placebo response could shrink the gap, though a GLP-1/GIP agonist producing large weight loss should still clearly separate.
rationale: HRS9531 is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist that produced substantial weight loss in Chinese obesity trials. Tirzepatide reduced AHI by about half versus minimal change on placebo in SURMOUNT-OSA, with very large significance. With about 70 per arm and an SD near 45% for percent AHI change, a 30-40 point difference gives over 95% power. Still recruiting at launch, so results by mid-2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-OSA trial 1 (no PAP), tirzepatide reduced AHI by about 25 events/h versus about 5 events/h with placebo at 52 weeks.

reason: With about 35 per arm, a 15-20 point gain in modified Mayo remission gives roughly 50-60% power, and advanced-therapy-experienced patients dilute the anti-TNF component's effect.
rationale: Brivekimig pairs an anti-TNF nanobody, a validated UC mechanism, with OX40L blockade, and it was active in phase 2 HS. Placebo modified Mayo remission at week 12-16 in mixed naive/experienced populations runs about 5-15%. Remission of about 25-30% at the top dose is plausible, but 35 per arm gives only moderate power. Enrolment is complete, so a Sanofi disclosure, likely in Q1 or Q2 2027 results, is reasonably likely by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Placebo clinical remission at week 12 by modified Mayo score was about 1% in the phase 2 ARTEMIS-UC trial.

reason: Dose-ranging phase 2 with roughly 60-85 patients per arm; a tezepelumab-like FEV1 gain of about 120 mL against a between-patient SD near 380 mL gives only around 50% power per dose, and an early public statement is more likely a pipeline discontinuation than a positive readout.
rationale: PF-07275315 is understood to be a TSLP-pathway antibody; anti-TSLP (tezepelumab) improved pre-BD FEV1 by about 0.13 L versus placebo. Bronchodilator-reversibility enrichment helps, but arm sizes are small and FEV1 is noisy, so the top dose has roughly coin-flip odds of significance. Still recruiting in late 2026 with a March 2027 completion makes slippage likely; Pfizer rarely press-releases phase 2 asthma data, so any statement by mid-2027 tilts toward a portfolio discontinuation, lowering conditional p_met.

assumptions.claim: Tezepelumab improved pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by about 0.13 L versus placebo at week 52 in severe uncontrolled asthma.

reason: About 78 patients per arm and roughly 50-60 first exacerbations in the 40 mg versus placebo comparison over 24 weeks; even a WILLOW-sized hazard ratio near 0.6 is borderline for significance, and ASPEN showed the class effect on time to first exacerbation can be closer to 0.8.
rationale: XH-S004 appears to be a DPP1 inhibitor (exclusion of prior DPP1 therapy). Brensocatib in WILLOW gave HR 0.58-0.62 for time to first exacerbation with about 85 per arm, but the larger ASPEN showed smaller effects. This trial is similarly sized with two doses, so meeting the primary at one dose is close to even odds; Chinese sponsors are somewhat more likely to publicize positive results early.

assumptions.claim: In WILLOW, brensocatib 10 mg and 25 mg prolonged time to first exacerbation over 24 weeks with hazard ratios of 0.58 and 0.62 versus placebo.
In WILLOW, about 48% of placebo patients had an exacerbation within 24 weeks.

reason: Small open-label Sanofi phase 2 still recruiting in late 2026 with a February 2027 completion date for a 16-week endpoint; Graves' patients are hard to recruit off standard antithyroid drugs, so the date will likely slip, while termination is possible but unlikely.
rationale: Recruiting 30 patients across 24 sites with last-patient-in needed by about October 2026 suggests slippage beyond May 2027. Sanofi usually posts results within 12 months of completion, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. Exploratory indications can be dropped in portfolio reviews, giving a modest stop risk.

reason: Only 45 patients (about 22 per arm) with three co-primary motor outcomes that must all be significant; spontaneous recovery after stroke is large and variable (SD about 14 Fugl-Meyer points), so a p38-alpha inhibitor would need an implausibly large effect.
rationale: A proof-of-concept trial of 45 patients cannot reliably detect realistic differences in Fugl-Meyer, TUG and NIHSS motor change, and the round counts all three registered primaries as co-primary. Neflamapimod has no prior evidence in stroke recovery. CervoMed is listed and will likely report topline soon after the September 2026 completion, but a statistically significant win on all three is very unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Upper-extremity Fugl-Meyer recovery in the first 3 months after stroke averages about 70% of maximal potential recovery in most patients.
assumptions.source: Prabhakaran et al., Neurorehabil Neural Repair 2008

reason: HS trials have high and variable placebo responses (AN count often falls 25-35% on placebo), and IL-17A blockade alone gives modest separation; with about 82 per arm and a skewed percent-change endpoint (SD near 60%), a placebo-adjusted gain under 15 points would miss.
rationale: Tibulizumab (BAFF/IL-17A bispecific, from Lilly's LY3090106) should act through IL-17A, a validated HS pathway (secukinumab, bimekizumab, sonelokimab), but class effects on AN count over placebo are about 15-25 points. Percent change in AN count is more sensitive than HiSCR, and two doses give two chances, so about even odds. Zura is likely to announce topline within months of the September 2026 primary completion.

assumptions.claim: Secukinumab achieved HiSCR at week 16 in about 42-45% of patients versus about 31-34% with placebo in SUNSHINE and SUNRISE.

reason: GLP-1/GIP agonism robustly lowers AHI via weight loss; the realistic failure route is heavy missing data at 52 weeks (PSG with PAP pause) or GI-driven dropouts diluting the treatment-policy estimate in a 140-patient trial.
rationale: HRS9531 is a dual GLP-1/GIP agonist with weight loss comparable to tirzepatide in Chinese trials. In SURMOUNT-OSA trial 2 (on PAP) tirzepatide reduced AHI about 24 events/h more than placebo at 52 weeks. With 70 per arm and an SD near 22, even half that effect is significant. Still recruiting in late 2026 against a December 2026 primary completion means the 52-week readout is likely late 2027.

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-OSA trial 2 (participants on PAP), tirzepatide reduced AHI by about 24 events/h more than placebo at week 52, with placebo changing by about -6 events/h.

reason: PINNACLE restricts to milder edema (CST 320-400 microns) with baseline vision up to 78 letters, limiting room for BCVA gain, while sham patients may improve on background anti-inflammatory therapy or rescue, shrinking the difference.
rationale: KSI-101 (IL-6/VEGF bispecific) produced roughly 12-letter BCVA gains with marked CST reductions in the uncontrolled APEX phase 1b. Against sham with about 150 per arm and an SD near 10 letters, a 3-4 letter true difference is enough; the main doubt is the milder-edema population and sham response. Still recruiting in late 2026 suggests the February 2027 completion slips.

assumptions.claim: In PEACHTREE, 47% of suprachoroidal triamcinolone patients versus about 16% of sham patients with uveitic macular edema gained 15 or more letters at week 24.

reason: Efficacy is near-certain given the phase 2b LDL-C reduction of about 50% and about 1,500 patients per arm; only an unexpected safety finding or major data-integrity issue would derail the primary.
rationale: AZD0780, an oral PCSK9 inhibitor, cut LDL-C by about 51% versus placebo at 12 weeks in phase 2b PURSUIT on top of statins; oral PCSK9 inhibition (enlicitide) replicated similar effects in phase 3. With about 3,100 patients, even a much smaller effect is significant. AstraZeneca usually announces phase 3 high-level results in its quarterly updates, so a statement by mid-2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: AZD0780 30 mg reduced LDL-C by about 50.7% versus placebo at 12 weeks on top of statin therapy in the phase 2b PURSUIT trial.

reason: PCSK9 inhibition works in heterozygous FH because LDL receptors are partly functional; with about 470 patients randomized 2:1 and an expected 45% placebo-adjusted reduction, only an unforeseen safety or conduct problem would cause a miss.
rationale: AZD0780 lowered LDL-C by about 51% versus placebo in phase 2b; PCSK9 antibodies and oral enlicitide have shown similar or only slightly smaller effects in HeFH. Power is overwhelming for any plausible effect. AstraZeneca will likely state high-level results with the sister AZURE-LDL trial in its 2027 quarterly updates, supporting an LDL-lowering filing.

assumptions.claim: AZD0780 30 mg reduced LDL-C by about 50.7% versus placebo at 12 weeks on top of statin therapy in the phase 2b PURSUIT trial.
Evolocumab reduced LDL-C by about 60% versus placebo at week 12 in heterozygous FH.

reason: Small-sponsor psychedelic phase 2 still recruiting one month before its registered primary completion; a 7-day endpoint keeps the tail short, but enrolment of medically ill adjustment-disorder patients usually runs a few months past plan.
rationale: Status is recruiting with primary completion registered for November 2026, so the date will almost certainly move; whether it moves past February 2027 depends on how close the 100-patient target is. Reunion is a small, cash-limited company, so posting results on ClinicalTrials.gov within months of completion is unlikely. A dose-controlled single-dose design with a fixed Day 7 MADRS primary rarely gets its primary outcome rewritten.

reason: Enrolment is closed and the 6-month double-blind period should finish close to the registered November 2026 date; the study supports DBV's toddler BLA, so stopping is unlikely and posting is likely to come near the 12-month deadline.
rationale: Active, not recruiting, with a fixed 26-week blinded period, so primary completion should land close to November 2026. The safety study is a regulatory requirement for the Viaskin Peanut toddler filing, which makes a stop unlikely. Results posting is due about November 2027, after the read date, so posting by August 2027 needs an early submission. A safety-only primary outcome is rarely changed in substance.

reason: Recruiting 36 Parkinson's patients from mid-2026 across 8 US sites with a December 2026 completion date is ambitious; slippage past March 2027 is more likely than not.
rationale: The trial opened on 30 June 2026 and needs 36 patients plus 14 days of dosing and 30 days of follow-up, all within six months. Small Parkinson's safety studies run through the Parkinson Study Group usually enrol more slowly than that. A small private sponsor rarely posts results within months, and a safety-only primary outcome is rarely changed.

reason: Adding an anti-CD73 antibody to PD-1 plus chemotherapy in an unselected first-line NSCLC population has no positive randomized precedent, and with about 95 PFS events only a hazard ratio near 0.67 or better would reach two-sided significance.
rationale: Sintilimab plus platinum doublet is a strong control: median PFS about 8.9 months in nonsquamous disease (ORIENT-11) and 5.5 months in squamous disease (ORIENT-12), so a mixed-histology arm should land near 7-8 months. CD73 blockade has shown response signals (uliledlimab with toripalimab, oleclumab in COAST) but no randomized phase 3 PFS win in metastatic disease. Enrolment is not restricted to CD73-high tumours, which dilutes any effect. With 150 patients the trial can detect only a large hazard-ratio benefit at two-sided 0.05.

assumptions.claim: Sintilimab plus pemetrexed-platinum gave a median PFS of 8.9 months in first-line nonsquamous NSCLC.
assumptions.source: ORIENT-11, Yang et al., J Thorac Oncol 2020

assumptions.claim: Sintilimab plus gemcitabine-platinum gave a median PFS of 5.5 months in first-line squamous NSCLC.
assumptions.source: ORIENT-12, Zhou et al., J Thorac Oncol 2021

assumptions.claim: Durvalumab plus oleclumab improved PFS over durvalumab alone in unresectable stage III NSCLC in a randomized phase 2 (HR about 0.44).
assumptions.source: COAST, Herbst et al., J Clin Oncol 2022

reason: A reversible MAO-B inhibitor has no proven weight-loss effect in humans; with 22 versus 11 patients over 12 weeks, the 240 mg dose would need about 2.5 points of placebo-adjusted loss to reach significance.
rationale: Placebo patients on a structured 500 kcal deficit typically lose 1-3% in 12 weeks. MAO-B inhibitors such as selegiline are not known as weight-loss drugs, and the phase 1 signal is unpublished. Each stage is small, so with SD about 3.5% only a placebo-adjusted effect beyond about 2.5 points reaches significance. The sequential three-stage design with safety reviews between stages makes a January 2027 completion unlikely, so a public result by June 2027 is improbable.

assumptions.claim: In a phase 2 obesity trial with lifestyle counselling, placebo weight change was only about -2% over 26 to 36 weeks.

reason: EMERALD enrols a broad, mixed DEE population rather than the SCN2A/SCN8A gain-of-function patients where relutrigine looked strongest; syndromes that respond poorly to sodium-channel drugs could dilute the effect below significance.
rationale: In EMBOLD cohort 1, relutrigine cut motor seizures by about 46% against placebo in SCN2A/SCN8A DEE. Potent anti-seizure drugs usually win DEE trials of this size (fenfluramine and cannabidiol in LGS). About 53 patients per arm gives good power for a placebo-adjusted reduction of 20-25 percentage points, and two doses give two chances. The broad DEE population is the main uncertainty, as is Praxis's mixed record outside epilepsy. Enrolment is closed with completion in December 2026, so Praxis will likely announce topline in Q1 2027.

assumptions.claim: In EMBOLD cohort 1, relutrigine reduced monthly motor seizures by about 46% versus placebo in SCN2A/SCN8A DEE.
assumptions.source: Praxis Precision Medicines press release, EMBOLD cohort 1 topline, 2024

assumptions.claim: In the fenfluramine LGS phase 3, the placebo arm's median reduction in drop-seizure frequency was about 8%.

reason: Superiority over placebo on percent weight change at 80 weeks is near certain; the only realistic threat is very high discontinuation diluting the treatment-policy estimate, which would still leave a large significant difference.
rationale: In REDEFINE 1, CagriSema lost 20.4% of body weight against 3.0% on placebo at 68 weeks (treatment-policy estimand). This trial runs 80 weeks in motivated participants without diabetes, so a placebo-adjusted difference of about 15-23 points is expected, far beyond what 609 patients need for significance. Novo usually issues topline company announcements about 2-3 months after primary completion, which would mean around May 2027. The key secondary may be reported only descriptively in a press release, which lowers its scored probability.

assumptions.claim: In REDEFINE 1, CagriSema gave a mean weight change of -20.4% versus -3.0% with placebo at week 68 (treatment-policy estimand).
In STEP 1, the placebo arm lost 2.4% of body weight at week 68.

reason: Anti-TSLP blockade has been weak in atopic dermatitis (tezepelumab missed); with 55 patients per arm, ATI-045 needs about a 15-point placebo-adjusted EASI reduction to win.
rationale: Tezepelumab with topical steroids did not significantly beat placebo on EASI-50 at week 12, which casts doubt on TSLP as an AD target. Aclaris argues bosakitug is more potent, and early Chinese data were encouraging but small. The 24-week endpoint gives a slow-acting mechanism more time, and percent EASI change is the most sensitive endpoint available. Placebo response at week 24 with rescue counted as failure should be around 25-35%. Primary completion was September 2026, so Aclaris should announce topline soon.

assumptions.claim: Tezepelumab plus topical corticosteroids did not significantly improve EASI-50 versus placebo at week 12 in moderate-to-severe AD (about 65% vs 48%).
assumptions.source: Simpson et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2019

assumptions.claim: The placebo arms of SOLO 1 and SOLO 2 had a mean EASI change of about -31% to -38% at week 16.

reason: Palmoplantar pustulosis is refractory, and a topical pan-JAK cream has to cross thick palm and sole skin and act on an IL-36/IL-17-driven process; with about 67 per arm, it needs roughly a 13-14 point PPPASI-75 gain over vehicle.
rationale: Delgocitinib cream works on the hands in chronic hand eczema (DELTA 1/2), which supports penetration on palms. But PPP has defeated targeted drugs such as spesolimab, and only apremilast has a clear oral signal. Vehicle cream should give a PPPASI-75 rate around 10-15%. A 16-week proof-of-concept with about 135 patients is powered only for a large gap. The trial is still recruiting, so completion slips into 2027 and a public result before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Delgocitinib cream 20 mg/g was superior to vehicle on IGA-CHE treatment success at week 16 in chronic hand eczema.
Spesolimab did not significantly improve PPPASI-50 versus placebo at week 16 in palmoplantar pustulosis.
assumptions.source: Mrowietz et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2021

assumptions.claim: In a Japanese phase 2, about 28% of placebo patients with PPP reached PPPASI-50 at week 16.

reason: A two-site radiolabelled recovery study needing 120 healthy donors, each with a 35-day storage cycle, is still recruiting just before its December 2026 completion date; moderate slippage is likely, but the study supports Cerus's INTERCEPT RBC PMA, so a stop is unlikely.
rationale: Still recruiting in late October 2026 with primary completion registered for 15 December 2026. Each subject needs 35 days of storage before infusion, so completion likely moves into early 2027; whether it passes mid-March 2027 is roughly a coin flip. Device sponsors often delay results posting until after approval, and the 24-hour recovery primary outcome is a standard FDA metric that is unlikely to change.

reason: If enoxaparin is dosed US-style (30 mg twice daily) at many sites or venography adequacy is poor, the control VTE rate and evaluable numbers shrink, though FXI antibodies have repeatedly cut venographic VTE by 60-80% vs enoxaparin.
rationale: Every FXI-targeting agent tested in TKA (FXI-ASO, osocimab, abelacimab, milvexian, and REGN7508 in Regeneron's phase 2) beat enoxaparin on venographic VTE, with enoxaparin rates around 20%. With about 667 per arm and an expected relative risk near 0.4, superiority vs enoxaparin is very likely; the main uncertainty is whether the trial's own primary is framed differently (e.g. versus apixaban) and whether topline lands before end-June 2027 given primary completion in February 2027.

assumptions.claim: Enoxaparin 40 mg once daily gave a venography-based VTE rate of about 22% after TKA in ANT-005.
A single 150 mg dose of abelacimab reduced post-TKA VTE to about 4% vs 22% with enoxaparin.
Milvexian 200 mg twice daily gave 7% VTE vs 21% with enoxaparin after TKA.

reason: Sixteen patients in a two-period crossover with a noisy diary endpoint (days with abrasion symptoms) and episodic events; placebo lubrication effects and possible carryover leave little power unless the effect is large.
rationale: B-VEC restores COL7 and worked on skin wounds (GEM-3), and compassionate ophthalmic use suggested corneal benefit, so biology is plausible. But 16 patients, a symptom-day diary with episodic abrasions, and crossover carryover risk make significance uncertain. Still recruiting in October 2026 with 24 weeks of treatment, so results before mid-2027 are unlikely; Krystal does press-release toplines promptly.
evidence: B-VEC ophthalmic compassionate-use case, Bascom Palmer 2023-2024

assumptions.claim: Topical B-VEC achieved significantly more complete wound healing than placebo at 6 months in DEB.

reason: Small AstraZeneca China platform study; enrolment of 16 versus about 48 planned suggests sub-study 2 may be dropped, which could lead to a terminated status or removal of its primary outcome, while results posting follows AZ's 12-month policy.
rationale: Primary completion October 2026 with AZ's routine disclosure makes posting by August 2027 possible but more likely near the 12-month mark; low enrolment raises some chance of sub-study 2 being cut.

reason: Botulinum toxin has repeatedly failed to separate from placebo in episodic migraine, and injection trials carry a large placebo response at month 6, so the true effect of Xeomin may be under 1 day per month.
rationale: OnabotulinumtoxinA is approved only for chronic migraine; older episodic trials and a JAMA meta-analysis found no meaningful benefit. Merz's 997-patient design with two doses is powered for a small effect (about 0.7-0.8 days) and the injection placebo response is large, so success is roughly a coin flip. Merz is private and may hold topline until a congress, so public results by June 2027 are uncertain.
evidence: Jackson et al., JAMA 2012 (botulinum toxin meta-analysis)

assumptions.claim: A meta-analysis found botulinum toxin A no better than placebo for episodic migraine prevention.
Placebo reduced monthly migraine days by about 2.8 days over months 1-6 in an episodic migraine CGRP antibody trial.

reason: Chronic migraine injection trials show a large placebo response at month 6 (around 5-6 migraine days), which can erode the roughly 1.5-2 day difference seen with onabotulinumtoxinA in PREEMPT.
rationale: Botulinum toxin A is an established chronic migraine preventive (PREEMPT pooled: about 2 fewer migraine days than placebo at week 24), and incobotulinumtoxinA is pharmacologically similar. With about 269 per arm and SD near 6.5, a 1.5-day effect gives good power, but the placebo response is large and dose A may be suboptimal. Merz is private, so a public topline by June 2027 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: In the PREEMPT pooled analysis onabotulinumtoxinA reduced migraine days by about 2 days more than placebo at week 24 in chronic migraine.
Discontinuation due to adverse events was about 3.8% with onabotulinumtoxinA vs 1.2% with placebo in PREEMPT.

reason: Chinese multi-cohort ADC phase 2 still recruiting in late 2026 with a February 2027 primary completion; cohort expansions usually push dates out, and Chinese sponsors rarely post CT.gov results.
