rationale: Kelun-Biotech single-arm style cohorts with 192 patients and PFS in a primary outcome rarely finish on time; registry updates are irregular; posting of results on ClinicalTrials.gov is uncommon for this sponsor.

reason: Small open-label Vera dosing study, active not recruiting with primary completion around September 2026; likely to complete normally, with results posting due near September 2027, so posting by end-August 2027 is possible but not the base case.
rationale: Atacicept is in late-stage development/approval for IgAN, so a monthly regimen study supports lifecycle plans and is unlikely to stop; FDAAA-style 12-month posting puts the deadline just after the read date.

reason: The response definition is not public; if it requires a stringent composite (e.g. gradient below 30 mmHg plus NYHA class I) or LVEF-driven dose interruptions are frequent, the difference could shrink, though cardiac myosin inhibitors have shown large gradient effects.
rationale: Cardiac myosin inhibitors (mavacamten, aficamten) have consistently produced large, highly significant improvements in LVOT gradient and NYHA-based responder endpoints versus placebo in oHCM, including in Chinese patients (EXPLORER-CN). HRS-1893 is Hengrui's myosin inhibitor with supportive phase 2 data, and 114 per arm gives ample power for a 30-40 point responder difference. Timing of public disclosure is the main uncertainty.

assumptions.claim: In EXPLORER-HCM, 37% of mavacamten vs 17% of placebo patients met the primary composite functional endpoint.
Mavacamten improved KCCQ-CSS by about 9 points more than placebo in EXPLORER-HCM.
Aficamten significantly improved peak VO2, Valsalva LVOT gradient and NYHA class versus placebo at 24 weeks.

reason: Non-obstructive HCM has resisted symptom-endpoint wins (mavacamten failed ODYSSEY-HCM); a metabolic modulator over 12 weeks may shift KCCQ-CSS only a few points against an SD near 15, below what 82 per arm can detect.
rationale: IMPROVE-HCM showed ninerafaxstat was safe with a VE/VCO2 signal and KCCQ gains mainly in more symptomatic patients, but KCCQ-CSS in nHCM is noisy with a placebo response near 5 points. With 82 per arm, a true effect around 3-4 points gives under 50% power, and mavacamten's ODYSSEY-HCM failure shows how hard nHCM is. Still recruiting in October 2026, so topline before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In IMPROVE-HCM, ninerafaxstat met its safety primary and improved VE/VCO2 slope versus placebo in non-obstructive HCM.
Mavacamten did not significantly improve KCCQ-CSS or peak VO2 versus placebo in symptomatic non-obstructive HCM.
assumptions.source: ODYSSEY-HCM, Bristol Myers Squibb press release 2025

reason: Adding a DPP-4 inhibitor on top of an SGLT2 inhibitor plus metformin gives a modest incremental HbA1c drop (about 0.3-0.5%); a smaller-than-expected add-on effect is the only realistic path to failure with 163 per arm.
rationale: Prusogliptin is an approved Chinese DPP-4 inhibitor; factorial triple-combination trials (saxagliptin, linagliptin, retagliptin with SGLT2i plus metformin) consistently show significant 0.3-0.5% added HbA1c lowering. With 163 per arm and SD about 0.9, power exceeds 95% for a 0.35% difference. Chinese sponsors disclose slowly, so public results by June 2027 are uncertain.
evidence: DeFronzo et al., Diabetes Care 2015 (empagliflozin/linagliptin factorial)
Kim et al., Diabetologia 2013 (DPP-4 inhibitors in Asians meta-analysis)

assumptions.claim: Saxagliptin plus dapagliflozin plus metformin lowered HbA1c by about 0.27% more than dapagliflozin plus metformin at 24 weeks.
DPP-4 inhibitors lower HbA1c more in Asian-dominant than in non-Asian study populations.

reason: Forty patients with flare-driven, highly variable blister area and natural regression of flares give little power to show a significant 2-month difference against placebo gel.
rationale: Novel topical keratin-aggregate agent with no published controlled efficacy data. Topical EBS programmes have a poor record: diacerein looked positive in a small crossover but its larger phase 2/3 missed. Blister area fluctuates with season, trauma and spontaneous flare resolution, so placebo improvement is large and 20 per arm gives low power. Still recruiting with a January 2027 completion, so a result by mid-2027 is unlikely; an early disclosure would lean favourable.
evidence: Wally et al., diacerein crossover trial in EBS, J Am Acad Dermatol 2018
Castle Creek diacerein 1% phase 2/3 in EBS, 2020

assumptions.claim: A small randomized placebo-controlled crossover trial of topical diacerein 1% in EBS reduced blister counts versus placebo.
assumptions.source: Wally et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2018

assumptions.claim: A larger phase 2/3 trial of diacerein 1% ointment in EBS did not meet its primary endpoint.

reason: Single-site Italian cosmetic-patch study by a small sponsor that is still listed as recruiting past the point needed for a November 2026 completion; records like this are often left stale or extended, and results posting is improbable.
rationale: Recruiting 72 patients with 4 months per patient at one site, still recruiting in late 2026, so if the record is updated the primary completion likely moves into 2027. Small cosmetic sponsors rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov or substantively change safety primaries.

reason: Both region-specific primaries likely need to succeed; the EU/UK SALT<=10 analysis, with low absolute response rates in a treatment-refractory subset of about 69 per arm, is the weaker link, though near-zero placebo regrowth leaves margin.
rationale: In ALLEGRO-2b/3 (age 12+), ritlecitinib 50 mg gave week-24 SALT<=20 of 23% vs 1.6% placebo and SALT<=10 of about 13% vs 1.5%; JAK inhibitors behave similarly in children and placebo regrowth in severe AA is near zero. With about 69 per arm the higher dose should clear both region-specific primaries. Pfizer rarely press-releases paediatric label-expansion studies, so disclosure by June 2027 is unlikely; posting and a congress presentation are more likely in the second half of 2027.

assumptions.claim: In ALLEGRO-2b/3, 23% on ritlecitinib 50 mg vs 1.6% on placebo reached SALT<=20 at week 24.
In ALLEGRO-2b/3, about 13% on ritlecitinib 50 mg vs 1.5% on placebo reached SALT<=10 at week 24.

reason: Perlane Lidocaine is an effective approved volumiser, so the trial succeeds only as non-inferiority; if the hidden hypothesis were superiority, or the margin unusually tight, the high comparator responder rate would sink it.
rationale: HArmonyCa Lidocaine (hyaluronic acid with CaHA microspheres) is CE-marked and volumises at least as well as HA fillers; mid-face filler pivotal trials report month-6 MFVDS responder rates around 80-90%. With 2:1 randomisation, about 252 patients and a typical 10-15 pp margin, the lower confidence bound should clear the margin. AbbVie tends to post results about a year after completion, so a public statement by June 2027 is uncertain.
evidence: Jones & Murphy, Juvederm Voluma mid-face pivotal trial, Dermatol Surg 2013

assumptions.claim: In the US pivotal trial of Juvederm Voluma XC, about 86% of treated participants were MFVDS responders at month 6.

reason: Allosteric TYK2 inhibition has failed in UC (deucravacitinib LATTICE-UC), so even a more potent molecule may give only a modest remission gain that about 60 per arm cannot resolve.
rationale: D-2570 is InventisBio's oral allosteric TYK2 inhibitor with strong psoriasis phase 2 data, but the class failed in UC with deucravacitinib (week-12 remission about 15% vs 16% placebo), possibly from low exposure. IL-23 pathway blockade works in UC, so a more potent TYK2 inhibitor could add 10-15 pp; with about 60 per arm and placebo near 10%, power for that is only about 50-60%. A listed Chinese sponsor discloses faster when positive.

assumptions.claim: In LATTICE-UC, deucravacitinib 6 mg twice daily gave week-12 clinical remission of 14.8% vs 16.1% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Danese et al., J Crohns Colitis 2024 (LATTICE-UC)

reason: A 12-week FVC endpoint with about 40 per arm needs a roughly 60 mL effect to reach significance, larger than most antifibrotic candidates show over 3 monthly infusions.
rationale: BI 765423 is likely Boehringer's anti-IL-11 antibody; IL-11 is a strong fibrosis target in mice but its human role is debated and there are no efficacy data. Placebo FVC loss over 12 weeks on background therapy is about 40-60 mL with an SD near 130-150 mL, so a significant result needs an effect only nerandomilast has shown at 12 weeks. A phase 2a may be judged on a Bayesian or descriptive basis, and early disclosure would favour a positive result.

assumptions.claim: In the 12-week phase 2 trial of nerandomilast, placebo FVC change was about -82 mL without and -59 mL with background antifibrotic therapy.

reason: The 8-week BEM/RZR course could relapse more often than 12-week SOF/VEL in genotype 3 or cirrhotic patients common in the ex-North America sites, pushing the lower bound past the margin.
rationale: In phase 2, 8-week BEM/RZR gave SVR12 of about 98% in the efficacy-evaluable population and about 95% ITT, close to SOF/VEL's results. With about 440 per arm the 95% CI half-width is about 3 pp, so non-inferiority at a typical 6-10 pp margin holds unless the shorter regimen relapses in genotype 3 or cirrhosis. Atea, a small public company, will press-release topline soon after the late-2026 primary completion.

assumptions.claim: In Atea's phase 2 trial, 8 weeks of BEM/RZR achieved SVR12 of about 98% in the per-protocol efficacy population.
In ASTRAL-1, 12 weeks of SOF/VEL achieved SVR12 of 99%.

reason: If lansoprazole heals most LA C/D lesions by week 4 or the C/D subset is small, the margin over a P-CAB may not reach significance in the restricted primary population.
rationale: Linaprazan glurate is a long-acting potassium-competitive acid blocker; its phase 2 showed much higher 4-week healing than lansoprazole in LA C/D, and vonoprazan beat lansoprazole most clearly in severe grades (PHALCON-EE). Lansoprazole heals roughly 55-70% of C/D by week 4 versus about 85% expected for a P-CAB twice daily, giving about 20 pp; with roughly 60-80 C/D patients per arm that is well powered. Cinclus is listed and will press-release topline promptly.
evidence: Cinclus linaprazan glurate phase 2 in erosive esophagitis, 2023

assumptions.claim: In PHALCON-EE, week-2 healing in LA grade C/D was 70.2% with vonoprazan vs 52.6% with lansoprazole.
In Cinclus's phase 2 trial, linaprazan glurate healed a markedly higher share of LA C/D patients at 4 weeks than lansoprazole.

reason: Rovatirelin (KPS-0373) missed its SARA primary in two earlier phase 3 trials; a sub-1-point true effect against a placebo arm that also improves leaves 71 per arm with limited power.
rationale: KPS-0373 is rovatirelin, an oral TRH analogue. Two prior Kissei phase 3 trials (KPS1301, KPS1305) did not reach significance on SARA total score, with between-arm differences well under 1 point and placebo arms improving; pooled analyses hinted at benefit in selected patients. This third confirmatory study (142 patients, 24 weeks, mild-moderate ataxia) is likely enriched based on those analyses but remains small for an effect near 0.5-0.7 SARA points with SD around 2.4, so success probability stays low.
evidence: Rovatirelin phase 3 KPS1301 and KPS1305 (Nishizawa et al., J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2020)
Taltirelin approval for SCD in Japan (2000)

assumptions.claim: Rovatirelin did not significantly reduce SARA total score versus placebo in the primary analysis of either of two earlier phase 3 trials in spinocerebellar degeneration.
assumptions.source: Nishizawa et al., J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2020

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in the earlier rovatirelin phase 3 trials showed a decrease (improvement) in mean SARA total score from baseline over about 6 months.
assumptions.source: Nishizawa et al., J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2020

reason: PRRT effect versus octreotide after SSA progression is large (NETTER-1 HR about 0.2); the main residual risk is slow-growing G1 disease keeping the octreotide arm progression-free, or trial conduct issues at a single-site Chinese sponsor.
rationale: 177Lu-DOTATATE versus octreotide LAR in SSA-progressed, SSTR-positive G1/G2 GEP-NETs replicates NETTER-1, where PFS hazard ratio was about 0.2 and 20-month PFS in the high-dose octreotide arm was around 11%. Including pancreatic NETs and a Chinese generic-type product adds some uncertainty, but the effect size is so large that 184 patients give very high power. Still recruiting on a registered primary completion of Nov 2026 with an 18-month endpoint, so a result by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: NETTER-1 final OS (Strosberg et al., Lancet Oncol 2021)

assumptions.claim: In NETTER-1, 177Lu-DOTATATE reduced the risk of progression or death versus high-dose octreotide LAR with a hazard ratio of about 0.21.
In NETTER-1, estimated PFS at month 20 in the high-dose octreotide LAR control arm was about 11%.

reason: A GLP-1/GIP dual agonist added to basal insulin versus placebo for 40 weeks should lower HbA1c by well over 1 point; only heavy insulin up-titration in the placebo arm or high dropout could narrow the gap enough to matter.
rationale: HRS9531 is Hengrui's GLP-1/GIP dual agonist with strong phase 2 glycaemic and weight data in Chinese patients. The analogous SURPASS-5 trial of tirzepatide added to basal insulin showed HbA1c falls of about 2.3 points versus 0.9 with placebo at 40 weeks. With 100 per arm and SD near 1.0, even a much smaller effect would be highly significant, so the primary is near-certain if reported. The main uncertainty is timing: the record still shows recruiting against a Feb 2027 primary completion.
evidence: SURPASS-AP-Combo (Gao et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2023)

assumptions.claim: In SURPASS-5, tirzepatide 15 mg added to basal insulin lowered HbA1c by about 2.3 percentage points versus about 0.9 with placebo at 40 weeks.
HRS9531 is a dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist developed by Jiangsu Hengrui and its subsidiaries.
assumptions.source: Hengrui pipeline disclosures; ClinicalTrials.gov HRS9531 records

reason: Denosumab biosimilars have consistently matched Prolia on LS-BMD; the only real risk is that 278 patients give a confidence interval too wide for a tight protocol margin, or excess dropouts.
rationale: QL1206 is Qilu's denosumab biosimilar, already developed against Xgeva in oncology. Every denosumab biosimilar comparative trial in postmenopausal osteoporosis reported so far has met equivalence on LS-BMD percent change at 12 months. With about 139 per arm and SD near 3.5%, the 90-95% CI half-width is about 0.7-0.8 points, inside typical margins of about 1.45-2.0 points. Still recruiting against a Jan 2027 completion with a 12-month endpoint makes a public result before mid-2027 unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Denosumab biosimilar candidates (e.g., Sandoz GP2411, Samsung Bioepis SB16, Celltrion CT-P41) each met equivalence versus Prolia on percent change in lumbar spine BMD at month 12.
assumptions.source: ROSALIA (2023); SB16 phase 3 (Langdahl et al. 2024); CT-P41 phase 3 (2024)

assumptions.claim: Denosumab 60 mg every 6 months increases lumbar spine BMD by about 5% at 12 months in postmenopausal osteoporosis.

reason: MDD monotherapy trials fail often because placebo response of 9-12 HAM-D points swamps a modest GABA-A neurosteroid effect, which in zuranolone trials was largest early and faded by week 6.
rationale: SPT-300 is an oral allopregnanolone prodrug (Glyph lymphatic-targeting platform), a GABA-A positive modulator like zuranolone. Zuranolone's MDD programme was mixed (WATERFALL positive at day 15 by about 1.7 HAM-D points, MOUNTAIN missed, effects waning by day 42). SPT-300 is dosed continuously through day 42, which may sustain effect, and 180 per arm give fair power for a 2-point difference with SD about 7.5. Historical phase 2 MDD success rates near 40-50% and high placebo response in US/European sites keep the estimate below even.
evidence: WATERFALL zuranolone MDD (Clayton et al., Am J Psychiatry 2023)
MOUNTAIN zuranolone MDD (Clayton et al., J Clin Psychiatry 2023)
Brexanolone PPD trials (Meltzer-Brody et al., Lancet 2018)

assumptions.claim: In WATERFALL, zuranolone 50 mg improved HAM-D-17 at day 15 versus placebo by about 1.7 points.
assumptions.source: Clayton et al., Am J Psychiatry 2023

assumptions.claim: In the MOUNTAIN trial, zuranolone 30 mg did not meet its primary HAM-D-17 endpoint at day 15 in MDD.
assumptions.source: Clayton et al., J Clin Psychiatry 2023

reason: With about 20 patients per arm, exercise and nutrition guidance in both arms, and SPPB changes near 1 point SD 1.6, only an implausibly large drug effect would reach significance in 12 weeks.
rationale: No drug has yet shown a reproducible SPPB benefit in sarcopenia; bimagrumab and others failed when both arms received lifestyle support, which lifts the placebo arm. This small Korean phase 2 has about 20 per arm, three doses and a 12-week window, so the highest-dose comparison needs roughly a 1-point SPPB difference to reach p<0.05. Any one dose winning raises the odds slightly, as does a small sponsor's tendency to announce positive results earlier.
evidence: Bimagrumab sarcopenia phase 2b (Rooks et al., J Cachexia Sarcopenia Muscle 2020)

assumptions.claim: In a phase 2b trial in older adults with sarcopenia given exercise and nutrition support, bimagrumab did not improve SPPB more than placebo; both arms improved.
assumptions.source: Rooks et al., J Cachexia Sarcopenia Muscle 2020

assumptions.claim: A change of about 0.5-1 point is the usual minimal clinically important difference for SPPB.
assumptions.source: Perera et al., J Am Geriatr Soc 2006

reason: A small-cap psychedelic sponsor running single-dose psilocybin therapy in cancer patients with adjustment disorder at 5 Australian sites will likely enrol slowly, pushing primary completion past mid-2027.
rationale: Started Oct 2025 with 87 patients needed and a Week 10 endpoint, so the registered March 2027 completion requires full enrolment by about January 2027; psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy trials with day-long dosing sessions in medically ill patients usually enrol slower than planned. Psyence is thinly funded, giving a non-trivial stop risk. Australian-only sponsor, so results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov is very unlikely.

reason: Two SC formulations of the same antibody should match on AUC; the realistic failure is Cmax falling outside 0.80-1.25 because of absorption differences or body-weight variability in a parallel design of about 96 per arm.
rationale: Roche is bridging a new ocrelizumab SC formulation to the marketed SC product (approved after OCARINA II). Same antibody, same route: AUC equivalence is very likely, and with about 96 per arm and between-subject CV near 35%, the 90% CI for the ratio is roughly plus or minus 8%, inside 80-125% if the true ratio is near 1. Cmax for SC monoclonals is more variable and could drift if excipients or concentration change absorption, which is the main risk. Roche usually presents such data at ECTRIMS, so mid-2027 publication is uncertain.
evidence: OCARINA II, ocrelizumab SC vs IV (ECTRIMS 2024)

assumptions.claim: OCARINA II showed ocrelizumab SC 920 mg was non-inferior to IV 600 mg on serum AUC from week 1 to 12.
assumptions.source: OCARINA II, Roche press release and ECTRIMS 2024 presentation

reason: A 50-patient PK/PD study that has finished enrolling, with a 16-week treatment period, should complete close to its registered Dec 2026 date under an experienced sponsor.
rationale: Status is active, not recruiting, so the last patient should finish the 16-week treatment around Dec 2026 to early 2027, within the 90-day window. Galderma runs nemolizumab trials reliably, so stopping is unlikely. CPUO is not an approved use, so results posting can lawfully be delayed and is unlikely by Aug 2027 (due about Dec 2027 at the earliest).

reason: If the revised titration, likely meant to cut hypoglycaemia, makes icodec dosing more conservative, HbA1c lowering could trail glargine enough for the upper CI bound to cross the likely 0.3-point margin.
rationale: In ONWARDS 6 (T1D), icodec was non-inferior to degludec on HbA1c (difference about 0.05 points) but had more hypoglycaemia. ONWARDS 11 likely tests an adjusted dosing approach against glargine U100. With 877 patients the SE of the difference is about 0.065, so non-inferiority at a 0.3-point margin holds unless icodec trails by more than about 0.17 points. Superiority on time in range is unlikely given ONWARDS 6 showed no TIR advantage.
evidence: ONWARDS 2 (Philis-Tsimikas et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2023)

assumptions.claim: In ONWARDS 6 in type 1 diabetes, insulin icodec was non-inferior to degludec on HbA1c change at 26 weeks, with an estimated treatment difference of about 0.05 percentage points.
In ONWARDS 6, combined level 2 or 3 hypoglycaemia rates were higher with icodec than with degludec.

reason: About 40 patients per arm gives only moderate power for a 15-20 point remission gap; a higher placebo remission rate in a partly biologic-naive Russian population could erase significance.
rationale: Anti-TL1A antibodies have consistently shown placebo-adjusted clinical remission gains of roughly 16-27 points in UC phase 2 trials (tulisokibart, duvakitug, afimkibart). BCD-261 is a new Biocad antibody against the same target; assuming similar potency, the high-dose arm versus placebo with ~40 per arm has about 60-70% power at two-sided 0.05. Placebo remission on modified Mayo is typically 5-20%. Biocad tends to report positively, but timing of disclosure is uncertain since the trial was still recruiting in late 2026.

assumptions.claim: Tulisokibart achieved clinical remission at week 12 in about 26% of UC patients vs about 1% on placebo.
Duvakitug high dose gave about 48% clinical remission at week 14 vs about 20% on placebo in UC.
assumptions.source: TUSCANY-2 topline, Sanofi/Teva press release Dec 2024

reason: Dapagliflozin lowers HbA1c about 0.8-1.0% on metformin; if HDM1002 400 mg is less potent than orforglipron or GI intolerance limits titration, the gap may not reach superiority.
rationale: HDM1002 is an oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist; the class (orforglipron) beat dapagliflozin on HbA1c in a phase 3 head-to-head. GLP-1 agonists typically lower HbA1c 1.5-2.0% from a baseline near 8.5%, versus about 0.8-1.0% for dapagliflozin, so a 0.5-0.7 point difference at week 40 with 200 per arm and SD near 1.0 gives high power. Risks are weaker potency of this molecule and GI dropouts. If the protocol tests non-inferiority first, success is even more likely.
evidence: Yang et al. 2016 dapagliflozin add-on to metformin in Asian patients

assumptions.claim: Dapagliflozin 10 mg added to metformin in Asian patients lowered HbA1c by about 0.8% at 24 weeks.
assumptions.source: Yang W et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2016

assumptions.claim: Oral orforglipron was superior to dapagliflozin on HbA1c reduction in type 2 diabetes on metformin.

reason: With 30 patients randomized 2:1 and perhaps 12-18 PFS events, only a hazard ratio near 0.35 or lower would reach significance, and the trial is likely descriptive.
rationale: A 30-patient open-label phase 2 with PFS over two years cannot be adequately powered for a formal superiority test; few events will accrue by any 2027 readout. Pazopanib first-line median PFS is about 8-11 months. Unless IBR854 is dramatically active, the hazard ratio will have a confidence interval crossing 1. The registered primary completion of December 2026 is unrealistic given ongoing recruitment, so any 2027 report would be immature.

assumptions.claim: First-line pazopanib had a median PFS of 8.4 months in advanced clear-cell RCC.

reason: Eighty patients split across five infection types leave only small cUTI, mortality and cIAI subsets; such CRE-vs-best-available-therapy trials are usually descriptive, and all three co-primaries would have to be met.
rationale: Pathogen-focused CRE trials against best available therapy (TANGO II, CARE, CREDIBLE-CR) are small, open-label and descriptive, without formal hypothesis tests. Here 80 patients are split across HABP/VABP, BSI, cIAI and cUTI, and three co-primaries must all be met. Best available therapy in China increasingly includes ceftazidime-avibactam, which works well against KPC, narrowing any gap. A sponsor claim that all primaries were met with statistical significance is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: TANGO II compared meropenem-vaborbactam with best available therapy in CRE infections descriptively, without formal hypothesis testing.
assumptions.source: Wunderink et al., Infect Dis Ther 2018

assumptions.claim: In CREDIBLE-CR, clinical cure rates were broadly similar between cefiderocol and best available therapy in cUTI.
assumptions.source: Bassetti et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021

reason: Capsid assembly modulators suppress residual viremia on top of NAs, but if neracorvir's add-on effect in HBeAg-positive low-level viremia is modest, the gap over continued NA could narrow, though 263 per arm still gives large power.
rationale: Neracorvir is a capsid assembly modulator that adds a second antiviral mechanism to nucleos(t)ide analogues. In HBeAg-positive patients with persistent low-level viremia on NA, continuing NA alone yields modest rates of HBV DNA below LLOQ, while CAM add-on in earlier studies clearly deepened suppression. With 263 per arm, even a 15-point difference would be highly significant. The sponsor moved to a 526-patient phase 3 after phase 2, implying a clear signal. Main uncertainty is timing of disclosure, not the result.
evidence: GST-HG141 phase 2 add-on in NA-treated CHB (Akeylink, 2023-2024)

assumptions.claim: Adding the capsid assembly modulator vebicorvir to NA therapy produced deeper HBV DNA suppression than NA alone in suppressed CHB patients.
assumptions.source: Yuen MF et al., J Hepatol 2022 (Study 201)

reason: Little risk: SGLT2 inhibitor add-on to metformin plus DPP-4 inhibitor reliably lowers HbA1c 0.6-0.8 points versus placebo; only an unusually low baseline HbA1c could shrink the effect.
rationale: Empagliflozin is an approved SGLT2 inhibitor with well-characterized effects; added to metformin plus a DPP-4 inhibitor it lowered HbA1c about 0.7-0.8 points versus placebo at 24 weeks. With about 85 per arm and SD near 0.8, power exceeds 99%. Korean triple-combination registration trials of this kind almost always meet their primary endpoint. Main uncertainty is whether and when Celltrion discloses results.
evidence: Softeland et al. 2017 empagliflozin add-on to linagliptin plus metformin
Mathieu et al. 2015 dapagliflozin add-on to saxagliptin plus metformin

assumptions.claim: Empagliflozin 10 mg added to linagliptin plus metformin lowered HbA1c about 0.8 points more than placebo at 24 weeks.
assumptions.source: Softeland E et al., Diabetes Care 2017

assumptions.claim: Ertugliflozin added to metformin plus sitagliptin lowered HbA1c about 0.7 points more than placebo at 26 weeks.
assumptions.source: VERTIS SITA2, Dagogo-Jack et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2018

reason: A 24-patient crossover in genetically confirmed non-dystrophic myotonia still recruiting in late 2026 is likely to finish beyond its January 2027 date; results will likely go to the EU registry rather than ClinicalTrials.gov.
rationale: Each patient needs about 29 weeks (screening, two 12-week periods and washout), so a January 2027 primary completion required the last patient enrolled by mid-2026, yet the record still says recruiting. Rare-disease recruitment in a single country tends to slip. Lupin is unlikely to post results on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027, and safety primaries are rarely changed.

reason: Low risk: if HRS-7249 is an APOC3 or ANGPTL3 silencer, TG falls 40-60% versus placebo; failure would require a weak molecule or a very small highest-dose arm.
rationale: A phase 2 with triglycerides as the sole efficacy primary in hyperlipidemia points to an APOC3- or ANGPTL3-targeted injectable. Such drugs (plozasiran, zodasiran, olezarsen) cut triglycerides by about 50-60% placebo-adjusted with between-patient SD near 30%, so even 30-40 patients per dose arm give near-certain significance. Hengrui's subsidiary completed dosing (primary completion Sept 2026), so a congress or press readout in 2027 is plausible.

assumptions.claim: Plozasiran reduced triglycerides by roughly 50-60% placebo-adjusted at week 24 in mixed hyperlipidemia.
Zodasiran reduced triglycerides by roughly 50-60% placebo-adjusted at week 24 in mixed hyperlipidemia.

reason: Espindolol's anabolic signal comes from cancer cachexia; during semaglutide-driven weight loss a 100-200 g per 4 weeks lean-mass benefit is plausible but underpowered with ~40 per arm, and both primaries (during and after semaglutide) must be met.
rationale: Semaglutide causes roughly 3 kg lean-mass loss over the first 20 weeks, about -600 g per 4 weeks. (S)-pindolol benzoate (espindolol) increased lean mass versus placebo in cancer cachexia (ACT-ONE), but in obese patients on semaglutide the effect is unproven. With ~40 per arm and SD near 350 g per 4 weeks, a 130 g benefit gives under 50% power, and the second primary (post-semaglutide, PROACT 2) must also succeed. Small private sponsor; disclosure timing uncertain.

assumptions.claim: In the STEP 1 DEXA substudy, semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced lean body mass by about 5.3 kg over 68 weeks.
Espindolol 10 mg twice daily increased body weight and lean body mass versus placebo over 16 weeks in cancer cachexia.
assumptions.source: Stewart Coats et al., J Cachexia Sarcopenia Muscle 2016 (ACT-ONE)

reason: Statin initiation or intensification after ACS cuts LDL-C substantially in the placebo arm, shrinking the absolute percent difference, but inclisiran's ~50% relative lowering still leaves a large, highly significant gap.
rationale: Inclisiran consistently lowers LDL-C about 50% versus placebo (ORION-10/11), and Day 150 falls 60 days after the second dose, near peak effect. In ACS, standard-of-care statin intensification gives the placebo arm a 20-35% fall (EVOPACS placebo -35%), so the between-arm difference in percent change will be about 35-40 points. With 150 per arm and SD near 25%, significance is essentially certain. Results likely appear at ESC or AHA 2027, after June.

assumptions.claim: Inclisiran lowered LDL-C by about 50% placebo-adjusted in ORION-10 and ORION-11.
In EVOPACS, LDL-C fell about 35% with placebo plus atorvastatin 40 mg and about 77% with evolocumab at 8 weeks after ACS.

reason: BFB759 is a novel-target biologic from a private biotech with little public clinical data; a high and variable placebo EASI response in modern AD trials can swamp a modest drug effect.
rationale: Phase 2 dose-ranging trial of a first-in-class antibody from Bluefin with no public efficacy data. Novel AD mechanisms succeed in phase 2 about half the time (OX40/OX40L positive, several others failed). Placebo percent change in EASI at week 16 runs -15% to -41% in recent phase 2b trials, so the highest dose needs roughly -55% or better. Enrollment is complete and the week-16 readout is likely in H1 2027; a private sponsor is more likely to announce a positive result quickly, so the June conditional is nudged up slightly.

assumptions.claim: Placebo mean percent change in EASI at week 16 was about -41% in the lebrikizumab phase 2b trial.
Placebo mean percent change in EASI at week 16 was about -15% in the rocatinlimab phase 2b trial.

reason: Small Chinese dose-optimisation study of an anti-PD-L1 ADC in CRC still recruiting with an ORR endpoint; the end-2026 primary completion will probably be pushed back if the record is updated.
rationale: Still recruiting at the snapshot, with a staged design (pause after 5 per arm, then expand two doses), so finishing by December 2026 is unlikely and any update probably pushes the date out. Henlius is prioritising HLX43, but CRC could be dropped if the signal is weak, which gives a small stop risk. Chinese sponsors rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov.

reason: All four primaries (NPS and NCS overall and in the ECRSwNP subset) must be met; anti-TSLP is validated in CRSwNP, but a Chinese population with more non-eosinophilic polyps and the smaller ECRSwNP subset NCS test are the weak points.
rationale: Anti-TSLP is validated in CRSwNP: tezepelumab in WAYPOINT cut NPS by about 2.1 points and NCS by about 1.0 versus placebo, both p<0.001. Chinese phase 3 biologic trials in CRSwNP (stapokibart CROWNS-2) also hit NPS and NCS co-primaries. With 123 per arm, power for NPS is near 100% and for NCS high. The main risk is that all four primaries, including the subset tests, must be met. Enrollment is done; topline is likely mid-2027 through an HKEX announcement.

assumptions.claim: Tezepelumab reduced nasal polyp score by about 2.07 points versus placebo at week 52 in CRSwNP.
Tezepelumab reduced nasal congestion score by about 1.03 points versus placebo at week 52.

reason: Clinical cure needs every sign and symptom at zero on day 28, two weeks after treatment; a sizable placebo response and boric-acid local irritation could shrink the gap below what 111 per arm can detect.
rationale: Boric acid is a well-established antifungal for VVC, especially non-albicans species, with high mycological cure rates in case series and older comparative studies, so superiority over placebo is likely. The strict composite clinical cure at day 28 still leaves a placebo cure of about 30-40% (placebo arms of recent VVC trials ran 28-44%), and with about 111 per arm the trial needs a gap of about 13 points or more. The trial completed in August 2026; a small private sponsor may announce topline or present at ACOG.

assumptions.claim: Placebo clinical cure in a recent pivotal VVC trial was about 29% at test of cure.
assumptions.source: VANISH-303, Schwebke et al., Clin Infect Dis 2022

assumptions.claim: Boric acid achieved mycological cure rates of roughly 40-100% in VVC, including non-albicans infections.
assumptions.source: Iavazzo et al., J Womens Health 2011

reason: With 40 per arm and a binary complete-clearance endpoint from a mild baseline (Oxford 1-2), a vehicle response near 20% means the drug needs a gap of over 20 points to reach significance.
rationale: rhPRG4 (lubricin) improved corneal staining and symptoms in a 2017 moderate dry-eye trial against hyaluronate, and small studies in ocular GVHD looked promising, but Sjogren's dry eye responds poorly to lubricants. The responder endpoint (complete resolution of staining at day 28) is demanding, vehicle drops also clear grade-1 staining in some patients, and 40 per arm gives low power unless the effect is large. A small private sponsor reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Lambiase et al., JAMA Ophthalmol 2017 (rhPRG4 vs hyaluronate in dry eye)

assumptions.claim: rhPRG4 improved corneal fluorescein staining and symptoms versus sodium hyaluronate in moderate dry eye over 28 days.

reason: Only 15 patients in a crossover with two co-primary endpoints (corneal staining and total symptom VAS) that must both reach significance; a 14-day washout may also allow carryover.
rationale: rhPRG4 has shown benefit on staining and symptoms in small dry-eye and ocular GVHD studies, and a within-patient crossover gains some power, but 15 patients and two co-primaries (staining and total VAS) that must both be significant make a formal win unlikely. Oxford grades change by fractions of a grade over 28 days. Still recruiting in a rare population at an Australian sponsor, so slow enrolment and late or no public reporting are likely.
evidence: Lambiase et al., JAMA Ophthalmol 2017 (rhPRG4 in dry eye)

assumptions.claim: rhPRG4 improved corneal staining and dry-eye symptoms versus an active comparator in a 28-day randomized trial.

reason: Chinese multiple-ascending-dose IPF safety study still recruiting near its registered end-2026 primary completion, so any update will probably push the date out; posting on ClinicalTrials.gov is unlikely.
rationale: The study started in November 2025, needs 48 patients across ascending-dose cohorts with about a year of follow-up, and was still recruiting at the snapshot, so a December 2026 primary completion is not achievable and an updated record would show a later date. Small Chinese sponsors seldom post results. The safety-only primary outcome is unlikely to be changed.

reason: A first-in-class dual agonist must at least match titrated cinacalcet on both the >50% and >30% iPTH responder endpoints; unknown dosing and a margin not stated in the record leave room for a non-inferiority miss.
rationale: Head-to-head trials of newer calcimimetics against cinacalcet (etelcalcetide, evocalcet) met non-inferiority, and etelcalcetide was superior on the >50% reduction endpoint (52% vs 40%). A double-dummy phase 3 after phase 2 suggests MT1013 lowers PTH robustly, so non-inferiority on both responder co-primaries is likely. Still recruiting at the snapshot with a 26-week treatment period, so the November 2026 completion date will slip and topline before mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Block et al., JAMA 2017 (etelcalcetide vs cinacalcet)
Fukagawa et al., Kidney Int 2018 (evocalcet vs cinacalcet)

assumptions.claim: In the etelcalcetide vs cinacalcet head-to-head trial, 40.2% of cinacalcet patients achieved >50% PTH reduction during weeks 20-27.
Evocalcet was non-inferior to cinacalcet for PTH target achievement in Japanese hemodialysis patients.

reason: With 85 per arm and a pembrolizumab-chemo control near 20% pCR in non-squamous disease, IBI363 needs an improvement of about 14 points or more to reach significance, and the randomized phase 2 may be reported descriptively without a formal test.
rationale: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy gave 18% pCR in KEYNOTE-671, and non-squamous tumours respond less than squamous; Chinese neoadjuvant trials ran 25-40% across histologies. IBI363 (PD-1/IL-2 bispecific) is active in IO-resistant NSCLC, mostly squamous, but its added benefit in IO-naive non-squamous disease with chemotherapy is unproven. An 85-per-arm phase 2 has limited power, and the design and alpha are not stated, so a descriptive report that does not count as met is plausible. Innovent presents often (ASCO, WCLC), but enrolment was still ongoing at the snapshot.

assumptions.claim: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy produced a pCR rate of 18.1% in KEYNOTE-671.
Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus chemotherapy produced a pCR rate of 24.0% in CheckMate 816.

reason: Cabergoline is established as more effective and better tolerated than bromocriptine; the main risk is a well-titrated bromocriptine arm over 14 weeks narrowing the gap, but non-inferiority should still hold.
rationale: Cabergoline beat bromocriptine decisively in the 1994 NEJM trial (prolactin normalized in 83% vs 59%; ovulatory cycles 72% vs 52%; discontinuation 3% vs 12%), and meta-analyses confirm its superiority. A non-inferiority or even superiority test against bromocriptine is very likely met. The trial was still recruiting at the snapshot, so the November 2026 completion will slip; a Chinese sponsor seeking registration is unlikely to publish before mid-2027.
evidence: Webster et al., NEJM 1994 (cabergoline vs bromocriptine)
Dos Santos Nunes et al., Pituitary 2011 meta-analysis

assumptions.claim: Cabergoline normalized prolactin in 83% of women vs 59% with bromocriptine.
Discontinuation for drug intolerance was 3% with cabergoline vs 12% with bromocriptine.

reason: Tranexamic acid is already a highly effective antifibrinolytic in TKA, so a 90-per-arm phase 2 has little room to show a significant further cut in Gross-formula blood loss, whose between-patient SD is near 250-300 mL.
rationale: Superiority over IV tranexamic acid, the standard antifibrinolytic in TKA, is a high bar for a phase 2 dose-finding study; most such designs aim at comparable efficacy. TXA-treated Chinese TKA patients lose roughly 700-950 mL by the Gross formula with SD near 280 mL, so with 90 per arm the trial needs about a 80-90 mL advantage to be significant. Nothing public on BT-114143 suggests a large edge over TXA. Results from a private Chinese sponsor are unlikely to be public by mid-2027, and a positive readout is more likely to be announced.
evidence: Xie 2016 J Arthroplasty multiple-dose IV TXA in TKA

assumptions.claim: Total blood loss by the Gross formula with IV tranexamic acid in primary TKA RCTs is typically about 600-950 mL.
assumptions.source: Xie J et al., J Arthroplasty 2016

assumptions.claim: IV tranexamic acid significantly reduces blood loss and transfusion versus placebo in primary TKA.
assumptions.source: Fillingham YA et al., J Arthroplasty 2018 (AAOS clinical practice guideline meta-analysis)

reason: Undetectable HDV RNA (target not detected) is a strict bar and week 24 is early; if tobevibart+elebsiran mostly drives patients below LLOQ but still detectable, the TND rate gap over continued bulevirtide could be smaller than planned.
rationale: Control patients are by definition bulevirtide partial/non-responders still at HDV RNA >=500 IU/mL after >=24 weeks, so few will become undetectable in another 24 weeks on the same drug. Tobevibart+elebsiran in SOLSTICE produced multi-log declines with a large share below LLOQ, and these patients start from lower viral loads, which favours reaching TND. With 75 per arm a 15-20 point gap is already significant. Vir is public and treats ECLIPSE as registrational, so a topline release in 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: In MYR301, only a minority (about 12% on 2 mg) had undetectable HDV RNA at week 48 of bulevirtide monotherapy.
Tobevibart plus elebsiran achieved HDV RNA <LLOQ in a majority of participants by week 48 in SOLSTICE.

reason: Prednisolone acetate 1% clears most anterior chamber cells within 14 days; a topical JAK inhibitor is unlikely to beat it and may fall short of a non-inferiority margin if its intraocular penetration is weaker than the steroid's.
rationale: An active-controlled phase 3 against prednisolone acetate is most likely powered for non-inferiority (as in the difluprednate program), which the trial's own hypothesis would decide; superiority is improbable. VVN461 is a topical JAK1/TYK2 inhibitor with phase 2 anti-inflammatory activity versus vehicle, but matching a potent steroid in acute anterior uveitis is uncertain. I put about 55% on non-inferiority success if that is the design, about 10% if superiority, giving roughly 0.45, with a positive readout more likely to be made public.
evidence: Foster 2010 difluprednate vs prednisolone acetate in anterior uveitis (Arch Ophthalmol)
Sheppard 2014 difluprednate vs prednisolone acetate phase 3

assumptions.claim: The difluprednate versus prednisolone acetate anterior uveitis phase 3 used change in anterior chamber cell grade at day 14 with a non-inferiority design and met it.
assumptions.source: Foster CS et al., Arch Ophthalmol 2010

reason: The exclusions for nitrates and PDE5 inhibitors point to an NO/cGMP-pathway vasodilator, whose add-on office SBP effect may be only a few mmHg, too small to separate from a large office-BP placebo response with about 70 patients per arm.
rationale: Office SBP in uncontrolled hypertension shows a 5-10 mmHg placebo fall and an SD of change around 14 mmHg, so 70 per arm needs roughly a 4.5-5 mmHg placebo-adjusted drop at week 4. Any of three doses may succeed, which helps. The mechanism (likely NO/cGMP, judging by the PDE5 and nitrate exclusions) usually gives modest add-on reductions, unlike aldosterone synthase inhibitors. With the record still recruiting and a 12-week treatment period, readout before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In BrigHTN, the placebo arm's seated office SBP fell by about 9 mmHg over 12 weeks in treatment-resistant hypertension.

reason: With about 50 patients per arm, a 20-point difference in undetectable HDV RNA at week 48 is only borderline significant, and a phase 2b may report the comparison descriptively rather than as a formal superiority test.
rationale: Bulevirtide 2 mg yields undetectable HDV RNA in only about 10-20% of naive patients at week 48, while tobevibart+elebsiran reached <LLOQ in a majority in SOLSTICE, with TND in perhaps 40-50%. A 25-30 point gap gives about 85% power at 50 per arm. The deductions are for a high-viral-load population (Moldova, Pakistan, Romania) that could blunt the combination's TND rate, and the chance that a phase 2b reports without a formal test. Vir is likely to present ECLIPSE 3 in 2027.

assumptions.claim: Bulevirtide 2 mg produced undetectable HDV RNA in roughly 12% of patients at week 48 in MYR301.
Tobevibart plus elebsiran achieved HDV RNA <LLOQ in a majority of SOLSTICE participants by week 48.

reason: With only about 40 patients per active arm, an unexpectedly high vehicle-PDT clearance rate or a weaker reformulation could shrink the gap, though ALA-PDT effects on face and scalp have historically been large.
rationale: Levulan ALA-PDT with blue light is an approved, well-characterised treatment that produced large complete-clearance gains over vehicle-PDT on the face and scalp in its pivotal trials. This study enrols only 4-8 mild-to-moderate lesions in a 25 cm2 field and allows a second PDT session, which favours high clearance. A reformulation of the same active is unlikely to lose much potency. The main uncertainty is disclosure: Sun Pharma rarely announces individual dermatology trial results, so public data before mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Piacquadio 2004 Arch Dermatol, Levulan face/scalp phase 3
Levulan Kerastick upper-extremity sNDA trials (2018 approval)

assumptions.claim: In the pivotal face/scalp phase 3, ALA-PDT with blue light gave a much higher week-12 complete clearance rate than vehicle-PDT.
assumptions.source: Piacquadio DJ et al., Arch Dermatol 2004

reason: Actinic keratoses on the arms are thicker and respond less to ALA-PDT than facial lesions, so complete clearance with the reformulated Kerastick could be modest, though 130 per arm leaves ample power for a 15-point gap.
rationale: Levulan ALA-PDT was approved for upper-extremity AK in 2018 on trials showing significantly higher complete clearance than vehicle-PDT, despite lower absolute rates than on the face. This trial limits lesions to 4-8 in a 25 cm2 field and allows a second session, both of which raise clearance, and its 130 per arm gives high power for a 15-20 point gap. A reformulation of the same active should keep most of its effect. Public results before mid-2027 are unlikely given Sun Pharma's disclosure habits.
evidence: Levulan Kerastick upper-extremity sNDA trials (2018 approval)
Piacquadio 2004 Arch Dermatol, Levulan face/scalp phase 3

assumptions.claim: Levulan Kerastick plus BLU-U blue light was approved by the FDA in 2018 for AK of the upper extremities on trials showing superior complete clearance versus vehicle.
assumptions.source: Levulan Kerastick US prescribing information (2018 revision)

reason: Failure would most likely come from a true exposure difference between QL2107 and Keytruda (for example from glycosylation or charge-variant differences) or from attrition reducing the cycle-7 steady-state PK set.
rationale: Monoclonal antibody biosimilar PK equivalence trials almost always succeed once analytical similarity is established, and the adjuvant setting keeps target-mediated clearance and tumour-burden variability low. With about 73 per arm and a between-patient CV near 30-35%, the 90% CI of the AUC ratio would be about +/-10%, comfortably inside a standard 80-125% margin if the products are truly similar. Qilu is private and rarely publicises trial results, so a public statement before mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Samsung Bioepis SB27 pembrolizumab biosimilar PK/efficacy trial (NCT06348199)

assumptions.claim: Biosimilar PK equivalence for monoclonal antibodies is conventionally judged by the 90% CI of the geometric mean AUC ratio falling within 80-125%.
assumptions.source: EMA Guideline on similar biological medicinal products containing monoclonal antibodies (EMA/CHMP/BMWP/403543/2010)

reason: TSLP/IL-13 blockade is unproven in CSU (tezepelumab missed at week 16) and IL-13 alone lacks dupilumab's IL-4 arm, so with 24 per arm and a sizeable placebo response a 5-point gap would not reach significance.
rationale: CM512 is Keymed's TSLP x IL-13 bispecific. In CSU, dupilumab (IL-4/IL-13) beat placebo by about 8 UAS7 points, but tezepelumab (TSLP) did not separate at week 16, and IL-13 alone has no CSU data. A small 48-patient Chinese phase 2 with SD around 12 has roughly 60% power only for an 8-point effect; a plausible 4-6 point effect gives well under half. Still recruiting near the registered primary completion, so readout slips into 2027 and disclosure by June 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Dupilumab improved UAS7 by roughly 8.5 points more than placebo at week 24 in omalizumab-naive CSU.
assumptions.source: LIBERTY-CSU CUPID Study A, Maurer et al. 2024

assumptions.claim: Tezepelumab did not significantly improve UAS7 versus placebo at week 16 in CSU.

reason: KLK5/KLK7 inhibition targets barrier proteases, a mechanism with no randomized AD efficacy data; with about 48 per arm the responder difference must be around 15-17 points to be significant, more than a barrier-directed antibody is likely to deliver.
rationale: TRIV-509 is an anti-KLK5/KLK7 antibody developed first for Netherton syndrome; its AD benefit is speculative. Phase 2a novel-mechanism AD trials succeed less than half the time, and 95 patients only detect large responder gaps (placebo EASI-75 typically 10-20%). Private sponsor more likely to announce if positive, lifting the conditional probability slightly. Enrolment complete, primary completion October 2026, so a topline release in early 2027 is plausible.

assumptions.claim: Placebo EASI-75 at week 16 in recent phase 2b AD monotherapy trials was roughly 10-20%.
assumptions.source: Rocatinlimab phase 2b, Guttman-Yassky et al. Lancet 2023

reason: Ciclosporin emulsion is an effective active comparator, so showing superiority on a coarse 0-5 staining scale at day 29 with 60 children per arm is unlikely; the trial may be estimation-only or non-inferiority.
rationale: Head-to-head phase 2 versus ciclosporin 0.1% cationic emulsion (Verkazia), which already lowers corneal staining in VKC. Superiority on a 0-5 ordinal scale over four weeks with 60 per arm needs a 0.5-point gap, larger than expected between two anti-inflammatory drops. The record does not state the hypothesis; if non-inferiority, success would be likelier, but superiority is assumed. Private French sponsor, India-only trial, so early disclosure is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Ciclosporin 0.1% cationic emulsion improved keratitis and symptoms versus vehicle over 4 months in severe VKC.

reason: GIP receptor agonism is antiemetic in ferrets and shrews but unproven in humans; on top of guideline triple or quadruple prophylaxis the delayed-phase CR is already near 65-75%, leaving little room to show a 13-point gain with about 100 per arm.
rationale: LY3537021 appears to be a long-acting GIP receptor agonist (GLP-1/GIP and thyroid-tumour exclusions). Preclinical work showed GIPR agonism blocks cisplatin emesis, but human translation is untested. Control delayed CR with NK1+5-HT3+dexamethasone runs 52-75% across trials; adding a new agent needs roughly a 13-point gain for significance with 102 per arm. Lilly usually discloses phase 2 results via ClinicalTrials.gov near the 12-month deadline, so June 2027 disclosure is unlikely.
evidence: Borner et al. Mol Metab 2020 (GIPR agonism and CINV, preclinical)

assumptions.claim: In the olanzapine trial, delayed-phase complete response was 67% with olanzapine versus 52% with placebo on triple prophylaxis.
GIP receptor agonism reduced cisplatin-induced emesis in shrews.

reason: Only 12 placebo patients, but a GLP-1 agonist giving 11-15% placebo-adjusted weight loss cuts fat mass by about 20%, far beyond the noise; failure would need unexpected dropouts or very poor adherence.
rationale: Aleniglipron produced double-digit placebo-adjusted weight loss at 36 weeks in ACCESS. GLP-1 agonists reduce fat mass by about 1.4-1.6 times the percent weight loss (semaglutide and tirzepatide DXA substudies), so a roughly 18-point fat-mass gap with SD near 9 is expected; even with 59 versus 12 patients this gives near-certain significance. Trial completed September 2026; Structure is a public company that discloses data actively, likely by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-1's DXA substudy, tirzepatide reduced total fat mass by about 34% versus about 8% with placebo at 72 weeks.
Aleniglipron gave double-digit placebo-adjusted weight loss at 36 weeks in the ACCESS phase 2b.

reason: HS trials have variable placebo responses, and HiSCR75 with roughly 50 per arm in a multi-dose design needs about a 20-point gap, so a high placebo rate could sink an otherwise active TNF/OX40L bispecific.
rationale: Brivekimig blocks TNF (validated in HS by adalimumab) plus OX40L, and Sanofi advanced it to phase 2b after a positive phase 2a in HS. IL-17 agents achieved HiSCR75 gaps of 20-30 points over placebo rates of 10-20%. With about 4 arms of ~52, power for the highest dose is around 65-75% and any dose counts. Still recruiting in late October 2026 against a February 2027 primary completion, so readout likely after June 2027.

assumptions.claim: Placebo HiSCR50 at week 16 was about 29-32% in BE HEARD I and II.
assumptions.source: Kimball et al. Lancet 2024 (BE HEARD I/II)

reason: Large 1,200-patient AF safety study still recruiting with a February 2027 primary completion, so recruitment will likely run past late 2026 and the registered date is likely pushed back; Regeneron keeps records current and the FXI programme is a priority, so stopping or early posting is unlikely.
rationale: Enrolling 1,200 AF patients at 89 sites in four countries in about 13 months is ambitious; with a 12-week bleeding endpoint, a February 2027 primary completion requires full enrolment by about November 2026, which looks tight while still recruiting. Regeneron updates records, so a slip would show. Results posting by August 2027 is unlikely given the 12-month window after primary completion.

reason: Anti-TL1A has no clinical RA efficacy data and many cytokine-targeted mechanisms beyond TNF, IL-6, JAK, CD80/86 and CD20 have failed in MTX-IR RA; with about 62 per arm ACR20 needs a 17-point gap.
rationale: Tulisokibart works in UC (ARTEMIS-UC), but TL1A's role in RA rests on preclinical and serum-level data; IL-17, IL-23 and other novel pathways failed in RA phase 2. Placebo plus MTX ACR20 at week 12 runs about 30-40%, so with ~62 per arm a ~17-point gap is needed. Multiple doses improve the odds slightly. Primary completion September 2026; Merck typically posts results near the 12-month deadline, so public data by June 2027 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Placebo plus csDMARD ACR20 at week 12 was about 36% in SELECT-NEXT.
Tulisokibart induced clinical remission significantly more than placebo in moderate-to-severe UC.

reason: A once-weekly incretin-class agent built for over 25% weight loss should beat placebo by a wide margin at 36 weeks; the realistic failure route is GI intolerance and dropouts eroding the top dose, not lack of efficacy.
rationale: NNC0662-0419 excludes recent GLP-1, GIP and amylin users and asks for willingness to lose over 25%, which suggests a potent multi-agonist (possibly the licensed triple agonist). Incretin agonists at 36 weeks typically give 10-20% placebo-adjusted weight loss with placebo at -1 to -3%, so significance is near certain for the highest dose. Novo often discloses phase 2 obesity headlines in quarterly reports or at ADA, plausible by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Placebo weight change was about -2% at 48 weeks in the retatrutide phase 2 obesity trial.

reason: Three co-primaries must all be won; a high vehicle IGA success rate, common in acne trials, could squeeze the IGA difference below significance even though lesion counts should separate.
rationale: Trifarotene 50 mcg/g beat vehicle on IGA success and both lesion counts in PERFECT 1 and 2 (IGA 29.4% vs 19.5% and 42.3% vs 25.7%). This bridging trial in China repeats that design with 280 per arm, giving high power for a 10-15 point IGA gap and the lesion counts. Main risk is a high vehicle response. Enrolment complete, primary completion end 2026; Galderma rarely press-releases regional bridging data, so public results by June 2027 are unlikely.
evidence: PERFECT 1 and PERFECT 2 (Tan et al. JAAD 2019)

assumptions.claim: In PERFECT 1 and 2, facial IGA success at week 12 was 29.4% vs 19.5% and 42.3% vs 25.7% for trifarotene vs vehicle.
assumptions.source: Tan et al. J Am Acad Dermatol 2019

assumptions.claim: Truncal PGA success was significantly higher with trifarotene than vehicle in both PERFECT trials.
assumptions.source: Tan et al. J Am Acad Dermatol 2019

reason: No oral agent has convincingly shrunk drusen in 24 weeks; percent change in drusen area is noisy and a TCM granule may have no measurable anatomical effect against a placebo arm whose drusen change little.
rationale: Oral supplements (AREDS formulations) slow progression over years but do not regress drusen in months, so a 24-week drusen-area effect from a TCM granule is biologically uncertain. Offsetting this, the sponsor advanced to phase 3 presumably on a positive phase 2, the endpoint is anatomical and single-country Chinese TCM trials report positive results at a high rate. 200 per arm gives decent power for a moderate effect. Still recruiting with March 2027 primary completion, so early reporting is very unlikely.

assumptions.claim: AREDS-type oral antioxidant/zinc supplementation reduced progression to advanced AMD over about 5 years but was not shown to regress drusen.

reason: CIAS has a long record of failed pro-cognitive mechanisms; with about 37 per arm over 28 days and practice effects on the BAC App, a KAT-II inhibitor needs a large effect to reach significance.
rationale: KYN-5356 lowers brain kynurenic acid via KAT-II inhibition, a plausible but clinically unproven CIAS mechanism. Recent CIAS programmes (iclepertin phase 3, luvadaxistat, encenicline, inidascamine) largely failed on cognition. The inpatient design reduces noise, three doses give multiple chances, and any dose meeting counts, but arms of about 37 make a nominally significant BAC composite difference unlikely. Completed in September 2026, so a topline from this private sponsor is plausible in early 2027.

assumptions.claim: Boehringer Ingelheim's phase 3 CONNEX programme of iclepertin did not meet its primary cognition endpoints in CIAS.
Luvadaxistat (DAAO inhibitor) failed to meet its primary cognitive endpoint in the phase 2 ERUDITE CIAS trial.

reason: Grade 0 throughout requires no faint erythema at any weekly visit; with 26 Gy in 5 fractions most patients still get grade 1, and topical radioprotectors have rarely shown clear benefit, so a 91-per-arm trial may not separate.
rationale: Topical amifostine thiol is a novel approach; systemic amifostine radioprotection is established but topical delivery is unproven in humans at scale. The endpoint (never any dermatitis) is stringent and grade 1 is subjectively scored, while ultra-hypofractionation causes mostly mild reactions, leaving a modest window. Two doses help under the any-dose rule. Small private sponsor, UK/France only, no FDAAA posting duty.

assumptions.claim: In FAST-Forward, acute breast skin reactions with 26 Gy in 5 fractions were mostly mild, with grade 3 reactions rare.
assumptions.source: Brunt et al., Radiother Oncol 2016 (FAST-Forward acute skin toxicity substudy)

reason: With 30 per arm and a between-patient SD of CAP change around 35 dB/m, only an effect of about 25 dB/m would reach significance, larger than probiotics usually achieve.
rationale: Probiotic RCTs in MASLD give mixed, mostly small effects on steatosis; CAP is noisy and placebo arms drift down through regression to the mean after a CAP >268 entry threshold. A single-site 60-patient trial is underpowered for realistic effects. Still recruiting with February 2027 primary completion, so results by mid-2027 are very unlikely; a supplement sponsor is unlikely to run a phase 3.

reason: About 53 per arm over 12 weeks with an FVC-change SD near 140 mL gives roughly 35-45% power even for an oral-nintedanib-sized effect of about 50 mL, so a real benefit can miss significance.
rationale: Nintedanib is a proven antifibrotic; in antifibrotic-naive patients a placebo arm loses about 60-80 mL over 12 weeks, and oral nintedanib separates by about 50 mL at that point. Inhaled delivery should give high lung exposure but the dose may be lower than oral. The main limit is power: 12 weeks, ~53 per arm. Two doses add a second chance. Still recruiting against a December 2026 completion, so a slip to mid-2027 topline is likely.

assumptions.claim: In INPULSIS-1 and -2, oral nintedanib reduced annual FVC decline by about 95-125 mL versus placebo.
In the 12-week nerandomilast phase 2, placebo patients not on background antifibrotics lost about 80 mL of FVC.

reason: The main risk is that MVA-BN grown in the CCX.E10 quail line yields lower neutralizing titres than chicken-fibroblast Jynneos so the GMT-ratio lower bound falls below the margin.
rationale: Manufacturing-comparability trials of the same vaccine strain are designed with ample power (about 485 per arm) and usually succeed; Bavarian Nordic previously showed freeze-dried MVA-BN non-inferior to liquid. The quail cell line is a deliberate scale-up move the sponsor would have checked in development. Residual risk is a real potency difference. As a listed company with strategic interest in the switch, BN is likely to report the outcome in its 2026 annual report or a release.

assumptions.claim: A phase 3 trial showed freeze-dried MVA-BN induced vaccinia neutralizing antibody titres non-inferior to the liquid-frozen formulation.
assumptions.source: Bavarian Nordic freeze-dried MVA-BN phase 3, NCT01668537

reason: Efficacy against placebo is near certain for an incretin triple agonist at 36 weeks; the only plausible failure route is high GI-driven discontinuation diluting the treatment-policy estimate.
rationale: HM15275 is a GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist; drugs in this class (retatrutide) give 20%+ weight loss at 36-48 weeks against about 2% on placebo, and even a weaker molecule would separate easily with about 53 per arm. Primary completion January 2027; Hanmi, a listed company, tends to disclose topline and present at ADA in June, so publication by June 2027 is roughly even.

assumptions.claim: Retatrutide 12 mg produced a mean weight change of -24.2% at 48 weeks versus -2.1% with placebo.

reason: Fully enrolled DoD-funded dose-finding vaccine study with a January 2027 primary completion; likely finishes near schedule, though Part 2 selection could push dates, and posting by August 2027 is unlikely before the FDAAA deadline.
rationale: Active, not recruiting, so dates should hold unless Part 2 regimens extend the primary window; government-funded plague vaccine work rarely terminates, and Dynavax typically posts near the one-year deadline.

reason: The composite needs investigator and patient to agree on a 2-grade gain at week 2, which caps responder rates near 40%, but placebo rates are near zero so failure is very unlikely.
rationale: IncobotulinumtoxinA reliably weakens platysma bands; the onabotulinumtoxinA phase 3 programme with the same composite design showed about 38-41% versus 1-4% responders at day 14. With 150 per arm the trial is powered for far smaller differences. Merz is private and EU-only here, so disclosure timing (congress or release) is the main uncertainty rather than the result.

assumptions.claim: In onabotulinumtoxinA phase 3 platysma prominence trials, composite investigator-and-subject responder rates at day 14 were about 38-41% versus 1-4% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Allergan Aesthetics BOTOX platysma prominence FDA approval, October 2024

reason: Fully enrolled PK bridging study with October 2026 primary completion and long extension; termination is unlikely and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely given non-US sites and a possible delayed-submission certification for the new route.
rationale: TG Therapeutics needs this AUC non-inferiority study for an SC ublituximab filing, so it will run to completion; posting on ClinicalTrials.gov typically lags or is deferred pending approval.

reason: Anti-IGF-1R antibodies give very large proptosis responses against a low placebo rate; the only real risk is that the subcutaneous VRDN-003 regimen gives lower exposure than the IV agents and a smaller-than-expected separation in 54 vs 54 patients.
rationale: IGF-1R blockade is a validated mechanism in active TED: teprotumumab (OPTIC 83% vs 10%) and veligrotug (THRIVE 70% vs 5%) gave proptosis responder differences of 60-75 points, and Chinese placebo arms run low. VRDN-003 is the half-life-extended subcutaneous sibling of veligrotug; even a materially weaker effect (30-40 points) would be significant with 54 per arm. Enrolment is complete, primary completion March 2027, so Zai Lab topline around mid-2027 is plausible but may slip past June.

assumptions.claim: In OPTIC, the week-24 proptosis responder rate was 83% with teprotumumab versus 10% with placebo.
In THRIVE, veligrotug gave a proptosis responder rate of 70% versus 5% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Viridian Therapeutics THRIVE topline press release, 2024

reason: All three viral-load time points are registered primaries; the Day 2 change comes after barely a day of dosing in older outpatients treated up to 72 h after symptom onset, when viral load is already falling, so the early difference may not reach significance even if Day 4 and Day 6 do.
rationale: S-337395 is an oral RSV L-protein (polymerase) inhibitor that cut viral load substantially in a human challenge study; polymerase inhibitors act quickly, so Day 4 and Day 6 differences of roughly 0.8-1 log are plausible. The binding constraint is the Day 2 co-primary: with about 90 evaluable per arm and between-patient SD near 1.3 log, a 0.5-log difference gives only about 65% power. Late treatment in naturally infected high-risk adults and floor effects at Day 6 add risk. Adult RSV outpatient trials enrol slowly, so the timeline likely slips.
evidence: S-337395 RSV human challenge phase 2, Shionogi 2024
Zelicapavir RSVHR phase 2b in high-risk adults, Enanta 2025

assumptions.claim: S-337395 significantly reduced RSV viral load AUC versus placebo in a phase 2 human challenge study.
assumptions.source: Shionogi press release on S-337395 challenge study, 2024

reason: With 30 patients per arm and an expected day-21 mortality around 10-15%, no plausible difference in all-cause mortality can reach significance; the phase 2 is built for safety and estimation, not to show superior survival over LAmB or voriconazole.
rationale: Turletricin is a less nephrotoxic amphotericin analogue; its case rests on renal safety, not on lower mortality. A 60-patient trial cannot show a mortality difference of the size possible here (expected deaths are about 3-5 per arm), so the formal superiority test, if run, will almost surely not be significant and the sponsor will describe results descriptively. Enrolment of early invasive mould infections in haematology patients is slow, so the December 2026 primary completion will likely slip and a public result before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In SECURE, all-cause mortality through day 42 was about 20% with voriconazole in invasive mould disease.

reason: With 50 per arm and a between-patient SD of about 13 points in time-in-range change, the 95% CI on the difference spans roughly plus or minus 5 points, so unless the unstated non-inferiority margin is generous a novel basal insulin with similar true efficacy can still fail to exclude the margin.
rationale: LY3938577 appears to be a novel basal insulin compared head to head with titrated degludec on CGM time in range. New basal insulins (efsitora, icodec) have matched degludec on glycaemic control, so a near-zero true difference is likely; the open question is precision. The margin is unstated; Lilly phase 2 NI designs usually use generous margins, but 50 per arm leaves real chance of an inconclusive interval, and a less potent mechanism (for example glucose-responsive insulin) would lower odds. Primary completion November 2026; ADA June 2027 or EASD September 2027 are the likely venues.

assumptions.claim: Once-weekly efsitora was non-inferior to degludec for HbA1c change in insulin-treated type 2 diabetes.

reason: Enrolment and the 180-day follow-up appear finished, so the trial should close out normally; a small BARDA-funded sponsor may post results near or after the 12-month deadline in September 2027.
rationale: Status is active, not recruiting with the registered primary completion (September 2026) already past, so termination is unlikely. As a US vaccine trial under IND it is an applicable clinical trial with a results deadline around September 2027, just after the read date; small sponsors often post late, so posting by end of August 2027 is unlikely but possible. Safety-only primaries in a completed trial rarely change.

reason: Combining an amylin agonist with a second incretin-class peptide should give double-digit placebo-adjusted weight loss; the main way to miss would be heavy GI-driven discontinuation in the combination arm eroding the treatment-regimen estimate in a 50-patient arm.
rationale: Eloralintide alone gave up to about 20% weight loss at 48 weeks in phase 2 obesity; people with type 2 diabetes lose less, and 32 weeks is shorter, but a placebo-adjusted loss near 10% or more is expected for the combination, far beyond what 50 per arm needs (SD about 6-7%). Placebo in T2D obesity trials loses about 2%. Primary completion March 2027, so data likely appear at EASD or ObesityWeek 2027 rather than by June.
evidence: SURMOUNT-2 (tirzepatide in obesity with T2D), Lancet 2023

assumptions.claim: Eloralintide produced mean weight loss of up to 20.1% at 48 weeks in its phase 2 obesity trial.
assumptions.source: Eli Lilly eloralintide phase 2 results, ObesityWeek 2025 / Lancet 2025

assumptions.claim: Placebo-treated participants with obesity and type 2 diabetes lost 3.2% of body weight at 72 weeks in SURMOUNT-2.

reason: The trial's own hypothesis is superiority of the combination over SnF2 alone and KNO3 alone as well as vehicle, on both Schiff and tactile endpoints; beating an active stannous fluoride dentifrice by a significant margin on both measures is the hard part.
rationale: Against vehicle, an SnF2 plus KNO3 dentifrice will almost certainly win on Schiff and tactile scores at week 8. But the record states the aim is superiority versus SnF2-only, KNO3-only and vehicle, with both endpoints co-primary. Differences between active desensitising dentifrices are usually 0.1-0.3 Schiff points; 180 per arm gives decent power for about 0.2, but the tactile threshold is noisy and all comparisons must succeed. Haleon/GSK legacy posts CT.gov results reliably, likely around the August 2027 deadline.
evidence: GSK 0.454% stannous fluoride dentifrice dentin hypersensitivity trials, J Clin Dent 2013-2016
Cochrane review of potassium-containing toothpaste for dentine hypersensitivity, 2006

assumptions.claim: The trial's stated aim is to show superiority of the SnF2 plus KNO3 dentifrice over SnF2-only, KNO3-only and vehicle dentifrices after 8 weeks.

reason: Failure is nearly impossible: oral PCSK9 inhibition plus a statin against double placebo in lipid-therapy-naive adults yields a 70-plus point LDL-C difference; only a gross conduct problem would change that.
rationale: Enlicitide 20 mg lowered LDL-C by about 56-60% versus placebo in CORALreef, and rosuvastatin 10-20 mg alone lowers it about 46-52%; multiplicative effects predict roughly 75% reduction for the combination versus about 0% on placebo. With about 250 per arm and SD near 18%, the primary is certain if reported. The factorial design suggests a fixed-dose combination filing. Primary completion August 2026; presentation at ACC or EAS 2027 or CT.gov posting near August 2027 are likely.
evidence: STELLAR (rosuvastatin dose comparison), Am J Cardiol 2003

assumptions.claim: Enlicitide 20 mg reduced LDL-C by about 55.8% versus placebo at week 24 in CORALreef Lipids.
Rosuvastatin 10 mg and 20 mg reduced LDL-C by about 46% and 52% respectively.
assumptions.source: Jones et al., Am J Cardiol 2003 (STELLAR)

reason: Paediatric bowel-preparation trials requiring a scheduled colonoscopy enrol slowly across many European sites, so the January 2027 primary completion will probably be pushed back.
rationale: Still recruiting in late 2026 with 212 children aged 1-17 needed across 46 European sites; paediatric procedure trials tied to a regulatory paediatric plan routinely run over schedule, so a revised primary completion date after April 2027 is likely. There are no US sites, so CT.gov posting is not mandatory and results would go to the EU register instead. Termination is uncommon for PIP-mandated studies.

reason: With 38 per arm the trial is small, but the expected 50-point placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction is more than ten standard errors from zero, so failure is very unlikely.
rationale: AZD0780, an oral PCSK9 inhibitor, cut LDL-C by about 51% versus placebo on top of statins at 12 weeks in PURSUIT. This Russian bridging study repeats that design after a rosuvastatin run-in; with SD near 17% and 38 per arm the standard error is about 4 points, so significance is near certain. The trial completed in September 2026; AstraZeneca usually posts summary results around 12 months, with little else likely to be published.

assumptions.claim: AZD0780 30 mg reduced LDL-C by 50.7% versus placebo at 12 weeks on top of statin therapy in the PURSUIT phase 2b trial.

reason: Ritlecitinib's BTK inhibition is weaker than remibrutinib's and JAK3 blockade is unproven in CSU, so the UAS7 gain over a ~10-point placebo response may fall short of the ~4.5 points needed with about 67 per arm.
rationale: Ritlecitinib inhibits JAK3 and TEC-family kinases including BTK, the target validated in CSU by remibrutinib (about 6-8 UAS7 points over placebo at week 12). Its BTK potency is modest, so the effect may be smaller; JAK3 blockade of IL-4/IL-13 signalling adds plausibility (dupilumab works in CSU). With ~67 per arm and a UAS7 SD near 12, a difference of about 4.5 points is needed; I put the true effect near that threshold, giving roughly even odds. Still recruiting in October 2026, so results most likely come after June 2027.

assumptions.claim: In REMIX-1, placebo UAS7 change from baseline at week 12 was about -13.8 points versus about -20 with remibrutinib.
Ritlecitinib irreversibly inhibits JAK3 and TEC-family kinases including BTK.
assumptions.source: Xu H et al., ACS Chem Biol 2019 (PF-06651600)

reason: Enrolment is complete and the Day 31 immunogenicity primary has passed, so the trial should run to its December 2026 completion without incident, with results posting likely around mid-2027.
rationale: Enrolment is complete and the Day 31 immunogenicity primary was due July 2026, leaving only safety follow-up to December 2026. Termination is very unlikely for a single-dose bridging study of a licensed vaccine. GSK generally posts results within about 12 months of primary completion, which falls near July 2027, so posting by August 2027 is somewhat more likely than not, though a China-only, non-IND study may wait for study completion. Primary outcomes are well defined; changes would most likely be wording only, which does not count.

reason: UACR is noisy and baxdrostat may already lower intraglomerular pressure, so dapagliflozin's add-on reduction could be nearer 15% than 25-30%, which 111 per arm may not detect.
rationale: SGLT2 inhibitors reliably cut albuminuria about 25-30% on top of RAS blockade, and CONFIDENCE showed the effect adds to mineralocorticoid blockade (finerenone plus empagliflozin about 30% lower UACR than either alone). Prior SGLT2i users are washed out, so dapagliflozin's full effect is tested. With 111 per arm and a log-UACR SD around 0.8, a 25% relative reduction gives roughly 75-85% power. Main risks are UACR variability and a smaller increment after baxdrostat has already lowered intraglomerular pressure.

assumptions.claim: In CONFIDENCE, finerenone plus empagliflozin lowered UACR by about 52% from baseline at day 180, roughly 30% more than either drug alone.
Dapagliflozin reduced UACR by about 29% versus placebo in DAPA-CKD.
assumptions.source: Jongs N et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2021

reason: An unproven immune-modulating antibody in treatment-refractory vitiligo, with 22-23 per arm, needs about a 20-point F-VASI gain at week 24, larger than most systemic agents achieve.
rationale: EI-001 has only phase 1 healthy-volunteer data and no published vitiligo efficacy. Repigmentation is slow; even oral JAK inhibitors gave only about 20-35% F-VASI improvement at week 24 against near-zero placebo change, and this population is treatment-refractory. With 22-23 per arm and an SD near 35 points, a difference beyond about 20 points is needed. The trial was still recruiting in October 2026, so a 24-week primary readout before mid-2027 is unlikely and the registered primary completion will probably slip.

assumptions.claim: In the ritlecitinib phase 2b vitiligo trial, the placebo arm's F-VASI was roughly unchanged at week 24 (about +2%).

reason: Incretin-type drugs have not consistently improved smoking abstinence, and with 111 per arm the trial needs about a 13-point gain over a placebo continuous-abstinence rate near one third.
rationale: Brenipatide appears to be a Lilly incretin-type peptide; related agents have mixed smoking data: exenatide with nicotine patches improved short-term abstinence in one small trial, while dulaglutide added to varenicline did not. Relapse prevention over 24 weeks in recent quitters gives a placebo continuous-abstinence rate around a third, and 111 per arm need roughly a 13-point gain. I expect a modest effect near 6 points. The trial was still recruiting in October 2026 with a 24-week primary, so a public result before mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Yammine et al., Nicotine Tob Res 2021 (exenatide)
Tonstad et al., JAMA 2006 (varenicline relapse prevention)

assumptions.claim: Adding weekly dulaglutide to varenicline did not improve 12-week smoking abstinence versus placebo.
Exenatide plus nicotine patch raised 6-week point-prevalence abstinence to about 46% versus 27% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Yammine L et al., Nicotine Tob Res 2021

reason: Intra-articular saline gives a large placebo response, and a single GLP-1 agonist injection may not add the ~0.7-point WOMAC pain gain at week 4 that 65 per arm require.
rationale: 4P004 is an intra-articular GLP-1 receptor agonist with anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects in animal OA models but no controlled human efficacy data. Intra-articular saline produces large pain responses, and most novel IA agents fail to separate at early time points. Enrichment for synovitis suits the mechanism, but with 65 per arm a difference of about 0.7 WOMAC-pain points (likely a 0-10 diary scale) is needed. The trial completed in August 2026, so a topline release in the following months is likely.
