evidence: Bannuru et al., Ann Intern Med 2015 (placebo network meta-analysis in knee OA)
Meurot et al., Sci Rep 2022 (liraglutide in OA models)

assumptions.claim: Intra-articular placebo produces larger pain relief than oral placebo in knee OA trials.
assumptions.source: Bannuru RR et al., Ann Intern Med 2015

reason: Injection procedures in knee OA carry a large saline placebo response, and 75 per arm leave little room if SL1002's 12-week benefit is under one NRS point.
rationale: SL1002 is a single-injection treatment whose eligibility requires a positive diagnostic nerve block, suggesting a nerve-targeted mechanism and enriching for responders. Saline injections in knee OA produce large placebo responses (about 2 NRS points), so the trial needs roughly 0.8 points of separation with 75 per arm. Moving to a phase 3 implies some earlier signal, but a small single-trial readout with a strong placebo arm leaves the odds just under even.
evidence: Bannuru et al., Ann Intern Med 2015 (placebo network meta-analysis in knee OA)

assumptions.claim: Placebo injections in knee OA trials produce substantial pain improvement, larger than oral placebo.
assumptions.source: Bannuru RR et al., Ann Intern Med 2015

reason: A high placebo response in adjunctive MDD and an unvalidated mTORC1 mechanism make a separation of 2.3 MADRS points or more at day 29 unlikely.
rationale: SPN-821 (NV-5138) is an oral mTORC1 activator with preclinical rapid-antidepressant data and open-label phase 1b signals, but no controlled efficacy data. Adjunctive MDD trials have high placebo responses (about 10 MADRS points at 4 weeks) and novel mechanisms usually fail in phase 2. With 115 per arm and an SD near 9, a difference of about 2.3 points is needed; I expect around 1-1.5. Supernus is publicly listed and will likely announce topline around the first half of 2027.
evidence: Kato et al., J Clin Invest 2019 (NV-5138)

assumptions.claim: SPN-821 (NV-5138) is an oral sestrin modulator that directly activates mTORC1 and had rapid antidepressant effects in rodents.
assumptions.source: Kato T et al., J Clin Invest 2019

reason: Ritlecitinib lacks JAK1 inhibition, so its HiSCR50 gain may be under the ~16 points needed with 64 per arm against a placebo response near 30%.
rationale: JAK inhibition works in HS: upadacitinib, povorcitinib and Pfizer's brepocitinib each beat placebo on HiSCR in phase 2, by roughly 15-20 points. Ritlecitinib spares JAK1, the main HS signalling node, so its effect may be smaller; the loading dose suggests Pfizer is pushing exposure. Placebo HiSCR50 at week 16 runs near 30%, and with 64 per arm a difference of about 16 points is needed, so the odds are a little under even. Pfizer tends to disclose phase 2 results late, via congresses or registry posting.

assumptions.claim: In a phase 2 HS trial, upadacitinib 30 mg achieved HiSCR at week 12 in about 38% versus about 19% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Kimball AB et al., 2023 (upadacitinib phase 2 in HS)

reason: ZT006 appears to be an oral incretin (GLP-1 class exclusions, calcitonin screen, up-titration); a weak or poorly absorbed molecule giving under ~3-4% placebo-adjusted loss at 28 weeks is the main way it misses with 46 per arm.
rationale: Exclusions (prior GLP-1 use, pancreatitis, calcitonin) and daily up-titrated tablets point to an oral GLP-1-class agent. Oral GLP-1 agonists at high dose give roughly 8-12% placebo-adjusted weight loss over 26-36 weeks, while Chinese placebo arms lose about 0-2%. With ~46 per arm and SD ~6%, any effect beyond about -3% is significant, so the high dose very likely beats placebo. Residual risk is an unusually weak or poorly bioavailable molecule. Extension safety co-primaries carry no hypothesis. Disclosure timing is the bigger uncertainty for a small private sponsor.

assumptions.claim: In the orforglipron phase 2 obesity trial, mean weight change at week 36 was -9.4% to -14.7% with orforglipron versus -2.3% with placebo.
Placebo weight change in Chinese obesity trials of incretins has been small, around -1% to -3% over 26-52 weeks.

reason: Novel mechanism (possibly the IL-13/TSLP bispecific from the Proteologix deal, unconfirmed); several new AD mechanisms have given only modest EASI-75 gains at week 12, which with ~50-60 per arm could miss significance.
rationale: Janssen phase 2b dose-ranging trial versus placebo in moderate-to-severe AD, EASI-75 at week 12. If JNJ-95597528 is an IL-13-pathway biologic (likely the Proteologix bispecific), effects of 25-35 points over a 10-20% placebo rate are typical and the highest dose should separate comfortably. Uncertainty about the molecule and the record of failed novel AD mechanisms (IL-22, IL-33, H4) keep this below 0.8. Week 12 is a bit early for biologics. Disclosure by June 2027 depends on J&J using an earnings pipeline update or congress.

assumptions.claim: In SOLO 1 and SOLO 2, placebo EASI-75 at week 16 was about 12-15%.
In the lebrikizumab phase 2b trial, EASI-75 at week 16 was about 61% with the top dose versus 24% with placebo.

reason: About 52 patients per arm cannot detect the 5-10 point gains in mRS 0-1 that even effective late-window reperfusion therapy delivers; a significant highest-dose-vs-placebo difference is unlikely.
rationale: Phase 2 of an injectable agent in 4.5-24 h ischemic stroke without thrombolysis or thrombectomy; reperfusion and recanalization secondaries suggest a thrombolytic-type drug. TRACE-III showed tenecteplase raised mRS 0-1 from 24% to 33% in a similar window, which needed ~260 per arm. With ~52 per arm and three doses, power for any single dose is about 15-25%, and Chinese phase 2 dose-finding trials often report descriptively. Completed already, so a congress or press disclosure in 2027 is plausible but not assured.

assumptions.claim: In TRACE-III, mRS 0-1 at 90 days was 33.0% with tenecteplase versus 24.2% with standard medical treatment in 4.5-24 h LVO patients without thrombectomy.

reason: OTX-TKI produced little 2-step DRSS improvement in the HELIOS phase 1, so success rests on the ordinal endpoint capturing fewer worsening eyes than sham; a modest worsening rate in sham could leave too little separation.
rationale: Phase 3 in moderately severe to severe NPDR with a three-category DRSS change endpoint at week 52, which rewards prevention of worsening as well as improvement. The HELIOS phase 1 suggested axitinib implants mainly reduce progression and vision-threatening events rather than regress DRSS like aflibercept. With ~310 per arm the ordinal comparison is well powered if worsening is cut meaningfully. Still recruiting in Oct 2026 with a 52-week endpoint, the registered March 2027 completion is impossible, so topline before late 2027 is very unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In PANORAMA, about 15% of sham eyes achieved a 2-step or greater DRSS improvement at week 52.
In the HELIOS phase 1 NPDR trial, OTX-TKI reduced DRSS worsening and vision-threatening complications versus sham, while 2-step improvement was uncommon.

reason: With ~45 per arm and SD near 30 points, a placebo arm that improves itch by 30%+ (as seen in some PN trials) could shrink the difference below significance.
rationale: ICP-332 is InnoCare's TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor with strong phase 2 data in atopic dermatitis. JAK1 inhibition is itch-active in PN (povorcitinib phase 2, abrocitinib open-label). Placebo percent change in PP-NRS at week 16 in PN trials runs around -20% to -30%, and active drugs reach -45% to -60%. A ~22-point difference with SD ~30 and 45 per arm gives z near 3.5. Still recruiting with a March 2027 completion, so disclosure before mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: PRIME and PRIME2 dupilumab (Yosipovitch, Nat Med 2023)

assumptions.claim: In OLYMPIA 2, 20.9% of placebo patients achieved a 4-point or greater PP-NRS improvement at week 16 versus 56.3% with nemolizumab.
In its phase 2 atopic dermatitis trial, ICP-332 produced EASI-75 rates far above placebo within 4 weeks.

reason: JAK1 inhibition is well validated in AS; the main failure path is an unusually high placebo ASAS40 rate in a Chinese population with low baseline CRP, narrowing a well-powered comparison.
rationale: LNK01001 is a selective JAK1 inhibitor. Upadacitinib and tofacitinib both beat placebo on ASAS40 by 25-28 points at weeks 14-16, and Chinese JAK1 (ivarmacitinib) and IL-17 trials in AS succeeded with similar margins. With 176 per arm, a 15-point difference is detectable with high power. Main uncertainty is disclosure timing by a private Chinese sponsor, more than the outcome.
evidence: Tofacitinib AS phase 3 (Deodhar, Ann Rheum Dis 2021)

assumptions.claim: In SELECT-AXIS 1, ASAS40 at week 14 was 52% with upadacitinib versus 26% with placebo.
assumptions.source: van der Heijde et al., Lancet 2019 (NCT03178487)

assumptions.claim: In the tofacitinib AS phase 3, ASAS40 at week 16 was 40.6% versus 12.5% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Deodhar et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2021 (NCT03502616)

reason: Completed nutritional bioavailability study by an Australian CRO with an ingredient-company partner; not an FDA-regulated product trial, so results posting is unlikely and the record will probably stay as is.
rationale: Already completed in August 2026, so termination is essentially ruled out. Omega-3 supplement bioavailability studies sponsored by dsm-firmenich are usually published in journals rather than posted on ClinicalTrials.gov, and there is no FDAAA posting obligation. Primary outcome changes after completion are rare.

reason: Enzalutamide already drives PSA undetectable in about two-thirds of low-volume mHSPC patients; showing superiority of another AR inhibitor with ~103 per arm needs a 15+ point gap, though an unstated non-inferiority design would raise the odds.
rationale: Head-to-head of two second-generation AR inhibitors on 6-month PSA undetectable rate. Rezvilutamide is pharmacologically similar to enzalutamide; plausible differences are 0-10 points. Superiority at ~103 per arm needs about 15-17 points, so a pure superiority test likely fails; a label-expansion design could instead be non-inferiority, which Hengrui would likely meet. I weight the two at roughly 60/40. Still recruiting with a 6-month endpoint, so results before mid-2027 are improbable.
evidence: CHART rezvilutamide vs bicalutamide (Gu, Lancet Oncol 2022)

assumptions.claim: In ARCHES, 68.1% of enzalutamide plus ADT patients reached undetectable PSA (<0.2 ng/mL) versus 17.6% with placebo plus ADT.
In CHART, rezvilutamide plus ADT improved rPFS and OS versus bicalutamide plus ADT in high-volume mHSPC.

reason: About 20 patients per arm gives a standard error near 14 points on the HiSCR75 difference, so even a bimekizumab-sized 15-20 point effect would usually miss p<0.05.
rationale: Small phase 2 of SCT650C, a Sinocelltech antibody presumed to act on the IL-17 pathway, in HS with ~20 per arm. IL-17 agents raise HiSCR75 at week 16 from about 15-20% on placebo to 30-45%. Power for the highest dose versus placebo is roughly 25-35%, and small phase 2 trials often report descriptively. Still recruiting with a March 2027 completion, so a result by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In BE HEARD I and II, placebo HiSCR75 at week 16 was below 20% while bimekizumab reached about 33-35%.

reason: Complete clearance of every treatable wart within four sessions is a stringent bar; cantharidin may clear many but not all warts per patient, narrowing the gap over a vehicle arm that also gets paring and occlusion.
rationale: VP-102 (0.7% cantharidin) is approved for molluscum and cleared about half of treated common warts in open-label phase 2 COVE-1. Vehicle complete clearance of all warts in 12 weeks should be low (~10%), and 151 per arm gives >90% power for a 15-point gap. Blistering weakens blinding in the drug's favour. Enrollment is complete and Verrica, a small public company, should press-release topline around Q1 2027. Main risk is the all-warts endpoint diluting the effect in multi-wart patients.
evidence: CAMP-1 and CAMP-2 phase 3 VP-102 molluscum (Eichenfield, JAMA Dermatol 2020)

assumptions.claim: In open-label phase 2 COVE-1, about half of subjects achieved complete clearance of treated common warts at day 84 with VP-102 plus occlusion.
In the pivotal molluscum trials, complete clearance at day 84 was roughly 46-54% with VP-102 versus 13-18% with vehicle.
assumptions.source: CAMP-1/CAMP-2, Eichenfield et al., JAMA Dermatol 2020

reason: Durable functional cure requires stopping NA therapy; relapse after cessation could shrink the off-treatment response, but a placebo rate near zero makes significance likely, so the risk is mostly magnitude and timing rather than outright failure.
rationale: AHB-137, an antisense oligonucleotide, produced HBsAg loss in about half of NA-suppressed patients with low HBsAg in phase 2, far above other agents, and this population is enriched (HBsAg 100-3000 IU/mL). Placebo plus NA gives near-zero functional cure, so even a 5-8% durable off-treatment cure rate is significant with 289 per arm. The main uncertainty is relapse after stopping NA, which affects magnitude more than significance. The off-treatment window likely pushes data to mid-to-late 2027.
evidence: AHB-137 phase 2 in NA-suppressed CHB (AASLD 2024 / EASL 2025)

assumptions.claim: AHB-137 given for 24 weeks produced HBsAg loss in roughly half of NA-suppressed patients with low baseline HBsAg by end of treatment.
In B-Clear, bepirovirsen sustained HBsAg and HBV DNA loss 24 weeks off treatment in about 9-10% of patients, highest with low baseline HBsAg.

reason: Still recruiting a 100-child sickle cell population in the US and Dominican Republic with a day-181 safety primary outcome; enrollment pace will likely push primary completion into mid-to-late 2027, with no results posting by the read date.
rationale: Status is recruiting in late October 2026 while primary completion is registered as January 2027, yet one primary outcome runs to day 181 after vaccination, so completion must move past April 2027; Sanofi keeps records updated. Posting by August 2027 is unlikely given that timing. Termination risk is low but not nil given portfolio decisions on the PCV21 program.

reason: Challenge-model cryptosporidial diarrhea is self-limited and wanes by days 3-5 on its own, so a parasiticidal drug started after onset may not lower average stool grade enough to separate with about 40 per arm.
rationale: EDI048 is a gut-restricted PI(4)K inhibitor with strong in vitro and neonatal calf efficacy, but no anti-cryptosporidial drug has shown robust clinical benefit beyond modest nitazoxanide effects. Treating after diarrhea onset in self-limited challenge disease leaves a short window; placebo stool grades fall naturally by days 3-5, and 40 per arm with a noisy averaged ordinal score gives limited power. Novartis rarely announces such phase 2 data quickly; a congress or paper is more likely late 2027.
evidence: C. parvum human challenge study (Chappell et al., 2006)

assumptions.claim: Healthy adults challenged with C. parvum develop self-limited diarrhea typically lasting several days.
assumptions.source: Chappell et al., J Infect Dis 2006

assumptions.claim: Nitazoxanide, the only approved drug, shortened diarrhea only modestly in immunocompetent patients.
assumptions.source: Rossignol et al., J Infect Dis 2001

reason: Ocular MG symptoms are mild and fluctuating, with placebo improvement on stable standard care; a narrow ocular PRO scale and AChR-negative patients may dilute telitacicept's effect with only 60 per arm.
rationale: Telitacicept (TACI-Fc) beat placebo strongly on MG-ADL in the Chinese generalized MG phase 3 and is approved there for gMG. Ocular MG has a smaller dynamic range, more AChR-negative patients and placebo response on stable SOC; 60 per arm gives roughly 75-85% power for a 2-point gap with SD ~3.5. Chinese sponsor phase 3s with an active drug usually succeed. Still recruiting with a 24-week endpoint, so data likely late 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the Chinese phase 3 in generalized MG, telitacicept improved MG-ADL by roughly 4-5 points more than placebo at week 24.
MGII is a validated MG scale with patient-reported and examination items, higher scores meaning more impairment.

reason: Repigmentation at week 24 is still early; if SHR0302 doses are low or the single-centre population has long-standing stable lesions, the F-VASI response could be modest, though prior JAK data point to a clear win.
rationale: Oral JAK inhibitors (upadacitinib, ritlecitinib, povorcitinib) and topical ruxolitinib all beat placebo on F-VASI at week 24; adding SHR0302 gel to the oral JAK1 inhibitor should give a large effect (~30 points) against a placebo near -5%. With about 59 per arm and SD ~35, power is very high, and either active arm meeting suffices. Hengrui rarely announces phase 2 readouts and the trial is still recruiting, so public data before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Upadacitinib 11-22 mg reduced F-VASI by roughly 35-50% at week 24 versus under 10% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Passeron et al., upadacitinib vitiligo phase 2, 2024

assumptions.claim: Ritlecitinib 50 mg reduced F-VASI by about 21% versus a small worsening on placebo at week 24.

reason: A probiotic lozenge is unlikely to counteract three weeks of unchecked plaque; the expected bleeding-on-probing difference is small relative to between-person variability with 30 per arm.
rationale: Probiotic lozenges have shown inconsistent, small effects on gingival inflammation. In the experimental gingivitis model, plaque accumulation drives bleeding on probing strongly, and a salivaricin-producing S. salivarius is unlikely to offset it substantially. With 30 per arm and a between-subject SD of BOP change around 12 points, only a large effect would be significant. Academic sponsor; results likely via a paper or IADR abstract late 2027 or later.
evidence: Experimental gingivitis in man (Loe, Theilade, Jensen, 1965)

assumptions.claim: Abstaining from oral hygiene for about three weeks produces clinical gingivitis in healthy subjects, which reverses after hygiene resumes.

reason: Daily hGH already produces strong catch-up growth in SGA children, so the higher PEG-rhGH dose is unlikely to show statistically superior height velocity with about 24 per arm.
rationale: Active-controlled phase 2 comparing PEG-rhGH at a higher weekly dose with daily hGH. Earlier Jintrolong trials show height velocity similar to daily GH at matched exposure; a higher weekly dose might add about 0.5 cm/yr, but with 24 per arm and SD ~2 cm/yr power for superiority is low. The phase 2 is likely descriptive or non-inferiority-oriented, and a met non-inferiority hypothesis would count. Still recruiting; GenSci rarely publicizes phase 2 data early.
evidence: Jintrolong PEG-rhGH phase 3 in GHD (Luo et al., JCEM 2017)
KIGS SGA growth response analysis (Ranke et al., 2003)

assumptions.claim: Weekly PEG-rhGH 0.2 mg/kg/week produced height velocity comparable to daily rhGH in Chinese children with GHD.
assumptions.source: Luo et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2017

assumptions.claim: First-year height velocity on daily GH in short SGA children is roughly 9-11 cm/year.

reason: cGAS inhibition may not suppress the skin interferon signature enough in four weeks if interferon in CLE is driven mainly by plasmacytoid dendritic cell TLR7/9 signalling; 12 per arm leaves little power.
rationale: VENT-03 is an oral cGAS inhibitor; cGAS-STING contributes to type I interferon in CLE skin, but pDC/TLR-driven interferon may dominate. With 12 per arm, a 4-week course and a variable biopsy gene signature, only a large reduction (~50%) reaches significance. Pharmacodynamic biomarkers move more easily than clinical scores, so odds are moderate. The private sponsor will likely announce topline once the slow-enrolling global study completes, plausibly mid-to-late 2027.

assumptions.claim: Type I interferon signatures are strongly elevated in active cutaneous lupus lesions and can be lowered by targeting interferon-producing pathways.

reason: IL-17A blockade reliably beats placebo on ASAS40 in AS; the only realistic failure route is an unusually high placebo response in a large Chinese multicentre trial shrinking the gap.
rationale: 608 is 3SBio's anti-IL-17A antibody, already positive in psoriasis. Every IL-17A/F antibody tested in AS phase 3 (secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab, and Chinese agents such as vunakizumab, xeligekimab, gumokimab) beat placebo on ASAS40 at week 16, with gaps of roughly 20-35 points. With 250 per arm, a 15-point gap is easily significant. Main uncertainty is timing of disclosure, not efficacy; Chinese placebo ASAS40 sits around 15-22%.

assumptions.claim: In COAST-V, ASAS40 at week 16 was about 48% with ixekizumab Q4W versus 18% with placebo.
In MEASURE 1, ASAS40 at week 16 was about 42% with secukinumab versus 13% with placebo.
In BE MOBILE 2, ASAS40 at week 16 was about 45% with bimekizumab versus 22.5% with placebo.
assumptions.source: BE MOBILE 2, van der Heijde Ann Rheum Dis 2023

reason: ANGPTL3 silencing works through LPL, so patients with impaired LPL function in a severe-HTG population respond less; with only about 30 per arm, a diluted effect plus noisy TG could still miss.
rationale: Solbinsiran is Lilly's GalNAc siRNA against hepatic ANGPTL3. ANGPTL3 inhibition (evinacumab, zodasiran) cuts triglycerides by roughly 50-80% when LPL is functional, and FCS is excluded here. Placebo arms in sHTG drift down 10-20% from regression to the mean. A 40-50 point placebo-adjusted gap against an SD near 35% gives near-certain significance even with 30 per arm. Disclosure before mid-2027 is unlikely: still recruiting with a 24-week endpoint, and Lilly rarely press-releases phase 2.

assumptions.claim: The ANGPTL3 siRNA zodasiran lowered triglycerides by about half or more versus placebo at week 24 in mixed hyperlipidemia.
Evinacumab lowered triglycerides strongly in severe HTG patients without bi-allelic LPL-pathway loss-of-function and much less in those with it.

reason: Small single-country HFpEF phase 2 still recruiting with a 24-week endpoint and March 2027 primary completion, so a date slip past mid-2027 is about as likely as not; results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov is very unlikely.
rationale: Still recruiting in October 2026 with a 24-week safety endpoint means the March 2027 completion needs enrolment to finish almost now; HFpEF trials with narrow echo/KCCQ criteria often slip. Hengrui keeps records reasonably updated but rarely posts results to ClinicalTrials.gov for China-only trials. Termination is uncommon but possible if the myosin-inhibitor programme is reprioritised.

reason: Myostatin-pathway blockade shifts body composition (less fat, more lean) more than it lowers total body weight, so the net weight change versus placebo at 24 weeks may be too small to reach significance.
rationale: Taldefgrobep alfa is an anti-myostatin adnectin that failed its SMA phase 3. Myostatin-selective agents raise lean mass and modestly lower fat, leaving total weight nearly flat; only broader ActRII blockade (bimagrumab) has given about 6% weight loss over 48 weeks. As monotherapy without a GLP-1, a 1-2 point weight gap at 24 weeks is my central case, which a trial of this size (possibly split across doses) detects only some of the time. Biohaven may emphasize fat mass instead.

assumptions.claim: Bimagrumab reduced total body weight by about 6.5% versus 0.8% with placebo over 48 weeks, with fat loss and lean mass gain.
assumptions.source: Heymsfield et al., JAMA Netw Open 2021

assumptions.claim: Taldefgrobep alfa did not meet the primary endpoint of the phase 3 RESILIENT trial in spinal muscular atrophy.

reason: Weekly oral peptide delivery is unproven; low or variable oral bioavailability plus a short 20-week titration could leave the top Schedule A dose with a modest weight gap in an arm of only about 34 patients.
rationale: Ecnoglutide is a GLP-1 agonist with double-digit weight loss as an injection in Chinese phase 3. Any GLP-1 agonist with meaningful exposure gives 4-10 points more weight loss than placebo by 20 weeks (oral semaglutide, orforglipron). With about 34 per arm and SD near 5%, even a 3-point gap is significant. The main risk is that weekly oral absorption is weak, but the sponsor ran five dose arms after phase 1, so at least the top dose should separate.

assumptions.claim: Orforglipron reduced body weight by 8.6-12.6% at 26 weeks versus about 2% with placebo.
Injectable ecnoglutide produced double-digit percent weight loss versus placebo in a Chinese phase 3 obesity trial.

reason: Two artificial tears usually improve OSDI by similar amounts; if the protocol tests superiority over Refresh Optive rather than non-inferiority, the comparator is likely too strong for ABBV-444 to beat.
rationale: Allergan/AbbVie artificial-tear trials against a marketed Refresh product are typically non-inferiority studies on OSDI. With about 130 per arm and an OSDI SD near 17, a usual 7-8 point margin is shown almost always, and a 5-point margin most of the time. If the hypothesis is superiority instead, success is unlikely because artificial tears differ little. Weighting about 70-75% for a non-inferiority design gives p_met around 0.7. Disclosure probably comes through ClinicalTrials.gov posting near the August 2027 deadline.

assumptions.claim: Head-to-head artificial tear trials typically show OSDI improvements of 10-20 points in both arms over about 3 months with small between-arm differences.
assumptions.source: Allergan artificial tear trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov

reason: Add-on to existing binders over only 8 weeks; if TS-172's extra phosphorus lowering is smaller than tenapanor's, or diarrhoea forces dose limits, the gap in target achievement with 50 per arm could fall short.
rationale: TS-172 is Taisho's gut-acting phosphate-absorption inhibitor (NHE3 class like tenapanor) and lowered serum phosphorus in Japanese phase 2. Tenapanor added to binders in Japanese hemodialysis patients raised the share reaching target phosphorus at week 8 well above placebo, with placebo achievement in the single digits to low teens. A 25-30 point gap with 50 per arm is clearly significant. Diarrhoea-driven dropouts are the main tolerability issue.
evidence: Tenapanor Japanese add-on phase 3 with phosphate binders (Kyowa Kirin)
TS-172 phase 2 in Japanese hemodialysis patients (Taisho)

assumptions.claim: Tenapanor added to phosphate binders in Japanese hemodialysis patients significantly increased the share reaching target serum phosphorus at week 8 versus placebo.
assumptions.source: Tenapanor Japanese phase 3 add-on trial, Kyowa Kirin

reason: Semaglutide 2.4 mg is a strong comparator; if the HRS9531 dose used is not the top dose or open-label discontinuations dilute the gap, superiority at 52 weeks could be narrower than expected.
rationale: HRS9531 is Hengrui's GLP-1/GIP dual agonist (KAI-9531 at Kailera) with tirzepatide-like weight loss in Chinese phase 2/3. Tirzepatide beat semaglutide by about 6.5 points in SURMOUNT-5. Semaglutide 2.4 mg gives about 12% loss in Chinese adults at 44-52 weeks. With 286 per arm and SD about 7, a 3-point gap is already significant, so superiority is likely. The trial may test non-inferiority first, which only makes success easier.

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide produced about 20% weight loss versus about 14% with semaglutide at 72 weeks in SURMOUNT-5.
Semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced body weight by about 12% at 44 weeks in mostly Chinese adults with obesity.

reason: About 17 boys per arm over 12 weeks, with noisy dynamometry and growth-related strength gains on placebo, gives little power to show a significant strength difference even if the drug acts.
rationale: SAT-3247 is an oral AAK1 inhibitor meant to restore muscle stem-cell polarity. Only open-label adult phase 1b data exist. A 12-week placebo-controlled phase 2a in boys aged 7-10 with about 17 per arm, and strength measured by dynamometry, is underpowered for a significant difference. The record frames efficacy as exploratory, so a press release may describe trends rather than a formally met primary. Satellos is likely to release top-line Part 1 data in the first half of 2027.

reason: If the long-acting injection loses much of its effect by month 6 or the highest dose is modest, the 24-h ambulatory SBP gap versus placebo in a split multi-dose design could shrink toward non-significance.
rationale: HRS-9563 appears to be a long-acting injectable antihypertensive (6-month ABPM endpoint), consistent with an angiotensinogen-silencing siRNA like zilebesiran. Zilebesiran gave placebo-adjusted 24-h SBP reductions above 10 mmHg at 3 and 6 months in KARDIA-1. Against an SD near 12 mmHg and roughly 40-120 patients per arm, a gap of 8 mmHg or more is clearly significant. Placebo ABPM change is usually near zero.

assumptions.claim: Single doses of zilebesiran lowered 24-h ambulatory systolic BP by more than 10 mmHg versus placebo at month 3 in mild-to-moderate hypertension.

reason: ALT normalization can lag viral suppression, so the week-24 composite could be lower than hoped, but with an untreated control near 0% even a modest response rate should be significant.
rationale: Untreated chronic HDV almost never reaches a composite of >=2 log HDV RNA decline plus ALT normalization in 12 weeks (MYR301 delayed arm 2% at week 48). Brelovitug phase 2 showed near-universal virologic response with substantial ALT normalization by 24-48 weeks. With 40 vs 20 patients and control near zero, a composite response around 40-50% gives a highly significant difference; failure would need a surprising efficacy shortfall or operational problems.

assumptions.claim: In MYR301 the delayed-treatment arm had a combined response of about 2% at week 48.
In MYR301 bulevirtide 2 mg achieved a combined response of about 45% at week 48.

reason: A novel oral first-in-class agent with no published efficacy data must beat a placebo arm that typically improves EASI by about a third, with only about 52 patients per arm.
rationale: ENV-294 is a first-in-class oral anti-inflammatory with only phase 1 safety/PK data; novel oral AD mechanisms often fail or show modest effects. Placebo EASI percent change in moderate-severe AD trials runs about -25 to -40%, with between-patient SD around 40 points, so ~52 per arm only detects a 20-25 point difference. Success requires efficacy approaching the oral JAK or biologic range, which is unlikely without a validated target.

assumptions.claim: In SOLO 1 the placebo arm had a mean EASI percent change of about -38% at week 16.

reason: With about 590 per arm and a 90-day window, a low 2026 symptomatic COVID-19 attack rate (around 1-2%) could leave too few events for significance even with a strong antibody effect; variant escape is a second risk.
rationale: Monthly IM VYD2311 should give high neutralizing titers, and mAb prophylaxis matched to circulating variants has shown 70-85% efficacy (PROVENT 77%). The constraint is event count: 1770 participants over 90 days with a placebo attack rate of maybe 1.5-3% gives roughly 10-20 placebo cases per arm. Either VYD2311 arm meeting significance suffices. Escape by new lineages (as sipavibart saw with F456L) is a residual risk.

assumptions.claim: In PROVENT, tixagevimab-cilgavimab reduced symptomatic COVID-19 by 77% vs placebo, with about 1% of placebo recipients affected in the primary analysis.

reason: Small 50-patient safety-primary asthma study at 20 US sites, still recruiting two months before its registered primary completion; enrolment of exacerbation-prone ICS/LABA patients usually slips by a quarter or more.
rationale: Private sponsor, phase 2 with a safety primary; slow asthma recruitment makes a slip past March 2027 somewhat more likely than not, but termination and early results posting are unlikely.

reason: No oral drug has shown efficacy on BFM in adult multifocal dystonia in a controlled trial; anticholinergic benefit seen mainly in young generalized dystonia may not carry over, and BFM is noisy with concurrent botulinum toxin use.
rationale: VIM0423 is a once-daily oral agent targeting striatal cholinergic imbalance (likely M4-selective antagonism), building on trihexyphenidyl's benefit in young patients with generalized dystonia. Adults with segmental/multifocal dystonia respond less and tolerate anticholinergics poorly. With 50 per arm and a BFM change SD around 6, roughly a 3.5-point difference is needed; a first-in-patient phase 2 in a field with repeated oral-drug failures gives about 30%.
evidence: Jankovic, Lancet Neurol 2013 dystonia treatment review

assumptions.claim: In a double-blind trial of high-dose trihexyphenidyl in 31 mostly young patients with dystonia, about 71% improved.

reason: Lavender oil must beat a large placebo response on three separate primary outcomes (PSS, BAI and sleep quality) with 60 per arm; a modest supplement effect is unlikely to reach significance on all three.
rationale: Silexan-type lavender oil has modest anxiolytic evidence, but in a moderately stressed non-clinical population placebo PSS improvements of 4-6 points over 8 weeks are typical and the plausible drug effect is about 1-2 points (SD ~6). The round requires all three primary outcomes (PSS, BAI, sleep quality) met by the same arm, which with 60 per arm is unlikely even if one reaches significance.
evidence: Kasper 2010 Silexan subthreshold anxiety RCT (Int Clin Psychopharmacol)

assumptions.claim: Silexan 80 mg/day reduced HAMA vs placebo in patients with subthreshold anxiety over 10 weeks.
assumptions.source: Kasper et al., Int Clin Psychopharmacol 2010

reason: With 20 per arm against an active comparator app, a significant PCL-5 difference needs an effect size near 0.9; a realistic 4-6 point difference would not reach significance.
rationale: OTX-601 delivers interoceptive exposure targeting anxiety sensitivity, which has shown moderate effects on AS and smaller effects on PTSD symptoms. A 40-patient NIMH-funded pilot vs a comparator app, with PCL-5 change SD around 13, is powered only for very large effects. The key secondary (ASI-3) is the direct target and more likely to separate.
evidence: Schmidt et al. CAST anxiety sensitivity RCTs (2014-2017)

assumptions.claim: Brief computerized anxiety sensitivity training reduces ASI-3 scores more than control interventions.
assumptions.source: Schmidt et al., computerized anxiety sensitivity treatment RCTs, J Psychiatr Res 2014

reason: Psychiatry phase 2 with 100 patients at 11 US sites, still recruiting about three months before its registered January 2027 primary completion; SAD trials with strict exclusions commonly slip.
rationale: Private sponsor, safety primary, modest site count; a slip past May 2027 is close to even odds, and termination or early posting is unlikely.

reason: GalNAc-siRNA silencing of LPA reliably cuts Lp(a) 80-95%; failure would need an operational or analysis problem rather than lack of efficacy.
rationale: Kylo-11 is an LPA-targeting siRNA; the class (olpasiran, lepodisiran, zerlasiran) consistently gives 80-98% placebo-adjusted Lp(a) reductions with tiny variance relative to effect. The highest dose vs placebo is near-certain to be significant. The uncertainty is mainly whether this private Chinese sponsor discloses by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Olpasiran 75 mg or more every 12 weeks reduced Lp(a) by more than 95% placebo-adjusted at week 36.
Lepodisiran 400 mg reduced time-averaged Lp(a) by about 94% placebo-adjusted from day 60 to 180.

reason: ANGPTL3 antibodies reliably cut triglycerides by roughly half against placebo, so failure would need an unexpectedly weak dose or high variability; risk is small.
rationale: SHR-1918 is Hengrui's anti-ANGPTL3 monoclonal antibody. ANGPTL3 inhibition (evinacumab, zodasiran, solbinsiran) consistently lowers triglycerides by about 40-60% versus placebo in moderate hypertriglyceridemia, and early SHR-1918 data showed large dose-dependent TG reductions. With ~367 patients and a percent-change endpoint whose SD is about 30%, power for an effect of ~45 points is essentially complete. Placebo change typically near zero. Main uncertainty is not efficacy but whether a result is public by June 2027, given March 2027 primary completion and Hengrui's reporting habits.

assumptions.claim: Evinacumab reduced triglycerides by roughly 50% or more versus placebo in patients with moderately elevated triglycerides.
Zodasiran (ANGPTL3 siRNA) reduced triglycerides by about 50-60% placebo-adjusted at week 24 in mixed hyperlipidemia.
SHR-1918 is a monoclonal antibody targeting ANGPTL3 developed by Jiangsu Hengrui.

reason: With 32 per arm over 14 days and a latanoprost-controlled baseline, an incremental IOP drop of about 2 mmHg from the added KATP opener may not reach significance against PF latanoprost.
rationale: Patients are run in on PF latanoprost and must still have IOP >=19 mmHg, so the latanoprost arm should change little (regression to the mean only), while the FDC adds QLS-111, a KATP channel opener that lowers episcleral venous pressure. In Qlaris's phase 2 Osprey, QLS-111 added to latanoprost gave further IOP lowering of a few mmHg. With SD about 3 mmHg and 32 per arm, a 2 mmHg difference gives roughly 70-80% power. Some chance the primary is read as within-arm change, which would favour being met.
evidence: Osprey phase 2 QLS-111 adjunct to latanoprost (NCT05995132), 2024
Kestrel phase 2 QLS-111 in normal-tension glaucoma, 2024

assumptions.claim: QLS-111 added to latanoprost lowered IOP more than vehicle plus latanoprost in the phase 2 Osprey study.
assumptions.source: Qlaris Bio press release on Osprey topline results, 2024

assumptions.claim: QLS-111 lowers IOP by opening ATP-sensitive potassium channels and reducing episcleral venous pressure, a mechanism additive to prostaglandin analogues.
assumptions.source: Qlaris Bio / Roy Chowdhury et al., Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci preclinical studies

reason: Office SBP in a small 2-site trial is noisy, and a large placebo response from regression to the mean and lifestyle advice could shrink the separation below significance at 80 per arm.
rationale: VCT220 is an oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist; GLP-1 agents with ~8-12% weight loss lower SBP by about 4-7 mmHg versus placebo in obese/overweight adults, more in hypertensive patients. With ~80 per arm, SD ~12-13 mmHg, a true 6 mmHg effect gives roughly 85-90% power. Uncertainty from unknown dose, 20-week duration, possible dose titration limiting exposure, and noisy office BP in a small Chinese trial lowers the estimate.

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced SBP by about 5 mmHg more than placebo at 68 weeks in adults with obesity.
Tirzepatide lowered 24-h ambulatory SBP by about 7-10 mmHg versus placebo at 36 weeks.
assumptions.source: SURMOUNT-1 ABPM substudy, de Lemos et al. Hypertension 2024

assumptions.claim: Orforglipron, an oral small-molecule GLP-1 RA, produced 9-15% weight loss at 36 weeks in phase 2.

reason: Orexin-2 agonist effects reverse within days of stopping, so placebo patients should lose ESS response quickly; the only plausible failure is a lenient loss-of-response threshold or very few randomized patients.
rationale: TAK-861 (oveporexton), an oral orexin-2 receptor agonist, produced very large ESS and MWT improvements in phase 2b and phase 3 NT1 trials, and its effect is concentration-dependent with no lasting carryover; phase 1/2 data show symptoms return after washout. In a 4-week randomized withdrawal of responders, most placebo patients should relapse on ESS while those continuing TAK-861 stay stable, giving a hazard ratio far below 1 even with roughly 80-90 randomized patients. Statistical failure is unlikely; the main uncertainty is when Takeda makes the result public.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2b trial, TAK-861 improved ESS by roughly 8-13 points more than placebo at week 8 in NT1.
Takeda reported both phase 3 NT1 trials of oveporexton met all primary and secondary endpoints.

reason: Enrollment is complete and the 7-month follow-up from a January 2026 start should end well before the registered March 2027 primary completion, so an on-time finish with no stop is likely; posting results within five months of completion is less likely.
rationale: This Vaxcyte VAX-31 co-administration safety and immunogenicity study with Flublok has no efficacy hypothesis. It is active, not recruiting, and its follow-up is short, which points to completion on schedule. Posting on ClinicalTrials.gov usually comes close to the 12-month deadline, so results by August 2027 are unlikely. The many safety and immunogenicity primary outcomes are seldom changed in substance.

reason: Small single-centre German ovulation-inhibition study in healthy women run by a CRO-style site; likely completes near schedule, though still recruiting in late Oct 2026 with an 84-day treatment plus pre-treatment cycle suggests some slip past Nov 2026.

Already active, not recruiting with primary completion Dec 2026, so on-time completion is likely; as a single-country Australian phase 2a from a small sponsor, posting results on ClinicalTrials.gov within months is unlikely.
rationale: Enrollment appears complete (active, not recruiting) ahead of a December 2026 primary completion, so a delay past March 2027 is unlikely, though small sponsors sometimes leave dates unupdated. Traws Pharma is a small, cash-constrained company, which adds modest stop risk, but with dosing finished termination is unlikely. Australian-only trials without a US IND component rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov quickly. The safety primary outcomes are generic and unlikely to change.

reason: Remifentanil is a highly effective, titratable comparator in ICU analgesia-sedation, so success rates near 85-95% in both arms leave little room for a significant superiority difference with about 40 patients per arm.
rationale: Small dose-exploration phase 2 (about 40 per arm) of tegileridine, a biased mu-opioid agonist approved in China for postoperative pain, against remifentanil, a strong titratable comparator. Responder endpoints in ICU analgesia-sedation trials typically show high success in both arms; the record states no superiority hypothesis, so any report will likely describe comparable efficacy rather than a significant advantage. Superiority at p<0.05 with this sample would need a gap of roughly 20 points, which is implausible against remifentanil. Hengrui rarely posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov and Chinese phase 2 papers usually take over a year.
evidence: Tegileridine phase 3 postoperative pain trials, China (Hengrui, 2023)
Remifentanil vs fentanyl ICU analgosedation trials (Muellejans 2004)

assumptions.claim: Remifentanil-based analgosedation keeps most mechanically ventilated ICU patients within target sedation for the majority of the infusion time.
Tegileridine fumarate injection was approved in China in 2024 for moderate-to-severe postoperative pain.

reason: The strict durable CSBM endpoint gives low response rates; with about 173 per arm, an effect under roughly 7 points over a low placebo rate could miss significance.
rationale: Tenapanor 50 mg BID is approved for IBS-C, where it clearly raised CSBM responder rates (T3MPO-1/2). Other secretagogues (linaclotide, plecanatide) beat placebo on the same strict durable CSBM endpoint in CIC, with placebo rates of about 3-10% and gains of 8-15 points. With about 173 per arm, an effect of about 11 points gives roughly 85% power. The main uncertainty is whether NHE3 inhibition works as well in CIC, a population without pain, and whether placebo response is high in a US-only trial.
evidence: Linaclotide CIC phase 3 trials, Lembo NEJM 2011

assumptions.claim: In CIC phase 3 trials, linaclotide 145 mcg gave durable CSBM responder rates of about 16-21% vs 3-6% for placebo.
Plecanatide 3 mg gave durable CSBM response of about 21% vs 10% for placebo in CIC.
assumptions.source: Miner et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2017

assumptions.claim: In T3MPO-2, about 6.5% of tenapanor 50 mg BID patients stopped treatment because of diarrhea over 26 weeks.
assumptions.source: Chey et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2021 (T3MPO-2)

reason: Antifibrotic pirfenidone has a modest effect on gas transfer, and DLCO partly recovers on its own after steroid-treated radiation pneumonitis, so a 3-4 point difference against a noisy SD near 10 gives only about half power at 99 per arm.
rationale: Pirfenidone slows lung-function decline in IPF but its DLCO effect there is small; RILI data are limited to small Chinese studies. With 99 per arm, an SD of change near 10 points and a plausible 3-4 point benefit, power is about 50%, helped slightly by the second dose counting. The sponsor (maker of Chinese pirfenidone) has an incentive to report positively. Recruitment of 298 started March 2026, so the registered December 2026 primary completion is implausible and a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Pirfenidone reduced the proportion of IPF patients with FVC decline of 10% or more or death at 52 weeks versus placebo.

reason: A GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist at its highest dose over 28 weeks should beat placebo by well over 10 points; the main threat is GI intolerance and dropouts at the top dose diluting the treatment-policy estimate.
rationale: UBT251 is a weekly GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist licensed by Novo Nordisk from United Laboratories. The class benchmark, retatrutide, gave about 17.5% weight loss at 24 weeks versus 1.6% on placebo, so even a less potent analogue at 28 weeks should be highly significant against placebo. The uncertainty is mostly about when Novo discloses it (quarterly report, ADA or EASD) rather than whether it works.
evidence: Retatrutide phase 2 obesity (Jastreboff et al., NEJM 2023)

assumptions.claim: In the retatrutide phase 2 obesity trial, mean weight change at 24 weeks was about -17.5% at 12 mg versus -1.6% with placebo.

reason: Pilot already closed to enrolment at 8 of a planned 40 subjects, so it should finish around the registered February 2027 date with a modest chance of being relabelled terminated; FDAAA results are not due before early 2028.
rationale: Enrolment of 8 against a planned 40 with status active, not recruiting suggests early closure of recruitment; 24-week dosing means completion near February 2027. Small sponsor may relabel as terminated. Results due one year after primary completion, after the read date.

reason: Neuroprotective or kallikrein-type add-on therapies in non-reperfused stroke usually give small or no functional gains, and 80 per arm only detects a difference of about 20 points on mRS 0-1.
rationale: QHRD106 appears to be a long-acting tissue kallikrein, a mechanism with Chinese urinary-kallidinogenase precedent but weak randomized evidence. Most stroke neuroprotectants have failed on mRS endpoints; at 80 per arm a realistic 5-10 point gain gives low power, though three doses each get a chance. Still recruiting at its registered primary completion, so a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Nerinetide did not improve the proportion with mRS 0-2 at 90 days overall versus placebo in ESCAPE-NA1.

reason: Zinc citrate toothpastes reliably reduce organoleptic malodor versus regular fluoride paste in sponsor studies, but with 40 per arm and four-judge scoring after a 6-hour fast the margin can be small.
rationale: Colgate runs many near-identical organoleptic malodor studies of zinc formulations against regular fluoride toothpaste and these are almost always reported as significant. The trial is already completed, so the only questions are a small-sample miss and whether Colgate voluntarily posts results or publishes by mid-2027.

reason: IL-4R-based biologics give large EASI gains, so the main risk is a high placebo response in a small 24-patient placebo arm narrowing the difference.
rationale: IBI3002 is Innovent's IL-4Ralpha/TSLP bispecific; blocking IL-4R alone (dupilumab) gives about -70% EASI versus -30 to -38% on placebo at week 16. With 24 per arm and an SD near 32 points, a 30-plus point difference is highly significant, and several doses can count. Primary completion is March 2027, so disclosure by June 2027 is unlikely; Innovent's interim report or EADV 2027 is more probable.
evidence: SOLO 1 and SOLO 2 (Simpson et al., NEJM 2016)

assumptions.claim: In SOLO 1, mean percent change in EASI at week 16 was about -72% with dupilumab every 2 weeks versus about -38% with placebo.

reason: Completed small US phase 2 safety study; results are due on ClinicalTrials.gov about September 2027, so posting by the end of August 2027 is possible but less likely than not.
rationale: Already completed in September 2026, so stopping is near impossible. As an applicable US trial, results are due within a year of primary completion; small biotechs often post near or after the deadline. Outcome changes would be limited to restructuring at results entry.

reason: Mechanism and dose potency of CMS-D002 are unstated; if it is a hormonal agent (for example a GnRH antagonist) responder gains are large, but a weaker or non-hormonal mechanism at 30 per arm could miss.
rationale: Responder endpoints in fibroid bleeding trials show large drug-placebo gaps for oral GnRH antagonists (about 70% versus 15-20% with relugolix combination therapy). If CMS-D002 works by a similar mechanism, 30 per arm is ample and any of three doses can count. Uncertainty about mechanism and the 50 mg dose's potency keeps this below 0.85. Still recruiting in late 2026, so the January 2027 completion will likely slip.
evidence: Elagolix Elaris UF-1/UF-2 (Schlaff et al., NEJM 2020)

assumptions.claim: In LIBERTY 1, about 73% of women on relugolix combination therapy met the MBL <80 mL and >=50% reduction responder endpoint versus about 19% on placebo.

reason: A 20-patient randomized trial in very rare primary vitreoretinal lymphoma still recruiting late in 2026 will probably miss its December 2026 completion, with some risk of being stopped by a resource-constrained sponsor.
rationale: PVRL is rare, so 20 biopsy-proven patients within about ten months is ambitious; primary completion will likely be pushed into 2027. Aldeyra is a small company that may deprioritize the program; results posting by August 2027 is unlikely given the late completion.

reason: Small Chinese phase 2a still recruiting 13 months after start, so the December 2026 primary completion is likely to slip; posting results on ClinicalTrials.gov is unlikely for this sponsor.
rationale: Only 24 patients are planned but recruitment has run since September 2025, suggesting slow enrolment; with 8 weeks of dosing the end date will likely move into 2027. Chinese biotech sponsors rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov.

reason: PRK pain is a sensitive model, but with about 43 eyes per arm and a pain SD near 2.4 points the drug needs roughly a 1-point mean reduction over vehicle in the first 24 hours to reach significance.
rationale: Post-PRK pain is a well-established, assay-sensitive analgesia model where topical NSAIDs and TRPV1 antagonists have separated from vehicle. BL1332 is an undisclosed Bausch + Lomb asset in a small three-arm phase 2 (about 43 per arm), so power depends on an effect of about 1 point on the 0-10 NRS. The mechanism is unknown, which keeps the prior near a coin flip. Early disclosure by a large company is uncertain; a vague 'positive' pipeline mention would count as not met.
evidence: SAF312 (libvatrep) TRPV1 antagonist phase 2 in post-PRK ocular pain, Novartis, about 2021-2022
Topical ketorolac/nepafenac vehicle-controlled post-PRK pain trials

assumptions.claim: Vehicle-treated patients report moderate ocular pain in the first 24-48 hours after PRK, peaking on day 1.

reason: Pharmacological treatments for sepsis-associated ARDS have almost uniformly failed to improve ventilator-free days; with a VFD SD near 10 days, about 155 per arm needs a gain of 3+ days, which few agents have ever shown.
rationale: ARDS drug trials (statins, interferon beta, many anti-inflammatories) have consistently shown no VFD benefit. YD0743 is an undisclosed agent from a small Chinese sponsor; 309 patients at a single registered site with a December 2026 primary completion is unrealistic, so a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely. VFD is noisy (SD about 10 days) and mortality-driven. Base rate for phase 2 success in this indication is low.
evidence: ROSE early neuromuscular blockade in ARDS, 2019

assumptions.claim: In SAILS (sepsis-associated ARDS), mean ventilator-free days to day 28 were about 15 in both arms with no drug effect.

reason: Botulinum toxins essentially never fail placebo-controlled glabellar-line trials; the only plausible failure is an unexpectedly weak dose or formulation of the new recombinant neurotoxin.
rationale: Every pivotal botulinum toxin glabellar-line trial has beaten placebo by a wide margin: composite investigator+subject ≥2-grade responders 45-75% versus 0-1% on placebo. Corabotase (IPN10200) is Ipsen's recombinant next-generation neurotoxin that has already passed phase 2, and about 155 per arm gives near-certain power. Ipsen typically announces phase 3 readouts by press release or with results, so a public statement in H1 2027 is likely. Filing timing depends on long-term safety data from LAURITE 2.

assumptions.claim: Placebo composite ≥2-grade (investigator and subject) responder rates at week 4 were about 0-1% in SAKURA 1 and 2.
assumptions.source: Carruthers et al., Plast Reconstr Surg 2020 (SAKURA 1/2)

assumptions.claim: PrabotulinumtoxinA composite ≥2-grade responder rates at day 30 were 67.5% and 70.4% versus about 1% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Beer et al., Aesthet Surg J 2019 (EV-001/EV-002)

reason: A small three-site US PK/safety phase 2 of Regeneron's in-licensed GLP-1/GIP agonist that is already active, not recruiting, so it should complete close to its November 2026 date; results posting is due only by late 2027.
rationale: Enrolment is complete and the registered primary completion (November 2026) follows a fixed ~30-week schedule, so a >90-day slip is unlikely. Termination of a fully enrolled PK/safety study is rare. Regeneron generally posts results near the 12-month deadline (November 2027) or defers for unapproved products, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. Safety/PK primary outcomes rarely change in substance.

reason: On-demand SERT inhibition (dapoxetine) lengthens IELT only modestly over a sizable placebo response; a 4-week crossover in 40 men can detect a dapoxetine-sized effect but not much less.
rationale: Dapoxetine, the on-demand SERT inhibitor benchmark, roughly doubled to tripled geometric mean IELT versus about 1.6-fold with placebo, which a 40-patient crossover can detect. Sublingual ODT dosing 15 minutes before sex may limit exposure versus oral 1-3 h dosing, and on-demand 4-week periods are short. The study is still recruiting past its primary completion date, and the sponsor is a small private company, so early disclosure is uncertain and possibly selective.
evidence: Dapoxetine phase 3 trials, Pryor et al. Lancet 2006
Dapoxetine integrated analysis, McMahon et al. 2011

assumptions.claim: In dapoxetine phase 3 trials, arithmetic mean IELT rose from about 0.9 min at baseline to about 1.8 min with placebo and 3.3 min with dapoxetine 60 mg at week 12.

reason: Large placebo-controlled glabellar-line toxin trials are near-certain wins; failure would require an unexpectedly weak dose of the new recombinant neurotoxin.
rationale: Placebo-controlled botulinum toxin glabellar-line trials uniformly succeed: composite ≥2-grade responders typically 45-75% versus 0-1% on placebo. LAURITE 2 is a large double-blind phase with an open-label extension, so power is overwhelming. Ipsen will probably report the double-blind topline with LAURITE 1 in H1 2027. The key secondary (ILA none/mild through week 24) should stay significant for a long-acting toxin. Filing likely waits for long-term repeat-dose safety, which pushes it toward 2028.

assumptions.claim: Placebo composite ≥2-grade (investigator and subject) responder rates at week 4 were about 0-1% in SAKURA 1 and 2.
assumptions.source: Carruthers et al., Plast Reconstr Surg 2020 (SAKURA 1/2)

assumptions.claim: PrabotulinumtoxinA composite ≥2-grade responder rates at day 30 were 67.5% and 70.4% versus about 1% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Beer et al., Aesthet Surg J 2019 (EV-001/EV-002)

reason: About 35 patients per arm with a CLASI-A percent-change SD near 40% and a placebo response of 15-30% on stable background therapy leaves power near 60-70% even for a real TYK2 effect.
rationale: TYK2 inhibition has shown strong skin activity in lupus (deucravacitinib in PAISLEY), and type I interferon pathway drugs (litifilimab, anifrolumab) reduce CLASI-A substantially. ICP-488 is an allosteric TYK2 inhibitor already active in psoriasis. However, 35 per arm, a variable percent-change endpoint and placebo responses of 15-30% make significance uncertain. Recruitment in China started April 2026 with a March 2027 target, so a readout by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: LILAC litifilimab phase 2 part B, NEJM 2022

assumptions.claim: In LILAC part B, placebo mean CLASI-A percent change at week 16 was about -15%, versus about -56% with litifilimab 450 mg.
In PAISLEY, CLASI-50 at week 48 was about 70% with deucravacitinib 3 mg BID vs about 17% with placebo in patients with CLASI-A ≥10.

reason: A two-site safety-primary phase 2 enrolling by invitation; 155 patients with 16-week follow-up make a primary completion slip past March 2027 plausible but not likely, and results posting is due only by end-2027.
rationale: Tarsus is a commercial-stage company with lotilaner experience (Xdemvy), and the study is enrolling by invitation at two sites. To hit a December 2026 primary completion with 16-week dosing, enrolment had to close by about September 2026, which is feasible but not certain. Termination is unlikely for a safety study of an approved molecule. Posting before August 2027 would be well ahead of the 12-month deadline, so it is unlikely.

reason: If HRS-9190 is not a genuinely faster-offset agent than cisatracurium, or the small four-arm phase 2 is reported descriptively without a formal test, recovery time will not show significant superiority.
rationale: Making recovery time after infusion the primary endpoint against cisatracurium suggests HRS-9190 is designed for rapid spontaneous offset, which would make a large, significant difference likely. Uncertainty remains: the mechanism is undisclosed, the study pools anaesthesia types across about 34 versus 33 patients, and the stated hypothesis is descriptive. The trial is completed in China, so publication by mid-2027 depends on a congress abstract or journal paper.
evidence: Gantacurium phase 1, Belmont et al. Anesthesiology 2004

assumptions.claim: After cisatracurium is stopped, spontaneous recovery to a TOF ratio of 0.9 takes tens of minutes, with a 25-75% recovery index of about 12-15 minutes.

reason: With about 10 women per arm, even a 50-point difference in Lactobacillus dominance (6/10 vs 1/10) misses two-sided p<0.05 on Fisher's test, and estrogen priming in the mock cycle may raise the placebo response.
rationale: Live vaginal Lactobacillus products can colonise after antimicrobial pretreatment (Lactin-V), so a large effect on Lactobacillus dominance is plausible. But about 10 per arm needs roughly a 60-point difference for significance, the ≥90% threshold across specified species is strict, and estradiol in the mock FET cycle may raise spontaneous dominance on placebo. The trial was still recruiting past its primary completion date, and the small private sponsor may report descriptively, so a public result by mid-2027 is uncertain.
evidence: Lactin-V (L. crispatus CTV-05) phase 2b, Cohen et al. NEJM 2020

assumptions.claim: Vaginal L. crispatus CTV-05 after metronidazole reduced BV recurrence at 12 weeks to 30% versus 45% with placebo.

reason: Oleoylethanolamide has no human evidence of lowering plasma imidazole propionate; a novel, highly variable gut-metabolite endpoint in 90 healthy adults over 8 weeks is unlikely to move significantly.
rationale: Supplement-industry trial (RDC Clinical for Gencor) testing a speculative mechanism: OEA altering histidine-metabolising gut bacteria to cut plasma ImP. No prior human data; ImP varies widely between people and is driven by diet and microbiome composition, so 45 per arm over 8 weeks in mostly normoglycaemic adults gives modest power. Sponsor bias toward positive framing exists, but the round needs the registered primary met. RDC usually publishes 1-2 years after completion, so a result by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Koh et al., Cell 2018 (imidazole propionate impairs insulin signalling)
Molinaro et al., Nat Commun 2020 (ImP and prediabetes/T2D)

assumptions.claim: Plasma imidazole propionate is elevated in people with prediabetes and type 2 diabetes and is linked to microbiome composition and diet.

reason: Blocking the aldosterone pathway lowers blood pressure strongly in primary aldosteronism, but with about 30 per arm, background antihypertensives and office-BP noise, a modest dose could still miss significance.
rationale: HRS-1780 is Hengrui's aldosterone-pathway (non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor) blocker; primary aldosteronism is the setting where this mechanism has its largest BP effect, with MR antagonists typically lowering office SBP by 10-20 mmHg versus a few mmHg on placebo. With an SD near 13 mmHg, 30 per arm gives roughly 80-90% power for a 10 mmHg difference. Enrolment is complete. Hengrui rarely publishes phase 2 results quickly, so disclosure by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Parthasarathy et al., J Hypertens 2011 (spironolactone vs eplerenone in PA)
Esaxerenone in primary aldosteronism, Japan phase 3, 2021

assumptions.claim: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists lower office systolic BP by more than 10 mmHg in patients with primary aldosteronism.
Placebo office SBP change in short antihypertensive RCTs is typically between 0 and -6 mmHg.
assumptions.source: Meta-analyses of placebo response in hypertension trials

reason: Enrolment of 102 is complete with a 20-week treat-to-target period, so Hengrui should hit the December 2026 primary completion; Chinese sponsor rarely posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov.
rationale: Active, not recruiting at launch with a short fixed treatment period; Hengrui runs many such phase 2 studies to schedule and seldom posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov.

reason: A PCSK9 antibody versus placebo on percent LDL-C change almost never fails; only an operational or data-integrity problem would sink it.
rationale: IBI306 is tafolecimab, Innovent's approved PCSK9 antibody. CREDIT-1, -2 and -4 showed roughly 57-65% placebo-adjusted LDL-C reductions; PCSK9 antibody monotherapy without statins gives similar effects (MENDEL-2 about -55 to -57%). With about 99 per arm and an SD near 17%, the trial is massively powered. Primary completion has passed; Innovent may report it in annual results or at a Chinese congress as support for a monotherapy label.

assumptions.claim: Tafolecimab reduced LDL-C by about 57-65% versus placebo in Chinese non-familial hypercholesterolaemia patients.
PCSK9 antibody monotherapy reduced LDL-C by about 55-57% versus placebo at week 10-12.

reason: Enrolment of 438 at 34 US sites is complete with a 12-week primary, so primary completion should land on time; Regeneron typically posts results close to the 12-month deadline (end of 2027), after the read date.
rationale: Large US industry dose-ranging study already active, not recruiting; short follow-up makes delay unlikely. FDAAA posting is due within a year of primary completion, which falls after August 2027.

reason: The record lists nine primary outcomes (fMRI, JORT, learning indices, STAI) and the round needs all of them met; a single-dose 24-person crossover will not make every one significant.
rationale: SYT-510 is an endocannabinoid reuptake inhibitor in early development. This is an experimental-medicine crossover with nine registered primary outcomes; even if amygdala BOLD shifts, the chance that all nine behavioural, imaging and questionnaire measures reach significance after one dose in 24 people is very small. Recruiting unmedicated right-handed GAD participants for fMRI in one UK site often runs late, and a small private biotech may disclose results only at a later congress.

reason: Recruitment of 120 symptomatic BV patients across four arms at two German sites, with menses-timed dosing and 10 weeks of follow-up, is tight for a March 2027 primary completion.
rationale: Still recruiting seven months in; last patient must be in by about December 2026 to meet the date. Small EU biotech, non-US sites, so ClinicalTrials.gov posting is unlikely.

reason: Zelicapavir's earlier pediatric and adult phase 2 studies showed modest, inconsistent clinical benefit; a 150-child trial on time to complete resolution needs a hazard ratio near 1.5 to reach significance.
rationale: Oral RSV N-protein inhibitor; prior RSVPEDs and RSVHR phase 2 data gave numerical rather than robust symptom benefits, and pediatric antivirals have mixed records (ziresovir positive, rilematovir dropped). With about 110 resolution events, power is under 50% for a realistic HR of 1.2-1.3. Enrolling 150 in one Thai RSV season by December 2026 is ambitious, so readout may slip into late 2027.

assumptions.claim: Ziresovir significantly reduced bronchiolitis scores in hospitalized infants with RSV versus placebo.
assumptions.source: AIRFLO trial, Zhao et al., NEJM 2024

reason: Anti-TL1A has proven efficacy in IBD but none yet in psoriatic arthritis; if joint efficacy is modest (about 15 points over placebo), 47 per arm gives limited power.
rationale: Tulisokibart worked in UC and Crohn's (ARTEMIS-UC, APOLLO-CD), and TL1A drives Th1/Th17 inflammation, but no PsA data exist and several plausible mechanisms have disappointed in PsA. Placebo ACR20 at week 16 runs 20-30%. If efficacy matches IL-23 agents (about 30 points), power is high; if modest, it fails. Enrolment is complete; Merck tends to disclose phase 2b via ACR/EULAR abstracts, so June 2027 disclosure is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Placebo ACR20 response in recent PsA biologic trials was roughly 20-33%.
Tulisokibart induced clinical remission significantly more often than placebo in ulcerative colitis.

reason: HIF-PH inhibitors routinely match ESAs on titrated hemoglobin; failure would need AND017 dosing or titration to underperform against an unstated non-inferiority margin.
rationale: AND017 is an oral HIF-PH inhibitor; every class member tested against ESAs in non-dialysis CKD (daprodustat, vadadustat, roxadustat) met hemoglobin non-inferiority because both arms are titrated to the same 10-12 g/dL target. With 120 per arm and an SD near 1 g/dL, the trial is well powered for a margin around -0.75 to -1.0 g/dL. Still recruiting in October 2026 with 27 weeks to the primary, so primary completion will slip and results are unlikely by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Daprodustat was non-inferior to darbepoetin for mean hemoglobin change in non-dialysis CKD.
Vadadustat met hemoglobin non-inferiority versus darbepoetin in non-dialysis CKD.

reason: Mechanism is not disclosed; if QLS1410 is not as potent as the aldosterone synthase inhibitors its design mirrors, a 65-per-arm comparison against a sizeable Chinese placebo response could miss.
rationale: Eligibility (uHTN on 2 drugs incl. diuretic, rHTN on 3+, K+ 3.5-5.0, eGFR >=45) copies the baxdrostat BaxHTN design, so QLS1410 is likely an aldosterone synthase inhibitor. That class gives 9-11 mmHg placebo-adjusted office SBP falls at 12 weeks; with SD ~14 and 65 per arm the top dose has >85% power if similarly potent. Discounted for unknown mechanism/potency and a possibly large placebo response in a Chinese setting.

assumptions.claim: Baxdrostat 2 mg lowered seated SBP by about 11 mmHg more than placebo at week 12 in treatment-resistant hypertension.
In BaxHTN, placebo-adjusted seated SBP reductions at week 12 were about 8.7 mmHg (1 mg) and 9.8 mmHg (2 mg).

reason: Doses chosen for long-term safety of a DNP-derived mitochondrial uncoupler may be lower than those that cut liver fat in short studies, and both PDFF co-primaries (percent change and >=30% responders) must be met with ~45 per arm.
rationale: HU6 is a controlled mitochondrial uncoupler (2,4-DNP prodrug) that reduced liver fat and weight in an earlier phase 2a in obese NAFLD. Uncouplers act directly on hepatic lipid oxidation, so a 25-30 point placebo-adjusted relative PDFF reduction at 26 weeks is plausible; with SD ~28 and 45 per arm that gives high power, and the >=30% responder co-primary should follow. Risks: dose limited by tolerability, 4-arm split, and still recruiting with a Feb 2027 completion date, so readout by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: HU6 phase 2a in obese NAFLD, Rivus 2022

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in 12-week MASH MRI-PDFF trials showed small relative liver fat declines of about 10% or less.
assumptions.source: Resmetirom phase 2, Harrison et al. Lancet 2019

assumptions.claim: HU6 reduced liver fat versus placebo in a phase 2a study in obese participants with NAFLD.

reason: Non-inferiority on mean Hb is usually met by HIF-PH inhibitors versus ESA; the residual risk is under-correction from a conservative oral dose-titration scheme or an unexpectedly tight margin.
rationale: AND017 is an oral HIF-PH inhibitor. Every HIF-PHI tested against ESA in dialysis patients (roxadustat, daprodustat, vadadustat, enarodustat, desidustat) met non-inferiority on Hb maintenance, typically with a difference of about 0 to +0.3 g/dL and NI margins of -0.75 to -1.0 g/dL. With 150 per arm and SD ~1.0, the trial is well powered for NI. The registered completion date has passed while still recruiting, so a readout before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In Chinese dialysis patients, roxadustat was non-inferior to epoetin alfa, with mean Hb change of +0.7 vs +0.5 g/dL.
Daprodustat was non-inferior to ESA for mean Hb change in dialysis patients with a difference near 0.2 g/dL.

reason: The trial's own success is likely judged on CBER-style lower confidence bounds for seroprotection and seroconversion by age group; the main threat is a weaker response in adults 65 and older missing the 60%/30% bounds.
rationale: mRNA-1018 phase 1/2 interim data reported HAI >=1:40 rising from about 2% at baseline to roughly 98% three weeks after dose 2. Superiority over placebo is trivial, and immunogenicity thresholds (seroconversion LB >=40%/30%, seroprotection LB >=70%/60%) should be cleared with 2000+ vaccinees; older adults are the only real risk. Enrolment is complete and Day 43 data exist, so Moderna may disclose topline at quarterly results in early 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the mRNA-1018 phase 1/2 study, the share with HAI titer >=1:40 rose from about 2% at baseline to about 98% three weeks after the second dose.
assumptions.source: Moderna press release on mRNA-1018-P101 interim results, 2025

assumptions.claim: FDA accelerated-approval criteria for pandemic influenza vaccines require the lower 95% bound for seroconversion >=40% (18-64) and seroprotection >=70% (18-64).
assumptions.source: FDA CBER guidance, Clinical Data Needed to Support Licensure of Pandemic Influenza Vaccines, 2007

reason: If surgeons with good preoperative CT localization rarely miss lesions, the share of patients with a clinically significant event could fall near the pre-specified lower-bound threshold.
rationale: Same endpoint construction (patient-level clinically significant event rate against a low fixed threshold) let pafolacianine succeed in ELUCIDATE with 53% of patients having a CSE. Abenacianine's phase 2 VISUALIZE showed lesion localization and occult lesion detection in a meaningful share of patients. With ~115 evaluable patients, a CSE rate of 25-40% would put the lower bound well above a ~10% threshold. Timing is the bigger uncertainty: still recruiting with a Dec 2026 completion date.

assumptions.claim: In ELUCIDATE, pafolacianine NIR imaging produced at least one clinically significant event in about 53% of lung-surgery patients, meeting its primary endpoint.
assumptions.source: Sarkaria et al. J Thorac Cardiovasc Surg 2023 (NCT04241315)

reason: Icovamenib's durable off-treatment HbA1c effect has been modest in unselected patients; with 32 per arm a true effect below ~0.5 points will not reach significance at week 26.
rationale: COVALENT-111 gave only modest placebo-adjusted HbA1c reductions at week 26 in the overall population, with larger effects claimed in post-hoc subgroups (insulin-deficient, specific backgrounds). This trial enriches for that phenotype (BMI <=32, non-insulin oral background) but subgroup effects usually shrink. With SD ~1.0 and 32 per arm, significance needs about -0.5 points; my central estimate sits just below that. Biomea is cash-constrained and will likely announce topline promptly.

assumptions.claim: In COVALENT-111, 12 weeks of icovamenib produced a modest placebo-adjusted HbA1c reduction at week 26 overall, with larger reductions reported only in subgroups such as severe insulin-deficient diabetes.

reason: Vehicle drops themselves improve corneal staining in dry eye trials, compressing the treatment difference; many phase 2 dry-eye programmes miss on CFS despite large samples.
rationale: DFL24498's mechanism is undisclosed and the study is labelled exploratory. Dry-eye trials with corneal fluorescein staining as primary have a mixed record: vehicle arms improve by 1-2 NEI points and true drug-vehicle differences are often 0.3-0.8 points. With ~208 per arm and SD ~2.8, the trial detects about -0.6 points with reasonable power, so success depends on a better-than-typical drug effect. Dompé is private and may not disclose phase 2 results quickly.

assumptions.claim: In GOBI, the saline control arm improved total corneal fluorescein staining by about 1 NEI point at day 57 while NOV03 improved by about 2 points.
Lifitegrast met its symptom co-primary but missed inferior corneal staining in OPUS-2.

reason: Molecular CR is near-universal with arsenic plus ATRA, so non-inferiority would fail mainly through early deaths, differentiation syndrome or dropouts counted as non-responders, or a PK co-primary judged unmet.
rationale: Arsenic plus ATRA yields molecular remission in essentially all evaluable low/intermediate-risk APL patients, and oral arsenic formulations (realgar-indigo naturalis, oral ATO) were non-inferior to IV ATO in randomized trials. Non-inferiority on mCR is therefore highly likely if the oral formulation achieves adequate exposure. Timing is the binding constraint: enrolling 150 low-risk APL patients plus ~8 months of treatment cannot finish by March 2027, so a primary readout by mid-2027 is very unlikely.
evidence: Oral RIF vs IV ATO in APL (Zhu, Lancet Oncol 2018)

assumptions.claim: In APL0406, ATRA plus IV arsenic trioxide achieved molecular remission in essentially all evaluable low/intermediate-risk patients after consolidation.
Oral realgar-indigo naturalis formula plus ATRA was non-inferior to IV arsenic trioxide plus ATRA in non-high-risk APL.
assumptions.source: Zhu HH et al. Lancet Oncol 2018

reason: THR-beta agonists have shown little or no weight loss on their own; over an 11-week window on escalating semaglutide, any added weight effect is likely under 1 point and the five primaries (weight and liver fat) must all be met.
rationale: Resmetirom and other THR-beta agonists cut liver fat strongly but did not cause meaningful weight loss. Here ECC4703 is added to semaglutide during escalation (weeks 9-20), when semaglutide alone delivers about 5-6% loss; an incremental ~0.7 point effect with SD ~3 and 75 per arm has under 40% power. Liver fat primaries in the imaging sub-study are likelier to be met, but the round needs all primaries, including weight and >=5% responder, so p_met is low.

assumptions.claim: In STEP 1, semaglutide 2.4 mg produced about 4% weight loss by week 8 and about 10% by week 20 during dose escalation.
Resmetirom, a THR-beta agonist, did not produce meaningful weight loss versus placebo over 52 weeks.

reason: AGT knockdown by a GalNAc antisense is near-certain; failure would come from operational issues (slow enrolment of recently hospitalized patients, Part A redesigning Part B) rather than the drug.
rationale: Tonlamarsen (formerly IONIS-AGT-LRx) is a GalNAc-conjugated antisense against hepatic angiotensinogen; earlier studies showed large, dose-dependent AGT reductions, and siRNA zilebesiran shows >90% knockdown. A 50-60% placebo-adjusted fall in plasma AGT by week 4 is expected and would be highly significant even in a small Part B. The main uncertainty is timing: a two-part trial in a hard-to-recruit post-discharge population will not complete by December 2026.

assumptions.claim: IONIS-AGT-LRx (tonlamarsen) produced substantial dose-dependent reductions in plasma angiotensinogen versus placebo in phase 2 hypertension studies.
Zilebesiran reduced serum angiotensinogen by more than 90% and lowered 24-h SBP versus placebo at month 3.

reason: Undisclosed novel mechanism; the third-molar model separates NSAIDs easily but has rejected many novel analgesic mechanisms, so failure would most likely reflect insufficient single-dose analgesic efficacy.
rationale: Third-molar extraction is a high assay-sensitivity acute pain model run at an experienced single CRU, and the top dose of a dose range is scored, which favours separation if the target is analgesic in acute inflammatory pain. Against that, LY4515100's mechanism is undisclosed and the model has a long record of novel mechanisms failing while NSAIDs succeed. The highest-dose arm is smaller than 106 if several doses share the 212. Phase 2 first-efficacy readouts in pain succeed roughly half the time.
evidence: Suzetrigine phase 2 abdominoplasty and bunionectomy trials, NEJM 2023
Cooper & Desjardins, dental impaction pain model review, 2010

assumptions.claim: The Nav1.8 inhibitor suzetrigine at its highest dose significantly reduced SPID48 versus placebo after abdominoplasty and bunionectomy, while lower doses did not.

reason: P2X3 antagonism has no human proof of visceral analgesia; against a 1.5-2 point placebo improvement in IBS abdominal pain, a modest true effect would not separate with about 100 patients per arm.
rationale: Camlipixant's clinical evidence is in chronic cough; P2X3 antagonism for visceral pain is untested in humans. IBS trials carry large placebo responses on abdominal pain (around -1.5 to -2 points by weeks 7-12) and novel visceral analgesics such as olorinab have failed. With roughly 100 per arm and SD near 2, a true effect of -0.4 points gives about 30-40% power; several doses add a little. GSK funding a 420-patient phase 2b signals preclinical conviction but no human IBS data.
evidence: SOOTHE camlipixant phase 2b in refractory chronic cough, 2022
Lembo et al., eluxadoline IBS-D phase 3, NEJM 2016

assumptions.claim: Olorinab, a peripherally acting CB2 agonist, did not significantly improve abdominal pain versus placebo in the overall population of the phase 2b CAPTIVATE trial in IBS.

reason: With 18 per arm there is under 50% power even for a 30-point cure-rate gain over placebo gel, and a small phase 2a may report only descriptively, which counts as not met.
