rationale: Placebo clinical cure (signs and symptoms score 0) in acute VVC runs roughly 25-45% around test-of-cure in the VANISH trials, likely lower at day 8 with an inert gel; a novel topical antifungal might reach 45-60%. With 18 per arm, even a 30-point difference gives under 50% power, and a safety-focused phase 2a from a small private sponsor may report without formal testing. Inclusion of recurrent VVC adds variability.

assumptions.claim: In VANISH-303, clinical cure at the day-10 test-of-cure visit was 50.5% with ibrexafungerp versus 28.6% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Schwebke JR et al., Clin Infect Dis 2022

reason: Tirzepatide gives roughly 13-17% weight loss in Chinese adults; showing significant superiority at week 40 needs about a 3-point edge that another incretin agonist is unlikely to deliver.
rationale: Tirzepatide is a very strong comparator (-13.6% at 10 mg, -17.5% at 15 mg at week 52 in SURMOUNT-CN), and HDM1005, reported as a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist, has no clear mechanistic edge. Superiority at two-sided 0.05 with about 93 per arm needs roughly a 3-point advantage. Open-label design and a possibly lower tirzepatide dose give some upside, but the trial is likely descriptive versus tirzepatide, which counts as not met.

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-CN, tirzepatide 10 mg and 15 mg reduced body weight by 13.6% and 17.5% at week 52 versus 2.3% with placebo in Chinese adults with obesity.

reason: High placebo response in acute schizophrenia sank the emraclidine M4 PAM trials; with 50 per arm a modest drug effect would be lost in placebo noise.
rationale: NS-136 is reported as an M4 muscarinic positive allosteric modulator; the muscarinic class signal is mixed (KarXT positive, emraclidine failed both phase 2 trials on high placebo response). With about 50 per arm and PANSS SD near 14, a difference of about 7-8 points is needed for p<0.05; two doses give two chances. A private sponsor is more likely to publicize early if positive, lifting the conditional probability somewhat.
evidence: EMERGENT-2 KarXT, Kaul et al., Lancet 2024

assumptions.claim: Emraclidine (an M4 PAM) did not show a statistically significant improvement in PANSS total over placebo at week 6 in either EMPOWER-1 or EMPOWER-2.
In EMERGENT-2, KarXT reduced PANSS total by 9.6 points more than placebo at week 5 (-21.2 vs -11.6).

reason: The 15-minute whitening effect is near-certain; the risk sits in the second primary, durable redness reduction 14 hours after a single dose, which exceeds what approved redness relievers claim.
rationale: Topical alpha-agonist vasoconstrictors reliably whiten the eye within minutes; low-dose brimonidine separated from vehicle by about 1 point on the same 0-4 scale from 1 minute to 8 hours. Apraclonidine 0.125% should match that at 15 minutes. Both registered primaries must be met, and the 14-hour endpoint after a single dose is the real test; Alcon choosing it as a phase 3 primary, with 16 hours as a secondary, implies supportive phase 2 data.
evidence: McLaurin et al., brimonidine 0.025% phase 3, Optom Vis Sci 2018

assumptions.claim: Low-dose brimonidine 0.025% reduced ocular redness significantly versus vehicle from 1 minute through 8 hours after instillation in phase 3 trials.
assumptions.source: McLaurin E et al., Optom Vis Sci 2018

reason: Mechanism undisclosed; if HSK55718 is a non-opioid or peripheral analgesic, its SPID advantage over placebo with rescue opioids allowed may be too small to detect with about 40 patients per arm.
rationale: An injectable analgesic tested against placebo with a morphine reference after abdominal surgery, a setting where potent analgesics usually separate on SPID over 24 hours. Haisco has run several successful Chinese post-operative pain programmes. With about 40 per arm, an effect size of 0.6-0.8 SD gives 70-90% power if the drug works; rescue-medication imputation and the undisclosed mechanism are the main uncertainties. Early disclosure is likelier if positive.
evidence: HSK21542 post-operative pain trials in China, Haisco
APOLLO-2 oliceridine, Singla et al., J Pain Res 2019

assumptions.claim: Oliceridine, an IV mu-opioid agonist, was superior to placebo on analgesic response after abdominoplasty in the phase 3 APOLLO-2 trial.
assumptions.source: Singla NK et al., J Pain Res 2019

reason: With 25 per arm a roughly 35-point IHS4-55 difference is needed for significance, larger than effective HS biologics usually achieve over placebo at week 12.
rationale: LAD328 is a biologic of undisclosed mechanism tested in a 50-patient single-site proof-of-concept. Placebo IHS4-55 and HiSCR50 responses in HS run about 20-30% at weeks 12-16, so with 25 per arm a difference near 35 points is needed for two-sided significance, more than IL-17 blockers typically achieve (about 15-30 points). A proof-of-concept may use relaxed one-sided alpha, which helps slightly.
evidence: BE HEARD I/II bimekizumab, Kimball et al., Lancet 2024

assumptions.claim: In BE HEARD I and II, placebo HiSCR50 response at week 16 was about 29-32%.

reason: The genotype hypothesis comes from an exploratory subgroup of the earlier phase 2; if it does not replicate, the drug's effect on ocular discomfort is too small against a large vehicle response.
rationale: The TNFR1-genotype enrichment rests on an exploratory subgroup from the licaminlimab phase 2 (RELIEF), and post-hoc biomarker subgroups often fail to replicate. Dry-eye symptom endpoints have large vehicle responses and frequent pivotal misses. The primary population is only the genotype-positive part of 160 enrolled, limiting power. Enrolment is complete and Oculis is a listed company, so a topline release in early 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: In the RELIEF phase 2 trial, the licaminlimab treatment effect was concentrated in a subgroup carrying a specific TNFR1 genotype identified in exploratory analysis.
assumptions.source: Oculis press releases on RELIEF phase 2, 2023

reason: With 20 versus 10 patients, only a very large reduction in treatment failure reaches p<0.05; a typical 25-30 point benefit would leave p around 0.1.
rationale: Treatment-failure designs in active non-anterior NIU show placebo failure of roughly 65-80% (VISUAL I 78.5%, HUMBOLDT 67%), and effective drugs cut this by 25-30 points. With 20 versus 10 patients, a 30-point difference gives p around 0.1, so only a very large effect reaches significance. Mechanism undisclosed, single-centre Chinese trial likely to report descriptively.
evidence: VISUAL I adalimumab, Jaffe et al., NEJM 2016

assumptions.claim: In VISUAL I, treatment failure occurred in 78.5% of placebo and 54.5% of adalimumab patients with active non-infectious uveitis.

reason: Small private sponsor running a 24-patient, 6-site dose comparison in tightly defined mild iDFU with external specialist eligibility review; enrolment is likely to run past the January 2027 target, with no results posting expected by mid-2027.
rationale: Started August 2026 with a five-month window to primary completion for 24 patients needing Wagner grade 1, IDSA-mild infection, adequate perfusion and external confirmation; such screen-heavy wound trials from microcap sponsors usually slip. Results posting before the 12-month deadline is unlikely; stopping for funding is a modest risk.

reason: With about 27 eyes per arm on a coarse 0-3 NEI staining grade and a vehicle (artificial tear) arm that also improves, a plausible 0.3-grade benefit gives well under 50% power.
rationale: Lacripep is a lacritin-derived peptide whose earlier Sjogren's dry-eye phase 2 missed its primary endpoints, leaving only exploratory staining signals. Stage 1 NK patients on TID vehicle drops typically improve somewhat, and regression from grade 3 adds to the vehicle response. A 54-patient trial on an ordinal 0-3 scale can detect only a large effect, so I put success near one in four.
evidence: Lacripep phase 2 in Sjogren's dry eye (Tauber 2023)

assumptions.claim: Lacripep did not meet its primary endpoints in its phase 2 trial in primary Sjogren's-associated dry eye.
assumptions.source: NCT03226444; Tauber et al., Ocular Surface 2023

reason: About 22 per arm, high spontaneous regression of ASC-US/LSIL and a second efficacy primary (hr-HPV clearance at day 50) that must also be met make a significant result on both unlikely.
rationale: Low-grade cytology frequently regresses to NILM within months, so placebo responders will be common, while hr-HPV clearance within about seven weeks is rare in either arm. Earlier green-tea catechin (Polyphenon E) work in HPV-positive CIN1 was negative. With 45 patients and two efficacy primaries that both need significance, success needs a very large effect from an unproven EGCG plus quinine suppository.
evidence: Garcia FA et al., Cancer Prev Res 2014 (Polyphenon E in CIN1)
Ahn WS et al., Eur J Cancer Prev 2003 (EGCG in cervical lesions)

assumptions.claim: Oral Polyphenon E (EGCG) did not significantly improve clearance of HPV-positive CIN1 compared with placebo.
assumptions.source: Garcia FA et al., Cancer Prevention Research 2014

reason: Fifteen patients per arm, a 12-week window and an insensitive mVSS scale for established keloid or hypertrophic scars leave little power for a modest systemic anti-IL-11 effect.
rationale: 9MW3811 is Mabwell's anti-IL-11 antibody; IL-11 is a credible fibrosis driver, but there is no human proof that systemic blockade remodels mature scars within 12 weeks. Mature scars barely change on placebo, so any effect must come from the drug, yet mVSS moves in coarse steps and 30 patients give little power. I expect a numeric trend more often than significance.
evidence: Schafer S et al., Nature 2017 (IL-11 in fibrosis)

assumptions.claim: IL-11 acts as a key profibrotic cytokine downstream of TGF-beta in fibroblasts.

reason: The 15-minute effect of an alpha-agonist vasoconstrictor is near certain; the risk sits with the co-primary at 600 minutes, when blanching may have worn off enough to lose significance.
rationale: Topical alpha-adrenergic agonists blanch conjunctival vessels within minutes; low-dose brimonidine cut redness by over one Ora Calibra unit against vehicle. Apraclonidine adds alpha-1 activity and longer duration, and Alcon chose a 600-minute co-primary, which suggests earlier data supported it. With 89 per arm, the 15-minute endpoint is near certain; the 10-hour one is the main uncertainty.

assumptions.claim: Brimonidine 0.025% reduced ocular redness versus vehicle by more than one scale unit within minutes of instillation in phase 3 trials.
assumptions.source: McLaurin E et al., Optometry and Vision Science 2018

reason: The age-enriched design follows a subgroup signal from the earlier phase I/II; against the large intra-articular placebo response, a modest true effect is unlikely to reach significance on both WOMAC pain and function.
rationale: Intra-articular placebo injections produce some of the largest placebo responses in medicine, often 30-40% pain reduction at 3 months. Allocetra's rationale for age-related OA rests largely on a subgroup of a smaller phase I/II, and subgroup-driven confirmations usually shrink. Both WOMAC pain and function co-primaries must be significant, which lowers the odds further.
evidence: Zhang W et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2008 (placebo in OA)
Enlivex Allocetra phase I/II knee OA (topline 2025)

assumptions.claim: Placebo responses in osteoarthritis trials are large, and larger with intra-articular than with oral placebo.
assumptions.source: Zhang W et al., Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2008

reason: APOC3-targeting siRNAs consistently cut triglycerides by about half against placebo; failure would require an unexpectedly low dose or weak GalNAc-siRNA potency, which 20 patients per arm would still likely detect.
rationale: RBD5044 is a GalNAc-siRNA against APOC3, the target validated by plozasiran and olezarsen, which cut triglycerides by roughly 45-60% placebo-adjusted in moderate hypertriglyceridaemia. Percent TG change has an SD near 25-30%, so a 40-50 point difference with 20 per arm gives near-certain significance. Enrolment is already complete.

assumptions.claim: Plozasiran reduced triglycerides by roughly 44-62% versus placebo at week 24 in patients with mixed hyperlipidaemia (TG 150-499 mg/dL).
assumptions.source: MUIR, Ballantyne CM et al., NEJM 2024

reason: Mild-to-moderate AD starts from low EASI, so vehicle emollient response compresses the window; an unknown-potency topical may separate too little in four weeks.
rationale: Topical small molecules, especially JAK or PDE4 inhibitors, usually beat vehicle on EASI in mild-to-moderate AD, and 60 per arm gives good power for a 2-point difference. The record gives no mechanism, dose or prior data for VC005, and a 4-week endpoint is short, so I discount from the class success rate.

assumptions.claim: Ruxolitinib cream 1.5% produced IGA treatment success in about half of mild-to-moderate AD patients versus about 15% on vehicle at week 8.
assumptions.source: TRuE-AD1/2, Papp K et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2021

reason: Around 20 per arm in an ultra-rare epilepsy with highly variable seizure counts means only a very large effect will reach significance, and mean percent change is dragged by outliers.
rationale: ABS-1230 is a selective KCNT1 inhibitor aimed at the gain-of-function mechanism, a better-targeted approach than quinidine, which failed in a randomized crossover trial. Precision drugs in monogenic epilepsies can give large seizure reductions, but a 12-week placebo-controlled part with about 20 children per arm and skewed seizure data needs a big effect. Part 2 also depends on finishing Part 1 first, so any result by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Mullen SA et al., Neurology 2018 (quinidine in KCNT1 epilepsy)

assumptions.claim: Oral quinidine did not significantly reduce seizure frequency in a randomized crossover trial in KCNT1-related epilepsy.

reason: With about 42 per arm and plaque index as a co-primary, the stannous fluoride benefit on plaque (smaller and less consistent than on gingivitis) could miss significance even if gingivitis is clearly reduced.
rationale: Colgate single-site 6-month gingivitis/plaque studies of stannous fluoride dentifrices versus regular fluoride almost always report significant reductions in Loe-Silness GI and usually in Quigley-Hein plaque. The sponsor designs and runs these in experienced panels with tight inclusion thresholds (GI>=1.0, PI>=1.5). Main uncertainty is the plaque co-primary with 85 subjects. Public results most likely come via ClinicalTrials.gov posting or a J Clin Dent paper, often after mid-2027.
evidence: Seriwatanachai et al. 2019, SnF/zinc phosphate dentifrice 6-month plaque/gingivitis RCT
Johannsen et al. 2019 systematic review of stabilized SnF dentifrices

assumptions.claim: Stannous fluoride dentifrices reduce gingivitis versus regular fluoride dentifrices in 6-month clinical trials.

reason: Bempedoic acid is an active comparator lowering LDL-C about 16-18%; failure would need obicetrapib to underperform its roughly 30-33% placebo-adjusted effect seen in BROADWAY/BROOKLYN, which is unlikely with 213 per arm.
rationale: Obicetrapib 10 mg lowered LDL-C about 30-36% versus placebo at day 84 on top of maximally tolerated therapy (BROADWAY, BROOKLYN, TANDEM), while bempedoic acid on statins gives about 16-18% placebo-adjusted (CLEAR Harmony, CLEAR Wisdom). Expected head-to-head gap of about 14 points with SD near 27% and 213 per arm gives power well above 99% for the true effect; residual risk is execution or an unexpectedly weak obicetrapib effect in this UK population. Timing to public result is the bigger uncertainty.

assumptions.claim: Bempedoic acid added to statins lowered LDL-C by 16.5% at week 12 versus a 1.6% rise with placebo.
assumptions.source: CLEAR Harmony, Ray et al. NEJM 2019

assumptions.claim: Obicetrapib 10 mg reduced LDL-C by about 33% versus placebo at day 84 in patients on maximally tolerated lipid-lowering therapy.

reason: A short GSK crossover safety study supporting the low-GWP HFA-152a propellant switch; likely to complete close to schedule, with results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov within about a year of completion, often after August 2027.
rationale: GSK runs these regulatory propellant-switch studies efficiently and posts results reliably, but usually 6-12 months after primary completion; with completion planned for late February 2027 and possible slippage of a few months for 110 participants across 18 sites, posting by 31 August 2027 is less likely than not. Termination and primary-outcome changes are rare for this kind of descriptive AE study.

reason: Elismetrep is a first-in-class TRPM8 antagonist with a single phase 2 behind it; phase 3 effects are often smaller than phase 2, and both co-primaries (pain freedom and MBS freedom) must be met.
rationale: Acute migraine phase 3s use well-characterised endpoints with placebo 2-hour pain freedom of 10-17%; approved gepants show 8-10 point gains. With 900 per arm the trial can detect about 5 points, so the question is whether TRPM8 blockade replicates its phase 2 signal on both co-primaries. Novel mechanism and co-primary MBS keep p_met near 0.6. Enrolling 1800 by early 2027 is ambitious, so topline may slip past June 2027.

assumptions.claim: In rimegepant Study 303, 2-hour pain freedom was 21.2% with rimegepant versus 10.9% with placebo.
In ACHIEVE I, 2-hour pain freedom was 21.2% with ubrogepant 100 mg versus 11.8% with placebo.

reason: About 100 evaluable crossover patients give good but not overwhelming power; if the inhaled DHE effect is nearer 10 points than the 18 seen with MAP0004, or many patients fail to treat both attacks, significance could be missed.
rationale: Orally inhaled DHE (MAP0004) gave 28.4% versus 10.1% 2-hour pain freedom in phase 3, and DHE delivered systemically by inhalation acts fast. A within-patient crossover with 108 patients has roughly 75-85% power for a 13-16 point gain, less for smaller effects or with dropouts between periods. A small private sponsor makes early public reporting unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In FREEDOM-301, orally inhaled DHE (MAP0004) produced 2-hour pain freedom in 28.4% versus 10.1% with placebo.

reason: A Pfizer local-registration safety and immunogenicity study of Abrysvo in India with 1-month immunogenicity and 3-month safety follow-up; likely completes near schedule, with ClinicalTrials.gov posting usually 6-12 months later.
rationale: Indian regulatory bridging vaccine studies of 540 adults typically enrol quickly at experienced sites, and follow-up is only 3 months, so completion around early 2027 is plausible though some slippage is possible since the trial was still recruiting in late October 2026. Pfizer posts results routinely, but often close to the 12-month mark, so posting by end of August 2027 is uncertain. Stopping is very unlikely for an approved vaccine.

reason: SAL0140 is an unvalidated aldosterone synthase inhibitor; insufficient selectivity or dosing, plus a sizeable placebo response in Chinese office-BP trials, could shrink the placebo-adjusted fall below what 63 per arm can detect.
rationale: Aldosterone synthase inhibitors consistently lower seated SBP by about 8-11 mmHg versus placebo at 12 weeks in uncontrolled or resistant hypertension (BrigHTN, BaxHTN, Target-HTN, Launch-HTN); only HALO missed, on a smaller effect with a large placebo response. With about 63 per arm and SD near 14 mmHg, power exceeds 90% for a 9 mmHg effect, and any of three doses can meet the objective. Risk lies in the new molecule's potency and selectivity.

assumptions.claim: Baxdrostat 2 mg lowered seated SBP by 11.0 mmHg more than placebo at 12 weeks in resistant hypertension.
In BaxHTN, baxdrostat 1 mg and 2 mg lowered seated SBP by 8.7 and 9.8 mmHg more than placebo at week 12.

reason: Only a much weaker NLRP3 pathway effect at the phase 2 doses than in phase 1, combined with the noisy, skewed hsCRP distribution in 40 per arm, could prevent significance.
rationale: Oral NLRP3 inhibitors reliably cut hsCRP by roughly 60-80% versus placebo within weeks in people with obesity and elevated hsCRP, and BGE-102 showed deep hsCRP reductions in phase 1. hsCRP is a direct pharmacodynamic readout, so even with 40 per arm and high variability a placebo-adjusted fall of more than 40% is very likely significant; any of three doses suffices. BioAge is listed and has guided to near-term topline, so a press release in early 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: BGE-102 produced large (about 80% or more) reductions in hsCRP in a phase 1 cohort of participants with obesity and elevated hsCRP.
assumptions.source: BioAge Labs BGE-102 phase 1 data release, 2025

reason: An oral tablet of a GLP-1/GIP peptide depends on absorption enhancement; low or erratic bioavailability could leave the top dose with only a small weight effect at 20 weeks.
rationale: Incretin agonists given orally (oral semaglutide, orforglipron) produce clear placebo-adjusted weight loss of 6-10% by about 20 weeks, and injectable BGM0504 is already in phase 3 in China. With SD near 5% and 40 per arm, a 4% gap is enough for significance, and four doses give several chances. The main risk is weak oral exposure of the peptide. Chinese sponsor reporting habits make results by June 2027 less likely than not.

assumptions.claim: Oral semaglutide 50 mg reduced body weight by 15.1% versus 2.4% with placebo at 68 weeks.
Orforglipron reduced body weight by up to 14.7% at 36 weeks versus 2.3% with placebo.

reason: A botanical polyphenol extract has little proven pharmacology against chemotherapy-related fatigue, placebo responses on BFI are large, and two fatigue primaries must both reach significance.
rationale: Nuvastatic is an Orthosiphon stamineus extract with only small sponsor-run studies behind it. Pharmacological treatments for cancer-related fatigue (methylphenidate, modafinil, ginseng) usually give small effects that are hard to separate from placebo. With 90 per arm and an SD near 2 BFI points, a 0.6-point difference is borderline. Both co-primary fatigue scales have to be met. A small nutraceutical sponsor reporting early would tend to call the result positive, so I nudge the conditional probability up slightly.
evidence: Barton 2013 American ginseng for cancer-related fatigue (NCCTG N07C2)
Minton 2010 meta-analysis of drug therapy for cancer-related fatigue
Moraska 2010 methylphenidate RCT for cancer-related fatigue

assumptions.claim: In a randomized trial of American ginseng for cancer-related fatigue, the fatigue improvement over placebo was modest, a few points on a 100-point scale.
assumptions.source: Barton 2013, NCCTG N07C2 (J Natl Cancer Inst)

assumptions.claim: Meta-analyses of drug treatments for cancer-related fatigue find small pooled effects and large placebo responses.

reason: Viscous lidocaine also gives real topical analgesia; over a 3-hour window the advantage of a slow-release bupivacaine lozenge may be too small for 75 per arm, and dropouts by the last day of radiotherapy shrink the analysed set.
rationale: A Danish randomized phase 2 found a bupivacaine lozenge gave better oral-mucositis pain relief than standard treatment. Bupivacaine acts much longer than lidocaine, whose relief fades within about an hour, so a 3-hour total-pain-reduction endpoint favours the lozenge. The open-label design also tends to favour the new product on a patient-rated endpoint. The risks are an active comparator, attrition before the last day of radiotherapy, and a modest sample. The registered timeline is unrealistic: enrolment began July 2026 and each patient needs about seven weeks of radiotherapy, so results probably come late in 2027.
evidence: Mogensen 2017 bupivacaine lozenge vs standard treatment for oral mucositis pain in head and neck cancer (phase 2)

assumptions.claim: In a randomized phase 2 in head and neck cancer patients with oral mucositis, the bupivacaine lozenge reduced oral pain more than standard pain treatment.
assumptions.source: Mogensen et al. 2017, Support Care Cancer

assumptions.claim: Topical lidocaine gives short-lasting relief of oral mucositis pain, well under 3 hours.

reason: The only realistic failure is a WD-890 dose with too little exposure to beat placebo on both PGA 0/1 and PASI 75 at week 16; placebo rates in Chinese psoriasis trials are low.
rationale: WD-890 is an oral allosteric TYK2 inhibitor. That class reliably beats placebo in moderate-to-severe psoriasis: deucravacitinib got sPGA 0/1 in about 50-55% versus about 7-9% on placebo at week 16, and newer Chinese TYK2 inhibitors have shown similar or larger phase 2 effects. With 375 patients, both co-primaries (PGA 0/1 and PASI 75) are very likely highly significant. The record still showed recruiting in late October 2026 with a November 2026 primary completion, so the readout will slip.

assumptions.claim: In POETYK PSO-1, sPGA 0/1 at week 16 was about 54% with deucravacitinib versus about 7% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Armstrong et al. 2023, J Am Acad Dermatol (POETYK PSO-1)

assumptions.claim: In the Asian POETYK PSO-3 trial, deucravacitinib was significantly better than placebo on both sPGA 0/1 and PASI 75 at week 16.

reason: Failure would need GQ1005 to be clearly less potent than other topoisomerase-I-payload HER2 ADCs, or ILD and toxicity-driven dropouts to erode its PFS advantage over T-DM1.
rationale: Every topoisomerase-I-payload HER2 ADC tested head-to-head against T-DM1 in second-line HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer has shown a large PFS benefit. DESTINY-Breast03 gave HR about 0.28-0.33 for T-DXd, and Chinese analogues (trastuzumab rezetecan, SHR-A1811 and others) report similar margins. On BICR, T-DM1 median PFS in these trials runs about 6-7 months. With 228 patients and a likely HR near 0.35-0.4, the trial has ample power. OS is usually immature at the PFS analysis.

assumptions.claim: In DESTINY-Breast03, BICR PFS hazard ratio for T-DXd versus T-DM1 was 0.28 at the primary analysis, with median PFS for T-DM1 of 6.8 months.
assumptions.source: Cortes et al. 2022, N Engl J Med (NCT03529110)

assumptions.claim: In DESTINY-Breast03, about 7% of T-DM1 patients discontinued treatment because of adverse events.
assumptions.source: Cortes et al. 2022, N Engl J Med

reason: Adult data suggest about a 1-point rTNSS benefit over placebo on top of background therapy; with 68 per arm and an SD near 2.4, power is only about 60-70%, and pollen-season variability can shrink the difference.
rationale: Stapokibart (anti-IL-4Ra) met its primary rTNSS endpoint in a large adult phase 3 in uncontrolled seasonal allergic rhinitis, with a placebo-adjusted gain of about 1 point on top of background therapy, and it is approved in China for this indication. Adolescents should respond similarly. The adolescent trial is small, though, and the placebo arm on background INCS and antihistamines improves substantially. Whether the result is significant depends mainly on sample size and how heavy the pollen season is.
evidence: Stapokibart (CM310) phase 3 in seasonal allergic rhinitis, Nat Med 2025
Dupilumab in seasonal allergic rhinitis (Weinstein 2018, NCT02805790)

assumptions.claim: In the adult phase 3 trial of stapokibart in uncontrolled seasonal allergic rhinitis, daily rTNSS improved significantly more than placebo over 2 weeks, by roughly 1 point.
Stapokibart is approved in China for seasonal allergic rhinitis in adults.

reason: The anti-IL-4Ra benefit on rTNSS over a strong placebo-plus-background response is only about 1 point; a mild pollen season or modest exposure could shrink it below significance even with 110 per arm.
rationale: SHR-1819 is Hengrui's anti-IL-4Ra antibody, the same target as stapokibart, whose adult seasonal allergic rhinitis phase 3 met its 2-week rTNSS primary endpoint with about a 1-point placebo-adjusted benefit. With 220 patients and an SD near 2.5, power is about 80-85%. Enrolment is complete and the primary completion date is near, so the timeline is not at risk. The main uncertainty is the effect size relative to a large placebo response.
evidence: Stapokibart (CM310) phase 3 in seasonal allergic rhinitis, Nat Med 2025
Weinstein 2018 dupilumab in seasonal allergic rhinitis (NCT02805790)

assumptions.claim: Anti-IL-4Ra blockade with stapokibart significantly reduced daily rTNSS over 2 weeks versus placebo in adults with uncontrolled seasonal allergic rhinitis.

reason: A magnesium-salt oral spray has no proven antitussive mechanism in refractory chronic cough, placebo arms cut cough frequency by about 20-30%, and 30 per arm can detect only a large effect.
rationale: Refractory chronic cough trials show large placebo reductions in objective cough frequency. Even potent P2X3 antagonists such as gefapixant and camlipixant reach only about 15-30% placebo-adjusted reductions. SC0032 is a topical magnesium salt spray from a company whose earlier products target airway hygiene, with no published efficacy in cough. This is a 60-patient pilot run on a consumer cough monitor (HYFE), so significance needs a large effect, and the odds of that are low.

assumptions.claim: In the COUGH-1 and COUGH-2 trials, the placebo-adjusted reduction in 24-hour cough frequency with gefapixant 45 mg was about 15-18%.
Placebo arms in refractory chronic cough trials typically show 20-40% reductions in 24-hour cough frequency.

reason: Topical ascorbic acid may protect the endothelium only modestly; with endothelial cell loss SD near 300 cells/mm2 and 100 per arm, a benefit under about 80 cells/mm2 is unlikely to reach significance.
rationale: Phacoemulsification of hard nuclear cataracts typically costs about 8-15% of endothelial cells at 3 months, roughly 250-350 cells/mm2, with a wide spread between patients. Small studies of ascorbic acid in the irrigation solution or given systemically suggest it reduces free-radical endothelial damage, but the effects were modest and inconsistent. It is uncertain whether a topical 5% drop gets enough into the anterior chamber. A trial of 100 per arm has only moderate power for a 60-80 cell difference.
evidence: Lee 2016 ascorbic acid in irrigation solution and endothelial cell loss in phacoemulsification
Rubowitz 2003 ascorbate and corneal endothelial damage in phacoemulsification
Walkow 2000 endothelial cell loss after phacoemulsification and nucleus hardness

assumptions.claim: Endothelial cell loss after phacoemulsification increases with nuclear hardness and is commonly 8-15% at 3 months for dense nuclei.
assumptions.source: Walkow et al. 2000, J Cataract Refract Surg

assumptions.claim: Adding ascorbic acid to the irrigation solution was associated with less endothelial cell loss after phacoemulsification in a small randomized study.

reason: Palonosetron alone already gives roughly half of high-risk patients a complete response, and rescue use is partly nausea-driven, so the NK1 add-on benefit may be only about 10-15 points, borderline with about 87 per arm.
rationale: Adding an NK1 antagonist (aprepitant, fosaprepitant) to a 5-HT3 antagonist reliably cuts postoperative vomiting and improves complete response by about 10-20 percentage points in high-risk patients. HRS5580 is an injectable NK1 antagonist from Hengrui. With about 87 per arm and two doses, at least one dose should reach p<0.05 if the effect is near 15-20 points. Rescue driven by nausea dilutes the complete-response gain more than the vomiting-free gain.
evidence: Diemunsch 2007 aprepitant vs ondansetron for PONV

assumptions.claim: Aprepitant added to standard prophylaxis markedly reduced postoperative vomiting at 24 and 48 hours compared with ondansetron alone, with smaller gains in complete response.
assumptions.source: Diemunsch et al. 2007, Br J Anaesth

assumptions.claim: In patients with 3 or more Apfel risk factors, the baseline PONV risk is about 60-80%.

reason: Facial repigmentation by week 24 is often still partial with oral JAK-pathway inhibitors, and with about 50 per arm and a high SD in percent F-VASI change, a weaker compound may miss significance.
rationale: Oral JAK inhibitors have consistently beaten placebo on F-VASI percent change at 24 weeks in non-segmental vitiligo. Upadacitinib 11-22 mg gave roughly -36% versus about -8% on placebo in phase 2, and ritlecitinib and povorcitinib showed similar significant separation. Assuming QY201 is a JAK-pathway inhibitor, its 20 mg arm should separate from placebo. With about 50 per arm, power is good for a 20-30 point difference but limited if the compound is weaker.

assumptions.claim: In the upadacitinib phase 2 trial in non-segmental vitiligo, F-VASI improved significantly more than placebo at week 24 with 11 mg and 22 mg.
In the ritlecitinib phase 2b vitiligo trial, F-VASI percent change at week 24 was significantly better than placebo at 50 mg.
assumptions.source: Ezzedine et al. 2023, J Am Acad Dermatol (NCT03715829)

reason: PASI 100 at week 12 is a demanding endpoint; with about 30 per arm and near-zero placebo response, the drug needs roughly 15-20% complete clearance to reach significance, which a weaker or slow-onset biologic could miss.
rationale: Placebo PASI 100 at week 12 is almost always 0-1% in moderate-to-severe psoriasis, so any potent biologic (IL-17 or IL-23 class drugs reach 25-40% at week 12) separates even with 30 per arm. Choosing PASI 100 as primary signals sponsor confidence in high potency. The risk is a novel mechanism or modest dose with slower onset giving only 10-15% PASI 100, which with Fisher's exact test at this size is borderline. Hengrui rarely publishes phase 2 results quickly, so public reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In ERASURE, PASI 100 at week 12 was about 29% with secukinumab 300 mg versus under 1% with placebo.
In UNCOVER-2, ixekizumab every 2 weeks gave about 40% PASI 100 at week 12 versus about 1% with placebo.

reason: Whether GIPR antagonism adds meaningful weight loss on top of semaglutide in people with type 2 diabetes is unproven in humans; over only 13 weeks during semaglutide titration the add-on effect may be about 1% or less, below what 50 per arm can detect.
rationale: AT673 is presumably Antag's GIP receptor antagonist peptide, tested as an add-on to semaglutide titrated to 1.0 mg. Preclinical and MariTide data suggest GIPR antagonism can enhance GLP-1 weight loss, but a standalone antagonist's added effect over 13 weeks in T2D (where weight loss is blunted) is likely small, about 1%. With an SD near 3.5% and 50 per arm, the SE is about 0.7%, so power is modest; two doses give two chances. HbA1c benefit beyond semaglutide is less likely.

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide 1.0 mg reduced body weight by about 4.5 kg at 30 weeks versus about 1 kg with placebo in drug-naive T2D.
assumptions.source: SUSTAIN-1, Sorli et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2017

assumptions.claim: People with T2D lose less weight on semaglutide than those without diabetes (about 9.6% at 68 weeks with 2.4 mg in STEP 2).

reason: Enrollment is done, but the registered primary completion of Feb 2027 looks computed from the study start, while the 240-day post-dose-2 SAE window for the last enrollees likely runs into mid-2027.
rationale: Small Canadian academic-industry vaccine trial with 47 participants already enrolled; stopping is unlikely. The SAE primary outcome runs to 240 days after the second dose (about day 60), so if the last participants were enrolled in mid- to late 2026 the true primary completion falls around mid-2027, after the 90-day lateness threshold, provided the record is updated. No US sites, so results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov is unlikely, and safety-outcome changes to the record are rare.

reason: Rocuronium gives good or excellent intubation conditions in over 90% of patients; if HRS-9190 has a slower onset at the chosen intubation time, its rate could fall below the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: Phase 3 non-inferiority against rocuronium on a near-ceiling endpoint (good or excellent Cooper conditions above 90%). Hengrui will have picked the dose from phase 2 to match intubating conditions, and Chinese anesthesia phase 3 trials of this kind usually succeed. With 160 per arm and a likely 10-percentage-point margin, non-inferiority is very likely if true rates are similar. The main risk is slower onset at the protocol's intubation time. Public reporting by mid-2027 is uncertain, since Hengrui often discloses only at NDA filing.
evidence: Tran 2015 Cochrane review (rocuronium vs succinylcholine intubation conditions)

assumptions.claim: Rocuronium 0.6 mg/kg produces good or excellent intubating conditions in most (above 90%) of elective surgery patients within 60-90 seconds.
assumptions.source: Zemuron US prescribing information; Tran et al., Cochrane 2015

reason: With about 15 patients per arm and two co-primary endpoints (corneal staining and OSDI) that must both reach significance against a vehicle with a sizeable placebo response, the trial has low power even if the drops work.
rationale: A small sponsor's amniotic-derived eye drop has only open-label support in ocular GVHD. Dry-eye trials often fail objective staining endpoints even with hundreds of patients because vehicle drops also improve the ocular surface. Here 30 patients must show significance on both staining (SD about 1 grade) and OSDI (SD about 20 points); joint power is probably under 25% even for a real effect. Enrolling a rare population at 5 sites makes the March 2027 completion date optimistic.

assumptions.claim: In OPUS-2, lifitegrast met the symptom co-primary but failed the inferior corneal staining co-primary despite about 700 patients.

reason: The design mirrors aldosterone synthase inhibitor trials, where the effect is about 8-10 mmHg; a weaker drug or a large Chinese placebo response, plus the second primary needing week 4 and 8 significance too, could sink it.
rationale: The population (uncontrolled on 2 drugs including a diuretic, or resistant on 3 or more) copies the BaxHTN design, suggesting SAL0120 is an aldosterone synthase inhibitor or similar add-on. Such drugs give 8-10 mmHg placebo-adjusted seated SBP falls at 12 weeks. With 64 per arm and an SD of about 14 mmHg, the SE is about 2.5, so the high dose would very likely reach significance if it is in that class. The second primary (weeks 4 and 8) adds modest extra risk. The trial completed in July 2026; disclosure timing is unclear.

assumptions.claim: In BaxHTN, baxdrostat 2 mg lowered seated SBP by about 9.8 mmHg more than placebo at week 12 in uncontrolled or resistant hypertension.
In BrigHTN, baxdrostat 2 mg reduced SBP by about 11 mmHg versus placebo in treatment-resistant hypertension.

reason: An oral incretin peptide's success depends on adequate oral bioavailability; if exposure at the top dose is low, weight loss at 20 weeks could be only a few percent, though 48 per arm still detects about 3%.
rationale: MWN109 is an incretin-class peptide (Minwei reports multi-receptor agonism) given orally with titration for 20 weeks. Oral semaglutide and other incretin agonists give 5-10% placebo-adjusted weight loss by about 20 weeks; Chinese placebo arms lose about 1%. With about 48 per arm and an SD near 5.5%, the SE is about 1.1%, so even a 3% effect would be significant. The trial completed in July 2026; data may appear at ADA June 2027 or later.

assumptions.claim: Oral semaglutide 50 mg produced about 15% weight loss versus about 2.4% with placebo at 68 weeks in adults with obesity.
Placebo-treated Chinese adults with obesity lost about 2-3% of body weight at 52 weeks in SURMOUNT-CN.

reason: Injectable incretin agonists reliably beat placebo by 10% or more over 36 weeks; the only plausible failure is an unexpectedly weak molecule or high dropout in a 31-per-arm trial.
rationale: Injectable MWN109, titrated to the highest of three doses over 36 weeks, is in a class (GLP-1-based, possibly multi-agonist) where placebo-adjusted weight loss of 10-20% by 9 months is typical: retatrutide gave about 16% at 24 weeks and mazdutide 9 mg in China about 15-18%. With 31 per arm and an SD around 7%, even a 5% effect is significant. The trial completes in late 2026, so public data by mid-2027 depend on an ADA presentation or press release.

assumptions.claim: Retatrutide 12 mg produced about 17.5% weight loss at 24 weeks versus 1.6% with placebo.
Semaglutide 2.4 mg gave about 14.9% versus 2.4% weight loss at 68 weeks in STEP 1.

reason: Incretin agonists lower HbA1c by about 1 point versus placebo in metformin-treated T2D; failure would need very poor oral exposure, since 40 per arm detects about 0.5 points.
rationale: Oral MWN109 at its highest dose for 20 weeks in Chinese T2D with HbA1c 7.5-11% on metformin or diet. Oral semaglutide 14 mg cut HbA1c about 1.1 points more than placebo in PIONEER 1, and incretin multi-agonists do more; placebo arms typically drift down 0.3-0.5. With 40 per arm and an SD near 0.9, the SE is about 0.2, so any real effect above 0.5 points is significant. The trial is still recruiting with a March 2027 completion, so results by mid-2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Oral semaglutide 14 mg lowered HbA1c by about 1.4 points versus about 0.3 with placebo at 26 weeks.
Tirzepatide monotherapy lowered HbA1c by about 1.9-2.1 points versus +0.04 with placebo at 40 weeks.

reason: Open-label maintenance extension that is fully enrolled and past its registered completion; it will most likely just be marked completed without posted results.
rationale: Chinese single-sponsor extension study that is active, not recruiting, with a primary completion date already passed; termination is unlikely. Chinese sponsors without US sites rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov, and primary outcome edits after completion are uncommon.

reason: With about 30 patients per arm and a large vehicle response typical of dry eye trials, a realistic staining difference under one NEI point is unlikely to reach p<0.05 even with two doses tested.
rationale: Small single-site Korean phase 2 (about 30 per arm) of an undisclosed dry eye agent vs vehicle on NEI corneal staining at 12 weeks. Vehicle arms in dry eye trials improve substantially, and drug-vehicle staining differences are usually modest relative to an SD near 2-2.5 points, so power is limited; two doses give two chances. Korean sponsors often report phase 2 outcomes via press with favourable framing, which slightly raises the conditional chance of a reported met result.

assumptions.claim: Vehicle arms in 12-week dry eye trials show meaningful improvement in corneal fluorescein staining.

reason: Coartem cures about 95% of African children by PCR-corrected ACPR, leaving no room for a significant superiority result with 60 per arm; the cohort is descriptive and not built to beat the standard of care.
rationale: Open-label platform cohort testing a single-dose cipargamin plus ganaplacide-lumefantrine combination vs Coartem in children. Coartem PCR-corrected ACPR is typically 90-98% in Africa, so superiority cannot be shown at n=60 per arm; the cohort is estimation-focused with no stated hypothesis. Novartis will likely report descriptively on ClinicalTrials.gov months after a February 2027 primary completion, mostly after June 2027. Parasite clearance with cipargamin should be faster, but a formal test may not be reported.

assumptions.claim: In the KALUMA phase 3, Coartem PCR-corrected cure was about 94% and ganaplacide-lumefantrine about 97%.
assumptions.source: Novartis KALUMA topline press release, November 2025

assumptions.claim: Cipargamin clears P. falciparum parasitemia faster than artemisinin derivatives (parasite clearance half-life about 1 hour).

reason: Two co-primaries must both be met; the anterior chamber cell endpoint is the weaker one, as Dextenza's second phase 3 missed day-14 cell clearing when the vehicle arm cleared 31% of eyes on its own.
rationale: A 4 mg subconjunctival triamcinolone depot vs sham (no anti-inflammatory) after cataract surgery should clear anterior chamber cells and pain far more than no treatment; 125 per arm gives good power for a 20-30 point difference. Precedent: Dextenza and Dexycu phase 3s mostly met both endpoints, but one Dextenza trial missed ACC at day 14 when vehicle clearing was high. Co-primary requirement and a variable sham response are the main risks. Harrow, a public company, will likely announce topline in 2027.

assumptions.claim: In Dextenza phase 3 study 1, absence of anterior chamber cells at day 14 was 33.7% vs 14.6% with vehicle, and absence of pain at day 8 was 80.4% vs 43.4%.
assumptions.source: Walters et al. 2016, J Clin Exp Ophthalmol (OTX-DP phase 3)

assumptions.claim: In a later Dextenza phase 3, day-14 anterior chamber cell clearing was 52.3% vs 31.1% with vehicle.
assumptions.source: Tyson et al. 2019, J Cataract Refract Surg

reason: With 160 per arm and an SD near 14 mmHg, any placebo-adjusted office SBP fall beyond about 4 mmHg is significant; failure needs a weak dose or a large placebo response in office readings.
rationale: GW906 is a subcutaneous long-acting agent with PD characterisation and 6-month dosing, most likely an angiotensinogen-targeting siRNA like zilebesiran, which lowered 24-h SBP by about 14-17 mmHg vs placebo. With roughly 160 per arm, a placebo-adjusted office SBP reduction of 6-12 mmHg would be highly significant. Main risks are a large placebo response in office measurements and an undisclosed low dose. Chinese sponsors report selectively, so public disclosure by mid-2027 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Zilebesiran reduced 24-hour mean ambulatory SBP at month 3 by about 14-17 mmHg vs placebo in KARDIA-1.

reason: Three primaries (gingivitis, bleeding, plaque) must all be significant with about 40 per arm; the plaque index is the likeliest to miss against a regular fluoride paste.
rationale: Colgate's stannous fluoride dentifrices reliably reduce gingivitis and bleeding vs regular fluoride paste in 6-month trials, with effects large relative to the SD of whole-mouth indices; plaque reductions are smaller but usually significant. With three primaries required and 40 per arm, the plaque index is the main risk. Colgate typically publishes in journals a year or more later and posts on ClinicalTrials.gov irregularly, so disclosure by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Johannsen et al. 2019 systematic review of stabilized SnF dentifrice (Heliyon)
Valkenburg et al. 2019 systematic review of SnF dentifrice on gingivitis

assumptions.claim: Stannous fluoride dentifrices reduce gingival index and bleeding vs regular sodium fluoride dentifrice in 6-month clinical trials.
assumptions.source: Valkenburg et al. 2019, Int J Dent Hyg (systematic review)

reason: A 24-adult EB trial in Taiwan with matched lesion pairs started in October 2026 and must finish enrolment and 12 weeks of treatment and follow-up by March 2027, which a rare-disease sponsor will likely miss.
rationale: Epidermolysis bullosa is rare and the eligibility rules (paired 10-40 cm2 lesions of similar size, present 3 weeks to 9 months) narrow the pool further in Taiwan alone, so reaching 24 subjects and completing the 85-day primary window by mid-June 2027 is unlikely. A small Taiwanese sponsor rarely posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov, and a safety primary is seldom amended.

reason: With 15 per arm, a moderate placebo withdrawal peak and the slow onset of cebranopadol could leave early withdrawal unsuppressed, so the peak-COWS difference may not reach significance.
rationale: Cebranopadol is a NOP/mu agonist with proven analgesia at 400 micrograms, so it should suppress withdrawal in patients on 50-90 MME; 800 micrograms per day is a substantial dose. Placebo patients should reach moderate peak COWS around 10, giving a plausible 4-5 point difference with SD near 4.5. With only 15 per arm, power is around 60-80%, and two dose arms give two chances. Slow absorption could blunt the effect on an early peak.
evidence: Cebranopadol chronic low back pain phase 2 (Christoph et al. Pain 2017)

assumptions.claim: Cebranopadol 400 micrograms met its primary pain endpoint vs placebo in the ALLEVIATE-1 phase 3 trial after abdominoplasty.
assumptions.source: Tris Pharma ALLEVIATE-1 topline press release, 2024

assumptions.claim: Cebranopadol reduced chronic low back pain vs placebo in a phase 2 trial at doses of 200-600 micrograms once daily.
